channel.description: CTIPilot day-by-day cyber threat intelligence coverage for Swiss government entities: autonomously generated, source-linked, IOC-free.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-13
item.description:
• NetScaler: 28 flaws fixed, one reaches every default ADC and Gateway; update to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39. Cloud Software Group's bulletin CTX697305 of 2026-11-12 fixes 28 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, 9 of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.0 or above; CVE-2026-120868 (9.3) needs no feature or authentication and affects every deployment in default configuration, and CVE-2026-107412 (9.5) reaches Gateway and AAA virtual servers. The fixed builds are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS and 13.1-37.293, and bulletin CTX697320 fixes an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass in 14.1-74.34; the bulletins describe the impact as unpredictable behaviour or denial of service, offer no workaround and state no exploitation status, while CERT-EU writes that Citrix reports none and no source reports an attack. →
  • Huntress: device-code phishing posing as a Teams booking skips URL reputation checks; hunt Cmsi:Cmsi sign-ins. Huntress describes a mid-October 2026 intrusion in which a spear-phish impersonating a company executive led, through a Safe Links-wrapped Google share link that sidestepped URL reputation checks, to a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler whose 'Booking Reference' is a Microsoft device code, with a phishing kit shipped as AES-256-GCM ciphertext that the browser decrypts and a fallback that restarts the device-code session when MFA is required. The account had no MFA enrolled and the captured session was replayed from a residential proxy, showing as a device-code (Cmsi:Cmsi) sign-in followed by programmatic user agents; Huntress names no victim country and no Swiss link. →
  • Group-IB: DarkLunnen's FortiOS chain leaves a 'service' super_admin; Swiss FortiGates are scan targets only. Group-IB found an open directory on a Latvian server that documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen and links to no known actor: a modified public exploit for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that creates an administrator named service with super_admin privileges, among other tools. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 Swiss FortiGate scanning targets, which it says does not confirm vulnerability or exploitation, and restic commands that accessed an S3 backup repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, without naming an organisation or confirming success. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01NetScaler: 28 flaws fixed, one reaches every default ADC and Gateway; update to 14.1-73.57 or 13.1-64.39. Cloud Software Group's bulletin CTX697305 of 2026-11-12 fixes 28 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and Gateway, 9 of them scored CVSS 4.0 9.0 or above; CVE-2026-120868 (9.3) needs no feature or authentication and affects every deployment in default configuration, and CVE-2026-107412 (9.5) reaches Gateway and AAA virtual servers. The fixed builds are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS and 13.1-37.293, and bulletin CTX697320 fixes an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass in 14.1-74.34; the bulletins describe the impact as unpredictable behaviour or denial of service, offer no workaround and state no exploitation status, while CERT-EU writes that Citrix reports none and no source reports an attack. →
  2. 02Huntress: device-code phishing posing as a Teams booking skips URL reputation checks; hunt Cmsi:Cmsi sign-ins. Huntress describes a mid-October 2026 intrusion in which a spear-phish impersonating a company executive led, through a Safe Links-wrapped Google share link that sidestepped URL reputation checks, to a fake Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler whose 'Booking Reference' is a Microsoft device code, with a phishing kit shipped as AES-256-GCM ciphertext that the browser decrypts and a fallback that restarts the device-code session when MFA is required. The account had no MFA enrolled and the captured session was replayed from a residential proxy, showing as a device-code (Cmsi:Cmsi) sign-in followed by programmatic user agents; Huntress names no victim country and no Swiss link. →
  3. 03Group-IB: DarkLunnen's FortiOS chain leaves a 'service' super_admin; Swiss FortiGates are scan targets only. Group-IB found an open directory on a Latvian server that documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen and links to no known actor: a modified public exploit for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that creates an administrator named service with super_admin privileges, among other tools. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 Swiss FortiGate scanning targets, which it says does not confirm vulnerability or exploitation, and restic commands that accessed an S3 backup repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, without naming an organisation or confirming success. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 3Trending vulnerabilities 4Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 12

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures3 items

NOTABLEexploitedNATOB2

DarkLunnen: Group-IB's exposed operator directory shows mass exploitation of FortiOS CVE-2024-55591 that plants a 'service' super_admin account, a 4,725-target Swiss FortiGate scan list and restic access to an S3 backup repository at a 'Swiss domain'; Group-IB does not confirm any Swiss victim

Group-IB reports that in late July 2026 it found an open directory on a Latvian server that held the operator's /root/ directory, 457 files of which 35 were recovered, and documents more than 14 months of operations against Europe by an operator it tracks as DarkLunnen; Group-IB links it to no known actor and does not establish nationality or state affiliation (Group-IB, 2026-11-11). The main campaign used a modified watchTowr proof of concept for FortiOS CVE-2024-55591, designed to create a backdoor super-admin account named service (Group-IB, 2026-11-11); the recovered results list about 600 devices in Turkey (hospitals, industry and municipalities), 16 in Ukraine, 14 in Azerbaijan and 1 in Algeria, and a stolen FortiGate configuration from a Romanian organisation carried the same account and yielded 10 cleartext VPN passwords (Group-IB, 2026-11-11).

The Swiss content is thin. Group-IB recovered a list of 4,725 FortiGate scanning targets for Switzerland and says such lists identify scanning targets but do not confirm vulnerability or successful exploitation; a table of additional operations also lists restic commands with AWS credentials accessing an S3 repository at a Swiss domain in May and June 2025, with production snapshots enumerated, and the report names no organisation and says that for several operations the evidence is limited to recorded commands (Group-IB, 2026-11-11). Fortinet's advisory FG-IR-24-535 lists FortiOS 7.0.0 through 7.0.16 and FortiProxy 7.2.0 through 7.2.12 and 7.0.0 through 7.0.19 as affected, fixed in 7.0.17, 7.2.13 and 7.0.20, names FortiOS 7.2, 7.4, 7.6 and 6.4 as not affected and offers disabling the HTTP/HTTPS administrative interface as the workaround (Fortinet PSIRT, 2025-01-14).

Exposure
A FortiOS 7.0 device below 7.0.17, or a FortiProxy below its fixed release, whose HTTP/HTTPS administrative interface was ever reachable from the internet; a device exposed while vulnerable can carry an account that patching does not remove (Group-IB, 2026-11-11).
Detection
In FortiGate event logs, an administrator named service with the super_admin profile, any unexplained administrator or local user, and super_admin logins or account creation through the jsconsole interface, which Fortinet lists among its indicators; in VPN logs, logins with accounts whose secrets sat in an exposed configuration (Group-IB, 2026-11-11).
Defender takeaway
Hunt for the account on patched devices too, assume the configuration was read on a device that was exposed while vulnerable and rotate the VPN user passwords, administrator passwords, IPsec pre-shared keys and LDAP or RADIUS credentials it stored, review VPN logs and enforce MFA, and enable private data encryption, which is off by default (Group-IB, 2026-11-11); no source says that a Swiss organisation was compromised.

Builds on: 2026-08-11/gunra-raas-fortios-mfa-backdoor-linux-prng-recoverable

threat13 Nov 04:05Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Group-IB Threat Intelligence · Fortinet PSIRT (FG-IR-24-535)
NOTABLENATOB2

Device-code phishing disguised as a Microsoft Teams meeting booking: Huntress traces an October intrusion from a spear-phish through a Microsoft Safe Links-wrapped Google share link to a scheduler page whose 'Booking Reference' is the device code, an in-browser decrypted kit that restarts the flow when MFA is required, and a token replayed through a residential proxy

In mid-October a Huntress SOC saw an employee of a construction company receive a spear-phishing email from a typosquatted domain impersonating another company's senior vice president; the link in the mail was wrapped by Microsoft Safe Links and pointed to a Google share link that redirected server-side to the lure page, so the mail body held the Google link and not the lure domain, which Huntress says sidestepped URL reputation checks for email security (Huntress, 2026-11-12). The page posed as a Microsoft Teams meeting scheduler, and behind it the backend started a Microsoft device-code sign-in; the "Booking Reference" shown to the victim is the device code, which the victim enters in a genuine Microsoft sign-in window (Huntress, 2026-11-12).

The kit is shipped as AES-256-GCM ciphertext that the browser decrypts, so that to an email scanner or crawler that does not run JavaScript the page is an encrypted blob; if Microsoft answers AADSTS50076 or interaction_required because MFA is required, the kit starts a new device-code session and restarts the flow (Huntress, 2026-11-12). After the victim finished, the attacker held a session token and the device-code login (Cmsi:Cmsi) was routed through a residential proxy; the compromised account had no MFA enrolled and was used from an unmanaged device, and Huntress contained the incident before it escalated (Huntress, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
A Microsoft 365 tenant that allows the device-code flow for users with no device that needs it, particularly accounts without MFA.
Detection
In Entra sign-in logs, a successful device-code authentication shown as Cmsi:Cmsi, programmatic user agents such as python-requests and node afterwards (often only in the non-interactive log), and a change of ASN and region inside the same session ID; in mail and proxy telemetry, a Google share link that redirects to a freshly registered lookalike domain (Huntress, 2026-11-12).

Triage: Huntress treats a device-code prompt that follows a link, a booking request or another unexpected interaction as suspicious, and the captured session shows up as a replay from another ASN and region within one session (Huntress, 2026-11-12).

Defender takeaway
Restrict or monitor device-code authentication where it is not needed, enforce phishing-resistant MFA, and investigate unfamiliar device sign-ins from unmanaged devices, new regions or residential proxy networks (Huntress, 2026-11-12).

Builds on: 2026-11-05/vaud-m365-device-code-phishing-campaign-romandie

threat13 Nov 04:07Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Huntress
NOTABLENATOB1

WFX Phantom: stolen GitHub tokens push a CI secret stealer into repositories from 2026-11-10, steal Actions secrets, runner memory and cloud tokens, plant AWS and Azure persistence designed to outlast rotation and delete the workflow runs; StepSecurity counts more than 63,000 probe pull requests

StepSecurity reports that from 2026-11-10 an attacker uses stolen GitHub tokens of real developer and bot accounts, as a developer would, not a bug in GitHub Actions, to push a CI secret stealer into repositories those tokens can write to (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). It first opens a pull request titled "docs: dependency audit notes" from a branch named wfx-docs that only proves write access; StepSecurity counts more than 63,000 such probes by 2026-11-12 (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12), Aikido, which tracks the campaign as wfx-loot, counts 4,837 compromised accounts and at least 1,835 repositories where the payload ran, and Endor Labs counts 8,926 infected repositories (Aikido, 2026-11-12; Endor Labs, 2026-11-12); BleepingComputer reports that the compromised accounts included those of the US General Services Administration and the French government (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12).

Where the token's permissions and the repository's setup let it run, the attacker pushes a script of about 1,500 lines through an edit to an existing workflow or CI shell script, a new workflow on a short-lived branch or a hidden script that an npm hook runs, and the script collects every Actions secret, the job token, the memory of the runner worker process and credential files for the major clouds and registries, then uses the job's OIDC token to open AWS, GCP and Azure sessions (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). It plants persistence meant to outlast rotation, a rewritten AWS role trust policy with new access keys and federated identity credentials on Azure applications, sends the archive over HTTP and from 2026-11-12 through a Telegram bot, and within about a minute pushes a revert commit and deletes the workflow run, leaving a gap in the run numbers that StepSecurity calls the most reliable sign the stealer ran (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). How the tokens were obtained is not known: some probes came through the Fly.io GitHub App, and StepSecurity has no evidence of a breach of Fly.io (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12). BleepingComputer's report of Aikido's findings gives the same probe title and start date (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
Any account or bot with write access to repositories you own or build from whose token may be exposed (a personal access token, an OAuth grant, a GitHub App user token), and any build with cloud OIDC trust or long-lived secrets; bots that bypass branch protection raise the risk (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12).
Detection
In source-control data, pull requests titled "docs: dependency audit notes", branches named wfx-docs and commits since 2026-11-10 with the messages "ci: refresh build cache", "ci: restore", "ci: cleanup", "chore: add ci helper" or "chore: add dependency audit workflow", and in CI run history a gap in the run numbers right after one; in AWS and Azure audit logs, changes to role trust policies, newly created access keys and federated credentials named wfx-ci (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12).

Triage: a probe pull request alone shows that the account that opened it is compromised, even if nothing else happened; the payload probably ran where a commit with one of those messages is paired with a deleted run (StepSecurity, 2026-11-12).

Defender takeaway
Treat the account behind any probe or payload commit as compromised and revoke its tokens; where the payload ran, rotation is not enough because the persistence is designed to outlast it, and Endor Labs says secrets rotated after the first wave were likely stolen again in 1,838 repositories (Endor Labs, 2026-11-12).

Builds on: 2026-10-10/ghostaction-fake-audit-workflow-git-history-credential-theft

threat13 Nov 04:04Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: StepSecurity · Aikido Security · Endor Labs · BleepingComputer

02Trending vulnerabilities4 items

HIGHCVE-2026-120868 +28NATOA2

Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: 28 flaws fixed on 2026-11-12, among them CVE-2026-120868 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) in packet processing on every deployment in default configuration, plus an unauthenticated NetScaler Console authentication bypass (CVE-2026-120869); no exploitation reported

Cloud Software Group's bulletin CTX697305 of 2026-11-12 fixes 28 flaws in customer-managed NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12). The bulletin describes the impact as unpredictable or erroneous behaviour or denial of service, while its CVSS 4.0 vectors score confidentiality, integrity and availability impact High on ten rows, and no source says that code execution is possible (CERT-EU, 2026-11-12). The row that applies everywhere is CVE-2026-120868 (9.3), a memory overflow in packet processing with the precondition "All NetScaler ADC and NetScaler Gateway deployments (Default configuration / No additional feature required)" and no authentication or user interaction (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12). CVE-2026-107412 (9.5) covers several overflows on an appliance configured as a Gateway (SSL VPN, ICA Proxy, CVPN or RDP Proxy) or an AAA virtual server, which CERT-EU, citing the vendor, says can be reached without authentication (CERT-EU, 2026-11-12); further rows at 9.3 or 8.7 each depend on one configured feature, such as an SMPP, DNS-over-HTTPS or PUSH virtual server or a SAML, WebAuth, email OTP, certificate or LDAP authentication action, and CVE-2026-120863 needs only a path from an untrusted host to the management address NSIP or NSIP6 (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12). Bulletin CTX697320 fixes CVE-2026-120869, an unauthenticated authentication bypass on the NetScaler Console, scored 9.4 with an adjacent vector in the bulletin (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12) and 9.3 with a network vector in ENISA's record (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-12).

The fixed builds are 14.1-73.57, 13.1-64.39, 14.1-73.58 FIPS and 13.1-37.293 for 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12), and 14.1-74.34 for the Console (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12); Secure Private Access Hybrid deployments must upgrade their NetScaler instances (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12). Neither bulletin states an exploitation status or a workaround. CERT-EU writes that Citrix reports no exploitation and no confirmed public proof of concept (CERT-EU, 2026-11-12), NCSC Switzerland lists the exploitation status as unknown (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-12), and none of the CVEs is in CISA's catalog. heise reports that Citrix will publish NetScaler security fixes monthly on a fixed date close to Patch Tuesday from now on, with out-of-cycle updates for urgent cases such as active exploitation (heise, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
Every customer-managed NetScaler ADC or Gateway below the fixed build of its branch is in scope for CVE-2026-120868 whatever its configuration; the other rows apply where the named feature is configured, which the bulletin tells you to find with configuration searches such as add vpn vserver, add authentication vserver or add authentication samlAction (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12).
Detection
No source states a detection method or a check for compromise. The stated impact is a crash or denial of service, so unexplained packet-engine restarts, core files or reboots after inbound traffic to a Gateway or AAA virtual server are the telemetry to review; this is an inference, not a source statement. Where a logout had occurred, /var/log/httperror.log can hold authentication material (one of the rows), so limit who can read that file (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade internet-facing Gateway and AAA appliances first, then every other ADC, to the fixed build of the branch, because CVE-2026-120868 needs no feature (CERT-EU, 2026-11-12) and neither bulletin offers a workaround (Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12; Cloud Software Group, 2026-11-12); keep NSIP and the Console IP on a management network.

Builds on: 2026-10-23/netscaler-php2shell-management-gui-fixes-2026-10-27

vulnerability13 Nov 04:00Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Cloud Software Group (CTX697305) · Cloud Software Group (CTX697320) · CERT-EU (advisory 2026-020) · NCSC Switzerland (Cyber Security Hub post 13175) · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2026-124482) · heise online
NOTABLENATOB2

SignDrop: a public Windows local privilege escalation to SYSTEM that turns Microsoft's CLFS authentication mitigation against itself through Defender's signature-update RPC; proof of concept published 2026-11-10, no CVE and no patch, no exploitation reported

Cyderes Howler Cell reports that the exploit was published on 2026-11-10 under a GitHub handle, the same day as November Patch Tuesday, with no coordinated disclosure, no CVE and no patch, and that its team reproduced a SYSTEM shell from a standard user session (Cyderes, 2026-11-12). The chain is a logic bug with no memory corruption: CLFS containers are created through Object Manager symbolic links, an oplock on a bait file confirms that Microsoft Defender has engaged, a call to Defender's signature-update RPC makes clfs.sys create its .cnpf authentication-signature file as SYSTEM at an attacker-chosen path, here hid.dll in the Common Files\microsoft shared\ink directory, a file that does not ship in that directory; the content is replaced with a payload DLL and a runas request makes consent.exe load it, which starts a SYSTEM conhost.exe on the user's desktop (Cyderes, 2026-11-12). Like every release of the same cluster it needs a foothold on the host first. It applies where the CLFS authentication Mode value, under HKLM\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication, is 0 or 1 (Cyderes, 2026-11-12).

Cyderes says the feature ships enabled on current Windows versions and that the researcher tested Windows 11 26H2 and experimental builds of Windows 11 and Windows Server 2025; the researcher's estimate that 80% of Windows installations are vulnerable has no data behind it (Cyderes, 2026-11-12). The researcher adds that, because the privileged file creation appears to come from the antimalware engine's own process, the technique can be used against any antimalware engine's self-defense; that claim rests on his statement alone (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-12). No source reports exploitation, and Microsoft had not commented publicly as of 2026-11-11 (SecurityOnline, 2026-11-11).

Exposure
Any Windows host on which an attacker can already run code as a standard user and whose CLFS authentication Mode is 0 or 1; Cyderes tells defenders to read the Mode value on every host to size the population (Cyderes, 2026-11-12).
Detection
File-creation telemetry for hid.dll in the ink directory, which Cyderes counts, with the Defender signature-update RPC call, among its two highest-signal observables because the file does not ship in that directory; that RPC called from a process outside the Defender service tree; symbolic-link churn under \BaseNamedObjects\Restricted\ correlated with Defender RPC activity; consent.exe loading a DLL from the ink directory; and a SYSTEM conhost.exe on the interactive desktop right after a hid.dll write. The exploit deletes hid.dll afterwards, so keep file-creation and image-load telemetry rather than relying on a disk sweep (Cyderes, 2026-11-12).

Triage: Cyderes calls a hid.dll creation in the ink directory and a Defender signature-update RPC from outside the Defender service tree rare enough in a typical estate to alert on rather than hunt, and the first is a successful write whatever the variant (Cyderes, 2026-11-12).

Defender takeaway
No patch exists, so inventory the Mode value, restrict untrusted local code execution with application and script control, and do not switch CLFS authentication off as a workaround, because that re-exposes the older memory-corruption attacks it blocks; Cyderes counts sixteen public releases from the same researcher in roughly thirty-one weeks, so expect more (Cyderes, 2026-11-12).

Builds on: 2026-10-08/bigdiskbuster-defender-update-starvation-disk-exhaustion-poc

vulnerability13 Nov 04:03Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Cyderes Howler Cell · BleepingComputer · SecurityOnline
NOTABLECVE-2026-124007 +6NATOB2

Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO refrigeration supervisors: VulnCheck published 14 CVEs on 2026-11-12, seven scored CVSS 4.0 9.2 to 9.3 (unauthenticated command injection that runs as root, a hard-coded Administrator password, Administrator and root passwords computed from the MAC address and date); Copeland ended support on 2026-03-16 and ships no fixes; no exploitation reported

VulnCheck, the assigning CNA, describes unauthenticated command injection in XWEB EVO through the password field (VulnCheck, 2026-11-12) and the username field (VulnCheck, 2026-11-12) of its login and API scripts, and through the sh parameter of the setuid xwconsole.cgi (VulnCheck, 2026-11-12), all reaching root; a hard-coded password for the built-in Administrator account that gives a full session in one request (VulnCheck, 2026-11-12); and Administrator and root passwords that can be computed offline from the device MAC address and the date (VulnCheck, 2026-11-12; VulnCheck, 2026-11-12; VulnCheck, 2026-11-12). The cluster holds 14 records, and the seven scored 9.2 or higher are the ones covered here (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-12). The records' ranges end before 5.6.2 or 5.7.0 or run through 5.8.8, but Copeland's download pages list EVO packages only up to 5.2.3 of 2018 (Copeland, 2026-11-13), and its bulletin says software support ended on 2026-03-16 with no further firmware or security updates (Copeland, 2026-03-16), so no source shows where a fixed build can be had.

No source reports exploitation or a public proof of concept for these CVEs, and none ties them to the compromises of Danfoss, Copeland and Dixell controllers. Copeland's bulletin of 2026-10-14, carried in the Dixell France guide that CERT-FR links, acknowledges a vulnerability on an end-of-life generation of XWEB EVO controllers and tells operators to remove all XWEB EVO units from the public internet immediately (translated from French) (Dixell France, 2026-10-14); NCSC Switzerland says that guidance addresses end-of-service XWEB EVO systems and that the public information does not confirm exploitation of the Danfoss CVEs it lists (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-06), and BACS lists Copeland and Dixell XWEB as potentially affected (BACS, 2026-11-10). The one compromised-unit log read concerns an XWEB Pro, not an EVO (Ransom-ISAC, 2026-11-06).

Exposure
An XWEB EVO unit, sold until October 2023 (Copeland, 2026-03-16), whose login page appears when the site's public address is opened from outside the site network, which is the vendor's own test (Dixell France, 2026-10-14).
Detection
No source gives log artefacts for these flaws. After suspected access the vendor's procedure is to review the user list and profiles and the alarm categories, levels and recipients with a test alarm, and to read product temperatures directly in the cabinets because setpoints or alarm thresholds may have changed; CERT-FR says a factory reset removes persistence but leaves an end-of-life unit vulnerable (Dixell France, 2026-10-14; CERT-FR, 2026-10-16).
Defender takeaway
No fix is coming, so keep XWEB EVO units off the internet and reach them only through a VPN, and plan the move to the supported XWEB Pro (Dixell France, 2026-10-14).

Builds on: 2026-10-13/danfoss-ak-sm-ak-sc-french-supermarket-refrigeration-attack · 2026-08-28/claroty-copeland-xweb-pro-refrigeration-unauth-root-rce

vulnerability13 Nov 04:02Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124007) · VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124002) · VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124010) · VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124004) · VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124012) · VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124005) · VulnCheck (CNA advisory CVE-2026-124006) · ENISA EUVD (VulnCheck records for Copeland) · Copeland (XWEB EVO end-of-support bulletin) · Copeland (XWEB EVO download page) · Dixell France (Copeland XWEB security recommendations) · NCSC Switzerland (Cyber Security Hub post 13054) · BACS (warning on refrigeration systems) · Ransom-ISAC · CERT-FR (alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012)
NOTABLECVE-2026-126325NATOA2

CVE-2026-126325, PTC Windchill and FlexPLM: deserialization of untrusted data lets an unauthenticated remote attacker run code (CVSS 4.0 9.2, high attack complexity); PTC announced a patch on 2026-11-11 and keeps the fixed releases behind its support login, no exploitation is reported, and an earlier Windchill flaw was exploited in June

PTC's CNA record, published on 2026-11-11, describes CVE-2026-126325 as a critical remote code execution flaw in PTC Windchill and PTC FlexPLM that may be exploited through the deserialization of untrusted data, scored CVSS 4.0 9.2 with high attack complexity, no privileges and no user interaction (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-11). NCSC Switzerland says successful exploitation lets remote attackers achieve code execution and potentially full system compromise through crafted network requests carrying malicious serialized data, with network access to the exposed system as the prerequisite (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-12); BSI describes a remote, anonymous attacker (translated from German) (BSI CERT-Bund, 2026-11-11). The affected release lines are Windchill 11.0 M030, 11.1 M020, 11.2.1.0, 12.0.2.0, 12.1.2.0, 13.0.2.0 and 13.1.0.0 to 13.1.4.0, with ten FlexPLM releases up to 13.1.3.0 (The Hacker News, 2026-11-12).

PTC's Trust Center says a patch has been available since 2026-11-11, that a Windchill administrator applies it, that PTC-hosted environments were patched on the customer's behalf, and that self-hosted customers are urged to apply it as soon as possible (PTC Trust Center, 2026-11-11). The vendor advisory sits behind a customer login, so no fixed release is public (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-12). NCSC Switzerland lists the exploitation status as unknown (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-12), and PTC's change log records no attack on this flaw (PTC Trust Center, 2026-11-11). The product has a history: CISA listed the earlier Windchill and FlexPLM flaw CVE-2026-12569 as exploited in June (The Hacker News, 2026-06-26), and Ransom-ISAC, eCrime.ch and DEFUSED reported Cl0p-linked attackers chaining a FlexPLM information disclosure with a Windchill login-servlet flaw to drop JSP web shells (The Hacker News, 2026-07-25).

Exposure
A self-hosted Windchill or FlexPLM server on one of the listed release lines that a hostile network can reach; PTC-hosted environments need no action (PTC Trust Center, 2026-11-11).
Detection
No source gives a detection for this flaw. For the June intrusions PTC told readers to search access logs for POST requests to /Windchill/login/ JSP files, which legitimate traffic does not make, and to look for persistent JSP web shells in the Windchill login directory (PTC Trust Center, 2026-11-11); whether the same pattern applies to CVE-2026-126325 is not stated.
Defender takeaway
Patch self-hosted Windchill and FlexPLM now, internet-reachable servers first, and ask PTC for the fixed release of your line through the support portal, because no fixed version is public (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-12).

ANSSI's second REACTIV report of 2026-11-12 counts 64 further breaches, five at ministries, says all exploit the weaknesses already listed and names the reuse of stolen secrets as the technique, with new cases of an SMS second factor validated by the attacker and IDOR flaws combined with infostealer credentials.

ANSSI's second REACTIV situation report, published on 2026-11-12, counts 64 new data breaches brought to its attention since the first report of 2026-09-30, five of them at ministries or bodies under their supervision, with a significant fall in breaches detected or claimed at ministry level; it says all of them exploit weaknesses already named in September and gives the reuse of stolen secrets to reach ministry applications as the technique, which lets attackers extract the data legitimately (translated from French) (ANSSI, 2026-11-12). The new cases it describes: stolen technical accounts reused against a foreign-ministry library portal after a server compromise; an IDOR flaw in the payment API of a public registration portal for the hunting-licence exam, exposing more than a thousand people; an agent's France Travail account compromised with the SMS second factor validated, with the data of more than 60,000 agents and professionals claimed on a forum; and partner-account credentials from infostealers without two-factor authentication, combined with an IDOR flaw on a URL exposing file identifiers, which let attackers extract close to 1.2 million files from the CAF's VACAF service in three days. Education nationale is now put at 25 of 30 académies, with lateral movement over the interministerial network (ANSSI, 2026-11-12). ANSSI's recommendations are renewing compromised or suspect secrets first, systematic strong authentication, strict control of privileged accounts and tighter filtering to prevent exfiltration (ANSSI, 2026-11-12).

Verification & coverage notes

Window: standard 26 h (gap to the previous fire 24.0 h). KEV sweep: no catalogue additions in the window and no ransomware-flag flips on covered entries. No closed-source drops present (S5 not spawned). Seven new entries (eight composed, one dropped by verification) and nine changelog records; no deep dive and no critical: nothing met the stop-and-act bar. The will-publish set exceeded eight items, so the Phase 4 deep read of the primaries was delegated to five scoped cti-research workers (DR-A to DR-E, saved bodies under work/<run-id>/bodies/); two of them did not report call telemetry (null in the block above), and the bridge-fetch counts of DR-A and DR-B are the workers' own approximations.

Inclusions with reduced confidence or carve-outs:

  • Citrix NetScaler ADC/Gateway CTX697305 (high): vendor bulletin plus watchTowr credit, no exploitation reported; high because the default-configuration gateway role is the constituency's exposed edge (the verifier questioned the call because the vendor states a crash or denial-of-service impact and no source reports code execution or exploitation; kept, since an unauthenticated default-configuration flaw scored up to 9.3 on an internet-facing gateway decides a 7-day patch window, and the body states both limits). Citrix revised the bulletin on 2026-11-12 after the slice captured it, correcting seven mistyped CVE numbers (now CVE-2026-111333 to CVE-2026-111339); the verifier caught it in iteration 4 and the entry now carries all 29 records.
  • PTC Windchill/FlexPLM CVE-2026-126325: the vendor's Trust Center and CNA record are the primary; NCSC Switzerland, BSI, ENISA and The Hacker News restate them and the fixed releases are behind a customer login, so confidence stays medium; references the two earlier Windchill entries.
  • DarkLunnen (Group-IB): admitted through the rotational-lookback rule (d); cves[] left empty so the entry does not collide with the Gunra and Gentlemen entries that carry the same FortiOS ids; references the Gunra entry.
  • SignDrop (CLFS LPE, public PoC, no patch): reproduction and detection tables from one research source plus the PoC publication; no CVE assigned yet, cves: [].
  • Dixell/Copeland XWEB EVO: VulnCheck CNA cluster, seven records all no-patch; actions: [] because the earlier Danfoss entry already carries the do-now step.
  • Check Point PHP2Shell update: priority raised notable to high on the vendor's new SK1000302 portal and VPN-gateway scope plus CVE-2026-123039; the main analysis was rewritten and stays above 550 words only by the structured record, flagged for the audit.
  • N-able N-central / Confluence: the 4EverAble2Shell exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 is recorded on the N-able entry as an update and cross-referenced in prose on the Confluence entry; the Confluence exploited status is not changed (its own product is not shown exploited).

Borderline drops (PD-11 and the incident floor):

  • borderline-drop: Siemens SSA-166980 PHP2Shell energy and building products: control-centre products, no Swiss public-body link, exploitation needs a reachable PHP portal
  • borderline-drop: Azul Payara CVE-2026-110003 and CVE-2026-90908: admin interface not normally reachable, no exploitation
  • borderline-drop: PwnEscape CVE-2026-99999: local guest-to-host vector, lab-only bundle, not on KEV, prior reopen conditions unmet
  • borderline-drop: Ivanti CSA 5.0.8.1: relay-only and contradicted by its own table, Ivanti pages unreadable on every transport
  • borderline-drop: Microsoft 365 outage MO1550821: outage, not an attack
  • borderline-drop: Poland ePUAP: attack repelled per the ministry, no vector or actor
  • borderline-drop: Mittwald MCP breach: out-of-nexus hosting provider, cause is the vendor claim alone
  • borderline-drop: Operation Endgame Gootloader, CastleRAT and StealC takedown: commodity loaders, no Swiss defender step named
  • borderline-drop: Symantec AI-assisted retailer intrusion, Unit 42 CL-STA-1238 Cairn AI framework: out of nexus or already saturated in the store
  • borderline-drop: Elastic SANSAR Ray GPU cryptomining, Akamai StrikeStub: niche hosts or a single sample, no defender decision (StrikeStub delivers a ClickFix lure from a compromised Swiss site that Akamai does not name, and ClickFix delivery is already covered, so there is no named Swiss victim to act on)
  • borderline-drop: React Flight CVE-2026-126187: application-code preconditions, no exploitation or PoC, advisory date discrepancy (2026-10-14 vs 2026-11-10)
  • borderline-drop: Fireworks AI and Notion AI, FBI/DOJ FaceStealer: supplier read-across or a single secondary source with no constituency link
  • borderline-drop: CNIL ten sanctions on French authorities: swept by the 2026-11-10 fire, outside the window, generic failings
  • borderline-drop: Liechtenstein VwbP audit tender, Bitdefender Threat Debrief November 2026: governance-only delta or periodic statistics
  • borderline-drop: Patch Tuesday uncovered 9.8 rows (Xbox Live, Media Foundation, Color Management, DirectMusic, VFP): client-side, exploitation unlikely, fixed by the same cumulative update

Contradictions and source conflicts: the ScreenConnect SCKit entry keeps the Huntress and Blackpoint explanations of the delivery path attributed to each source rather than merged; the CNA record CVE-2026-127063 was added as a structured field. The Citrix CVE-id collision above is the only structural data defect found.

Dropped by verification: the Saxony emergency pager entry (heise and Spiegel, one informant for the message content, no access vector or actor) fell below the incident floor and was removed before publish; it carried no CVEs, so no state needed unwinding.

Dedup: the four entity-overlap WARNs are deliberate decisions, not deltas: SignDrop shares the Windows entity with the Mark-of-the-Web zero-day and eMudhra entries, DarkLunnen the FortiOS entity with the October hardening-release entry, and the Huntress kit the Microsoft 365 entity with the Q3 email-landscape entry; each is a distinct finding on a ubiquitous platform.

Verification: six iterations, no double-CLEAN. Iteration 1 found 27 truth and editorial findings (18 truth, 9 editorial; the Saxony pager entry was dropped for falling below the incident floor), iteration 2 found 7, iteration 3 found 3, iteration 4 found 10 (the main one a Citrix bulletin revision that corrected seven CVE numbers, so the entry now carries 29 records), iteration 5 found 4, and iteration 6 returned NEEDS_FIXES with truth 1 (a citation split on the Check Point update section), editorial 0 and advisory 4, no F1 or F4, so decision rule 5 applied: the finding was fixed, the gate re-run clean (59 pass, 0 fail) and the fire published on that early exit without a seventh pass. The one residual truth finding is fixed but unverified by a further cold pass, as are two last advisory edits (the Citrix body wording and a BleepingComputer government-accounts clause on the WFX Phantom entry); the audit should give the Citrix, Check Point and WFX Phantom entries an independent read. Declined with rationale: the Citrix priority (kept high), the Cisco BroadWorks KEV item, the StrikeStub drop, the Copeland download-page citation date and the .NET Exposure Windows clause.

Operational notes: the jina reader pool is dead (every key HTTP 402, the anonymous tier 401), so pages that only the reader could serve were read by WebFetch or left unconfirmed. Research worker S1 left 18 stray scratch files at the filesystem root (/atlassian.*, /depthfirst.*, /nextjs.*, /picus.*, /qnap.*, /qnap_news.*, /ruby.*, /yeswehack.*, /znuny.*, each a .err plus a .txt, .json or .html); the sandbox safety check denied deleting them and the run did not work around it, so the operator may remove them. They hold fetch scratch output only and are not part of the repo.

Source health: all 314 records read clean after the sweep (UNSOLVED list cleared in the same run). Fixed: ahnlab-asec (WebFetch reads it, every in-container transport is refused with a bare 403; tools/source_health.py now classes a webfetch record whose direct transport is refused with 401/403/429/451 as webfetch-only, with a test in tools/test_source_health.py), schneier (health recipe now reads the home page through extract, the atom-feed titles alone carried too little vocabulary) and mozilla-ca-compliance-bugzilla (content_scope: general-news, the REST rows are CA incident titles). Recipe notes recorded for kaspersky-securelist, rapid7-research, huntress, checkpoint-support, citrix-netscaler-security-bulletins, picus-security-blog and connectwise-trust-center (working fetch target: the ConnectWise CNA disclosure repository on GitHub). Candidate sources added: cyderes-howler-cell, huntback, blackpoint-cyber (each with its reason in sources.json); arctic-wolf-labs, maire-info and dysruptionhub were proposed by the slices and left for a later run.

  • Essential-coverage: every essential record was attempted. Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport; GitHub disclosure repository substitutes), sygnia (403 on every transport), databreaches.net article pages (Cloudflare interstitial; feed pages only), Ivanti pages (unreadable on every transport), Atlassian bulletin index (stale extract), europol-newsroom (JS application, headline only).
  • Watchlist: none configured.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-12
item.description:
• ScreenConnect SCKit: second wave hits on-prem; disable RMM+, update technician clients to 26.6.5+. Huntress saw an operator use access to several cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels on 2026-11-11 to run Run Command as SYSTEM on groups of managed endpoints, installing an attacker-controlled second ScreenConnect client and the SCKit toolkit on at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations within 90 minutes; Sophos independently saw the same client deployments. Huntress later said the activity seems related to the third-party RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise's CNA record CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) says the extension uses a static API secret by default, names no fix and gives disabling as the mitigation, while a Huntress spokesperson says the panel-access vector is still unclear and Blackpoint calls the extensions' role unresolved. A second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations (Huntress) and appears to target on-premises instances with mitigations pending (Blackpoint); Microsoft describes a rogue client built to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, which ConnectWise says ScreenConnect clients 26.6.5 and later block. →
  • Plone anonymous RCE chain: update or install the 20261110 hotfix, block portal_modifier, check modifier conditions. The Plone and Zope security team released fixes on 2026-11-10 for a chain of issues that together let an anonymous visitor run code on the server in Plone 6.0, 6.1 and 6.2 and, per the team, back to at least 4.3; the entry point is a CMFEditions flaw rated 9.8 with no privileges required, and its advisory says a working proof of concept exists. The team's fixes are the updated packages or the hotfix package Products.PloneHotfix20261110, a workaround that blocks URLs containing portal_modifier has applied since the 2026-11-02 pre-announcement, CVE ids are requested and no source reports exploitation. →
  • Apache httpd mod_http2 RCE: update to 2.4.71 or drop h2/h2c from Protocols; Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine fixed. The Apache HTTP Server project released 2.4.71 on 2026-11-11 to fix CVE-2026-119618, a race in mod_http2 that it rates critical and says can lead to remote code execution in versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70; Red Hat adds that it is unauthenticated, affects only servers with HTTP/2 enabled through the Protocols directive, and that public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit, while no source reports exploitation. Red Hat has fixed RHEL 9 and 10, Debian bookworm and trixie and Alpine ship 2.4.71 packages, Ubuntu has shipped backported fixes, while a researcher's public test reproduces crashes on 2.4.70 and, per Wordfence, does not show code execution. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01ScreenConnect SCKit: second wave hits on-prem; disable RMM+, update technician clients to 26.6.5+. Huntress saw an operator use access to several cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels on 2026-11-11 to run Run Command as SYSTEM on groups of managed endpoints, installing an attacker-controlled second ScreenConnect client and the SCKit toolkit on at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations within 90 minutes; Sophos independently saw the same client deployments. Huntress later said the activity seems related to the third-party RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key; ConnectWise's CNA record CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) says the extension uses a static API secret by default, names no fix and gives disabling as the mitigation, while a Huntress spokesperson says the panel-access vector is still unclear and Blackpoint calls the extensions' role unresolved. A second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations (Huntress) and appears to target on-premises instances with mitigations pending (Blackpoint); Microsoft describes a rogue client built to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, which ConnectWise says ScreenConnect clients 26.6.5 and later block. →
  2. 02Plone anonymous RCE chain: update or install the 20261110 hotfix, block portal_modifier, check modifier conditions. The Plone and Zope security team released fixes on 2026-11-10 for a chain of issues that together let an anonymous visitor run code on the server in Plone 6.0, 6.1 and 6.2 and, per the team, back to at least 4.3; the entry point is a CMFEditions flaw rated 9.8 with no privileges required, and its advisory says a working proof of concept exists. The team's fixes are the updated packages or the hotfix package Products.PloneHotfix20261110, a workaround that blocks URLs containing portal_modifier has applied since the 2026-11-02 pre-announcement, CVE ids are requested and no source reports exploitation. →
  3. 03Apache httpd mod_http2 RCE: update to 2.4.71 or drop h2/h2c from Protocols; Debian, Ubuntu, Alpine fixed. The Apache HTTP Server project released 2.4.71 on 2026-11-11 to fix CVE-2026-119618, a race in mod_http2 that it rates critical and says can lead to remote code execution in versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70; Red Hat adds that it is unauthenticated, affects only servers with HTTP/2 enabled through the Protocols directive, and that public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit, while no source reports exploitation. Red Hat has fixed RHEL 9 and 10, Debian bookworm and trixie and Alpine ship 2.4.71 packages, Ubuntu has shipped backported fixes, while a researcher's public test reproduces crashes on 2.4.70 and, per Wordfence, does not show code execution. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 4Trending vulnerabilities 2Updates to prior coverage 8Action items 18

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures4 items

NOTABLENATOA2

Belgium's CCB warns that attackers abused Microsoft Entra ID SMS first-factor sign-in (phone number and one-time code, no password) to compromise several Belgian organisations; turning off 'Use for sign-in' is the priority step

The Belgian Centre for Cybersecurity (CCB) warned on 2026-11-10 that a trusted partner had observed successful attacks against multiple Belgian organisations in which attackers abused Microsoft Entra ID SMS as a first factor, the sign-in mode in which a phone number and a one-time code replace the password (CCB, 2026-11-10). The warning gives no victim count, sector, actor, date range or attack chain, and it does not say how the codes were obtained; its only statement on the factor itself is that SMS and voice can be phished, intercepted or SIM-swapped (CCB, 2026-11-10). No other source reports the Belgian attacks. Microsoft describes the method as designed for frontline workers, advises enabling it only for them, and says it is different from SMS as a multifactor method, which needs a username and password (Microsoft Learn, 2026-10-30). Microsoft is disabling first-factor sign-in in tenants with no such traffic in the previous 30 days (Microsoft Learn, 2026-10-30) and retires its own SMS and voice delivery on 2027-02-01 for all users except Global Administrators and external users, who follow on 2027-07-01; a customer-configured telephony provider can keep the methods working (Microsoft Learn, 2026-09-23).

Exposure
An Entra tenant whose SMS authentication method policy has first-factor sign-in turned on for any user or group; the CCB's path is Authentication methods, SMS, "Use for sign-in", and the Authentication methods activity report shows who actually uses it (CCB, 2026-11-10). Microsoft's how-to calls the same setting "Enable first factor sign-in" and says that leaving it unchecked limits SMS to multifactor authentication and self-service password reset (Microsoft Learn, 2026-10-30).
Detection
In Entra sign-in logs, look for successful sign-ins that used SMS as the authentication method; in audit logs, for phone-number or authentication-method changes; then for unusual locations or devices and follow-on mailbox rules or application consents, reviewing as far back as log retention allows (CCB, 2026-11-10).
Defender takeaway
Disable SMS first-factor sign-in now for everyone who has an alternative and restrict it to the smallest group where it must stay, as the CCB advises; remove SMS and voice for privileged accounts only after each has a working phishing-resistant method, and avoid a blind switch-off, which can lock users out or leave them with a password alone (CCB, 2026-11-10). Microsoft's own clearing reaches only tenants with no first-factor SMS sign-in traffic in the previous 30 days (Microsoft Learn, 2026-10-30), so a tenant that uses the method stays exposed until it acts.

Builds on: 2026-11-05/vaud-m365-device-code-phishing-campaign-romandie

threat12 Nov 04:03Zsingle-source · national CERTOpen finding →
Sources: Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) · Microsoft Learn
HIGHCVE-2026-127063updatedNATOB1

ScreenConnect: commands pushed through Run Command to at least 288 managed endpoints at 48 Huntress customers within 90 minutes on 2026-11-11 installed a rogue second client and the SCKit toolkit; Huntress links the activity to the RMM+ extension, whose versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key

On 2026-11-11 Huntress observed an operator using access to several cloud-hosted ScreenConnect panels to run commands as SYSTEM on groups of managed endpoints through the Run Command feature, hitting at least 288 hosts at 48 organisations within 90 minutes (Huntress, 2026-11-11). Each host installed an attacker-controlled second client and fetched SCKit, a 16-file toolkit delivered encrypted that sets the legitimate client to manual start so the attacker's copy replaces it and runs a per-host executable from a scheduled task (Huntress, 2026-11-11). A second wave on 2026-11-13 hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations with no follow-on executions observed (Huntress, 2026-11-13), and Blackpoint says it appears to target on-premises instances where mitigations are still pending (Blackpoint, 2026-11-13).

Huntress's later update says the activity seems related to RMM+, a third-party extension that bypasses ScreenConnect's accounts, roles and MFA: versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 accepted a blank access key when an administrator had never set one (Huntress, 2026-11-11). ConnectWise, as CNA, published CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) saying the extension uses a static API secret by default; it names no fixed version, removed the extension from cloud-hosted instances and tells on-premises customers to disable it and not reinstall it (ConnectWise, 2026-11-12).

Microsoft describes the technician stage: RelayTrap, a replacement client compiled on the endpoint with the .NET C# compiler and designed to deliver a payload to the technician who connects, and browser-access code that searches Chrome, Edge and Opera profiles for cookies named .ASPXAUTH, with a component designed to queue payloads through the console's Shared Toolbox (Microsoft, 2026-11-13). ConnectWise says clients 26.6.5 and later block the transfer, and Microsoft adds that a cloud-console update does not update technician clients (Microsoft, 2026-11-13); Huntress and Blackpoint saw no successful technician compromise (Huntress, 2026-11-11; Blackpoint, 2026-11-13).

Exposure
A ScreenConnect instance whose panel can run commands on managed endpoints, run by the organisation or an IT provider; an RMM+ extension at any version, since ConnectWise's record names a static default secret, with versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32 and a blank key as the condition Huntress describes; a technician host client older than 26.6.5; an endpoint with a second client service pointing at a foreign relay.
Detection
ScreenConnect instance audit logs, Run Command and Toolbox history for mass executions nobody started and RMM+ requests with no matching login (Huntress, 2026-11-11), and file-transfer-and-run events (event ID 201, per Blackpoint) (Blackpoint, 2026-11-13); process-creation telemetry with the ScreenConnect client service as parent of cmd, PowerShell or msiexec, curl or PowerShell downloads followed by a silent msiexec install (the Sophos pattern) (Sophos, 2026-11-11), a scheduled-task PowerShell watcher that compiles an executable with the .NET compiler (Microsoft, 2026-11-13), and a client service named like a Windows component (Huntress, 2026-11-13).
Defender takeaway
Treat Run Command or Toolbox executions you did not start as a compromise; disable RMM+ and the four other extensions the first notice named, update every technician host client to 26.6.5 or later, rotate ScreenConnect credentials and revoke active sessions and the browser and identity-provider sessions the toolkit could steal, and keep hosts and technician workstations out of service until the rogue client and persistence are gone (Huntress, 2026-11-11; Microsoft, 2026-11-13). Removing the rogue client alone leaves the persistence and the web sessions, and the cleanup script found in the kit must not be used (Microsoft, 2026-11-13).
Update13 Nov 2026 04:04 UTCrun 2026-11-13T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

ConnectWise, as CNA, published CVE-2026-127063 (CVSS 4.0 9.3) on 2026-11-12: the third-party RMM+ extension "uses a static API secret by default", no fixed version has been announced, disabling is the mitigation, and ConnectWise has removed the extension from cloud-hosted instances while on-premises customers must disable it and not reinstall it (ConnectWise, 2026-11-12). This differs from Huntress's account of a blank key in versions 1.0.31 and 1.0.32, and a Huntress spokesperson told The Record that it has seen no evidence of a new vulnerability and that how the attacker got panel access is still unclear, while ConnectWise says the extension's API is protected by a passphrase the partner sets (The Record, 2026-11-12). Blackpoint reverse engineered the toolkit, saw unauthorised deployments through legitimate cloud-hosted instances but no successful propagation to a technician workstation, and calls the extensions' role in the first panel access unresolved (Blackpoint, 2026-11-12).

Update14 Nov 2026 03:57 UTCrun 2026-11-14T0255Z-intelheadlinesummarytechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Microsoft published on 2026-11-13 its analysis of SCKit, which includes RelayTrap, a malicious replacement for the ScreenConnect client on an affected customer endpoint that is designed to deliver a payload to a technician's workstation when they connect for support (Microsoft, 2026-11-13). A watcher on the endpoint enumerates the ScreenConnect client services and builds RelayTrap for each with the .NET C# compiler, and the toolkit's browser code searches Chrome, Edge, Opera and Opera GX profiles for cookies named .ASPXAUTH; a console-distribution component is designed to combine the cookie with the anti-forgery and access tokens, upload a payload, queue it through the Shared Toolbox and remove the uploaded item afterwards (Microsoft, 2026-11-13). Microsoft relays ConnectWise's statement that clients 26.6.5 and later block the transfer; in its own words the fix for CVE-2026-84869 was released on 2026-09-08 and a cloud-console update does not automatically update technician clients, and it advises live response or another out-of-band method instead of ScreenConnect on a suspected device, with connecting technician workstations in scope, invalidation of ScreenConnect web and identity-provider sessions, and no use of a cleanup script recovered from the kit (Microsoft, 2026-11-13). Blackpoint's own test found that a current Host client did not fetch or run the queued transfer, and it found no technical link between the extensions and RelayTrap or the browser routines (Blackpoint, 2026-11-13).

Huntress's update of 2026-11-13 reports a second spike at 16:12 UTC that hit 205 hosts at 41 organisations with no follow-on executions observed, one incident at an organisation running a self-hosted RMM+, a rogue client persisting as a service called Windows Update Agent, and ConnectWise's updated advisory urging partners to verify that every technician client runs 26.6.5 or later (Huntress, 2026-11-13). Blackpoint's update says the second wave appears to target on-premises instances where mitigations remain pending (Blackpoint, 2026-11-13).

Builds on: 2026-09-12/cve-2026-84869-connectwise-screenconnect-worm-file-transfer

threat12 Nov 04:07Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Huntress · Sophos · BleepingComputer · ConnectWise (CNA disclosure CVE-2026-127063) · The Record · Blackpoint Cyber · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2026-124597) · Microsoft Threat Intelligence · Huntress (update of 2026-11-13) · Blackpoint Cyber (SITREP update of 2026-11-13)
NOTABLENATOB2

GSocket on compromised Linux web servers: Microsoft sees several unrelated actors install the open-source relay client after exploiting an internet-facing web application, so access outlives the patch; no inbound listener, no attacker-hosted infrastructure

Microsoft observed several unrelated threat actors deploy GSocket, an open-source remote access tool, on Linux servers after exploiting an internet-facing web application, and says it kept access after the exploited vulnerabilities were remediated (Microsoft, 2026-11-11). The chain starts with command execution as a child of the web server or application runtime, where curl fetches an installation script that bash runs; the script profiles the host, picks a client matching the architecture, stages it as a hidden, executable file in a writable or memory-backed path such as /dev/shm and opens encrypted outbound command and control through the Global Socket Relay Network (Microsoft, 2026-11-11). The client is then disguised with kernel-thread-like process names (bash exec -a), persisted through cron, systemd units, shell profiles, watchdogs and redundant copies, and the staging files are removed (Microsoft, 2026-11-11). In a few incidents the actors afterwards attempted the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-43284, known as Dirty Frag, to reach root; Microsoft gives no success statement and no affected or fixed versions (Microsoft, 2026-11-11).

Both the compromised host and the operator connect outbound to the public relay, so the host needs no inbound listener, inbound firewall rules do not see the traffic and a shared secret, not an address, pairs the endpoints, which lets the operator reconnect later from any compatible client; Microsoft therefore says that blocking an address or domain is unlikely to cut off access, while egress filtering and outbound monitoring can see it (Microsoft, 2026-11-11). Microsoft's telemetry is concentrated on web applications and hosting; education and research and technology and telecommunications were the largest shares of affected organisations, which Microsoft says reflect exposure more likely than deliberate sector selection (Microsoft, 2026-11-11).

Exposure
Any Linux web, CMS or hosting server whose internet-facing application was exploited, patched or not, in the months before the patch; Microsoft says the same persistence problem applies when initial access came through remote access services or cloud shell sessions.
Detection
Process-creation telemetry with parent lineage, where a web-server or application-runtime process starts curl and then bash, followed by a long-lived process whose name imitates a kernel thread but whose executable sits in a hidden or memory-backed path; file events in /dev/shm and /tmp; new cron entries and systemd units with plausible service names created in the same window as the download; shell startup file changes; and long-lived outbound sessions to a public relay from servers that have no reason to initiate them. After patching, remove the client, its persistence and staged files, and verify that the outbound relay connections stopped, because persistence is layered and stopping the process alone does not remove access (Microsoft, 2026-11-11).

Triage: Microsoft notes that the same relay model also serves legitimate remote administration, and says a match must be judged on process ancestry, execution context, persistence changes and related network activity; a client started from a web-service process tree, from a writable or memory-backed path and under a kernel-thread-like name is the pattern it describes (Microsoft, 2026-11-11).

Defender takeaway
Treat every Linux web server whose application was exploited as possibly holding a relay client, not only web shells, and hunt it on the host after patching; Microsoft's hardening steps are deny-by-default egress with monitoring of relay connections, non-executable mounts for temporary and memory-backed directories, and a review of cron entries, systemd units and shell startup files.

Builds on: 2026-05-09/cve-2026-43284-cve-2026-43500-linux-dirty-frag-deterministic

threat12 Nov 04:06Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
NOTABLENATOB2

Falcon: Unit 42 describes a browser-resident command-and-control framework planted in government webmail and web applications, with a script tag in Roundcube at a Middle Eastern foreign ministry and a sideloaded 'PDF Viewer' extension elsewhere; it shares its core with PeckBirdy

Unit 42 describes Falcon C2, also called XG and not the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor, a NodeJS command-and-control framework whose operator-controlled JavaScript implant runs inside the victim's browser, so the endpoint holds no file for it (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). A script tag placed in a trusted site makes each visit request the implant from the Falcon server, which returns a script obfuscated per browser session, and the implant then holds a TLS WebSocket to the server while the tab is open and runs operator JavaScript through eval (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). Unit 42 identified compromised government entities in one Middle Eastern and four Southeast Asian countries between March and May 2026, among them ministries and law enforcement agencies, and names no actor (Unit 42, 2026-11-11).

In April 2026 a script tag inserted into the Roundcube webmail portal of a Middle Eastern ministry of foreign affairs let the operator intercept credentials as users signed in and monitor sessions (39 Roundcube instances in that country, none observed elsewhere; how the tag got in is not stated) (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). In May 2026 a module in a Southeast Asian police web application harvested usernames and then showed a fake Adobe Flash Player update prompt to chosen users, which served the Antino implant that uses Microsoft OneDrive for command and control (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). Against a justice-department entity in another country, a Chrome extension named PDF Viewer, sideloaded in developer mode, checked in every 3 to 4 minutes for over three weeks and exfiltrated plaintext credentials for an internal correspondence system and a screenshot of a document the victim was viewing (Unit 42, 2026-11-11). The Jewelbug campaign also used an extension named PDF Viewer (Symantec, 2026-08-13); Unit 42 lists it only as a further resource.

Unit 42 assesses with high confidence that Falcon and PeckBirdy (Trend's JScript framework used by China-aligned actors since 2023) are variants of one core framework; that is code lineage, not who operates Falcon (Unit 42, 2026-11-11; Trend Micro, 2026-01-26).

Exposure
Internal webmail, ticketing and case-management portals whose templates or headers an attacker can edit (Roundcube is the named case), and managed Chrome browsers that allow extensions to be sideloaded in developer mode; Unit 42 does not say how the script tags or the extensions reached their targets.
Detection
Unit 42's four monitoring items, telemetry class first: template and header integrity on webmail, ticketing and case-management portals for a script tag loading a resource from an unfamiliar domain, especially one returning a heavily numeric JavaScript array with a small decoder loop; extension inventory for developer-mode extensions imitating utilities such as PDF viewers with broad permissions; Baidu Analytics-style cookie or local-storage keys on internal government web applications; and OneDrive traffic to tenants outside the organisation's own with repeated small JSON writes (Unit 42, 2026-11-11).

Triage: Unit 42's basis for the cookie check is that Baidu Analytics cookies are normal on sites that use that service and anomalous on internal government web applications where it has no reason to appear (Unit 42, 2026-11-11).

Defender takeaway
Compare the templates and headers of internal webmail and case-management portals with a known-good copy and list every external script source they load, and inventory the Chrome extensions installed in developer mode on managed browsers; a browser-resident implant leaves nothing on the endpoint for file-based tools to find.

Plone security fix of 2026-11-10: a chain of missing security declarations and opened modules lets an anonymous visitor run code on the server in every supported Plone version and back to 4.3; a working proof of concept exists, no CVE ids yet, no exploitation reported

The Plone and Zope security team says the fixes it released on 2026-11-10 close a chain of several issues that together let an anonymous visitor run code on the server, in all supported Plone versions (6.0, 6.1 and 6.2) and in older ones back to at least 4.3 (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10). The anonymous entry point is Products.CMFEditions: the conditional modifiers in portal_modifier had no security declarations, so an anonymous visitor could change a modifier's TALES condition and then run it, and the condition is also evaluated when an editor saves versioned content (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10). Products.CMFPlone, Products.MimetypesRegistry and plone.batching opened whole modules to restricted code, which let TALES expressions and Python scripts escape the sandbox and reach modules such as os, and plone.restapi opened the json module (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10). The CMFEditions advisory rates its flaw 9.8 with no privileges required and states that a working proof of concept exists; the team says details are public and that with current AI tools it may not take long to turn them into a working exploit, and no source reports exploitation (Plone, 2026-11-10; Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10).

The fixed packages are CMFPlone 6.2.3, 6.1.6 and 6.0.16 with the helper package versions the announcement lists, or the hotfix Products.PloneHotfix20261110, which covers Plone 4.3 to 6.2, and all Zope instances must be restarted afterwards (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10). The team's pre-announcement of 2026-11-02 already gave the workaround, to block any URL containing portal_modifier at the web server at any path depth, which only helps if Zope's own port cannot be reached directly; the team advises keeping it after updating (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-02). After the fix, restricted code can import only the names Plone itself needs from the closed modules, so custom scripts that import others now get an Unauthorized error (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10).

Exposure
Any Plone site reachable by anonymous visitors, on a version below the fixed packages; no source states a non-default setting that the anonymous path needs, and Plone 5.2 and older are out of security support, with the fix released as an exception.
Detection
Web-server access logs for anonymous requests whose path contains portal_modifier; and the stored state, which survives the update: a changed modifier condition stays in the database, so as Manager open @@check-modifier-conditions on the site root, or read the hotfix's startup log line that reports modified versioning conditions, and treat the server as compromised if a condition is not recognised, although defaults have changed over time so a difference alone is not an attack (Plone Security Team, 2026-11-10).
Defender takeaway
Update or install the hotfix and restart now on every internet-facing Plone site, keep the portal_modifier block in place, and run the modifier-condition check afterwards, because the fix does not remove a condition an anonymous request already stored.

CVE-2026-119618, Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70: a race in mod_http2 assign_headers() corrupts heap memory and leads to remote code execution on servers with HTTP/2 enabled; fixed in 2.4.71, Red Hat calls it unauthenticated and claims public exploit research, no exploitation reported

Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71, released on 2026-11-11, fixes CVE-2026-119618, a race in mod_http2's assign_headers() that the project rates critical and says can lead to remote code execution, in versions 2.4.55 through 2.4.70 (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11). The project publishes no CVSS score; Red Hat scores it CVSS 3.1 9.8 and says it allows unauthenticated remote code execution, with a worker thread writing into memory owned by the connection thread through a shared lock-free allocator (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11). Red Hat states that only servers with HTTP/2 (h2 or h2c) enabled through the Protocols directive are affected and that HTTP/1.1-only servers are not (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11); the project's own page is silent on that prerequisite (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11).

On exploitation the sources differ. Wiz wrote at its publication that no exploit was available and no exploitation in the wild was reported (Wiz, 2026-11-11), while Red Hat says public research has demonstrated a reliable exploit against a default-configured server with mod_http2 enabled, without linking it (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11). A researcher has since posted a test setup that reports memory corruption and Apache child-process crashes on 2.4.70, and Wordfence says it does not demonstrate remote command execution (Wordfence, 2026-11-12). No source reports attacks, and the project's advisory carries no exploitation or workaround statement (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11). Wiz advises disabling HTTP/2 temporarily as the interim measure (Wiz, 2026-11-11).

The upstream fix is 2.4.71. The project lists standalone mod_h2 releases from GitHub, 2.0.8 through 2.0.42, as affected and names no fixed standalone release (Apache HTTP Server project, 2026-11-11). Red Hat shipped mod_http2 errata for RHEL 9 (mod_http2-2.0.26-7.el9_9.1) and RHEL 10 (mod_http2-2.0.29-5.el10_3.1) on 2026-11-11, rates them Important (Red Hat, 2026-11-11; Red Hat, 2026-11-11), says the packages allocate each HTTP/2 stream from a separate allocator, which makes exploitation substantially more complex, and lists RHEL 8 and earlier as not affected (Red Hat Product Security, 2026-11-11); Debian's tracker lists apache2 2.4.71-1~deb12u1 for bookworm (DLA-4902-1) and 2.4.71-1~deb13u1 for trixie (DSA-6620-1) as fixed while forky is still vulnerable (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-11-13), Ubuntu's USN-9090-1 fixes 22.04 LTS to 26.10, and 20.04 LTS through ESM (Ubuntu, 2026-11-12), Alpine 3.21 to 3.24 ship 2.4.71-r0 (Alpine Linux, 2026-11-13) and SUSE lists the issue as pending (SUSE, 2026-11-13).

Exposure
An Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 to 2.4.70, or a distribution mod_http2 build without the vendor's fix, that has the mod_http2 module loaded and h2 or h2c in a Protocols directive for the server or a virtual host; the loaded modules and the Protocols directives of the configuration show it, and the distribution advisory, not the upstream version string, shows whether a backported fix is installed.
Detection
Neither the project nor Red Hat publishes indicators of compromise; the researcher's test shows the corruption as httpd child-process crashes inside the allocator and HTTP/2 stream code (researcher repository, 2026-11-12), so watch for child crashes in the error log; shells or interpreters started by an httpd worker are an inference from the flaw class, not a source statement.
Defender takeaway
Update internet-facing servers that serve HTTP/2 to 2.4.71 or the distribution's fixed package and restart, and where no fix is available yet remove h2 and h2c from Protocols until it is, because Red Hat describes an unauthenticated path and a public exploit while the project describes neither.

eMudhra: the private keys of eight ECDSA intermediate CA certificates were trivially recoverable, so anyone could forge trusted HTTPS certificates, and eight RSA intermediates were revoked on 2026-11-07 for key handling eMudhra cannot show compliant; browsers block them, clients with their own trust store or no revocation checking need an update (CVE-2026-111943 in Go)

First published 2026-10-21 · open finding →

Update12 Nov 2026 04:26 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

eMudhra's full incident report of 2026-11-10 says eight RSA-4096 issuers (G2B and G2C) were revoked on 2026-11-07 with the reason cessationOfOperation because their keys were handled in the memory of a Python script, so eMudhra cannot show compliance with its policy; it had said on 2026-10-19 that they were not impacted, no source says the keys leaked, and the G2C issuers had issued end-entity certificates.

eMudhra posted its full incident report in the Mozilla bug on 2026-11-10 (eMudhra, Mozilla bug 2083449, 2026-11-10). For the eight RSA-4096 issuers (G2B and G2C) it says the key integrity is intact, all signatures verifying, but that during re-import the private-key material was handled in the volatile memory of a Python process on the ceremony host, which is not consistent with its certification practice statement, so the RSA issuers are treated as not meeting it; it adds that logs cannot reliably establish or exclude how that material was handled (eMudhra, Mozilla bug 2083449, 2026-11-10). It identified this in early November after a root-program discussion, revoked the eight issuers on 2026-11-07 with the reason cessationOfOperation, not the compromise reason used for the ECDSA set, and had written on 2026-10-19 that the RSA issuers were not impacted (eMudhra, Mozilla bug 2083449, 2026-11-10; eMudhra, Mozilla bug 2083449, 2026-10-19). The G2C issuers were put into production in May 2026 and issued end-entity certificates, the last on 2026-11-03, after which issuance from them stopped; BleepingComputer reports that eMudhra says the affected customer certificates were replaced or migrated, and that the company has not detected malicious use of the keys (eMudhra, Mozilla bug 2083449, 2026-11-10; BleepingComputer, 2026-11-11). eMudhra also decided to exit public TLS, with all issuance from its emSign Root CA - G1 hierarchy to stop before 2026-11-16 and an independent review due 2026-12-04 (eMudhra, Mozilla bug 2083449, 2026-11-10). No page read from Google, Microsoft, Apple, Mozilla or the incident tracker names the G2B or G2C issuers or says a vendor blocked them.

CVE-2026-54121, Windows Server AD CS 'Certighost': a low-privileged domain user forges a DC certificate to DCSync, public PoC since 2026-07-24 and attempted in real intrusions by the Citrus ransomware group (CVSS 8.8)

First published 2026-07-25 · open finding →

Update12 Nov 2026 04:17 UTCrun 2026-11-12T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodycves

Kaspersky reported on 2026-11-11 that the Citrus ransomware group attempted Certighost in intrusions that began with stolen contractor VPN and RDP credentials, leaving machine accounts named GHOST plus eight random letters; it does not say an attempt succeeded and Microsoft's record still lists no confirmed exploitation.

Kaspersky's Citrus report of 2026-11-11 says the group attempted to exploit Certighost with an exploit published on GitHub, requesting a Machine-template certificate on behalf of a newly created account with the cdc attribute pointing the CA at a system it controlled, and that the group later deploys its Go ransomware domain-wide through a malicious Group Policy Object (Kaspersky, 2026-11-11). Kaspersky says that if exploitation succeeds the CA issues the certificate and the domain controller name in it lets the attackers authenticate as the domain controller account, and it never says an attempt succeeded (Kaspersky, 2026-11-11); Microsoft's record has not been revised since 2026-07-14 (Microsoft MSRC, 2026-07-14).

Verification & coverage notes

Window: standard 26 h (gap to the previous fire 24.0 h). KEV sweep: no catalogue additions in the window and no ransomware-flag flips on covered entries. Held backlog row left untouched: zohe-hainaut-est (no source found, expiry 2026-11-17).

  • borderline-drop: Node.js 2026-11-11 security releases (seven high CVEs), scheduled release, no exploitation or PoC, regular patch cycle (PD-11 b)
