Update05 Nov 2026 04:02 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysectorssourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

The French blood service EFS confirmed that an incident at its refrigeration supplier on 2 November altered the temperature and defrost thresholds of cold rooms at three of its sites, caught by its own alarms with no loss of blood products, so the case no longer rests on Le Canard enchaîné alone; ENISA, the European Commission, Europol and the CSIRTs Network advised organisations on 2026-11-04 to take immediate action, CSIRT Italia issued cold-chain measures, and no source ties the blood-service case to the Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell controllers.

The French blood service EFS confirmed on 2026-11-03 that on 2 November a refrigeration-equipment supplier suffered a cybersecurity incident that affected the supervision and control installations of cold rooms at three EFS sites, with temperature and defrost thresholds raised to very high values (translated from French) (EFS, 2026-11-03). EFS says its own monitoring and alarm systems identified the anomalies quickly, the affected equipment was brought under control without impact on the products or neutralised, the products stored in those cold rooms were transferred preventively to other installations, and no health impact or loss of blood products is to be reported; it names no supplier and gives no temperature figure (translated from French) (EFS, 2026-11-03).

BleepingComputer, heise and SRF identify the supplier as Coolworld, and SRF reports that the attackers reportedly entered through its remote maintenance (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04; heise, 2026-11-04; SRF, 2026-11-04). Coolworld's statement of 2026-11-04 says the incident involved remote monitoring software, that the vulnerability reported in the media relates to a component from a third-party supplier outside its control and that a limited number of its units were affected; it does not say that attackers exploited that component (Coolworld, 2026-11-04). BleepingComputer's account reads it the other way, saying Coolworld says the attackers exploited a vulnerability in a third-party component, which the statement does not state (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04). No source names Danfoss, Copeland or Dixell equipment for this case.

ENISA, the European Commission (DG CNECT), Europol's EC3, the EU CSIRTs Network and EU-CyCLONe issued a joint statement on 2026-11-04: since 11 October 2026 several commercial refrigeration systems and similar devices have been hit in a number of EU Member States, a new wave occurred on 1 to 2 November, affected Member States are investigating and issuing guidance, and organisations are advised to take immediate action to mitigate exposure in the affected systems; it names no product, actor or count and does not mention Switzerland (ENISA, 2026-11-04). CSIRT Italia's bulletin of 2026-11-04 extends its call to every operator of cold-chain technology, whatever the sector, to apply its earlier measures urgently, removing direct internet exposure of administrative and control interfaces and verifying that operating parameters and alarms are intact first (CSIRT Italia, 2026-11-04). Its bulletin of 2026-10-13, re-issued on 2026-11-04 as version 1.2, asks operators to limit supplier access to authorised resources and periods, to require multi-factor authentication on remote access, applied on the mediating system when the device cannot do it, and to check actual temperatures and alarms with instruments independent of the supervision platform (CSIRT Italia, 2026-11-04). The BSI had urged operators of networked freezer controllers to disconnect them from the internet or at least secure and patch them (heise, 2026-11-04).

CVE-2026-7273 and CVE-2026-107441, Zyxel GS1900 switches: GreyNoise caught a Red Heron-linked actor exfiltrating configurations and hashed root credentials from 996 switches in 48 countries, and Binarly shows its exploit targets a separate flaw that the June fix leaves open; only the .3C0 builds close it

First published 2026-09-22 · open finding →

Update05 Nov 2026 03:59 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyclassification

Binarly shows the exploit GreyNoise described works against all ten June-fixed GS1900 builds because it targets a separate flaw, CVE-2026-107441, which Zyxel fixed in the .3C0 builds on 2026-10-22 and disclosed on 2026-11-03; the .3C0 builds replace the .2C0 builds as the remedy, and exploitation of the new CVE rests on Binarly's exploit match, which neither Zyxel nor CISA confirms.

Binarly reports that the Python exploit GreyNoise described, which it found in an exposed archive on infrastructure that BleepingComputer ties to Red Heron (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04), targets a flaw in the request-parameter parser of the switches' CGI (dispatcher.cgi), not the stack overflow of CVE-2026-7273, and that it works without change against the "…(x).2C0" builds Zyxel advertised as the June fix; Binarly confirmed this against all ten builds on 2026-09-28 (Binarly, 2026-11-03). Zyxel treats the report as a separate vulnerability, CVE-2026-107441, fixed on 2026-10-22 in the "…(x).3C0" builds of GS1900-8, -8HP, -10HP, -16, -24, -24E, -24EP, -24HPv2, -48 and -48HPv2 and disclosed in an advisory of 2026-11-03 that credits Binarly and shows no score or exploitation statement (Zyxel PSIRT, 2026-11-03; Binarly, 2026-11-03). Binarly labels the flaw an in-the-wild zero-day on the strength of the exploit match, scores it 9.8 with a network vector against Zyxel's LAN-based wording, and says it will publish a minimised proof of concept; CISA's catalog of 2026-11-04 lists only CVE-2026-7273 (Binarly, 2026-11-03; Binarly, 2026-11-03; BleepingComputer, 2026-11-04; CISA KEV, 2026-11-04). Switches on the June build are therefore still exposed to the exploit until the "…(x).3C0" build is installed.

Sources: Zyxel PSIRT · GreyNoise · CISA · Acronis Threat Research Unit · Zyxel PSIRT (advisory, CVE-2026-107441) · Binarly (blog) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.11.04) · Binarly (advisory BRLY-2026-057) · BleepingComputer

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

First published 2026-10-24 · open finding →

Update05 Nov 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Splunk's advisory lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and lower, its Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA and Attack Analyzer as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them, with Splunk Enterprise 10.2 or higher as the upgrade target and the Visual Exporter app to be disabled, and Citrix names Unicon eLux Scout with hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR and 2605.1-3 as the fixes.

Splunk's advisory SVD-2026-1015, published on 2026-10-28 and updated through 2026-11-06, lists Splunk Enterprise, the Splunk Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA, Attack Analyzer, Python for Scientific Computing, several AppDynamics components and Smartlook as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them; the page gives no CVSS score, no attacker position and no exploitation statement, and it covers the Brotli flaw and three DNS and TLS hostname-validation flaws together, so it does not show which of them reaches a given product (Splunk, 2026-10-28). Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable while 9.4 and 10.2 or later are not (as revised on 2026-11-06), Splunk recommends upgrading to 10.2 or higher for the bundled Node.js runtime and plans to upgrade the packages in a future 10.0 release, and the upgrade does not remediate the Visual Exporter app, which every Splunk Enterprise version includes and which Splunk says to disable or remove (Splunk, 2026-10-28). The page gives no fix for the other listed products.

Citrix bulletin CTX697300, published on 2026-10-30 and revised on 2026-11-03 with remediation for the LTSR and Cloud Gateway products, lists Unicon eLux Scout as affected by CVE-2026-111497 alone and names the fixes as hotfix 2609.1 for Scout On-Prem, 2508 CU2 LTSR for Scout On-Prem LTSR and 2605.1-3 for Scout Cloud Gateway On-Prem, without a vulnerable version range or an exploitation statement (Citrix, 2026-10-30). Neither Splunk nor Citrix says anything on malicious use against its products.

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Xerox AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre printers and Fiery print controllers: AltaLink 82xx and 81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink remediated with PHP 8.2.35, exposure-reducing patches for WorkCentre and the AltaLink C80xx and B80xx models, Fiery patches due 2026-11-09 to 2026-11-23

First published 2026-11-02 · open finding →

Update05 Nov 2026 03:51 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-intelsummarycvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Xerox's bulletin of 2026-11-03 adds two interim measures for AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre devices, restricting the web interface to trusted networks or management hosts or disabling HTTP/HTTPS, and says the vulnerable PHP component serves a limited number of pages of the embedded web server; fix dates are unchanged.

Xerox revised bulletin XRX26-016 on 2026-11-03 and added a mitigation section for AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre devices, which the version of 2026-10-28 did not carry (Xerox, 2026-11-03; Xerox, 2026-10-28). It says the vulnerable PHP component is used by a limited number of pages in the device's embedded web server, and that until the fix is installed customers can restrict the web interface (HTTP/HTTPS) to trusted networks or management hosts, for example with a firewall or segmentation, or disable HTTP/HTTPS if remote web administration is not required, which also disables the embedded web server and the features that depend on it (Xerox, 2026-11-03). The section does not cover the Fiery Digital Front End or the Worldwide Ticketing Tool, and the affected table and the fix dates are unchanged.

Sources: Xerox (Security Bulletin XRX26-016, version of 2026-10-28) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.30) · Xerox (Security Bulletin XRX26-016, version of 2026-11-03) · Xerox (Security Bulletin XRX26-016, version of 2026-11-06)

05Action items12 items

  • In every Microsoft 365 tenant your organisation runs or administers, audit device code sign-ins with the authentication protocol filter of the sign-in logs and, where no documented device needs the flow, create a Conditional Access policy with the Authentication flows condition set to Device code flow and Block access, starting in report-only mode and excluding emergency-access accounts and, where devices register through it, the Device Registration Service.
    FindingVaud: device-code phishing against Microsoft 365 is…→
  • Move every managed iPhone and iPad to the newest iOS available for its model and every managed Android phone to Chrome 146 or later and the OEM patch level that fixes CVE-2025-27038, and list the devices that cannot go past iOS 16.7.x (iPhone 8, 8 Plus, X, iPad 5th generation, iPad Pro 9.7-inch and 12.9-inch 1st generation per Apple), because Sekoia's chains do not work against fully updated devices and CISA lists all eight flaws they deliver as exploited.
    FindingCVE-2024-27834 +7→
  • Upgrade every SEPPmail Secure Email Gateway to 15.1.1 now, moving 15.0.x gateways to the 15.1 branch because 15.0.7 is the last 15.0 release, and check each gateway's active address-replacement rules for values taken from the message and its Large File Transfer setting, the two conditions the CNA names.
    FindingCVE-2026-114424 +4→
  • Update every Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x runtime to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, including the Node binary inside container images (a Dockerfile that pins 24.22.0 keeps the flaw until the pin changes), and upgrade the PyPI Brotli package to 1.2.1 and brotlicffi to 1.2.1.0 wherever either is installed; judge a Node.js build by its release version, because process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched builds too, and move any application on an end-of-life Node.js line to a supported release. On every WordPress host, upgrade the operating system's libbrotli package to a patched revision (check the package revision, because Debian and Ubuntu backport the fix into 1.1.0) and rebuild WordPress container images, since the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable libbrotli1 when Patchstack wrote.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable. On every VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager apply Broadcom's workaround, KB460732 on 9.1.1 and KB460734 on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, until its patch ships. Upgrade every Splunk Enterprise 10.0 instance to 10.2 or higher and disable or remove the Splunk Visual Exporter app on every Splunk Enterprise instance, because the upgrade does not remediate it, and install Citrix hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR or 2605.1-3 on Unicon eLux Scout.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 lists every PAN-OS hotfix for this flaw as released.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Install each Zyxel GS1900 switch's "…(x).3C0" build now (2.90(AAHL.3)C0 on the GS1900-24, for example), including switches already moved to the June "…(x).2C0" build, which Binarly shows still carries the flaw the recovered exploit targets, and audit and rotate any switch still on its factory-default admin credentials: GreyNoise found 564 of 996 exploited switches (57%) on factory-default credentials.
    FindingCVE-2026-7273 +1→
  • List the computers in Active Directory that carry the service principal name the iSCSI Target Server registers and every host that listens on TCP 3260, then enable CHAP on each target and restrict TCP 3260 to the addresses of the cluster nodes, starting with targets whose volumes hold Hyper-V disks of domain controllers.
    FindingSpecterOps: iSCSI Target Server without CHAP lets a…→
  • Install release 123.xxx.006.29800 on every Xerox AltaLink 82xx, 81xx and EC81xx and release 123.xxx.006.30100 on every VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620; apply Xerox's exposure-reducing system software patch to WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 (XRX26-017) and to AltaLink C80xx and B80xx, EC8036 and EC8056 (XRX26-018), and keep the web interface of those models reachable only from trusted networks or management hosts until Xerox ships a fix.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fix and reboot as soon as it ships, then confirm the running version; Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu's generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Citrix and Sophos (Firewall hotfix HF110626.1, SD-RED firmware 3.0.012) updates are out, and XCP-ng says that a host which cannot reboot at once should take its iptables-based mitigation first and the update later; on Veeam appliances run Veeam Updater for kernel 5.14.0-570.60.1+27.2.el9_6_ciq, redeploy the virtual labs and Azure helper appliances that stay deployed and replace recovery media made before the update.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→
  • On hosts that cannot reboot yet, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options ahead of the TCP stack as CIQ, AWS and Vates describe, after testing on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not close the path.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→

Verification & coverage notes

  • Coverage window: standard, 26 h (previous intel run 2026-11-04T0256Z-intel, gap 24.0 h); no outage backfill. Source rotation ranked on the cursor; the previous two fires' attempts excluded 27 (S1), 31 (S2) and 37 (S3) standard records, and the exclusion was waived for S4 because all 14 breach-domain sources had been attempted by those fires.

  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA row stays held (S4 re-checked the ransomware.live record, a breach tracker, the ARX site, German and Italian searches and the Inside IT, Netzwoche and SRF feeds: no confirmation; expiry 2026-11-07 unchanged). The ChimeraZ row stays held (no commune, canton, zone or Swiss press confirmation; FrenchBreaches still calls the hack unconfirmed; expiry 2026-11-17 unchanged). Neither row changed state, so nothing is appended to them. The Amadeus hold of 2026-11-04 stays dropped (six Asian carriers, no European confirmation).

No RANSOMWARE row for a covered CVE appeared in the window. S1's diff against the 2026-07-29 snapshot found 26 older flips; the one that touches covered ground, CVE-2025-8088 (WinRAR, ClamAV's bundled UnRAR), is a borderline-drop below.
  • borderline-drop: S2-2 Federal Supreme Court blocking ruling: no obligation change for defenders

  • borderline-drop: CVE-2025-8088 ransomware flag, the KEV record reads Known in catalog 2026.08.07 and Unknown in 2026.07.29 (FU4 bracketed the flip from committed snapshots), so it is not a development of this window; CISA names no group, and no source names a ransomware actor using the flaw. Four store entries cite the CVE and none mentions ransomware; the 2026-10-29 MDaemon and ClamAV entry is the natural home if the audit judges it worth a line. FU4 also found two older defects for the audit: the 2026-06-02 Sekoia/Gamaredon entry dates the WinRAR 7.13 fix to "August 2025" while ESET says 2025-07-30, and the 2026-06-27 Turla STOCKSTAY entry says "Patch WinRAR to 7.11+" while ESET names 7.13 as the fix.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-04
item.description:
• Barracuda ESG: CISA lists both flaws as exploited, Barracuda reports attacks; update to 9.4.0.029 or later. Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway (CVSS 9.3) that lets an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive through the configuration-import function, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection in the timezone field (8.6) that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway; chained, they give root. watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the chain needs no account, one unauthenticated request to the login handler reaching the restore function, and Barracuda changed its advisory the same day to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative interface must be reachable; watchTowr published a detection tool. Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, without naming the flaw, the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 and marks both for forensic triage. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected. →
  • Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school estate's AD domains with new trusts after stealing Veeam credentials. Bitdefender MDR describes a September 2026 intrusion by a 3AM ransomware affiliate into a UK school estate that began as several unconnected Active Directory domains: a modified public Veeam script decrypted credentials stored on three backup servers, the attacker created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three domains with new two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents (anti-tampering blocked it) and encrypted machines. Initial access is unknown, every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host, and Bitdefender reads the 40 to 101 second retry cadence as a model-driven loop, flagged as its own interpretation; it says a new trust between domains is a rare change that is cheap to alert on. →
  • Binance's report: fake recruiter, trojaned pyenv, AI-tool pivot and a deployment token reached the signing service.   1. 01Barracuda ESG: CISA lists both flaws as exploited, Barracuda reports attacks; update to 9.4.0.029 or later. Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, without naming the flaw, the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 and marks both for forensic triage. Barracuda names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the fixed build while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected. →
  2. 02Bitdefender: a 3AM affiliate joined a school estate's AD domains with new trusts after stealing Veeam credentials. Bitdefender MDR describes a September 2026 intrusion by a 3AM ransomware affiliate into a UK school estate that began as several unconnected Active Directory domains: a modified public Veeam script decrypted credentials stored on three backup servers, the attacker created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three domains with new two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents (anti-tampering blocked it) and encrypted machines. Initial access is unknown, every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host, and Bitdefender reads the 40 to 101 second retry cadence as a model-driven loop, flagged as its own interpretation; it says a new trust between domains is a rare change that is cheap to alert on. →
  3. 03Binance's report: fake recruiter, trojaned pyenv, AI-tool pivot and a deployment token reached the signing service. Binance's report of 2026-11-03 says the theft of about USD 6.34 billion on 2026-10-29 was a multi-stage campaign: in September a software engineer contacted through a job platform was led through two fake interviews and told to download an assignment repository to his work computer, whose setup code replaced the pyenv executable in the Homebrew install with a malicious one that endpoint protection did not detect. On 2026-10-20 the attacker used that computer and an internal AI tool to take over two wallet-team engineers and found a container-deployment token, which on 2026-10-29 let it deploy a container and run a script that reached the wallet signing service. The FBI says North Korea was responsible and calls the activity TraderTraitor; Binance says some technical details stay confidential. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 3Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 6Action items 9

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures3 items

NOTABLENATOB2

3AM ransomware affiliate in a UK school estate: Bitdefender documents backup-credential theft, rogue domain admins and new two-way trusts between Active Directory domains, with a command-retry pattern it reads as a model-driven loop

Bitdefender MDR attributes the intrusion to a 3AM (ThreeAM) ransomware affiliate on the encryptor build and its command-line pattern; the target was a school estate in the UK whose domains began as separate Active Directory environments, and initial access is unknown (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 the attacker first took credentials from the backup software: a modified copy of a public script read the credentials stored in Veeam's databases on three backup servers and decrypted them with the Windows Data Protection API, and a browser credential database was copied from a terminal server (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03). It then worked with built-in tools (PowerShell, WMI, reg, netsh, rundll32) and a few public ones (an Impacket-like remote-execution tool that returns output over administrative shares, Mimikatz renamed to look like a monitoring binary), enumerated domain trusts from a domain controller, searched SYSVOL logon scripts for the names and subnets of other schools, created two backdoor domain-administrator accounts, joined three separate domains with two-way trusts within about three hours, tried to remove EDR agents, which anti-tampering controls blocked, deleted system-state backups and encrypted machines with a Rust-based encryptor (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Bitdefender's reading, which it calls interpretation and not a finding, is that a model drove part of the work: commands call the Veeam web interface on a port and with a login method that do not match the vendor documentation, output is self-labelled, scripts carry numbered revisions, and retries arrive 40 to 101 seconds apart whatever the size of the change, while a new task takes minutes. Every attacker action Bitdefender saw came from an unmanaged internal host with no agent, so the automation itself was never seen, and Bitdefender says it could not document anything about a language model (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
A Windows estate that runs Veeam Backup & Replication and has several Active Directory domains or a flat network that an unmanaged internal host can reach; the unmanaged host is the gap, because it ran no agent and sat outside Bitdefender's visibility.
Detection
In directory-service change events, new trust relationships between domains, which Bitdefender calls a rare change that is cheap to alert on, and new domain-administrator group members; in backup-server logs, Veeam web-interface calls and credential-store reads from hosts that are not backup administrators'; in endpoint telemetry, saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM registry hives by any process that is not a known backup or administration job, LSASS access, a Windows Defender exclusion for the temporary directory, and the same command re-issued with small edits at a steady cadence; across hosts, file contents staged into registry values, which Bitdefender calls an unusual channel and a strong indicator to hunt for, and sent out by HTTP POST to an internal host, and probe or confirmation artifacts such as a scheduled task named for the probe left on production hosts; in authentication logs, unmanaged hosts authenticating to domain controllers (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).
Defender takeaway
Alert on any new domain trust and on additions to the domain-administrator groups, alert on credential-reading access to backup-software databases and on saves of the SECURITY, SYSTEM or SAM hives outside known backup or administration jobs, put an endpoint agent on every machine because the staging host here was unmanaged, and limit remote execution and administrative shares to known management hosts (Bitdefender, 2026-11-03).
incident04 Nov 03:55Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Bitdefender Business Insights
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Binance's own report on the 2026-10-29 theft of about USD 6.34 billion: a fake recruiter's coding assignment compromised an engineer's laptop, an internal AI tool carried the attacker to two colleagues and a container-deployment token, and a deployed container reached the wallet signing service; the FBI attributes it to North Korea's TraderTraitor

Binance says the theft of about USD 6.34 billion in digital assets on 2026-10-29 was "a sophisticated, multi-stage campaign" and not a single breach or a simple phishing incident (Binance, 2026-11-03). In September 2026 a software engineer whose job-platform profile named Binance was approached by a person posing as a project director, interviewed by a purported HR representative on live video and then by a purported CEO in a chat application, and told to download an "assignment" repository onto his work computer; its setup code replaced the legitimate pyenv executable in the Homebrew installation with a malicious version, repointed the symlink and spawned a zsh shell, and the 0-day malware was not detected by endpoint protection (Binance, 2026-11-03). On 2026-10-20 the attacker used that computer and an internal AI tool to gain control over a wallet DevOps engineer and a second wallet software engineer, and found a container-deployment permission token on the first engineer's computer; on 2026-10-29 it logged onto the second engineer's computer with the stolen credentials, deployed a container and triggered a script that launched the attack on the wallet signing service (Binance, 2026-11-03). Binance reports an earlier supply-chain event in June 2026, when a wallet DevOps engineer installed a tampered Homebrew installation while searching for an AI coding tool, and says its security team blocked 57 suspected North Korea-linked cases in 2026 (Binance, 2026-11-03). The FBI says North Korea was responsible and calls the activity "TraderTraitor" (FBI, 2026-10-31). BleepingComputer notes that fake job interviews leading to malware installs are a common tactic of the North Korean campaigns known as Contagious Interview and Operation Dream Job, a comparison Binance does not make (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-03).

The transfer to other organisations is the access chain, not the loss: a developer endpoint reached through a recruiting lure, a trojaned version-manager binary that endpoint protection missed, an internal AI tool through which the attacker gained control over two colleagues, by a method Binance keeps confidential, and a deployment token that turned one workstation into code execution in a trusted pipeline.

Exposure
Any organisation whose developers, DevOps or administrators can be approached through job platforms and run third-party assignment code on managed laptops, and any internal AI assistant or agent reachable from a compromised employee endpoint.
Detection
In endpoint file-event telemetry, a version-manager or interpreter binary deleted, renamed and re-linked inside a package-manager directory followed by a shell spawned from it, which is the sequence Binance describes for pyenv in the Homebrew installation (Binance, 2026-11-03); in process lineage, shells started from a repository's setup scripts; in token-use logs, a container-deployment token used from a host that is not its owner's; in the access logs of internal AI tools, activity that touches other employees' accounts or endpoints from one user's session, a pattern the takeover of two colleagues through such a tool implies (an inference; Binance does not describe the mechanism).
Defender takeaway
Treat a recruiter's "assignment" repository as untrusted code and keep it off managed machines, restrict what an internal AI tool can reach with one user's session and what a stored deployment token can deploy, and alert on shells spawned from replaced developer-tool binaries; Binance's own stated fixes are tighter device controls, rebuilt systems and tools, rotated credentials and tokens, and AI-based behavioural anomaly detection (Binance, 2026-11-03).
Correction08 Nov 2026 14:05 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditbody

Binance's report says the attacker "used an internal AI tool to gain control over" two further engineers and that some technical details will remain confidential (Binance, 2026-11-03); it does not say how the tool was abused, so the earlier description of it letting one user act on colleagues' machines went beyond the source. The access-log pattern for internal AI tools is an inference from that takeover, not a mechanism Binance describes.

Builds on: 2026-09-21/tradertraitor-terraform-lockfile-nostr-dead-drop

incident04 Nov 03:50Zsingle-source · victim disclosureOpen finding →
Sources: Binance (Initial Findings and Response Update) · FBI · BleepingComputer
NOTABLENATOB2

OPSSHIELD cPGuard: an attacker who registered as a customer reached the vendor's billing and licensing server and shipped a fake update on 2026-11-02 that ran as root on about 2,950 Linux servers, copying root secrets and leaving a root shell and a scheduled task

OPSSHIELD says the attacker registered a customer account under a false identity on the vendor's billing portal, studied how the cPGuard agent talks to the licensing system with a trial install, sent crafted requests to the portal's callback pages, gained the ability to run commands on the billing and licensing server, took the keys used to publish updates and shipped a fake update for about 70 minutes on 2026-11-02; the vendor's logs do not record the exact request that gave access (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). cPGuard agents installed the fake update between 02:08 and 03:20 UTC, and it ran as root (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The script copied the local password hashes, root's SSH private keys and authorization files, the MySQL root password and root's shell history back to the attacker, and root's cloud storage keys on a small number of servers; it also left a hidden root shell and a scheduled task (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The vendor puts the affected servers at about 2,950 and the exposed billing-portal accounts, with name, company, postal address, e-mail and hashed password, at about 7,900 (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). A clean update, 5.88.26, removes the hidden root shell and a follow-up update removes the scheduled task (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), but credentials copied before cleanup may still be usable (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). The shared exposure is every operator of a cPGuard server: BleepingComputer says hosting firms and server administrators commonly run it alongside panels such as cPanel, DirectAdmin and Plesk (BleepingComputer, 2026-11-03).

Exposure
Any Linux server on which cPGuard was installed and online between 02:08 and 03:20 UTC on 2026-11-02; the vendor's earlier advisory framed the exposure as an install of versions 5.88.12 through 5.88.19 shown by "Successfully updated" entries in the product's install log, which proves installation and not that the script ran (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), and the later disclosure narrows the fake update to 02:08 to 03:20 UTC without repeating a version range or withdrawing that check (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03). Holders of a billing-portal account are exposed separately.
Detection
In the install log, the affected version entries of 2026-11-02; on the host, the hidden root shell and the scheduled task the update left, which the vendor says to confirm are gone after updating; in authentication logs, root logins and use of the copied SSH keys from new sources after 2026-11-02, on this server and on every server that trusted its keys; in egress logs, the update script's collection and outbound copy of root's files.
Defender takeaway
Treat any server that ran the fake update as compromised for credential purposes even after the update: reset root and all local passwords, from a trusted environment as the earlier advisory says (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03), create new root SSH keys and remove the old public keys from every server that trusted them, change the MySQL root password and any database passwords it holds, rotate every secret in root's shell history and any cloud storage keys, and treat servers reached with those keys as exposed; rebuild from a clean backup taken before 1 November any server the vendor says the attacker logged in to by hand, and reset the billing-portal password with two-factor login (OPSSHIELD, 2026-11-03).
incident04 Nov 03:45Zsingle-source · victim disclosureOpen finding →
Sources: OPSSHIELD (security incident disclosure) · OPSSHIELD (cPGuard security advisory) · BleepingComputer

02Trending vulnerabilities1 item

HIGHCVE-2026-116606 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-116606 / CVE-2026-111560, Barracuda Email Security Gateway: an unauthenticated configuration-import bypass chained with a root command injection, with watchTowr's detection tool public since 2026-11-03 and its full chain since 2026-11-05; patches are out, Barracuda reports exploitation against a small number of organizations and CISA lists both flaws as exploited (CVSS 9.3 and 8.6)

Barracuda's advisory of 2026-11-02 covers two flaws that, chained, give root on the appliance: CVE-2026-116606, a pre-authentication authorization bypass in the Email Security Gateway, and CVE-2026-111560, a command injection that also affects the Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Barracuda says successful exploitation requires access to the administrative interface and that, in combination, the flaws let an attacker bypass authorization controls and obtain root (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Mandiant's disclosure describes the first as letting an unauthenticated remote attacker invoke the gateway's configuration-import function and restore a crafted backup archive (Mandiant, 2026-11-02), and the second as shell metacharacters in the timezone configuration field that let an authenticated administrator run commands as root when the crafted value is processed (Mandiant, 2026-11-02). watchTowr Labs showed on 2026-11-05 that the two chain without any account on the gateway: one unauthenticated request reaches the restore function and the restored timezone value reaches the root command injection (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). NCSC Switzerland rated exploitation unknown on 2026-11-03 (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-03), and Barracuda changed its advisory on 2026-11-05 to say authentication is not required for CVE-2026-116606, only that the administrative user interface must be accessible to the attacker (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations, without naming the flaw (Barracuda, 2026-11-09), and the Canadian Cyber Centre says open-source reporting indicates CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-11-09). CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 (CISA, 2026-11-10) and marks both for forensic triage (CISA, 2026-11-10).

Barracuda released patches for each product and asks customers to apply any patch not applied automatically and confirm automatic patching is on (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). Its Campus article names firmware 9.4.0.029 or later for the Email Security Gateway (Barracuda Campus, 2026-11-02), while the CVE record lists versions earlier than 9.4.0.030 as affected (Mandiant, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
An Email Security Gateway of any version before the fix, or a Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall or Web Security Gateway for the command injection, whose administrative interface can be reached; NCSC Switzerland puts internet-exposed management interfaces at the highest risk (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-03), and Barracuda says organisations whose administrative interfaces are not publicly accessible from the internet are less exposed to this attack path (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). The installed firmware version is shown under Advanced > Firmware Update (Barracuda Campus, 2026-11-02).
Detection
Barracuda's advisory names no indicators. watchTowr's chain implies, in the interface's web access logs, a POST to /cgi-mod/index.cgi that submits a password change with two different passwords together with a backup file from a session that never logged in, followed by a restored configuration whose timezone value holds shell metacharacters (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05); the mechanism also implies root-owned child processes under the appliance's management service after a restore nobody made. After patching, repeat these checks on any appliance whose interface was reachable before the fix.
Defender takeaway
Take every affected Barracuda appliance's administrative interface off the internet and untrusted networks, update every Email Security Gateway to 9.4.0.029 or later (Barracuda Campus, 2026-11-02), apply the patch listed for each of the other products and confirm that automatic patching is on; Barracuda recommends restricting administrative interfaces to trusted internal networks (Barracuda, 2026-11-05).
Update06 Nov 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-11-06T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryprioritytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

watchTowr Labs published the full chain on 2026-11-05 after comparing firmware 9.4.0.027 with 9.4.0.029 (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). In the login handler a failed password-change attempt returns the login-screen role instead of ending the request, so one unauthenticated POST to /cgi-mod/index.cgi that submits mismatching new and retyped passwords with a backup upload reaches the backup-restore function (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). The restore accepts a backup whose checksum matches, and the checksum is built from the file bytes and a secret that is hard-coded in the product, so an attacker can build a valid archive (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). A restored system_timezone value then reaches an unescaped shell call that runs as root (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). watchTowr shares a Detection Artefact Generator so that owners can test their own appliances, and its post does not claim exploitation in the wild (watchTowr Labs, 2026-11-05). Its README describes a tool that takes a target URL and a command, builds a backup, uploads it to the target and attempts to check whether the target is vulnerable (watchTowr Labs README, 2026-11-03).

Barracuda changed its advisory the same day, 2026-11-05 at 2:30pm EST: the Authentication Required field for CVE-2026-116606 now reads No (Administrative UI Access Required), and the advisory says authentication is not required to exploit it but the administrative user interface must be accessible to the attacker (Barracuda, 2026-11-05). The advisory's entry for CVE-2026-111560 still reads Yes (Administrative Access) (Barracuda, 2026-11-05).

Update10 Nov 2026 03:35 UTCrun 2026-11-10T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Barracuda added on 2026-11-09 to its advisory that it has identified exploitation activity affecting a small number of organizations; the advisory does not say which flaw, how many organizations, since when or what the attacker did afterwards (Barracuda, 2026-11-09). The Canadian Centre for Cyber Security's update of the same day says open-source reporting indicates that CVE-2026-116606 is exploited in the wild, without naming the reporting (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-11-09). Barracuda's lever is unchanged: organizations whose administrative interfaces are not publicly accessible from the internet are less exposed to this attack path (Barracuda, 2026-11-09), so an appliance whose interface was reachable before patching should also be checked for a restore nobody made and a timezone value that is not a timezone name.

Update11 Nov 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-11-11T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CISA added both CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-10 "based on evidence of active exploitation" (CISA, 2026-11-10). The catalog describes the two as chainable, the first letting an unauthenticated remote attacker restore a crafted backup archive and the second letting an authenticated administrator run commands as root through a crafted timezone value, and marks both for forensic triage (CISA, 2026-11-10). The listing makes CVE-2026-111560 exploited as well; Barracuda's own statement of 2026-11-09 still names no flaw, and no source says how many organizations were hit or what the attacker did afterwards.

03Updates to prior coverage6 items

HIGHupdatedNATOA2

PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating

First published 2026-10-09 · open finding →

Update04 Nov 2026 03:32 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencebodysourcing_note

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich suspended its planned 2027 move to PK Softech's administration system; PK Softech, quoted by watson.ch, cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office has added the case to its criminal proceeding against the Akira group.

The Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich's foundation board suspended the introduction of PK Softech's administration system planned for early 2027 because of the supplier's cyberattack and will keep operating its existing system in 2027; it will decide whether, when and under what conditions to introduce a new system only once the attack and the possible data loss are worked through (translated from German) (Inside IT, 2026-11-03). PK Softech, quoted by watson.ch, says it cannot rule out that non-pseudonymised data was temporarily present in project-related work, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office confirmed to watson.ch that a notorious extortion gang is behind the attack and has added the case to its criminal proceeding against the Akira group, open since April 2024 (translated from German) (watson.ch, 2026-11-03).

Sources: Swiss Federal Administration (admin.ch) · PK Softech AG · watson.ch · Netzwoche · Netzwoche (running story, update of 2026-10-21) · Bernische Pensionskasse (BPK) · Bernische Lehrerversicherungskasse (BLVK) · Pensionskasse Post · Inside IT · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes) · cash.ch (AWP) · Pensionskasse Stadt Zürich (PKZH) · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes), page updated through 2026-10-21 · Cybercrimepolice (cantonal police platform) · SwissCybersecurity.net · NZZ · Blick (SonntagsBlick) · Tages-Anzeiger (Tamedia, paywalled) · Tages-Anzeiger (Tamedia, paywalled; summary lines readable) · 20 Minuten · Ticinonline (relaying Corriere del Ticino) · Istituto di previdenza del Cantone Ticino (IPCT, letter to its insured) · Ticinonline · TicinoNews · EDÖB (Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner), press release · Der Bund (Tamedia) · Publica (newsletter of 2026-10-22, Cyberangriff auf Softwarelieferanten: Was wir wissen und was nicht) · watson.ch (analysis) · Bernische Pensionskasse (BPK), notice page with its notices of 14 to 30 October 2026 · PK Softech AG (notice of 2026-11-10) · watson.ch (Keystone-SDA) · Publica (Pensionskasse des Bundes), correction of 2026-11-10 (Stand: 10.11.2026) · SRF
HIGHexploitedupdatedNATOA2

Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised in France, six more European countries and Switzerland, with France blaming the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh for the October campaign; Midnight Blue reports six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2

First published 2026-10-13 · open finding →

Update04 Nov 2026 03:30 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebodyactions

The attacks reached Germany: heise reports an Edeka market in Reisbach whose cooling systems were heated to 50 degrees overnight into 2 November, WDR quotes a CAP supermarket manager saying the attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely and reports that Rewe's head office confirmed an attack aimed at Danfoss; SentinelLABS says responsibility has not been publicly established; and Le Canard enchaîné reports that cold rooms of a contractor of the French blood service were programmed to 110 degrees overnight on 1 to 2 November, with no source tying that case to these controllers.

The first German cases followed on 2026-11-02: heise reports that the cooling systems of an Edeka market in Reisbach, Lower Bavaria, were heated to 50 degrees overnight into Monday and that the police have not confirmed a cyberattack as the cause, and WDR quotes a division manager at a CAP supermarket in North Rhine-Westphalia saying the actual attack hit the firm that maintains the cooling plants remotely, which is the operator's statement and not an authority finding, and Rewe's head office confirmed to WDR a cyberattack aimed specifically at the cooling-system supplier Danfoss, whose technology only a few regional Rewe stores use (translated from German) (heise, 2026-11-03; WDR, 2026-11-03). SentinelLABS' assessment of 2026-11-03 says responsibility for the European incidents has not been publicly established, calls Russian-aligned disruptive groups one credible hypothesis based on precedent, and says shared maintenance access deserves scrutiny (SentinelLABS, 2026-11-03). Le Canard enchaîné reports that Coolworld, a company that maintains refrigerated storage containers for the French blood service, was hacked overnight on 1 to 2 November and that cold rooms held at minus 30 degrees were programmed to reach 110 degrees; the blood service says an on-duty technician saw the temperature rise and acknowledges that frozen plasma intended for transfusion was among the products, and the Health Ministry says there was zero operational consequence because the situation was spotted (translated from French) (Le Canard enchaîné, 2026-11-03). The 110 degrees is the programmed set-point and not a measured temperature, and no source names the equipment, the vendor or the access method, or ties this case to the Danfoss and Copeland controllers.

CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, the root-escalation step was patched on 2026-10-29 and CISA lists all three chain flaws (CVSS 8.6)

First published 2026-10-14 · open finding →

Improvement04 Nov 2026 03:29 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-intelcvessourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Ivanti's own CVE record for CVE-2026-118527 (published 2026-11-03) now describes it as predictable filenames in Connect Secure before 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 that let a remote authenticated attacker upload files to a known location, and CERT-FR relays Ivanti's statement that all three chain flaws are actively exploited; the target builds and the compromise check are unchanged.

Ivanti's own CVE record for CVE-2026-118527, published on 2026-11-03, describes predictable filenames in Connect Secure before 25.1.1.3 and 22.8R2.6 that let a remote authenticated attacker upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk (ENISA EUVD, 2026-11-03). CERT-FR's advisory of 2026-11-02 relays Ivanti's statement that CVE-2026-104935, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527 are all actively exploited, lists Connect Secure 22.8Rx before 22.8R2.6, 25.1.1.x before 25.1.1.3 and 25.1.2.x before 25.1.3.1 as affected, and says Ivanti states that the 25.1.3.x releases are not affected by the last two (translated from French) (CERT-FR, 2026-11-02). The target builds and the compromise check above are unchanged.

Canton Vaud: unauthorised access to the IT-support platform of its Gymnases and professional schools copied the names, school e-mail addresses and support requests of about 3,500 teachers and 38,000 pupils; police arrested a 16-year-old pupil of the schools on 2026-10-31

First published 2026-11-01 · open finding →

Update04 Nov 2026 03:27 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagssourcesevidencesourcing_noteverificationbody

Vaud cantonal police announced on 2026-11-03 the arrest, on 2026-10-31, of a 16-year-old pupil of the affected schools, suspected of the intrusion into the IT-support platform between 23 and 26 October; he was questioned and released, his equipment was seized, and the juvenile court leads an investigation into how the intrusion happened and whether data were downloaded or passed to third parties.

Vaud's cantonal police announced on 2026-11-03 that a 16-year-old was arrested on Saturday 2026-10-31, suspected of intruding into the IT-support platform of the canton's post-compulsory schools and extracting data from it between 23 and 26 October 2026 (translated from French) (Le Temps, 2026-11-03). The education directorate says the suspect is one of its pupils and faces an administrative sanction, up to exclusion, that runs apart from the criminal case; he was questioned and released, his IT equipment was seized and is being analysed, and the investigation, led by the juvenile court, aims to establish the circumstances of the intrusion and whether data were downloaded or passed to third parties (Le Temps, 2026-11-03; Inside IT, 2026-11-03). The platform was disconnected from the internet on detection and then secured with the support of the canton's security operations centre, according to the police communiqué; the access method and the platform product are still not stated (Le Temps, 2026-11-03).

Sources: Etat de Vaud (press release of the Bureau d'information et de communication) · RTS · Inside IT (relaying Keystone-SDA) · Le Temps (ATS, relaying the Vaud cantonal police communiqué) · Etat de Vaud (Vaud cantonal police communiqué, published on vd.ch) · Etat de Vaud (education directorate release, published on vd.ch)

CVE-2026-76461: Cisco Secure Email Gateway unauthenticated SQL injection in email parsing reaches root command execution, exploited before disclosure (CVSS 9.8)

First published 2026-09-15 · open finding →

Update04 Nov 2026 03:26 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-intelcvesactionssummarybodyimmediate_actionreferencesheadline

Cisco re-released the 15.5.5-014 fix on 2026-10-31 in light of new information related to exploit code available online, and advisory revision 1.2 of 2026-11-03 tells administrators of 15.5 appliances patched earlier to confirm with retroscannerstatus that the Retro Remediation Engine runs version 4.0.2 or later; 16.5.0-780 needs no such check. Cisco's hardening advisory, revised on 2026-10-14, also says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be actively exploited, this SQL injection and the arbitrary file write CVE-2026-76519, and names no fixed 16.0 release for the hardening CVEs.

Cisco revised the advisory to version 1.2 on 2026-11-03 with the note "Updated information related to Release 15.5.5-014 in the Fixed Releases table"; its footnote says that, in light of new information related to exploit code that is available online, Cisco released an updated version of the 15.5.5-014 fix on 2026-10-31, and it does not say what the earlier build missed (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-09-14). An appliance on the 15.5 branch that took 15.5.5-014 before 2026-10-31 must run the CLI command retroscannerstatus and confirm that Cisco Retro Remediation Engine runs version 4.0.2 or later, while 16.5.0-780 addresses the flaw regardless of that version and Cisco still recommends that releases earlier than 16.5 migrate to it (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-09-14). Cisco's hardening advisory, in its revision of 2026-10-14, says two vulnerabilities from its internal review are known to be actively exploited, the SQL injection above and the separately advised arbitrary file write (Cisco PSIRT, hardening-release advisory, 2026-09-14). For a 16.0 appliance the hardening advisory's table names no fixed release and says to migrate to one (Cisco PSIRT, hardening-release advisory, 2026-09-14), so 16.0.4-302 closes the SQL injection only (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-09-14). Cisco does not say which exploit code it means.

WordPress core 4.7 to 7.1.3: an unauthenticated race in the core update process can lead to remote code execution, fixed in 7.1.4 and backported to every supported branch, listed by CISA as exploited; Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977

First published 2026-10-30 · open finding →

Update04 Nov 2026 03:25 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-intelcvesprioritytagsheadlinesummarytitlesourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03 on evidence of active exploitation, so the flaw is now listed as exploited; the catalog entry names no victim or method, and Wordfence's probing telemetry remains the only described activity.

CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03 on evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-03), and the Canadian Cyber Centre's advisory of the same day relays the listing for WordPress Core before 7.1.4 (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-11-03). The listing names no victim, attacker behaviour or exploitation method, so Wordfence's probing telemetry above remains the only described activity and Patchstack's high-complexity rating still stands. A site that ran a full-package core update on 4.7 to 7.1.3 while wp-content/upgrade/ was reachable needs the compromise check in the Detection line, not only the update.

Sources: WordPress.org · Wordfence · Patchstack · Wordfence Intelligence (CVE-2026-119977) · CISA · Canadian Centre for Cyber Security · Picus Security · The Hacker News

04Action items9 items

  • Find every Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controller, and any other refrigeration controller with a remote management interface because not every second-wave site's vendor is confirmed, in facilities you own or that a contractor manages for you and take its management interface off the internet now, restoring access only through a secure VPN or protected network (filtering to the contractor's source addresses is an emergency stop-gap, and CERT-FR asks you to check your insurance conditions before cutting the contractor's data uplink); an end-of-life unit that gets no fixes needs replacing, because a factory reset leaves it vulnerable and probably compromised again.
    FindingDanfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE…→
  • On every such controller that was reachable from the internet, check the whole configuration, defrost ranges, alarm thresholds and notification recipients included, against the intended one, verify the actual temperatures and test that alarms reach staff; for a Danfoss unit that may have been taken over, restart it or otherwise factory-reset it, restore access only through a secure VPN or protected network and reconfigure it for service, then update its firmware, set the security level to Strict and replace the default and any weak passwords, which do not close the six unpatched AK-SM 800A flaws that Midnight Blue and CCB report, so the interface stays off the internet; change all credentials where compromise is suspected and check the devices attached to the controllers, as BSI advises; and on every Copeland or Dixell XWEB unit confirm the factory Admin password was changed and give each contractor a named account with an expiry date.
    FindingDanfoss AK-SM 800A: six unpatched pre-auth RCE…→
  • Upgrade every Cisco Secure Email Gateway appliance (physical and virtual) to AsyncOS 15.5.5-014 as re-released on 2026-10-31 (on an appliance that took the earlier build, confirm with retroscannerstatus that Retro Remediation Engine runs 4.0.2 or later), 16.0.4-302, or 16.5.0-780 (Cisco's recommended target) now; 16.0.4-302 closes CVE-2026-76461 only, because the hardening advisory names no fixed 16.0 release, so move a 16.0 appliance to 16.5.0-780 to close the five hardening-release CVEs (CVE-2026-76440, CVE-2026-76441, CVE-2026-20353, CVE-2026-76443, CVE-2026-76442) as well, one of which, CVE-2026-76443, has a public Metasploit module according to its author.
    FindingCVE-2026-76461 +5→
  • Grep every appliance's mail_logs (and, if clustered, every cluster member's logs) for the pattern "COPY.*TO PROGRAM" and cross-check firewall/network logs external to the appliance for unexpected outbound connections; a successful exploit grants root, so an attacker may have removed local log evidence of their own access; a clean result does not rule out the S/MIME injection, which did not leave that pattern in the module author's reproduction.
    FindingCVE-2026-76461 +5→
  • Secure Email Cloud customers should confirm directly with Cisco whether their instance is among those where indicators of compromise were identified; Cisco states it has already proactively contacted affected Cloud customers and upgraded all Cloud instances.
    FindingCVE-2026-76461 +5→
  • Restrict the administrative interface of every Barracuda Email Security Gateway, Load Balancer ADC, Message Archiver, WAF Control Center, Web Application Firewall and Web Security Gateway to trusted internal networks now, update every Email Security Gateway to firmware 9.4.0.029 or later, the build Barracuda names (the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected), and apply Barracuda's patch to each of the other products (BNADC-16586 for the Load Balancer ADC and the Web Application Firewall, BNMA-32468, BNWF-60060, BNYF-24789), confirming that automatic patching is on.
    FindingCVE-2026-116606 +1→
  • On every Email Security Gateway whose interface was reachable before the patch, check its configuration for a restore nobody made and its timezone setting for anything other than a timezone name, because watchTowr's single unauthenticated request can reach both and CISA lists both flaws as exploited and requires forensic triage.
    FindingCVE-2026-116606 +1→
  • On every WordPress site your organisation, its web agencies or its hosting suppliers run, deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ in the web server configuration (not with an .htaccess file inside that folder) and confirm it answers 403 before installing 7.1.4 or the fixed release of its branch, because the update itself still unpacks with the old code and a firewall that WordPress itself loads does not run for that request; then confirm in Dashboard > Updates that each site is on 7.1.4 or the fixed release of its branch.
    FindingCVE-2026-119977→
  • On every Linux server that ran cPGuard on 2026-11-02, update to the latest version (the disclosure names 5.88.26 as the clean update), confirm that the hidden root shell and the scheduled task the fake update left are gone, then reset root and local passwords from a trusted environment and rotate the root SSH keys, the MySQL root password, any cloud storage keys and every secret in root's shell history; rebuild from a clean backup taken before 1 November any server the vendor tells you the attacker logged in to by hand.
    FindingcPGuard update channel pushed a fake root update to…→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-11-04T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 4 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Coverage window: standard (gap 24.0 h, previous run 2026-11-03T0256Z-intel; window 26 h; the 24.003 h gap is daily-cadence jitter, not an outage, so no outage-backfill sweep). Four new entries and six changelog records (5 update, 1 improvement); no deep dive (no candidate met the bar), no critical. The four new entries are Barracuda ESG (CVE-2026-116606 and CVE-2026-111560, notable), the cPGuard update-channel compromise (notable), Binance's own account of the 2026-10-29 theft (notable) and the 3AM affiliate intrusion into a UK school estate (notable).

Changelog records. update: CISA's KEV listing of CVE-2026-119977 on the WordPress core entry (the mechanical sweep's one COVERED-STALE row; priority notable to high); Cisco's re-release of the 15.5.5-014 fix and revision 1.2 on the Secure Email Gateway entry (critical stays; the exploit-code statement is Cisco's alone, and the pre-existing KEV-deadline wording in that entry was removed under the zero-warning rule, with immediate_action declared on the record); the arrest of a 16-year-old pupil on the Vaud school entry; the German cases, SentinelLABS' "responsibility not established" assessment and Le Canard enchaîné's blood-service cold-room report on the refrigeration entry (main analysis 737 words before and 736 after, so no growth; the entry stays over the 550 bound and is a candidate for the audit's trim); PKZH's suspended migration, PK Softech's non-pseudonymised-data statement and the Federal Prosecutor's addition of the case to its Akira proceeding on the Publica entry (the analysis is 1,148 words after 1,158, so it was not grown, the superseded PKZH sentence was rewritten in place). improvement (no float): CVE-2026-118527's CNA record and CERT-FR's confirmation that Ivanti calls all three chain flaws exploited, on the Ivanti Connect Secure entry.

KEV disposition. CVE-2026-119977 (COVERED-STALE) shipped as the update above; no RANSOMWARE rows and no NOT COVERED or MENTION-ONLY rows. Backlog. ARX Group SA / Aurora and the ChimeraZ commune claims were re-checked by S2 and S4: no victim, client, regulator or Swiss-press confirmation, so both stay held under their stated conditions (expiry 2026-11-07 and 2026-11-17) and no note was appended.

Source tension. Barracuda's Campus page names firmware 9.4.0.029 as the gateway fix while the CVE record lists builds before 9.4.0.030 as affected; the entry states both and resolves neither, and the mechanism and the per-product affected ranges come from Mandiant's per-vulnerability disclosures (the EUVD record returned an application-unavailable page). The vendor table calls CVE-2026-116606 pre-authentication while listing administrative access as the requirement, as NCSC Switzerland points out. cPGuard's earlier advisory estimate (32 retrieved files) and the spokesperson's 2,946 servers are kept only in the sourcing note, superseded by the vendor's later disclosure (about 2,950 servers and about 7,900 billing-portal accounts). The blood-service report rests on one weekly (Le Canard enchaîné); the 110 degrees is a programmed set-point. A composed BSI/Apple mercenary-spyware entry was withdrawn before the gate to match the 2026-11-03 incident-floor drop (see below).

  • borderline-drop: Control Web Panel CWP2Shell (ten VulnCheck CVEs, unauth chain to root, fixed 1.29), no constituency nexus established, no exploitation, niche hosting panel; marginal niche disclosure
  • borderline-drop: HPE Networking Fabric Composer HPESBNW05172 (46 CVEs, three 9.6-9.8), fix in regular cycle, no exploitation, no exposure-driven urgency, no constituency nexus
  • borderline-drop: Zyxel GS1900 CVE-2026-107441 and AP/FWA7 CVE-2026-76955, LAN-adjacent only (AV:A), no exploitation; regular patch cycle
  • borderline-drop: Kaspersky CyberStrikeAI (LLM orchestrator on the C2, education sector in Africa and Latin America), published 2026-11-02 08:00Z, outside the window; no constituency nexus; LLM-operated intrusion already covered (ARTEX, VAPOR PANDA, the 3AM entry)
  • borderline-drop: CERT-EU AI-agent harness backdoor lab experiment, lab experiment, no in-the-wild use; the in-the-wild analogue (Cursor marketplace extension) is covered
  • borderline-drop: GTIG/Mandiant LLMjacking, stolen cloud tokens drive fraudulent LLM spend, no constituency nexus; generic cloud-identity detection; unresolved CVE-2026-40217 mapping
  • borderline-drop: GTIG XCPE Android set-top-box botnet takedown, consumer/IoT residential-proxy botnet, no constituency nexus, no new decision for a SOC
  • borderline-drop: ESET APT Activity Report Q2-Q3 2026 (PD-9 periodic report), periodic recap; highly relevant findings already covered (UAC-0099/Sandworm entry); no Swiss-public-sector nexus; only the summary page read
  • borderline-drop: ESET Gorbag (Ukraine law-enforcement/defence targets), Ukraine-only victims, WinRAR CVE-2025-8088 already covered
  • borderline-drop: Team Cymru Cl0p second edition, planning-grade pattern recap of covered campaigns (first published 12 Aug, updated October), no new finding
  • borderline-drop: Check Point prompt adware (Codex jailbreak bundle), dual-use adware-style bundle, no constituency nexus
  • borderline-drop: WorkOS internal sales-app breach (ARTEX named by founder), CRM/support data only, no access path stated, no constituency nexus; ARTEX is already tracked
  • borderline-drop: Holcim confirms data theft, Emperador claim (~360 GB), incident floor: no access vector, actor behaviour or transferable lesson beyond the impact; private company
  • borderline-drop: Ukraine and Russia emergency-alert apps hacked (false nuclear warnings), already dropped on 2026-11-03; no vector, AP primary not read; no new fact in window
  • borderline-drop: Swiss GitLab exposure count (Inside IT relaying Shadowserver: 48 instances on CVE-2026-110264, 8 also on CVE-2026-97229), single secondary source, exposure count changes no action on an entry that already tells reader to patch now
  • borderline-drop: SiK-N motion 26.4717 (digital dependencies in procurement), a submitted parliamentary motion, no obligation or deadline for the constituency
  • borderline-drop: Federal Council transitional authorisation model for e-evidence to EU authorities, obligation concerns Swiss providers' legal handover, no defender-side consequence for the constituency
  • borderline-drop: BACS week 44 review (Plex and home-network compromises), private home networks, no public-sector nexus; Plex2Shell KEV date rests on search snippets
  • borderline-drop: Vaud CYBER26 crisis exercise 2026-11-12, an exercise invitation, not threat intelligence
  • borderline-drop: Zimperium Coruna/DarkSword chains by iOS version (update-of DeadTag), no change to the patch decision, the entry already tells readers to update iOS
  • borderline-drop: Android November bulletin (Framework RCE CVE-2026-58868 Critical), Chrome 157, Dell DSA-2026-416, Juniper JSA112183, Canonical LXD CVE-2026-112816, no exploitation reported or outside the window; regular patch cycle
  • borderline-drop: Amadeus breach, hold condition (Swiss or European carrier confirmation) unmet
  • borderline-drop: BSI: Apple mercenary-spyware threat notifications to Bundestag and government members (Apple: 99 countries), dropped on 2026-11-03 under the incident floor and nothing materially new in window beyond Apple's reach statement: no vector, actor or behaviour is public and no ATT&CK id is evidence-bound; the BSI guidance is individual-device hygiene and no source states a Swiss recipient or Swiss authority statement (composed as an entry in this fire, then withdrawn before the gate to stay consistent with the incident floor)

Source health: 291 probed; 287 relevant, 1 stale, 3 unreadable, every non-relevant record already handled (action breakdown 291 none), so no repair order was open. One new candidate, cert-eu-blog (S3: CERT-EU's own research blog outside the cert-eu advisories record); recipe notes added for zimperium-zlabs (working RSS feed set), bitdefender-threat-debrief, kaspersky-securelist, sentinellabs and nau-ch. extract fell back to the metered reader for the EUVD, CISA alert, Binance, FBI, SentinelLABS and Le Canard enchaîné pages in the deep read (eight reader calls: the three EUVD records, the CISA alert, Binance, FBI, SentinelLABS and Le Canard enchaîné); no WebFetch was needed by the main agent. The rotation ranked on the cursor (recent_attempts exclusion count 0, the cursor already spreads the pool).

Coverage gaps: ico-uk (403 on every transport, fourth run), connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport; status page read), sygnia (blocked), rapid7-research (feed not well-formed, outside the slice), lab52 (SSL EOF, outside the slice), ox-security (feed lists dated items, bodies 403, lead-only), edoeb-ch-press (stale listing). Completeness note for the next audit: the 14-day prior-coverage index was loaded in full for its first 40 records and as an id/headline/CVE/entity/last-development projection for the remaining 47 to keep the main context compositional (the sub-agents read the whole file).

Operator note: an early command of this fire used a stale run id and overwrote three tracked files in work/2026-W26-b78503e7/ (prior_coverage.json, prior_coverage_keys.json, state-summary.json) in the working tree; they are not staged and are not part of this commit (restore with git checkout -- work/2026-W26-b78503e7/).

Verification. Eight iterations. Iteration 1 returned NEEDS_FIXES (22 findings, two truth-class rewrites: the cPGuard entry was rebuilt around the vendor's fuller 2026-11-03 disclosure, and the Barracuda entry around Mandiant's per-vulnerability records); iterations 2 to 6 closed the remaining truth findings (the iteration-2 spawn was lost to a container restart and respawned with the same scope; iteration 3 left 18 claims unanswered and was followed by a pass that covered them); iteration 7 returned CLEAN and the cold, full-scope confirmation pass of iteration 8 (231 of 231 claims) returned CLEAN, so the entries publish on a confirmed double-CLEAN with no residual truth or editorial finding. The advisory items left open, all low confidence: four Bitdefender-mapped technique ids unmapped on the 3AM entry, "five further internally-found vulnerabilities" counting CVE ids on the Cisco entry, Cisco's "proactively contacted" wording, the Wordfence Intelligence citation date on the WordPress entry, the 57-case figure's victim-statistic character on the Binance entry, and the attribution of the mechanism sentence in the Barracuda summary. Improvements noticed and not needed this fire, for the next audit: the refrigeration (736 words) and Publica (1,148 words) analyses are far over the 550-word bound and want a trim; a quality-audit pass could add OPSSHIELD to sources/sources.json.

Gate note: the one remaining source-urls warning is the two Mandiant disclosure pages on github.com answering 403 to the gate's own link check (a UA filter); the main agent and the verifier read both through extract and the raw files.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-11-02
item.description:
• PHP2Shell: Xerox fixes AltaLink 82xx/81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink; WorkCentre gets an interim patch, Fiery due 9-23 Nov. Xerox's security bulletin XRX26-016, updated on 2026-11-06, marks AltaLink 82xx and 81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620 as remediated by releases that add PHP 8.2.35 against the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619. WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 and the newly listed AltaLink C8030 to C8070, AltaLink B8045 to B8090, EC8036 and EC8056 stay affected with a system software patch that Xerox says reduces exposure; Fiery patches are due between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-23 and the Worldwide Ticketing Tool fix is in development. The bulletin gives no statement on exploitation of Xerox devices, and CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited. →
  • CERT-UA: Dahua cameras are taken over through the Easy4IP cloud even with no port exposed; turn P2P off. Ukraine's CERT-UA reports, in an alert dated 2026-10-23, compromises of Dahua IP cameras and video recorders in which attackers viewed the stream, changed device settings and created accounts of their own. The main vector is Easy4IP, Dahua's peer-to-peer remote-access feature, which reaches a device through Dahua's cloud by its guessable serial number without any published port; passwords are then guessed or, CERT-UA says, the 2021 authentication-bypass flaws CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045 are used on outdated firmware, a use eSecurity Planet says is unconfirmed in these cases. →
  • Android 'SMS of Death': one hidden SMS drops calls, emergency calls included; Android 12 and 13 get no fix. An independent researcher published a working proof of concept on 2026-10-29 for a zero-click remote denial of service in Android's telephony framework: one malformed WAP Push data message crashes the com.android.phone process, drops active calls including emergency calls and, because the message is retried, can leave a phone in a restart loop. Google's November 2026 bulletin lists CVE-2026-58882, the identifier BleepingComputer gives for the flaw, as a critical denial of service fixed at the 2026-11-01 security patch level for Android 14 to 17 (the researcher had named the October update); Android 12 and 13 phones run the same code unfixed, and no source reports exploitation. →

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLECVE-2021-33044 +1exploitedNATOA2

Dahua cameras and recorders: CERT-UA warns that attackers take devices over through the Easy4IP cloud relay even when no port is exposed, then view video, change configuration and add accounts

CERT-UA's alert (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23; dated 2026-10-23 by Security Affairs, 2026-10-27) reports recorded compromises of Dahua IP cameras and DVRs in which attackers had the video stream, changed the device configuration and created accounts of their own (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27). The main vector is Easy4IP, Dahua's peer-to-peer remote-access feature: a device with it enabled opens an outbound connection to Dahua's cloud and registers by serial number, and access then runs through the cloud, bypassing NAT and firewall, with no published port and no public address (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23; Security Affairs, 2026-10-27). Serial numbers follow a predictable pattern, a 10-character model prefix and a five-character hexadecimal counter that rises almost sequentially, so attackers can guess them at scale and learn which devices are cloud-connected without hitting rate limits (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27). Authentication is then beaten with weak or known passwords or with the authentication-bypass flaws CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045 in outdated firmware, which CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalogue on 2024-08-21, although their use in the October cases remains unconfirmed (eSecurity Planet, 2026-10-27). Dahua fixed both in 2021 with model-specific firmware builds and rates them CVSS 8.1 (Dahua, 2021-11-15). CERT-UA does not say who was targeted, how many devices are affected or who is behind the activity (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27).

The Hacker News says the activity shares similarities with Hunt.io's earlier Operation CameraSwarm, which reported more than 14,530 Dahua cameras compromised between 2026-06-17 and 2026-07-22 with brute-forced credentials and the same two-flaw chain, nearly 2,000 of them given a backdoor account that survives a password change and, on most firmware, a factory reset (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27); eSecurity Planet says no connection to the October incidents has been established (eSecurity Planet, 2026-10-27). Dutch intelligence services warned in July that Russian state actors compromise IP cameras to collect intelligence on military transports (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
Any Dahua IP camera, NVR or DVR with Easy4IP enabled, whether or not it has a public address; CERT-UA warns that such devices may be vulnerable even when they cannot be reached directly from the internet (Security Affairs, 2026-10-27).
Detection
In each device's audit log, DVRIP authentication events from the local address 127.0.0.1, which CERT-UA reads as a sign of access through the P2P cloud, plus accounts nobody created and unauthorized configuration changes; text overlaid on the video image is another sign, but its absence proves nothing (The Hacker News, 2026-10-27; Security Affairs, 2026-10-27).

Triage: a login from 127.0.0.1 shows only that the session arrived through the P2P relay, so where staff or an installer legitimately use Easy4IP it is normal; the account name, the time and the configuration change that follows separate the two.

Defender takeaway
Turn Easy4IP off wherever it is not needed, keep cameras off the internet and reach them through a VPN limited to authorized addresses, review the account list and the cloud accounts linked to each device, and update the firmware by hand, CERT-UA's four steps (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23; Security Affairs, 2026-10-27); check all Dahua devices on the network, forgotten ones included (Security Affairs, 2026-10-27), and do not count on a password on outdated firmware, since those flaws make knowing it unnecessary (CERT-UA, 2026-10-23).
