ROUTINENATOB2

NIK C2: Talos documents a Go Windows implant that sends operator prompts to the OpenAI API from the infected host and falls back to the victim's own API key

Cisco Talos found a command-and-control framework it calls NIK C2, with a live server, whose 64-bit Go implant for Windows takes more than 52 commands: browser and Wi-Fi credential theft, keylogging, screen, camera, microphone and clipboard capture, hidden VNC, RDP session interaction, an embedded SOCKS5 and HTTP proxy with a reverse tunnel for lateral movement, AMSI patching, UAC bypass and process hollowing (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). It talks to its server over TLS WebSockets on port 443 with an HTTP polling fallback about every 250 milliseconds under AES-256-GCM, persists through registry Run keys and COM hijacking, masquerades under a system-process name such as svchost.exe and runs a watchdog process (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). The new part is the ai_generate command: the implant builds an OpenAI Chat Completions request from an operator prompt on the infected host, posts it to OpenAI from the victim's address and returns the answer to the panel; if the operator gives no key it reads the OPENAI_API_KEY environment variable, so OpenAI charges the victim's payment method and its logs show the victim's key (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29; Infosecurity Magazine, 2026-10-29). A screen-locking ransomware module encrypts no files: PowerShell copies the boot sector to a temporary file, and a looping batch file reopens a lock page shown through mshta.exe (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Talos sees at least three implant versions and assesses with moderate confidence that the framework is functional; its post names no victims, sector or delivery method (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Windows hosts; the post gives no initial-access method, so exposure cannot be read from an estate's configuration. A host that holds an OPENAI_API_KEY in its environment lends that key to the operator.
Detection
In egress and proxy telemetry, requests to the OpenAI API from a process that is not a sanctioned AI client, in particular a process named like a system binary such as svchost.exe that runs from the user's Roaming Microsoft Network folder, the install location the post describes; in process and registry telemetry, the fodhelper.exe UAC-bypass pattern (a command written under the ms-settings shell key and removed within seconds), an AMSI patch in a PowerShell session and, from the lock-screen module, a Run key that launches a looping batch file (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29); on the OpenAI side, usage or billing under a key the owner did not use.
Defender takeaway
Add the OpenAI API (and other LLM endpoints) to the list of destinations that only sanctioned clients may reach, and rotate any OpenAI key found on a host where this framework ran, because the implant bills and logs it as the victim's own.

Xerox's security bulletin XRX26-016, published 2026-10-23 and updated on 2026-11-06, marks AltaLink 82xx and 81xx and EC81xx as remediated by release 123.xxx.006.29800 and VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620 by release 123.xxx.006.30100, each of which adds PHP 8.2.35 with the fixes for the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (Xerox, 2026-11-06). WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 and the newly listed AltaLink C8030/C8035, C8045/C8055 and C8070, AltaLink B8045/B8055 and B8065/B8075/B8090, EC8036 and EC8056 stay affected, each with a system software patch that Xerox says reduces exposure (bulletins XRX26-017 and XRX26-018) (Xerox, 2026-11-06). Fiery's target patch dates are by 2026-11-09 for FS800, FS700, FS600 and FS500, by 2026-11-16 for FS400, FS350 and FS300, and by 2026-11-23 for FS200, each including the Pro editions, and the Worldwide Ticketing Tool fix is in development (Xerox, 2026-11-06). For the affected AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre devices Xerox says the vulnerable PHP component is used by a limited number of pages in the embedded web server and names two interim measures: restricting the web interface to trusted networks or management hosts, and disabling HTTP/HTTPS, which also disables the embedded web server and all authentication, authorization and accounting solutions, and cannot be re-enabled remotely (Xerox, 2026-11-06). The bulletin gives no statement on exploitation of Xerox devices, while CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 and describes each as allowing unauthenticated remote code execution in PHP (CISA KEV, 2026-10-30).

Exposure
The models above before their remediating release, the patched-but-unfixed models, and the Fiery controllers in FS200 to FS800 releases; on AltaLink, EC81xx, VersaLink and WorkCentre the affected component sits behind the embedded web server's HTTP/HTTPS interface, so that interface is the surface to restrict. Xerox lists as not impacted, among others, Lexmark printer firmware, VersaLink B400, B405, B600, B605, B610, B615, C400, C405, C500, C505, C600 and C605, C8000, C9000 and the C/B70xx and C/B71xx series, WorkCentre 3335, 3345 and 6515, and the Phaser and PrimeLink models it names, and says its review of other products is still underway (Xerox, 2026-11-06).
Defender takeaway
Install the remediating releases on AltaLink 82xx and 81xx, EC81xx and VersaLink now; on WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 and the AltaLink C80xx and B80xx models apply Xerox's exposure-reducing patch and keep the web interface restricted to trusted networks or management hosts until a fix ships, and, as Xerox names no interim measure for the Fiery controllers or the Ticketing Tool, treat network reachability as their lever until the Fiery patches land between 2026-11-09 and 2026-11-23 (Xerox, 2026-11-06). Xerox warns not to disable HTTP/HTTPS on a device that runs an AAA solution or is managed remotely, because recovery requires manual action at each device (Xerox, 2026-11-06).

Android telephony ('SMS of Death'): one hidden WAP Push message crashes the phone process and drops calls, emergency calls included; fixed for Android 14 to 17 at the 2026-11-01 security patch level per Google's bulletin row for CVE-2026-58882, the identifier BleepingComputer gives; Android 12 and 13 stay exposed, public proof of concept

A researcher who signs as Mark B published a working proof-of-concept app on 2026-10-29 for a zero-click remote denial of service in Android's telephony framework (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). One malformed WAP Push data message to port 2948 makes WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu() cast a 64-bit header length to a signed 32-bit integer and allocate a negative-sized array; the uncaught NegativeArraySizeException kills the com.android.phone process, which drops active calls, emergency calls included, and cuts service for one to two seconds per message (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). The poison message stays in the pending queue and is retried on every boot and on carrier redelivery: the researcher reports that about 20 messages leave a device unusable and that one Android 12 phone rebooted into recovery roughly every 90 seconds until the messages were deleted over ADB (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). The crash reproduced on Android 12 to 16, on a Pixel 9 and on Samsung Galaxy and A-series phones (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29); Security Affairs restates the mechanism and the October fix for Android 14 to 17 (Security Affairs, 2026-11-01).

Google's fix, titled "Fix remote DoS in decodeWapPdu", catches the exceptions the malformed messages trigger and deletes the malicious messages from the SMS database (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31); per the researcher it shipped in the October 2026 update for Android 14 to 17, so Android 12 and 13 phones outside the update window run the same code unfixed (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). Google's November 2026 bulletin lists CVE-2026-58882, the identifier BleepingComputer gives, as a critical denial of service in the System component fixed at the 2026-11-01 security patch level for Android 14, 15, 16, 16-qpr2 and 17 (Google, 2026-11-02; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31). BleepingComputer adds that the fix is not listed in Google's October bulletin (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31). The proof-of-concept app and its source are public (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-31), and none of the sources reports use in the wild.

Exposure
Any Android phone below the 2026-11-01 security patch level, which Google names as the fix level of CVE-2026-58882, BleepingComputer's identifier for the flaw (Google, 2026-11-02), and Android 12 and 13 phones outside the security-update window, which receive no fix; the attack needs only the target's phone number (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29). The patch level in device-management inventory shows which handsets have the fix.
Detection
On managed handsets, repeated crashes of the com.android.phone process in the device log, with a NegativeArraySizeException raised in WapPushOverSms.decodeWapPdu, calls that end with disconnect cause CS_DEATH, and a phone that restarts into recovery about every 90 seconds (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29); the message never appears in the inbox and the sender is not shown, so the crash log is the only trace on the phone.

Triage: a single telephony restart has many benign causes; a restart that recurs on every boot or on each carrier redelivery, with the exception above in the crash log, matches this flaw.

Defender takeaway
Move every managed Android handset to the 2026-11-01 security patch level or later, emergency-service and on-call staff first, and list for replacement the Android 12 and 13 phones outside the security-update window, which receive no fix and stay crashable by one message. A phone stuck in the loop should not be wiped from the recovery prompt: the researcher documents deleting the pending WAP Push rows over ADB from a computer, which avoids a factory reset (smsofdeath.com, 2026-10-29).

rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the Senate department for urban development's attack-detection licences covered only five percent of devices and that neither the entry endpoint nor the servers the data left from were covered; BSI told rbb24 it does not confirm that the Berlin attack followed the TerminalFix pattern.

rbb24 Recherche reported on 2026-10-21 that the attack-detection system introduced in 2026 had licences for only five percent of all devices, according to the Senate department for urban development, which also said that extending it to every device was not possible "for financial reasons"; rbb's research shows that neither the endpoint identified as the criminals' entry point nor the servers from which data later flowed were covered by it (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). Both departments also said that in 2024 the funds needed for IT security were available only in part to the extent required, although the state's information-security guideline has obliged agencies since 2017 to provide enough staff and money (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). The stolen data includes a copy of the transport senator's identity card and of her digital signature and, rbb's analysis shows, further identity-card copies and personal documents of employees; the mobility department confirmed to rbb that the data is mostly unstructured files from shared and personal directories (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21).

BSI told rbb that it had warned repeatedly since at least March 2025 of fake security prompts that make users run a malicious command themselves, publicly and in daily situation reports that also went to representatives of the federal states, and that it described the TerminalFix variant in September 2026; it does not confirm to rbb that the Berlin attack followed that pattern, saying only that it is in close contact with Berlin and supporting the response (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21). BSI's advisory of 2026-09-04 does not name Berlin (BSI, BITS-2026-287419-1032, 2026-09-04), so the link between TerminalFix and this incident rests on BSI's Mastodon post, which heise reads as confirmation (heise online, 2026-09-07), and not on a BSI statement to rbb that the Berlin attack followed that pattern. rbb describes the chain for such warnings: the Berlin-CERT run by the IT service centre ITDZ passes relevant reports to each agency's information-security officers, and each agency is itself responsible for acting on them; the ITDZ and the Senate Chancellery did not say whether BSI's warnings reached the two departments or what followed (translated from German) (rbb24, 2026-10-21).

Defender takeaway
The transferable gap is licence coverage, not the absence of a tool. Compare the endpoints and servers that actually run the detection agent, file servers holding shared and personal directories first, with the estate, and settle who in a federated administration is accountable for acting on a national-CERT warning, because in Berlin's chain the ITDZ and the Senate Chancellery left open whether the warnings reached the two departments.

The fixed builds are PHP 7.4.33-0122, PHP 8.0.30-0104, Calendar 2.4.8-10948 and Mail Station 30000002.3.19-10333 on DSM 7.0 to 7.1, and PHP 7.4.33-0010, Calendar 2.4.8-0948 and Mail Station 30000002.3.19-0333 on DSM 6.2; the table lists no PHP 8.0 build for DSM 6.2, gives the PHP 8.1 to 8.4 builds without a DSM split and still offers no fix for PHP 7.3 (Synology, 2026-10-31).

Sources: QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, revision V1.1) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, affected-products table as of 2026-10-27) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, revision V1.2) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-19, QNE (ADRA)) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · QNAP (statement on PHP2Shell) · Synology PSIRT (Synology-SA-26:14) · Synology PSIRT (Synology-SA-26:14, revision 4)

04Action items3 items

  • Turn off Easy4IP (P2P cloud access) on every Dahua camera and recorder that does not need it, and search each device's audit log for DVRIP logins from 127.0.0.1.
    FindingCVE-2021-33044 +1→
  • Install release 123.xxx.006.29800 on every Xerox AltaLink 82xx, 81xx and EC81xx and release 123.xxx.006.30100 on every VersaLink C/B415, C/B625 and C/B620; apply Xerox's exposure-reducing system software patch to WorkCentre 3655, EC7836 and EC7856 (XRX26-017) and to AltaLink C80xx and B80xx, EC8036 and EC8056 (XRX26-018), and keep the web interface of those models reachable only from trusted networks or management hosts until Xerox ships a fix.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Move every managed Android phone below the 2026-11-01 security patch level to that level or later, phones of emergency-service and on-call staff first.
    FindingCVE-2026-58882→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-11-02T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 4 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Quiet window (gap 24.0 h, window 26 h, the Sunday-into-Monday stretch): CISA KEV has no addition after 2026-10-30 (S1 read catalog 2026.10.30 and the mechanical sweep agrees), none of the Swiss, EU or national-CERT records published inside the window, and the yield came from rotational lookbacks and the 72 h developing-window sweep. Coverage window: standard (gap 24.0 h, previous run 2026-11-01T0256Z-intel).

Published. New: the Android telephony "SMS of Death" crash (S3, in window); the Xerox and Fiery PHP2Shell printer estate (S1, recovered after verifier iteration 1 under PD-7 (c): an advisory for a flaw whose exploitation is in-window news, with fixes still unreleased); the Dahua Easy4IP camera takeover (S3, lookback: true from the securityaffairs 168 h record, PD-7 d); NIK C2 (S3, lookback: true from the talos 168 h record, PD-7 d, routine and short). Changelog records: Synology-SA-26:14 revisions 3 and 4 added to the QNAP/Synology PHP2Shell entry (S1); rbb24's report of the Berlin departments' own answers added to the Berlin Landesnetz entry (S4); the US military commissary freezer investigation added to the Danfoss refrigeration entry (S2).

Recency note (PD-7 against PD-11). The Berlin and Danfoss records rest on sources older than 26 h (rbb24 of 2026-10-21, surfaced inside the developing window by Born's relay of 2026-10-30; Reuters of 2026-10-29 and Nextgov of 2026-10-30). I applied the update exemption (a changelog record carrying a delta new to the store inside the 72 h developing window) to those two and held every new entry to the 26 h window, a rotational lookback, or PD-7 (c). Verifier iteration 1 (F10) flagged the dropped Xerox and Fiery bulletin as a blind spot for a public-sector reader; I accepted it and published it under PD-7 (c). The other S1 PHP2Shell vendor estates stay dropped as out-of-window with weaker constituency nexus (Siemens energy, Delta Controls, pfSense and OPNsense): the next audit may recover them.

Source tension. The Berlin entry's sourcing note said BSI "now independently confirms" TerminalFix as the Berlin vector. rbb24 (2026-10-21) says BSI does not confirm that to rbb, and BSI's advisory BITS-2026-287419-1032 never names Berlin; the link rests on heise's reading of BSI's Mastodon post. The sourcing note is corrected in the changelog record; verifier iteration 1 (F16, F17) then led me to move the entry's priority to notable (a 66-day-old single-victim event whose new section adds a governance lesson), confidence to medium and credibility to 2, because the phishing click rests on Der Tagesspiegel alone and the TerminalFix link on heise's reading of BSI.

  • out-of-window: Siemens Spectrum Power, AMIS TS, Energy Engage and KACO blueplanet PHP2Shell (SSA-166980 V1.2), primary source 2026-10-29, window_hours=26; energy-utility nexus only.
  • out-of-window: Delta Controls enteliWEB and V4 controllers (SecB0015 rev 3, SecB0016 rev 2), primary source 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-28, window_hours=26; no Swiss deployment established.
  • out-of-window: pfSense and OPNsense PHP2Shell fixes, primary source 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22, window_hours=26; GUI is LAN-only by default.
  • out-of-window: Dell PowerProtect Data Domain DSA-2026-416, Juniper Session Smart Router and Conductor JSA112183, TianoCore EDK II CVE-2026-97631, TeamViewer TV-2026-1011, newest sources 2026-10-19 to 2026-10-30, window_hours=26; none exploited.
  • borderline-drop: Canonical LXD, MicroCloud and Incus CVE-2026-112816 (CVSS 10.0 certificate-chain authentication bypass), in window (The Hacker News 2026-11-01) but PD-11 relevance doubt: the HTTPS listener is opt-in, no constituency deployment established, no exploitation; revisit on exploitation or a KEV listing.
  • borderline-drop: Siemens Industrial Edge Management applications, Node2Shell (SSA-443410, 2026-10-30), industrial-edge OT niche, no constituency nexus, no exploitation against Siemens products reported.
  • borderline-drop: CVE-2025-8088 ransomware-use flag on the MDaemon/ClamAV entry, metadata only; CISA's flag is undated and attached to the WinRAR record, and it changes no decision on the covered mail-server path.
  • borderline-drop: BSI tells German MPs and ministers to assume their iPhones are compromised (ARD, heise, 2026-11-01), incident floor: no vector, actor or behavior, no Swiss case; revisit if a Swiss authority or Apple notices reach Swiss officials.
  • borderline-drop: Ukraine's Air Alert app pushing false radiation and chemical alerts (BBC, Fox News, BNO, 2026-11-01), no Swiss nexus, analogy to civil-protection alerting only, no vector.
  • borderline-drop: WIRED's report of a contractor's AI coding agent on a DoD NIPRNet environment (2026-10-29), single anonymous source contested by Accenture, low confidence.
  • borderline-drop: Talos VOLTA infostealer (2026-10-31), a distinct finding from NIK C2 (separate entry under item granularity), commodity crimeware with no sector, actor or vector; the LLM-API egress detection concept is carried by the NIK C2 entry.
  • out-of-window: ARTEX thread delta, Microsoft on DPRK Onyx Sleet and Pearl Sleet using ARTEX (2026-10-29) and CrowdStrike's gated report on four agentic actors (2026-10-30), older than the 72 h developing window, CrowdStrike detail gated; the audit may fold the DPRK sentence into the ARTEX entry.
  • borderline-drop: Swiss municipal forum claims (ChimeraZ selling data attributed to ebikon.ch, gersau.ch, meggen.ch, stadtwil.ch and davos.ch), FBI attribution of the Binance theft to TraderTraitor, Chainalysis breach, Universität Leipzig outage, French communes Cholet and Verrières-en-Forez, Holcim claim, Alpine Linux GitLab attempt, Ruag tank-fraud inquiry, per S4: PD-6 not cleared (single tracker relaying a forum advert, sample looks public), incident floor, not new, or not a cyber incident.
  • Single-source: 2026-11-02/android-sms-of-death-wap-push-telephony-crash; the researcher is the origin; BleepingComputer and Security Affairs restate it; which release carries Google's fix rests on the researcher's word. BleepingComputer's CVE-2026-58882 does not resolve (MITRE CVE API: record does not exist), so cves[] is empty.
  • Single-source: 2026-11-02/dahua-easy4ip-p2p-cloud-camera-takeover-cert-ua; CERT-UA's alert page is script-rendered; verifier iteration 3 read it through the reader and the entry now cites it as primary (its text carries no date, 2026-10-23 is Security Affairs' dating), with The Hacker News, Security Affairs and eSecurity Planet restating it (one assessor, four publishers). Dahua's 2021 advisory read directly for CVSS 8.1 and the per-model fixed builds.
  • Single-source: 2026-11-02/xerox-fiery-php2shell-printers-fixes-due-6-to-23-november, Xerox's own bulletin XRX26-016 (version 4), read through the PDF reader; CISA KEV listing read from the catalog (version 2026.10.30), which covers the PHP runtime and not these devices.
  • Single-source: 2026-11-02/nik-c2-go-implant-sends-prompts-to-openai-from-victim-host, Cisco Talos only; Infosecurity Magazine restates it. S3's suggested link to CAIRN and CLOSEDQUORUM was left out because the Talos post does not state it.
  • Backlog: ARX Group SA (Aurora leak-site claim, row surfaced 2026-10-24), held, state unchanged: S4 re-checked on 2026-11-02 (ransomware.live press: null, no victim statement, no Swiss press in DE, FR, IT or EN, name clash with an unrelated thermal-management company noted); hold condition unmet, expiry 2026-11-07, nothing appended to the row.
  • Candidate sources added: rbb24-recherche, xerox-security-bulletins. Left for a later fire: onyphe-blog, signalandsilence-substack, varonis-threat-labs, delta-controls-security (each flagged by one sub-agent; recipes verified only for varonis and the two Delta and Xerox pages).
  • Recipe changes from sub-agent findings: securityaffairs rss_url pinned (paged feed), resecurity moved to the bridge, notes appended for lumen-black-lotus-labs, cnil-fr, ncsc-nl-php2shell-tracker, ico-uk and ec-digital-strategy-newsroom.
  • Pre-existing history noted, not touched: the Danfoss entry's main analysis (about 1,290 words) and the Berlin entry's (about 710 words) exceed the 550-word bound; this fire's records did not grow either analysis, and trimming them is audit work.

Coverage gaps: ico-uk (every transport 403, host outage as on 2026-11-01); connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport, status page read, no security item); ox-security (feed parses, every article body 403); databreaches-net (site catching up after its own outage, newest post 2026-10-29); F5 K000163821, Check Point sk1000302, the Fiery Communities article and Juniper's support portal (script-only pages, revision stamps not comparable with covered entries).

Verification: six iterations of the single cti-verification definition, confirmed CLEAN at iterations 5 and 6 (two consecutive independent cold passes, each covering all 155 claims), final residual 0. Iterations 1 to 4 returned NEEDS_FIXES with 9, 5, 3 and 4 truth findings and 7, 1, 2 and 1 editorial findings; iteration 1 produced the Xerox and Fiery entry (F10), a Berlin recalibration (priority notable, confidence medium, credibility 2) and a corrected Berlin sourcing note, and iteration 3 turned CERT-UA's own page into the Dahua entry's primary source. Two iterations (4 and the Triage hedge before it) caught defects my own fixes introduced. Declined: the Danfoss update-versus-new suggestion (the section states the only stated link to the US commissary case is the investigators' contact; regions and sectors untouched) and the Dahua carve-out host remark (cip.gov.ua is now in NATIONAL_CERT_HOSTS, with the tool tests passing). Left as pre-existing: em dashes and a few "this entry" cross-references in the older Berlin sections, and Berlin's T1567.002 (BSI's TerminalFix-general sentence); the next audit may take them.

Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Updates to prior coverage 22Action items 19

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

ROUTINEupdatedNATOA2

Canton Vaud: unauthorised access to the IT-support platform of its Gymnases and professional schools copied the names, school e-mail addresses and support requests of about 3,500 teachers and 38,000 pupils; police arrested a 16-year-old pupil of the schools on 2026-10-31

The Swiss canton of Vaud says unauthorised access, detected on 2026-10-26, to the IT-support platform of its Gymnases and professional schools copied the names, school e-mail addresses and support requests of about 3,500 teachers and 38,000 pupils; passwords are not stored on the platform and no grades or pupil files are affected (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31). The canton names targeted fraudulent messages that pose as the school or IT support as the main risk (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31); it gives no access method, actor or platform product. Vaud police announced on 2026-11-03 the arrest, on 2026-10-31, of a 16-year-old pupil of the affected schools, suspected of the intrusion between 23 and 26 October; he was questioned and released, his equipment was seized, and the juvenile court's investigation aims to establish how the intrusion happened and whether data were downloaded or passed to third parties (Le Temps, 2026-11-03, translated from French; Inside IT, 2026-11-03).

Defender takeaway
The sources give no access method, so there is no patch or configuration change to prescribe; school and cantonal IT teams should brief users to expect impersonation of IT support and to report urgent or unusual messages, as the canton advises (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31).
Improvement03 Nov 2026 03:46 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-intelsummarysourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

The education directorate's deputy director said that at present much points to an internal matter, with the case and several indications passed to the police (translated from German) (Inside IT, 2026-11-02).

Update04 Nov 2026 03:27 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagssourcesevidencesourcing_noteverificationbody

Vaud's cantonal police announced on 2026-11-03 that a 16-year-old was arrested on Saturday 2026-10-31, suspected of intruding into the IT-support platform of the canton's post-compulsory schools and extracting data from it between 23 and 26 October 2026 (translated from French) (Le Temps, 2026-11-03). The education directorate says the suspect is one of its pupils and faces an administrative sanction, up to exclusion, that runs apart from the criminal case; he was questioned and released, his IT equipment was seized and is being analysed, and the investigation, led by the juvenile court, aims to establish the circumstances of the intrusion and whether data were downloaded or passed to third parties (Le Temps, 2026-11-03; Inside IT, 2026-11-03). The platform was disconnected from the internet on detection and then secured with the support of the canton's security operations centre, according to the police communiqué; the access method and the platform product are still not stated (Le Temps, 2026-11-03).

Improvement08 Nov 2026 14:09 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditsourcessourcing_note

The police communiqué, published on vd.ch, says the platform was disconnected from the internet as soon as the access was detected and then secured with the support of the canton of Vaud's operational security centre, that a criminal complaint was filed, and that the suspect was identified quickly and released after questioning; the cyber investigation division of the criminal police leads the inquiry under the juvenile court (translated from French) (Etat de Vaud, 2026-11-03). The education directorate's release adds that the incident was reported to the Federal Office for Cybersecurity and to the cantonal data-protection authority (translated from French) (Etat de Vaud, 2026-10-31).

First published 2026-10-31 · open finding →

The takeaway said CloudSOC SpanVA and CASMA have no fix; Broadcom's umbrella advisory lists none as of 2026-10-30, but their own advisories need a login, so the statement now says what the umbrella page shows.

The takeaway said CloudSOC SpanVA and CASMA have no fix. Broadcom's umbrella advisory 39404, last revised on 2026-10-30, lists both as affected and states no fix or workaround, while their own product advisories, 39429 and 39475, need a Broadcom login, so the absence of a fix is what the umbrella page shows, not a confirmed state (Broadcom, 2026-10-30).

HIGHCVE-2026-97229exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-97229, GitLab CE/EE: an integer overflow in the CI/CD regular-expression compiler allows code execution on self-managed servers; exploited, fixed in 19.4.2, 19.3.5 and 19.2.8 (CVSS 10.0)

First published 2026-10-13 · open finding →

Improvement01 Nov 2026 14:03 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodysourcestitle

The sibling flaw CVE-2026-110264 reaches every GitLab version from 7.0, with backports to 19.1.9, 19.0.10 and 18.11.13, so instances older than 19.2 are in scope and have a fixed build; the Ruby project says any application that compiles attacker-controlled regular expressions is exposed until Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 or 3.3.13.

GitLab's notes of 2026-10-21 give the sibling flaw CVE-2026-110264 a wider range than this one: every GitLab CE/EE version from 7.0 before 18.11.13, 19.0 before 19.0.10, 19.1 before 19.1.9 and 19.2 to 19.5 before their October 21 builds, with the fix backported to 18.11.13, 19.0.10, 19.1.9 and 19.2.9 (GitLab, 2026-10-21). An instance on a branch older than 19.2 is therefore not out of scope and has a fixed build to move to. The Ruby project says the regular-expression engine bugs behind these CVEs are reached whenever an application compiles a regular expression from a string an attacker controls, fixes all of them in Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13, and advises avoiding compiling regular expressions from untrusted input where an upgrade is not possible (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

Sources: GitLab (Critical Patch Release 19.4.2, 19.3.5, 19.2.8) · CERT-EU · NCSC Switzerland (Security Hub advisory) · BleepingComputer · GitLab (Critical Patch Release 19.4.1, 19.3.3, 19.2.7) · Rapid7 · Rapid7 researcher repository (proof-of-concept README) · CISA · Alpine Linux (incident post) · NCSC Switzerland (Security Hub advisory, update of 2026-10-29) · GitLab (Critical Patch Release 19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9) · Ruby (regexp compilation fixes)

VMSA-2026-0006, VMware vCenter: unauthenticated Directory Service auth bypass and Syslog traversal RCE (both CVSS 9.8), plus a VMXNET3 guest-to-host escape

Correction01 Nov 2026 14:03 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditactionsbodycvesheadlinesourcessourcing_notetitle

Broadcom's revisions of 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-19 (the 8.0 U2f express patches and the 7.0 extended-support path) are now in the fixed builds and actions; the Infosecurity Magazine attribution and date are corrected, CISA's ransomware-use flag on CVE-2026-59310 is recorded, the network attack vector of the two lower-severity flaws and the researcher credit are fixed, and the headline is current.

Broadcom revised the advisory twice after first publication: on 2026-08-03 (VMSA-2026-0006.1) the vCenter 8.0 U2f and ESX 8.0 U2f express patches became available, and on 2026-08-19 (VMSA-2026-0006.2) it added patch guidance for the 7.0 lines, where vCenter and ESX 7.0 customers are told to contact Broadcom Support under an extended support contract (Broadcom, 2026-08-19). The fixed-build statements above now include those paths. Broadcom scores CVE-2026-41703 and CVE-2026-41709 with a network attack vector that needs high privileges, and credits Maxim Suhanov by name (Broadcom, 2026-08-19).

The 2026-08-28 section said Infosecurity Magazine reported the same assessment as The Hacker News; its article of 2026-08-13 reports only QUIRSO's earlier assessment of a suspected APT actor and predates the China-nexus and Babuk findings (Infosecurity Magazine, citing QUIRSO GmbH, 2026-08-13). CISA's catalog now marks CVE-2026-59310 as known to be used in ransomware campaigns, without naming an actor or a ransomware family (CISA KEV, 2026-10-30), so the ransomware finding no longer rests on QUIRSO alone.

Update01 Nov 2026 14:01 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodyevidencesources

Morphisec reports PHP2Shell post-exploitation on a Windows server running IIS with PHP-CGI (the IIS worker starting php-cgi.exe, a command shell and a packed reverse-shell payload), the first such account it knows of; Siemens now points APE1808 operators to the available PAN-OS versions, and The Hacker News carries Unit 42's retraction.

Morphisec reports blocking post-exploitation on a customer's Windows server running IIS with PHP-CGI, where the IIS worker process w3wp.exe started the PHP-CGI handler php-cgi.exe, which ran a command shell that launched a packed payload; the payload used shellcode to load networking libraries and tried to open a reverse shell to an external server (Morphisec, 2026-10-28). Morphisec ties the chain to the PHP flaws but says its agent did not detect the PHP exploitation itself, and it describes one customer; it says every earlier confirmed exploitation report described a Linux environment (Morphisec, 2026-10-28). On Windows, the process signal is therefore php-cgi.exe under w3wp.exe starting cmd.exe or other executables.

Siemens' advisory for RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices, at version 1.1 of 2026-10-28, now tells operators to upgrade to the corresponding available PAN-OS version and to contact customer support for further patch information (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-28). The Hacker News has added a note to its 2026-10-25 article recording Unit 42's retraction (The Hacker News, 2026-10-25). Hunt.io puts watchTowr's report of exploitation of both flaws on its honeypots on 2026-10-21 earliest, ahead of Karimi's honeypot report (Hunt.io, 2026-10-28).

Update01 Nov 2026 13:58 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditactionsbodysourcessummarytechniquesevidence

GitGuardian counts at least 72,026 further GhostAction commits to 22,964 repositories between 13 and 21 October from mostly the same unrevoked accounts, and new payloads that reach developer machines through a hidden VS Code task outside GitHub's workflow hold, query cloud metadata and AWS roles, and install a cron job that survives cleaning the repository.

GitGuardian's analysis of 2026-10-27 counts, as lower bounds from its own feed, 72,026 commits from the operator to 22,964 public repositories between 13 and 21 October, 7,989 of them new victims, pushed by 1,792 accounts of which 1,382 had already pushed the 8 October payload: the tokens stolen earlier were never revoked (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). The campaign now ships five payload families and reaches beyond GitHub-hosted runners. One family is a Node.js stealer disguised as a font file and launched by a hidden VS Code task that runs when a developer opens the folder and trusts the workspace; it reads cloud, package-registry, Git, Kubernetes and AI-tool credential files, SSH keys and token-bearing environment variables, and since no workflow is involved, GitHub's workflow hold does not stop it. Self-hosted-runner workflows query the cloud instance metadata service for role credentials, and the revived 2025 workflow requests a GitHub OIDC token and tries to assume every AWS IAM role found in the environment (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). Three families install a cron job that fetches and runs a script from the operator's server every five minutes, so a developer laptop or runner that ran one stays under control after the repository is cleaned. GitGuardian found no successful run of the workflow payloads, which GitHub's hold caught (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). Between 22 and 26 October, loaders of a separate campaign, PolinRider, were added to GhostAction commits and force-pushed; GitGuardian sees no clear link between the two operators (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27). It warns against reverting the attacker's "Update" commits, which restores the previous malicious version, and has seen re-infection where tokens were kept after a clean-up (GitGuardian, 2026-10-27).

Sources: StepSecurity · Socket · GitGuardian · GitGuardian (October escalation)

Correction01 Nov 2026 13:56 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditaffected_productsbodycvessources

An earlier section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside the laboratory is dated to the day it held; NCSC Switzerland now rates the flaw actively exploited, and Zscaler's first-day decoy telemetry joins ELLIO's. Datadog's detection layers (decoder errors, worker crashes, leaked decompressed output) and what does not catch the attack are added, as is Palo Alto's Prisma Cloud Transporter Client.

The 2026-10-26 section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory held only for that day: CISA listed the flaw as exploited on 2026-10-27, and NCSC Switzerland's advisory, updated on 2026-10-29, now gives the status as actively exploited with a proof of concept available (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26). ELLIO's capture is not the only attack telemetry: Zscaler's decoys recorded 402 events from 20 source addresses against 12 customers within a day of disclosure, 60% of them exploitation attempts and the rest reconnaissance (Zscaler ThreatLabz, 2026-10-28).

Datadog, which reproduced the bug, finds no conventional indicators because no attacker infrastructure is involved and lays out three layers to correlate (Datadog, 2026-10-29): decoder errors, where a vulnerable Node.js build returns Z_BUF_ERROR "unexpected end of file" (which benign truncated input also produces) and a patched one ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH; process signals, a worker exiting with signal 139 right after a Brotli transfer or pinned at full CPU inside a decompression call; and decompressed output carrying bytes the client never sent, the memory-disclosure path, so endpoints that echo or reflect decompressed content are the ones to check first. Payload byte signatures, WAF content matching and body-size limits do not catch it, because the WAF forwards compressed bytes and the middleware counts decompressed size (Datadog, 2026-10-29). Palo Alto's advisory also lists Prisma Cloud Application Security Transporter Client before 0.2.9 as affected, fixed in 0.2.9 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

Microsoft removed seven eMudhra-hierarchy certificates from the Windows trust list in an out-of-band update of 2026-10-26 and from the Edge trust list on 2026-10-27; Cisco's advisory reached version 1.5 on 2026-10-30 with ISE fixes dated December 2026 and April 2027; GitLab's releases of 2026-10-29 distrust the eight intermediates, with GitLab Runner and the AI Gateway needing separate updates; Python's releases of 2026-10-26 carry the built-in denylist; and Oracle's revision of 2026-10-30 extends the Java alert to Oracle Database Server, Autonomous Health Framework and OPatch. Certificates that chain to the removed roots need replacing, and disconnected Windows devices need the updated trust lists.

Microsoft released an out-of-band Windows update on 2026-10-26 that removes seven certificates associated with the affected hierarchies, six eMudhra G3 roots and an AAA Certificate Services cross-sign, from the Windows trust list, and removed the same seven from the Edge trust list on 2026-10-27; removing a root is a separate and broader decision than blocking the compromised intermediates, which Microsoft had done through its Disallowed Certificate Trust List on 2026-10-20 (Microsoft, 2026-10-26). Microsoft tells organizations to keep automatic trust-list updates flowing, to make sure disconnected Windows devices receive the updated trust lists, and to replace certificates that chain to one of the seven before the change reaches their devices, and it warns that software that does not check revocation or the disallowed list could still accept certificates tied to the compromised keys if trust is restored locally (Microsoft, 2026-10-26).

Cisco's advisory is at version 1.5 of 2026-10-30. It lists remediation for Secure Firewall ASA, FTD and FMC (guidance page), Secure Email Gateway and Secure Email and Web Manager (updated automatically to Trusted Root 2.8, with the updatenow command where updates are manual) and Packaged and Unified Contact Center Enterprise (CSCwx36769); it dates the fixes for ISE and ISE-PIC to ISE 3.5P5 in December 2026 and 3.3P13 and 3.4P8 in April 2027, and still lists IOS XE Software, MDS 9000 and Nexus switches among the impacted products under investigation; Cisco says it is not aware of malicious use (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30). GitLab's patch release of 2026-10-29 removes trust for the eight intermediates in self-managed CE and EE and says GitLab Runner 19.5.1 and the AI Gateway must be updated separately because they verify certificates on their own (GitLab, 2026-10-29). Python's expedited releases of 2026-10-26, 3.15.2, 3.14.10, 3.13.18, 3.12.16 and 3.11.18, now carry the built-in denylist for the compromised intermediates (Python Insider, 2026-10-26). Oracle's revision 2 of Security Alert CVE-2026-114820, dated 2026-10-30, adds the Java component of Oracle Database Server (19.3 to 19.32, 21.3 to 21.23 and 23.4.0 to 23.26.3, not client-only installations), Autonomous Health Framework Trace File Analyzer 26.3 to 26.10, OPatch 12.2.0.1.16 to 12.2.0.1.52 and Hospitality Cruise Shipboard Property Management 23.3.4 to 23.3.6, each remotely exploitable without authentication at CVSS 3.1 9.1 (Oracle, 2026-10-30).

Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant report that since late August they have seen ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN operated inside incident-response cases, with ARTEX adopted by extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters whose victims include US government organizations; they track the Wiz-observed ARTEX campaign as UNC7228, overlapping Storm-0940, and say the original ARTEX repository was taken down in October while forks keep spreading it. The agent's log signature is bursts of roughly 2 to 25 seconds, error-driven retries and, in one case, MySQL general-log changes likely intended to write JSP web shells.

Google Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant report that since late August 2026 they have seen threat actors operate ARTEX, PentAGI, CAIRN and possibly custom harnesses inside Mandiant incident-response engagements, with agents carrying out significant parts of the attack lifecycle such as lateral movement, database exploitation and exfiltration preparation (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31). They say ARTEX has been adopted since late August by financially motivated extortion groups and suspected PRC-nexus clusters, whose operations affected organizations in government, technology, chemicals and materials, and manufacturing in the United States, and that the campaign Wiz tracks, which GTIG tracks as UNC7228, overlaps with Microsoft's Storm-0940 and dates back to at least August 2026 (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31). The original ARTEX repository was taken down by its creator in October because of abuse, but community forks, among them a commercial one, keep the framework in circulation (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31).

In several cases the operators handed ARTEX compromised credentials and told it to run the later stages. GTIG's log signature for the agent is execution in bursts of roughly 2 to 25 seconds, error-driven retries and forensically noisy trial and error; in one case, given valid credentials, the framework used an application's SQL API to point the MySQL general log at a web-accessible .jsp path and then ran SELECT statements carrying script tags, likely intended to write web shells under somewhat-incremental file names until they ran cleanly (GTIG and Mandiant, 2026-10-31).

A device that was exposed and unpatched therefore needs the compromise checks in the Detection line, not only the hotfix.

Twenty-four entries carry one record each from this fire (7 updates, 13 corrections, 4 improvements; 7 internal). Report: docs/audits/2026-11-01-quality-audit.md.

Verification & coverage notes

  • Claims: an open partial claim from cleanup wave 05 (2026-10-21T1147Z-audit, partial 2026-10-21T11:47:42Z wave=05) still stands on main; the scheduled audit ignores a partial claim (Phase 0 step 2), and it is more than 48 h old.
  • Budget: 13 of 20 spawns (six truth passes, G1 to G3, four verifier passes), 6,885,964 sub-agent tokens: 4,748,994 before the verifier loop and 2,136,970 in it (work/2026-11-01T1312Z-audit/budget.tsv).
  • Verification: four passes over this fire's changed claims, the run record and the report. Iterations 1 and 2 returned NEEDS_FIXES (7 and 3 truth findings), all remediated; iteration 3 returned CLEAN; iteration 4, the confirmation pass over all 242 claims, found no truth defect and two editorial ones (two cves[].affected strings not brought in line with this fire's own fixed-build additions), both applied. Decision rule 5 (truth plus editorial at most 2, no F1 or F4) publishes on that early exit; the residual is 2, the two editorial findings, which were applied after the pass and are unverified by a further pass. The pre-existing advisories left for the next truth pass are the Dream citation dates on the CVE-2026-46300 entry.
  • Truth passes: 54 entries in six batches, 1,651 ledger claims, every claim answered (12 unreadable in TA, mostly NetScaler's Tech Zone post that returns 403 on every transport). Verdicts: 30 clean, 22 imprecision, 2 factual error.
  • Records: 24 entries carry one record each (7 update, 13 correction, 4 improvement; 7 internal). The six re-sweep developments are records on covered entries; no new entry was needed.
  • KEV: ten additions since 2026-10-25, all covered (work/2026-11-01T1312Z-audit/kev-window.txt); no COVERED-STALE or RANSOMWARE row.
  • Backlog: ARX Group SA held to 2026-11-07; G2 found no victim, client or press confirmation.
  • borderline-drop: Adobe Campaign Classic APSB26-162 as a new entry: published instead as an update on the 2026-10-02 entry, whose fixed build it supersedes.
  • borderline-drop: ESET APT Activity Report Q2-Q3 2026, Talos VOLTA and NIK C2, Check Point Yoba, Elastic wesp.sys, Symantec AI relays, Group-IB MadApe, Microsoft's DPRK AI staging, Kaspersky cloud isolation, the MEP letter on ad-delivered spyware, Apple's notification wave, Zimperium's Coruna and DarkSword counts (G3): no constituency decision.
  • borderline-drop: Contact Form 7 6.2.4, Sophos UTM CVE-2026-118633, TeamViewer TV-2026-1011, the Drupal contrib wave of 2026-10-28, Splunk, Mitel, Jenkins, EPICS, Adobe Connect, LXD, Thales Sentinel, Teltonika, vsftpd, TightVNC, WolfVision, Grafana, the Synology SA-26:15 and Fortinet FG-IR-26-187 notices for the covered Brotli flaw (G1): unexploited, regular cycle, no constituency exposure, or a vendor notice that adds no decision to the covered entry.
  • borderline-drop: Sophos UTM CVE-2026-118633 (Sophos advisory 2026-10-28, pre-auth root RCE, all versions, end of life, manual patch): no exploitation or proof of concept reported, it needs the email proxy with scanning enabled and minutes of sustained racing (not a single-request path), EPSS 0.006, and the product is end of life with a manual patch as the only fix; verifier iteration 1 raised it as a missed angle (F10, low confidence) and the audit keeps the drop, to be reopened on an exploitation report.
  • borderline-drop: Camping.Care supplier-side statement (a Dutch campsite's notice of 2026-10-23, G2): it predates the window and adds only that the platform operator told campsites data was presumably taken, which the covered entry's incident framing already carries.
  • borderline-drop: SolNet, SIHF, SoftwareOne, Leipzig University, Fehmarnbelt FLC, Verrières-en-Forez, the Federal Council alerting dispatch, the e-evidence transitional rule, the Geneva e-voting step, the BACS week-43 WhatsApp wave, EFK report on ZEMIS (G2): below the incident floor or no defender consequence.
  • Declined truth-pass findings, with reasons in the report: Adobe Commerce Events for CVE-2026-48356, the MDaemon KEV ransomware flag (WinRAR vector), the WS_FTP CVE-2026-90867 mitigation (CVE record API only), the Gridbox high (low-confidence F16), T1611 on CVE-2026-46300, Publica's early volume statement.
  • Source health: sans-isc content scope set; ico-uk (timeouts), ssd-disclosure (transient) and connectwise-trust-center (flapping) investigated and left as they are; no webfetch-only record.
  • Reader pool (context): 6 of 10 jina keys live, balance about 46.8 M; G3 saw extract fall through to the reader seven times on Dark Reading.
  • ATT&CK pin: up to date (local v20.0 == upstream v20.0).
  • Tool change: tools/check_run.py now appends every run-scope gate output to work/<run-id>/gate.log; exercised on this fire's gate runs.
  • Coverage gaps: sygnia (blocked on every transport), cyberscoop and technadu feeds (10 items, 2026-10-25 to 10-27 not listed), F5 K000163821 and the per-product Broadcom advisories (JS shell or login), apa-ots (feed about 3 h deep), risikomonitor.ch (no DNS from the container).

2026-11-01T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 1 entry published

Verification & coverage notes

  • Window: standard class, gap 24.0 h to 2026-10-31T0256Z-intel, window 26 h. The window is a Saturday and a Sunday: every authority and trade feed in the slices has its newest item on 2026-10-30 or earlier (NCSC.ch security hub 2026-10-30T14:22Z, BACS pages 2026-10-27 and older, NCSC-NL, BSI, CERT-EU, CERT.at, CERT-PL, ENISA, NCSC-UK, CISA, Inside IT, Netzwoche). A thin window is the healthy outcome here, not a miss.
  • KEV sweep: kev_window_diff.py found no CISA KEV additions inside the window, and S1's own read of catalog 2026.10.30 agrees (the newest additions, the two Ivanti flaws of 2026-10-30, are covered). No KEV row needs a disposition.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA / Aurora row stays held. S4 re-checked on 2026-11-01 (DE, FR, IT and EN searches; Inside IT through 2026-10-30; the tio.ch, SRF, RTS, Netzwoche, ICTjournal and Blick listings; the arx.ing homepage) and found no statement from ARX, SBB, ASTRA or Swiss press; Ransomware.live still shows the bare claim with no press link. The row's expiry stays 2026-11-07, struck if the condition is unmet.
  • Dispositions (PD-8): the PAN-OS naming and the Unit 42 verification are an update on 2026-10-22/pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release; the Fragnesia entry carried the same stale "one unnamed vendor" statement and takes an improvement that names the vendor without re-floating it; the PHP2Shell main entry takes an update that names the vendor and adds GreyNoise's sensor data and Hunt.io's captures (follow-up FU1, spawned on the verifier's missed-angle finding). GTIG and Mandiant's incident-response report is an update on the ARTEX entry; Microsoft's trust-list removal, Cisco's advisory v1.5 and GitLab's release are an update on the eMudhra entry.
  • Recency (PD-7): the PAN-OS update rests on Dream Research (2026-10-29) and Unit 42 (2026-10-29), and the eMudhra update on Microsoft (2026-10-26), GitLab (2026-10-29), Python (2026-10-26) and Cisco v1.5 (2026-10-30), all dated before the 26 h horizon of 2026-10-31T00:56Z and none carried by the previous fire. They are admitted as first coverage from rotational sources' lookback (Dream through S3, GitLab through S1) and as changelog records on covered entries that predate them, each moving what a reader does (the post-patch compromise check and the Windows trust-list removal). The GreyNoise tracker (2026-11-01) and Hunt.io (2026-10-28, revised 2026-10-30) additions to the PHP2Shell entry come from the FU1 follow-up. The GTIG report is in window.
  • Sourcing: the Vaud entry is single-source-victim; RTS repeats the canton's release and adds a pupil suspicion without a further named source, which the entry attributes to RTS. The PAN-OS entry moves from single-source to multi-source (Dream Research and Unit 42 describe the chain; the two worked together, so credibility stays 2 and the actor claim rests on Dream's relay of Unit 42's CL-UNK-1280 designation). Hunt.io's PAN-OS rooting sentence relays Dream and Unit 42 and is not an independent vantage.
  • Source inconsistencies carried: GTIG's introduction lists ARTEX, Hexstrike and CAIRN while its observations list ARTEX, PentAGI and CAIRN (sourcing note of the ARTEX entry). Dream says the PAN-OS management web server also fronts the GlobalProtect portal, while Palo Alto's advisory says GlobalProtect is not affected; the entry states both, attributed (see the Contradiction line). Dream's page title counts 25 servers where earlier text counted 24 (24 batch-rooted firewalls plus the internal management server).
  • Contradiction: Dream says the PAN-OS management web server also fronts the GlobalProtect portal; Palo Alto's advisory says GlobalProtect is not affected. The PAN-OS entry states both, attributed. Hunt.io says PAN-OS runs one uniform PHP 8.0.30 build and that the exploit reliably roots it; Dream lists PHP 7.4.33 on PAN-OS 11.1 and 24 rooted of 240 targeted. The entries carry Dream's version and count only.
  • borderline-drop: ESET APT Activity Report Q2 to Q3 2026: no Swiss or public-sector finding beyond the MDaemon item already covered.
  • borderline-drop: Talos VOLTA and NIK C2 (AI-integrated implants): effort-displacement novelty with no decision change; NIK C2 is also outside the window.
  • borderline-drop: Kaspersky NetamLoader: one Asian victim, no attribution, no constituency nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Check Point Yoba: XMRig miner payload through fake AI-app repositories, no nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Huntress camera-management-software intrusion: vendor and initial access unknown, low confidence.
  • borderline-drop: Binance USD 6.36 billion theft: passes only the global-scale clause, no Swiss nexus, and the vector is one clause (a DevOps laptop and a service container) with no transferable technique detail.
  • borderline-drop: Chainalysis intrusion: method undisclosed, no Swiss customer named (incident floor).
  • borderline-drop: Northflank environment-variable exposure: no Swiss or public-sector nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Node2Shell vendor-list additions (Cisco still investigating, Prisma Cloud Transporter Client 0.2.9, Stormshield Management Center 3.9.4): marginal product-list additions on a covered entry.
  • borderline-drop: Android SMS of Death (CVE-2026-58882): denial of service only, and the CVE id comes from BleepingComputer alone with no NVD or EUVD record on 2026-11-01.
  • borderline-drop: TeamViewer TV-2026-1011 (CVE-2026-111585 and two more, fixed in 15.83): a user-interaction flaw that needs the viewer to connect to a hostile host, no exploitation known, patchable in the normal cycle; the sources date from 2026-10-28 to 2026-10-30.
  • borderline-drop: Sophos GOLD OGRE/Aur0ra AI-agent ransomware and Microsoft's North Korean AI-adoption post: no constituency decision.
  • borderline-drop: SIHF portal credential-abuse breach, Holcim leak-site claim, SALEG and INED claims, Oberspreewald-Lausitz district administration: no Swiss public-sector nexus or no victim confirmation.
  • Carry-forward for the next fire (S1): Cisco's advance notice of 2026-10-28 says advisories for ISE, UCS Central and Unified CM publish on 2026-11-04.
  • Candidate source added: vd-ch-press-releases (primary for cantonal disclosures; both S2 and S4 proposed it). Proposed and not added, to keep to about one per run: letemps-cyber, ms-trusted-root-program, remedio-research, php.events.greynoise.io (GreyNoise's per-flaw event tracker, worth a per-fire check while a flaw is in KEV). Recipe findings are in the sources_changed notes: mandiant-gtig (the FeedBurner feed lags and missed the 2026-10-31 post), enisa-euvd, lab52, swissinfo-ger, phorion.
  • Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport); ox-security (article bodies 403); lab52 (feed SSL EOF, listing read through the reader, nothing in horizon); Tamedia pages (tagesanzeiger.ch, 24heures.ch) fall to the metered reader or return page chrome.
  • Watchlist: not configured (product, supplier and standing-interest lists empty).
  • Source-health repairs of this fire (UNSOLVED list): sans-isc now reads its feed (fetch_method rss, health_cmd feed), frenchbreaches gets a feed health_cmd, vd-ch-press-releases is content_scope: general-news; ico-uk stays flagged needs-demote because the direct sitemap read, extract and WebFetch all timed out today, a transport timeout that never demotes (the recipe worked on 2026-10-22 and 2026-10-27).
  • Verifier iteration 1 (NEEDS_FIXES, 23 findings) was remediated before iteration 2; its follow-up research FU1 ran on the missed-angle finding. The run's own verification block carries the outcomes.
  • Verification: eight iterations, the cap. Iteration 1 returned NEEDS_FIXES with 23 findings and iteration 5 a first CLEAN (three advisories left); the confirmation pass, iteration 6, returned NEEDS_FIXES (two truth findings, both fixed), and iterations 7 and 8 returned NEEDS_FIXES on small wording, date and citation defects. The loop ended at the cap and publishes under the fail-open rule with verification_residual_count 3, the truth and editorial findings of iteration 8. Those three (a Threat ID range on the PAN-OS entry, an OpenJDK citation date on the eMudhra entry, a "first documented code execution" claim on the PHP2Shell entry) were corrected after the last pass and are not re-verified; the next quality audit should give those three entries an independent read.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-31
item.description:
• WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 admin-credential leak, five more critical flaws; fix 2025.0.4, 2024.0.7. Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, covers fifteen WS_FTP Server flaws on Windows, six of them critical: CVE-2026-84295, an improper-authentication flaw that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker reach administrative credentials (CVSS 3.1 10.0), and five command-injection, path-traversal and missing-authorization flaws (CVE-2026-90868 at 9.9, CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 at 9.1, CVE-2026-90865 at 9.0), four of which NCSC Switzerland describes as a route from the exposed administrator credentials to full server compromise. Builds before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 are affected, and CSIRT Italia says Progress will issue no patch for unsupported versions. NCSC Switzerland lists exploitation as unknown and no source reports it; CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, though a 2023 flaw in the same product is listed with known ransomware use. →
  • Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC. Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination. →
  • Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor. Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension. Coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor and Sophos say the attacker could not log in there, but the key, the persistence and a host report were still written. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised, and no source says how the attacker published under Anthropic's name. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01WS_FTP Server: unauthenticated CVSS 10.0 admin-credential leak, five more critical flaws; fix 2025.0.4, 2024.0.7. Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, covers fifteen WS_FTP Server flaws on Windows, six of them critical: CVE-2026-84295, an improper-authentication flaw that could let an unauthenticated remote attacker reach administrative credentials (CVSS 3.1 10.0), and five command-injection, path-traversal and missing-authorization flaws (CVE-2026-90868 at 9.9, CVE-2026-90866, CVE-2026-90864 and CVE-2026-90863 at 9.1, CVE-2026-90865 at 9.0), four of which NCSC Switzerland describes as a route from the exposed administrator credentials to full server compromise. Builds before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 are affected, and CSIRT Italia says Progress will issue no patch for unsupported versions. NCSC Switzerland lists exploitation as unknown and no source reports it; CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, though a 2023 flaw in the same product is listed with known ransomware use. →
  2. 02Microsoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick Assist ended in AD CS certificates for privileged accounts and a DC. Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any actor, in which an external Teams contact impersonating help-desk staff got a user to open Quick Assist, after which the operator staged a portable runtime and used Active Directory Certificate Services to reach privileged identities: a template open to ESC1 issued certificates for privileged accounts and DCSync followed within seconds, and in the second case PetitPotam was relayed to AD CS Web Enrollment (ESC8) for a certificate for a domain controller account. An issued certificate stays valid after a password reset or a reimage of the first workstation, and in the first case one privileged account excluded from automated containment stayed usable and was used to copy data to an external SFTP destination. →
  3. 03Cursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code extension for 11 hours; uninstalling leaves the SSH backdoor. Between about 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29 the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace served a modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, that appends an attacker's SSH key to authorized_keys, tries to enable SSH and open a reverse tunnel, and installs persistence that outlives the extension. Coding errors made the SSH step fail on most standard-user hosts, so Cursor and Sophos say the attacker could not log in there, but the key, the persistence and a host report were still written. Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised, and no source says how the attacker published under Anthropic's name. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 2Trending vulnerabilities 4Updates to prior coverage 5Action items 14

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLENATOB2

Teams help-desk impersonation to domain-controller identity: Microsoft traces two intrusions from a Quick Assist session to AD CS ESC1 certificates with DCSync, and to PetitPotam relayed to ESC8 Web Enrollment

Microsoft Threat Intelligence describes two human-operated intrusions, not attributed to any threat actor, that began with an external Teams contact (across the broader activity Microsoft saw organisation-themed tenant names and support-style display names) who persuaded a user to open Quick Assist and read out the connection code; the activity did not exploit a Teams vulnerability. In the session the operator placed an archive in Downloads, extracted it into a newly created KB-prefixed folder under the user profile and started the payload with a portable Python, JavaScript or Java runtime, which ran host and network discovery and assessed AD CS (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

In the first case a certificate template open to ESC1, where the requester supplies the identity, produced certificates for three privileged accounts, and about 90 minutes later for eight more after a second wave against 16 users; DCSync began within seconds of obtaining one privileged certificate. Defender's automated disruption blocked more than 1,000 SMB attempts, but a privileged account excluded from automated response stayed usable, reached a file server and ran a renamed Rclone that copied a share to an external SFTP destination (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). In the second case the operator used PetitPotam to make a domain controller authenticate to the attacker's host, relayed that NTLM authentication to an AD CS Web Enrollment endpoint, obtained a certificate from the Domain Controller template and used it for PKINIT to get a ticket-granting ticket for the controller's account; Defender raised ESC8 alerts and the customer isolated the workstation (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

Exposure
A forest with an enterprise CA whose authentication-capable templates accept requester-supplied identity with broad enrollment rights (ESC1), or whose Web Enrollment or Certificate Enrollment Web Service endpoints lack HTTPS and Extended Protection (ESC8), where Teams accepts external chats and calls and users can start Quick Assist; Defender for Identity's AD CS posture assessments, or an inventory of /certsrv endpoints and template permissions, shows the first two (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).
Detection
New external Teams contacts from help-desk-themed tenants; in process telemetry, a portable runtime started from a freshly created KB-prefixed folder under the user profile after a remote-support session; in CA records, certificate requests and issuances correlated by requester, subject alternative name and template with the first authentication using the certificate; and a domain controller account authenticating to Web Enrollment from a device that is not that controller, which Microsoft calls a strong pivot (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). After containment, revoke the unauthorized certificates and assess issued Kerberos tickets separately; a password reset and a reimage of the first workstation leave both in place.

Triage: a help-desk Quick Assist session is routine; what separates this one is an external-tenant initiator with no matching ticket and an interpreter runtime launched from a newly created user-writable folder rather than a managed install path.

Defender takeaway
Require HTTPS and Extended Protection on every enrollment web endpoint, drop the ones nobody needs, review authentication-capable templates and require approval where enrollment is broad, and enable the Certification Services audit subcategory and CA audit filter; limit Teams external access and restrict remote-support tools to approved ones. Treat a containment exclusion as an incident decision with a manual compensating step, because in the first case the one excluded privileged account was the route to the file server (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30).

Builds on: 2026-09-03/teams-helpdesk-impersonation-nodejs-implant-winrm-dc-pivot

threat31 Oct 03:51Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Microsoft Threat Intelligence
NOTABLENATOB1

Cursor marketplace: a tampered Claude Code extension (versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313) planted an SSH key, a reverse tunnel and persistence for about eleven hours on 2026-10-29; uninstalling it does not remove the persistence

Between about 2:27am PT and 1:35pm PT on 2026-10-29 (09:27 to 20:35 UTC) a maliciously modified copy of Anthropic's Claude Code extension, versions 2.1.312 and 2.1.313 for macOS and Windows, was served from the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace; Cursor removed it, shut the marketplace down briefly, rotated its keys, rebuilt it and had the hosting provider take the attacker's server offline (Cursor, 2026-10-29). Anthropic told Microsoft its systems were not compromised and that it did not build the package, and Microsoft confirms the packages were never published to the Visual Studio Marketplace or npm (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). How the attacker published under Anthropic's name is not disclosed in any source read. Cursor estimates up to 5,000 affected users (Sophos X-Ops, 2026-10-30).

The injected loader runs when the extension module loads. It reports host and user data (hostname, username, operating system, home and working directories, the configured Git email, environment-variable names and public IP address), appends an attacker-controlled SSH public key to authorized_keys, tries to enable the local SSH service and open a reverse SSH tunnel, and installs persistence outside the extension: a LaunchAgent on macOS, and on Windows a scheduled task that asks to run as SYSTEM with a Startup-folder fallback, with background scripts retrying the tunnel about every 60 seconds (Cursor, 2026-10-29). Microsoft's analysis adds a user crontab entry for Linux (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30). Because of coding errors the step that enables SSH fails unless Cursor was started with administrator privileges, so on most hosts the attacker could not log in through the tunnel, but the key, the persistence and the host report still happened (Cursor, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Any macOS or Windows host on which Cursor installed or auto-updated Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 inside the window; the code also carries Linux routines though Cursor names only macOS and Windows packages (heise online, 2026-10-30). Extension-install telemetry shows the version. NCSC Switzerland carried the incident on 2026-10-30 but places the backdoored extension on Open VSX and says Anthropic pulled versions from npm and the VS Code marketplace (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-30); Microsoft says the packages never reached the Visual Studio Marketplace or npm, and Cursor and Phorion name the Cursor marketplace, so the entry follows them.
Detection
In process-creation telemetry, an editor's extension host starting ssh or autossh with remote port forwarding and no command; in file-write telemetry, an editor process modifying authorized_keys; and, shortly after an extension update, a new LaunchAgent, scheduled task, Startup-folder script or @reboot crontab entry named after system-monitoring components. Phorion advises matching the attacker key's fingerprint rather than the comment string it carries (Phorion, 2026-10-30). Removing the extension does not remove the persistence scripts, which keep running (Cursor, 2026-10-29).

Triage: a running SSH process is not proof the attacker got in, since both ends must allow the connection (Microsoft Threat Intelligence, 2026-10-30); administrators run tunnels too, and what separates this one is an editor extension as the parent process and persistence written to user-writable locations rather than a managed service.

Defender takeaway
Treat a host that ran either version as backdoored whether or not the tunnel connected: remove the key, the persistence and the tunnel processes, rebuild where compromise cannot be excluded, and rotate credentials reachable from it. heise reports a cleaned release, with 2.1.314 as the minimum to install (heise online, 2026-10-30).
incident31 Oct 03:50Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Cursor (security notice) · Phorion · Microsoft Threat Intelligence · Sophos X-Ops · heise online · NCSC Switzerland (Cyber Security Hub, post 13121)

02Trending vulnerabilities4 items

NOTABLECVE-2026-84295 +6updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-84295, Progress WS_FTP Server: an unauthenticated remote authentication flaw can expose administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0), with two more unauthenticated flaws, fixed in 2025.0.4 and 2024.0.7; no exploitation found

Progress, as CNA, published CVE-2026-84295 on 2026-10-29: improper authentication in WS_FTP Server on Windows that "could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to access sensitive information, including administrative credentials"; its CVSS 3.1 vector is network, low complexity, no privileges and no user interaction, scored 10.0, and the record names no component or endpoint (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29). Two further flaws carry an unauthenticated vector with high attack complexity: CVE-2026-90865, an OS command injection that could allow command execution with elevated privileges under certain configurations (9.0) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), and CVE-2026-90867, improper access control in the Web Admin console that could expose administrative functionality to remote authentication attempts (8.1) (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29). CSIRT Italia counts 6 critical and 3 high flaws in the release, of types including authentication bypass, remote code execution and arbitrary file read and write (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30).

The record for CVE-2026-84295 names versions before 2024.0.6 and 2025.0.3 as affected (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), and the records for the other two name versions before 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 (ENISA EUVD, 2026-10-29), so 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4 is the build to reach. CSIRT Italia lists 2025.0.3 (10.0.3) and 2024.0.6 (9.0.6) and earlier as affected and says that for unsupported versions the vendor will not release a workaround or patch (translated from Italian) (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30). No source reports exploitation: CISA's catalog holds no 2026 WS_FTP flaw, although CVE-2023-40044 in the same product has been listed since 2023-10-05 with known ransomware use (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-10-30).

Progress's bulletin, as listed by heise, carries fifteen CVEs, six of them critical (heise online, 2026-11-02). Besides the three above: CVE-2026-90868, an OS command injection that could allow arbitrary command execution under certain configurations (9.9) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); CVE-2026-90866, a path traversal by a delegated Host Administrator, potentially enabling remote code execution (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); CVE-2026-90864, a path traversal that lets a delegated Host Administrator reach data beyond their permitted scope (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29); and CVE-2026-90863, missing authorization in the administrative interface (9.1) (GitHub Advisory Database, 2026-10-29). NCSC Switzerland describes the exposed administrator credentials as the start of a chain: command injection under certain configurations (CVE-2026-90868, CVE-2026-90865) or a scope escape (CVE-2026-90863, CVE-2026-90866) leads to a complete compromise of the server, and it lists exploitation as unknown (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-11-02). Builds 2024.0.7 and 2025.0.4 have been available since 2026-10-01 (heise online, 2026-11-02).

Exposure
Any WS_FTP Server on Windows below 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4; CSIRT Italia describes it as a secure file-transfer server used within organisations and with external partners, so instances reachable from partner or public networks come first (CSIRT Italia, 2026-10-30). The records name no component for the authentication flaw, so no configuration is known to make an instance safe.
Detection
No source publishes an indicator. For an instance that was reachable before the fix, the records to review are the web-server logs of the Web Admin console and the file-transfer server's own logons for administrator access from unfamiliar addresses, and process creation by the service or its web worker, since CVE-2026-90865 is command execution (an inference from the described flaw).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4, partner-facing instances first, and rotate the administrator credentials afterwards, because the upgrade does not change credentials an attacker already read; take an instance on an unsupported branch off the network or migrate it.
