CVE-2026-98432, Linux kernel IPv4 TCP: a use-after-free in connection setup, present since 4.4, has an Anthropic-built remote root exploit against MPTCP listeners that CloudLinux could not reproduce; Citrix XenServer, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu's generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10 and Sophos have fixes, Ubuntu 20.04 and older and some HWE, FIPS, NVIDIA and Azure variant kernels are in progress and WatchGuard and Fortinet have none for their products (CVSS 9.8)

The Linux kernel CVE team published CVE-2026-98432 on 2026-10-15; the kernel.org CNA scores it 9.8 while upstream rates it 8.1 with high attack complexity (CIQ, 2026-10-30). It is a use-after-free in the IPv4 TCP connection setup path, introduced in Linux 4.4 and fixed upstream in 6.12.113, 6.18.56, 7.2.10 and 7.3-rc7 (Linux kernel CVE team, 2026-10-15). An unauthenticated peer starts it by sending TCP SYN packets that carry IPv4 options, and a retransmitted SYN can then touch the freed option memory (CIQ, 2026-10-30).

Anthropic wrote on 2026-10-27 that Claude produced an exploit that gives a remote attacker root on a Linux server with a multipath TCP (MPTCP) listener (Anthropic, 2026-10-27), but CloudLinux's kernel team could not reproduce the claim (CloudLinux, 2026-11-02). Akamai is not aware of a public working exploit and says disabling MPTCP alone does not prevent exploitation (Akamai, 2026-11-02), whereas Vates, XCP-ng and WatchGuard say a public exploit exists or circulates (XCP-ng, 2026-11-04; Vates, 2026-11-04; WatchGuard, 2026-11-03). No source reports attacks, and NCSC-NL judges large-scale abuse unlikely given the exploit's complexity (NCSC-NL, 2026-10-30).

Debian, Red Hat, CIQ and AWS have fixed kernels (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-11-03; Red Hat, 2026-11-03; CIQ, 2026-11-01; AWS, 2026-11-02), and Ubuntu's tracker, last updated 2026-11-10, lists 22.04 LTS to 26.10 as fixed (linux 5.15.0-203.213, 6.8.0-149.149, 7.0.0-43.43 and 7.3.0-10.10) while 20.04, 18.04 and 16.04 are still in progress (Canonical, 2026-11-10). Citrix has fixed its XenServer appliances (Citrix, 2026-11-03). XCP-ng released a kernel fix (XCP-ng, 2026-11-04), MikroTik's RouterOS 7.25.1 and 7.24.6 changelogs list the CVE (MikroTik, 2026-11-02; MikroTik, 2026-10-30), Sophos released Sophos Firewall hotfix HF110626.1 on 2026-11-06 and SD-RED firmware 3.0.012 on 2026-11-05 (Sophos, 2026-11-06), and Veeam's KB4966 says its Software and Infrastructure Appliances, workers, helper appliances and recovery media include an affected kernel, delivered fixed through Veeam Updater (Veeam, 2026-11-10). WatchGuard lists Fireware OS, AP and Dimension as potentially affected with no fix (WatchGuard, 2026-11-03); Fortinet names no fixed build but added an IPS virtual patch in FMWP database update 26.113 on 2026-11-07 (Fortinet, 2026-11-07).

Exposure
A Linux host on a kernel below the fixed builds that accepts IPv4 TCP connections from an attacker; the demonstrated exploit needs an MPTCP listener, which sudo ss -M -l -n -p -e lists and which Go programs enable on Linux listen sockets by default since Go 1.24 unless the multipathtcp GODEBUG setting or a per-socket option overrides it (Akamai, 2026-11-02; Go team, 2026-10-29). CIQ's testing found that setting net.mptcp.enabled to 0 leaves the plain-TCP path reachable (CIQ, 2026-10-30), and Akamai reports a similar flaw when request-socket migration is on (Akamai, 2026-11-02).
Detection
No source publishes an indicator. Because the trigger is a SYN packet with IP options (CIQ, 2026-10-30) and a lost race only fails the handshake, so the attacker can retry (Anthropic, 2026-10-27), repeated option-bearing SYNs from one source toward a listener in firewall or flow telemetry are the pattern the mechanism implies.
Defender takeaway
Install the distribution kernel and reboot as soon as it ships and confirm the running version afterwards; Ubuntu 20.04 and older and some variant kernels were not out on 2026-11-10. Until then, drop IPv4 TCP packets whose header carries IP options before the TCP stack sees them, tested first on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not remove the path (CIQ, 2026-10-30).

CVE-2026-118539, Drupal Commerce Core: an access bypass in routes and entity fields is exploited against online stores, fixed in 3.3.13 and 8.x-2.41 (Drupal risk 21 of 25)

Drupal's advisory SA-CONTRIB-2026-254 of 2026-10-28 says Commerce Core "doesn't sufficiently protect certain routes and entity fields, leading to an access bypass that may financially impact the vendor" and that the flaw is being actively exploited in the wild (Drupal Security Team, 2026-10-28); The Hacker News carries the same wording (The Hacker News, 2026-10-30). The Drupal security team scores it 21 of 25, which SecurityWeek reads as exploitable without authentication whatever the module's configuration, and Drupal's statistics put the module on more than 42,000 sites (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30). The affected releases are Commerce Core 3.0.0 up to but not including 3.3.13 and earlier releases before 8.x-2.41 (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30). Drupal has not said how the bug is exploited, by whom, how many sites were targeted or whether it was exploited before the fix (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30); NCSC Switzerland's advisory of 2026-10-30 describes the impact as unauthenticated manipulation of order-related data with financial loss for the shop operator (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-30).

Exposure
Any Drupal site running Commerce Core below 3.3.13 on 3.x or below 8.x-2.41 on earlier releases, including shops built on the module's decoupled APIs rather than its own cart and checkout (The Hacker News, 2026-10-30); a public body that sells goods, permits or fees through such a site is in scope. The same day's batch holds 38 further Drupal advisories for 21 contributed projects, nearly a dozen rated critical, among them code execution, account takeover and Commerce orders marked as paid through Stripe without payment (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30).
Detection
Drupal's own guidance is an order audit for inconsistencies (SecurityWeek, 2026-10-30); checking each order's state, totals and payment status against the payment provider's records is the obvious test, an inference since no source names a method. The sources name no routes, parameters or request patterns; the web-server access log of the shop's API and checkout routes is the other record to review, an inference since nothing describes the requests.
Defender takeaway
Update Commerce Core to 3.3.13 or 8.x-2.41 now and audit orders; the flaw needs no login and the upgrade is the only mitigation the sources name. Check the other contributed modules the site runs against the advisories of 2026-10-28.

Apex Central and the Apex One on-premises server stay due on 2026-11-11, Deep Discovery Analyzer on 2026-11-12 and the Trend Micro Web Security cloud service on 2026-11-06, and Trend Micro still says it has seen no exploitation in its products (Trend Micro, 2026-10-30). Quest's knowledge-base article now also lists KACE SDA hotfix 9.3.313, published on 2026-10-29, which covers systems on hotfix versions 9.3.305-9.3.111 and on GA version 9.3.304 (Quest Software, 2026-10-29), and NetApp's advisory data adds ONTAP 9.19.1P4 to the fixed builds in revision 10.0 of 2026-10-29 (NetApp, 2026-10-29).

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, QNAP QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the NAS web components before authentication; fixed builds of 2026-10-23, and QVR Surveillance, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) now fixed

First published 2026-10-25 · open finding →

Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidenceactionsbody

QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 now lists Notes Station 3 as resolved by 3.9.15 (revision V1.2, 2026-10-28), while QNE (ADRA), moved to its own advisory QSA-26-19, still has no fixed version.

QNAP revised advisory QSA-26-18 to V1.2 on 2026-10-28 ("Notes Station 3 Resolved Published"), and its table now lists Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier as resolved by Notes Station 3 3.9.15 (QNAP, 2026-10-28). QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier is no longer in that table: it has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, released on 2026-10-22, whose status is Fixing and whose fixed version is still to be announced (QNAP, 2026-10-22). Both advisories still say QNAP has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products, and QSA-26-19 repeats that until fixed versions are available the most effective protection is to keep the device off the internet (QNAP, 2026-10-22).

CVE-2026-102764, BeyondTrust Remote Support: an unauthenticated file-operation flaw exploited as a zero-day since late August by a suspected China-nexus actor that left a web shell and boot-time sudo persistence (CVSS 4.0 9.3)

First published 2026-10-16 · open finding →

Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryimmediate_actionsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis of CVE-2026-102764 on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the unauthenticated file-write to code-execution chain; its successful request is an extensionless URL that rules matching only .php requests miss.

Rapid7 published a root-cause analysis on 2026-10-30 and says a Metasploit module now implements the chain, with PHP and Unix Command targets (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). An anonymous customer session, started through the public customer connection, sends a message whose source address carries a reserved local router ID; the appliance's customer worker accepts that address as proof that the request came from a local component, which exposes an internal file-transfer service with its native filesystem provider. Rapid7 used it to write a PHP file into the site's public directory and ran it as the site's operating-system user (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). The successful request was an extensionless URL, because the web server answers a direct .php request with 404 and maps an extensionless URL to the existing file, so detection that only searches for requests ending in .php would miss it; the appliance's thin-scc logs record file-transfer stream creation and rejected requests (Rapid7, 2026-10-30). Rapid7 tested Remote Support 24.1.2 and says other affected releases and fixed builds have not been established (Rapid7, 2026-10-30); BeyondTrust's advisory remains the reference for affected and fixed versions (BeyondTrust, 2026-10-15).

Sources: Google Threat Intelligence Group / Mandiant · BeyondTrust (advisory BT26-05) · BeyondTrust (blog) · Rapid7
HIGHCVE-2026-104935 +2exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-104935, Ivanti Connect Secure: an authentication bypass chained to code execution is exploited as a zero-day, the root-escalation step was patched on 2026-10-29 and CISA lists all three chain flaws (CVSS 8.6)

First published 2026-10-14 · open finding →

Update31 Oct 2026 03:37 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryimmediate_actioncvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Ivanti patched the root-escalation step of the exploited Connect Secure chain, CVE-2026-111357, on 2026-10-29, and CISA listed it and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, on 2026-10-30. The Canadian Cyber Centre and CISA now list builds 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5 as affected, so the builds of 2026-10-13 are no longer the target.

Volexity's report now carries an update banner saying Ivanti published a patch on 2026-10-29 for the privilege-escalation step, which is tracked as CVE-2026-111357 (Volexity, 2026-10-13). CISA added CVE-2026-111357 and a third chain flaw, CVE-2026-118527, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-30 (CISA, 2026-10-30). The catalog describes CVE-2026-118527 as a generation-of-predictable-numbers-or-identifiers flaw that lets a remote authenticated attacker upload files with attacker-controlled content to a known location on disk, and says it can be chained with CVE-2026-104935 and CVE-2026-111357 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-10-30). The Canadian Cyber Centre's bulletin on Ivanti's advisory, updated 2026-10-30, now lists the Connect Secure versions before 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.6 as affected (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-10-13), a range that takes in 25.1.1.2 and 22.8R2.5, the builds of 2026-10-13; CISA's alert, updated the same day, lists versions 25.1.1.2 and prior, 25.1.2.2 and prior and 22.8R2.5 and prior as affected by the three chain CVEs (CISA, 2026-10-13). Ivanti's advisory page could not be read, so which build carries which CVE's fix is not confirmed, and CVE-2026-118527 had no public CVE record, affected range or fixed build at that date.

Sources: Ivanti · Volexity · Rapid7 · CISA · Canadian Centre for Cyber Security · ANSSI / CERT-FR (CERTFR-2026-ALE-013) · GitHub Advisory Database · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2026-98816, Ivanti as numbering authority) · CISA KEV catalog · ANSSI / CERT-FR (CERTFR-2026-AVI-1442) · ENISA EUVD (EUVD-2026-115872, Ivanti as CNA)

04Action items14 items

  • Apply the BT26-05-RS patch to every self-hosted BeyondTrust Remote Support appliance now and confirm in the /appliance interface that it is installed (a build older than 24.3.1 must be upgraded first, which closes the hole but does not undo earlier exposure); apply it to self-hosted Privileged Remote Access appliances too, since BeyondTrust built and tested the patch for both products although its advisory names only Remote Support as impacted.
    FindingCVE-2026-102764→
  • For every appliance that was internet-reachable on a build up to 26.2.3 at any time since late August 2026: before any change, snapshot a virtual appliance with memory and export its disk, and collect the off-box syslog, reverse-proxy or WAF and perimeter firewall logs because the actor deletes on-appliance logs; then redeploy from a clean, fully patched image every appliance whose compromise status is confirmed or unknown, and rotate the credentials it held in dependency order, including the Remote Support Vault and any credential typed into a support session.
    FindingCVE-2026-102764→
  • Upgrade every Ivanti Connect Secure appliance to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 or 22.8R2.6 now, internet-facing appliances first: the Canadian Cyber Centre lists every earlier build as affected, so appliances that took only the 2026-10-13 builds 25.1.1.2 or 22.8R2.5 are still short of the root-step patch; 22.7.x and below are not affected.
    FindingCVE-2026-104935 +2→
  • Run a compromise check on every appliance that was reachable on an affected build, starting with proxy, load balancer or WAF logs back to at least 2026-10-03 for welcome.cgi requests that carry an X-DSCGI-PATH header; where compromise cannot be excluded, first cut the appliance off from the internet and the internal network and snapshot a virtual appliance's file system and memory without powering it down, then follow Ivanti's recovery steps and reset the domain service account, LAPS and local passwords, certificates, API keys, the Kerberos tickets of its service accounts and the licence-server authentication the appliance held, because CERT-FR knows of lateral movement using the LDAP and Active Directory secrets.
    FindingCVE-2026-104935 +2→
  • Upgrade every WS_FTP Server on Windows to 2024.0.7 or 2025.0.4 now, partner-facing and internet-reachable instances first, and rotate its administrator credentials afterwards, because CVE-2026-84295 can expose them to an unauthenticated attacker and the upgrade does not change what was already read; an instance on an unsupported branch gets no patch from Progress, so take it off the network or migrate it.
    FindingCVE-2026-84295 +6→
  • In every forest with an enterprise CA, list the AD CS Web Enrollment and Certificate Enrollment Web Service endpoints that lack HTTPS and Extended Protection for Authentication and the certificate templates that accept requester-supplied identity with broad enrollment rights, because both intrusions turned a Quick Assist session into a certificate for a privileged identity.
    FindingMicrosoft: Teams help-desk vishing into Quick…→
  • On every developer endpoint that runs Cursor, check extension-install telemetry for Anthropic.claude-code 2.1.312 or 2.1.313 installed between 09:27 and 20:35 UTC on 2026-10-29; where it is found, isolate the host, remove the unauthorized SSH key, the persistence and any running tunnel process, because uninstalling the extension removes none of them, and rotate every credential reachable from the host from a trusted system.
    FindingCursor marketplace served a trojanised Claude Code…→
  • Install Carbon Black App Control Server 8.12.2 or 8.13.2 (8.13.2 where the server already runs 8.13), confirm the SEPM fix build against Broadcom's login-gated advisory 39421 before treating 14.3.27716.10000 or 14.4.494.0000 as the target, and until each server is fixed limit the management console of every SEPM, App Control Server, CloudSOC SpanVA appliance and CASMA to administrator networks.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • On every internet-facing Linux server and every XenServer or XCP-ng host with its Workload Balancing and Conversion Manager appliances, install the vendor's fix and reboot as soon as it ships, then confirm the running version; Red Hat, Debian, CIQ, Amazon Linux, Ubuntu's generic kernels for 22.04 to 26.10, XCP-ng, MikroTik, Citrix and Sophos (Firewall hotfix HF110626.1, SD-RED firmware 3.0.012) updates are out, and XCP-ng says that a host which cannot reboot at once should take its iptables-based mitigation first and the update later; on Veeam appliances run Veeam Updater for kernel 5.14.0-570.60.1+27.2.el9_6_ciq, redeploy the virtual labs and Azure helper appliances that stay deployed and replace recovery media made before the update.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→
  • On hosts that cannot reboot yet, drop IPv4 TCP packets that carry IP options ahead of the TCP stack as CIQ, AWS and Vates describe, after testing on one non-production host because it also drops legitimate option-bearing traffic; disabling MPTCP alone does not close the path.
    FindingCVE-2026-98432→
  • Update Commerce Core on every Drupal site to 3.3.13 (3.x) or 8.x-2.41 (earlier releases) now, then audit orders back as far as your logs reach for inconsistencies, because Drupal says the flaw is exploited, names no other mitigation and does not say when exploitation began.
    FindingCVE-2026-118539→
  • Install Trend Micro's Apex Central Critical Patch build 7351 and Apex One Service Pack 1 Critical Patch build 20113 (both released 2026-11-11; the Apex One readme updates PHP to 8.2.35 without naming the flaw) on every server now and keep their consoles on administrator networks until done; for Mobile Security for Enterprise (patch due 2026-11-17, mitigation from Trend Micro support) and Deep Discovery Analyzer (due 2026-11-18) keep the interim mitigation until the patch ships; install the critical patches the table lists for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Install KACE SMA 15.0 CU5 or 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix 9.3.313 (9.3.312 where already installed), and until then block inbound ports 80, 443 and 52230 to every appliance, as Quest advises.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Update every QNAP NAS on QTS, QuTS hero or QuTScloud to the builds of 2026-10-23 (QTS 6.1.0.3656 or 5.2.11.3661, QuTS hero h6.1.0.3656, h6.0.2.3656 (h5.3.x included) or h5.2.11.3661, QuTScloud c5.2.9.3661), every QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) to 3.0.3.1756, every TVR OS to 1.0.5 and every Notes Station 3 to 3.9.15, and every QNE (ADRA) to 1.0.7.q327.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-31T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 6 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

A moderate window: six new entries and five changelog records. No deep dive and no critical entry: nothing new met the stop-and-act bar, and the one existing critical entry that moved (BeyondTrust CVE-2026-102764, where Rapid7 reports a Metasploit module on 2026-10-30) stays critical.

  • KEV sweep (work/2026-10-31T0256Z-intel/kev-window.txt): both additions of 2026-10-30 are Ivanti Connect Secure. CVE-2026-118527 (NOT COVERED) and CVE-2026-111357 (COVERED, but not yet cisa-kev or patch-available) are one update record on the covered chain entry, which also moves the fixed-build targets to 25.1.1.3, 25.1.3.1 and 22.8R2.6 on the Canadian Cyber Centre's affected-version lists. No COVERED-STALE and no RANSOMWARE row.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA row (Aurora leak-site claim) stays held. S2 and S4 re-searched in DE, FR, IT and EN and read the Swiss press feeds: ransomware.live still has no press field, and no statement from ARX, SBB, ASTRA/USTRA, BACS or Swiss press exists. Expiry 2026-11-07, struck then if unconfirmed.
  • Window: the previous intel run started 24 h earlier, so gap 24.0 h and window 26 h. The two earlier fires' attempts excluded 92 standard records from the slices; the breaches pool was small enough that S4 took its seven oldest-cursor records without the exclusion (bitdefender-threat-debrief, piyolog, ransom-isac, venarix, bleepingcomputer, cnil-fr, cyberinsider), so some were swept again.
  • Completeness follow-up: S1 dropped Progress WS_FTP Server and Veeam Management Pack on the strength of BSI's 'high' rating while CSIRT Italia counted 6 critical flaws including an authentication bypass, so one scoped follow-up (FU1, one continuation) read the vendor CNA records. WS_FTP clears PD-11(b) on its own mechanics: an unauthenticated network path to administrative credentials (CVSS 10.0) on a file-transfer server used with external partners, in a product whose 2023 flaw is in KEV with known ransomware use; no exploitation found, so it ships as notable with its fixed builds (2024.0.7, 2025.0.4). Progress's own bulletin is a script-rendered page no transport could read, so the entry's sourcing note says so.
  • borderline-drop: Veeam Management Pack for Microsoft System Center 9.x (KB 4961 of 2026-10-29), one unauthenticated RCE (CVE-2023-22793, CVSS 4.0 9.3, on servers running the Virtualization Extensions service) and two authenticated flaws; no exploitation, an internal management-plane add-in for System Center Operations Manager, and the fix is a move to 13.1.0.334 because 9.x gets no patch. Reopen on an exploitation report.
  • Source repairs from the health sweep: ec-digital-strategy-newsroom now reads through its RSS feed (general-news scope), sygnia joined the handled transport-blocked set, bfv-verfassungsschutz-de is checked through its feed recipe, and socprime is demoted on the content axis (its 20 newest feed items are product how-tos); ncsc-nl-php2shell-tracker and wordpress-org-news were promoted by the digest's promotion list; one new candidate, phorion.
  • Mid-run stop-hook nudges to commit were noted and ignored: the run commits atomically in Phase 6.
  • Spawn message error: the FU1 follow-up was told the time was about 04:40Z when it was about 03:55Z; its in-window anchor (2026-10-30T00:56Z) was stated explicitly and unaffected.
  • Single-source: Teams-to-AD CS (Microsoft Threat Intelligence is first-hand on both intrusions), Broadcom endpoint-security servers (Broadcom is the disclosing party; the SEPM fix builds rest on NCSC-NL's tracker and are marked unverified), and the Cisco, Trend Micro and QNAP revisions (vendor advisories for their own products). Each carries the matching sourcing_note.
  • Reduced confidence: Linux kernel CVE-2026-98432 carries confidence: medium because severity ratings disagree (9.8, 8.1, Critical for RHEL, 5.9 as BleepingComputer reported) and the exploit claim is Anthropic's alone; Broadcom SEPM fix builds as above. The drupal.org advisory answers a client challenge to extract, so its wording was read with WebFetch and the two quotes cited from it are not machine-checkable.
  • Dates: the Phorion post is dated 2026-10-30 with a 2026-10-31 update widening the version guidance from 2.1.313 to 2.1.312 and 2.1.313; Cursor's notice, Microsoft's analysis and Sophos agree. Broadcom's knowledge article 459982 shows a placeholder date (2026-01-01) in the extracted text; its structured data gives the publication date 2026-10-22, which the entry cites.
  • Contradiction: the Cursor extension entry. NCSC Switzerland's post 13121 places the backdoored extension on Open VSX and says Anthropic pulled npm and VS Code versions of 2.1.313; Microsoft says the packages were never published to the Visual Studio Marketplace or npm, and Cursor and Phorion name the Cursor marketplace only. The entry follows Microsoft, Cursor and Phorion and states the difference in its Exposure paragraph and sourcing note.
  • Contradiction held, not resolved: the Berlin Landesnetz entry records BSI's own confirmation that TerminalFix was the vector, while rbb24 writes that BSI did not confirm that pattern to it; no record was written (see the borderline-drop for that item).
  • borderline-drop: Pentagon commissary freezer failures (update-of the Danfoss refrigeration entry); attribution rests on two anonymous-source reports (Reuters via four officials, Nextgov via two people), no vector is stated, the lesson of the entry is unchanged, and the entry's analysis (1,291 words) is already far past the length bound, so a rewrite would be needed to carry it.
  • borderline-drop: Request Tracker 6.0.4 and 5.0.11, RTIR (30 CVEs), stored XSS from unauthenticated email and an authenticated code-execution bypass, no exploitation, and no source shows Swiss public-sector use; patch-cycle.
  • borderline-drop: Dell PowerProtect Data Domain DSA-2026-416, first published 2026-10-01 and last revised 2026-10-19, only NCSC-NL's relay of 2026-10-30 falls in the window; internal-facing backup appliance, no exploitation reported.
  • borderline-drop: Canonical LXD CVE-2026-112816 (CVSS 4.0 10.0, mTLS validation), niche stack, no exploitation, fixed 2026-10-29; patch-cycle.
  • borderline-drop: Siemens SSA-166980 revision 1.2; the revision predates the window and the energy products named have mostly no fix by design of the wave; the PHP2Shell OT entry already carries Siemens.
  • borderline-drop: GitLab 19.5.3 and the other 2026-10-29 patch releases removing the eight eMudhra intermediates (CVE-2026-111943), patch-cycle, no exploitation; the eMudhra entry's action already covers updating CA bundles and Go.
  • borderline-drop: Linux kernel PwnEscape CVE-2026-99999 (S1 bundled it with CVE-2026-98432), guest-to-host flaw, fixed since 2026-10-15, local vector; the expectation of exploits within weeks is the discoverer's, not an observation. It would be a separate entry if exploitation or a hypervisor exposure statement appears.
  • borderline-drop: Android 'SMS of Death' CVE-2026-58882, zero-click DoS on telephony, public PoC, fixed in the October bulletin; patch-cycle, status rests on heise alone.
  • borderline-drop: ReliaQuest victim-matched residential proxies in vishing-led SaaS intrusions, single vendor, the vishing pattern is covered by the Talos IR, Huntress and new Microsoft entries.
  • borderline-drop: TeamViewer TV-2026-1011 (CVE-2026-111585, viewer-side code execution), no exploitation, bulletin of 2026-10-28 outside the window; patch-cycle.
  • borderline-drop: CrowdStrike 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report (annual-report candidate), legal sector outside the constituency, report gated; the transferable content (IT-impersonation vishing into remote tools) is covered.
  • borderline-drop: Binance (about USD 6.36 billion, largest crypto theft on record; S3 and S4 returned it), clears breach limb (a) on scale only; no Swiss public-sector nexus, the stated vector (a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop) is covered ground, so an entry would be awareness only. Reopen if a post-mortem names a transferable technique.
  • borderline-drop: Berlin Landesnetz detection gap (rbb24, attack-detection licences covering 5 percent of devices); the rbb24 primary is 10 days old and only a blog relay is in the window; an organisational lesson that changes no detection decision.
  • borderline-drop: RMS Cloud and feratel Deskline booking-platform breaches, no Swiss customer named at either vendor; same WhatsApp booking-fraud pattern as the covered Camping.Care entry.
  • borderline-drop: SIHF and Swiss Basketball member-portal incidents, private associations; the 2026-10-30 fire dropped SIHF for the same reason, and the basketball claim rests on FrenchBreaches alone.
  • borderline-drop: Fehmarnbelt contractor FLC, Leipzig University and Charité, Ruag MRO law-firm investigation, FortiBleed 2.0 (Hudson Rock), no Swiss entity or no vector or actor (incident floor), the Ruag item is insider fraud without an intrusion, and the FortiBleed data is dated February with no new vector.
  • borderline-drop: S2's policy and enforcement candidates (Federal Council e-evidence transitional rule, DVS Microsoft 365 exit study, BACS WhatsApp fake-vote update, Qilin arrest, INTERPOL Serengeti III); no change to what the constituency's defenders are obliged or advised to do, or outside the window. Canton Bern's ICSG enters into force 2026-11-01 and is already in the store.
  • S3 left three out-of-window leads for the audit to weigh, none fetched as a primary: Microsoft Authenticator CVE-2026-80097 (2026-10-28), EDK II PXE flaw CVE-2026-97631 (seen only in a search summary), and the 2026-10-29 research posts from Talos (NIK C2), Securelist (NetamLoader) and Group-IB (MadApe).
  • Coverage gaps: ivanti advisory hub (login shell on every transport; per-CVE fixed builds unconfirmed); connectwise-trust-center (403, WebSearch only); ox-security (article bodies 403); resecurity, onapsis, openjdk-vulnerability-advisories, zimbra-security-advisories (listings unreadable or empty); broadcom advisories 39411 and 39421 (login-gated). Recipe findings are recorded in the sources_changed notes: schneier, blick-ch, qnap, synology, siemens, the NCSC-NL tracker change log.
  • Verification: iteration 3 returned NEEDS_FIXES with 2 truth and 0 editorial findings (none F1 or F4) on full coverage (238 of 238 claims); all five of its findings were fixed in the entries and the run published on the low-residual early exit without a fourth pass, so the two truth fixes are unconfirmed by a later cold read (residual count 2).

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-30
item.description:
• CISA lists WordPress core's upgrade-window RCE race as exploited; block wp-content/upgrade before installing 7.1.4. WordPress 7.1.4 of 2026-10-28 fixes a weakness in the core upgrade process that lets an unauthenticated attacker reach the staged installer and run code on the server during a full-package core update, in versions 4.7 to 7.1.3, with backports for every branch down to 4.7. CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03; Wordfence reports more than 18,500 probing requests in the first 21 hours, while Patchstack calls the race hard to win and says it needs a web-reachable staging directory. The discoverer says the update that installs the fix still unpacks with the old code, so the staging directory must be blocked before updating. →
  • Cisco ASA and FTD SSL VPN reload flaw is exploited and on CISA KEV; fixes in every branch, no workaround. Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 fixes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD that lets an unauthenticated attacker reload the device with a crafted connection request when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication, and says Cisco's PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026; CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29. Cisco names no actor, offers no workaround and lists first fixed releases for every ASA and FTD branch. →
  • Lumen: Volt Typhoon's Silent Train relay chains fronted zero-days against SD-WAN, N-central and KACE. Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon ran exploitation, credential access and exfiltration through Silent Train, rotating chains of compromised SOHO, IoT and enterprise devices that it rebuilt for each operation, and that its monitoring uncovered one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators, among them Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, N-able N-central and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator. The reported victims are US-centred and the report names no Swiss or European victim. →

VAPOR PANDA: CrowdStrike reports a China-nexus actor running the ARTEX agent framework against more than 200 organisations from 17 October, among them foreign ministries in Europe and a Greek government entity, and deploying the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor

CrowdStrike OverWatch reports that from 2026-10-17 a single ARTEX controller linked to VAPOR PANDA infrastructure directed exploitation against entities in at least 14 countries over 11 days, and that the campaign reached more than 200 organisations, including foreign ministries in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). One engagement focused on a single European country, its foreign ministry, presidency, prime minister's office and defence, justice, finance and intelligence entities, and another targeted 19 US organisations in pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, defence, nuclear and finance (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike confirmed post-exploitation at nine organisations and password spraying and credential scanning against at least 12 more, among them government entities in Europe (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). CrowdStrike states that the campaign is separate from the Storm-0940 ARTEX activity Microsoft reported and is VAPOR PANDA's first observed use of AI-driven tooling (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

The framework ran mainly on the DeepSeek model, with a human operator steering the agents at decision points while they pursued web, cloud, container, Active Directory, mail and VPN paths in parallel (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). In transcripts at a US pharmaceutical company the agent chained an unsigned SAML assertion with an XML external entity flaw to query the cloud instance metadata service and obtain a role that could issue administration commands to thousands of instances; at a second it deployed web shells, abused an unauthenticated orchestration service for root in a container environment, read LAPS passwords and abused resource-based constrained delegation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). Against a Greek government entity the operator supplied a 2022 directory export from the mail server whose authentication keys had likely not been rotated; the agent forged an administrator token, read mailboxes and used VPN configurations from a user's sent mail, with a VPN client key the operator described as coming from a May 2024 email leak, to reach the internal network (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). The operator also told the agents to find domain Windows hosts without the CrowdStrike Falcon sensor (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). At a Middle East interior ministry and a Latin American foreign ministry the actor loaded the BLOODALCHEMY backdoor through a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe that loads a malicious DLL (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29). No Swiss target is named.

Exposure
Government, mail, identity and VPN estates where a directory export or backup holding authentication keys has never been rotated, SAML service providers that accept unsigned assertions, and cloud instances that still allow instance metadata service version 1; CrowdStrike names foreign ministries and government entities in Europe among the targets (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Detection
Telemetry classes are authentication logs (password spraying and credential scanning against many accounts, an administrator token minted outside the identity provider, VPN logins that use a configuration or key from an old mailbox or leak), cloud control-plane audit (administration commands issued to many instances through the cloud systems manager, instance metadata queries from an application), process lineage (a legitimate GameHook binary renamed svchost.exe loading a malicious DLL) and endpoint inventory queries for hosts without the security agent; CrowdStrike lists ARTEX-named command-line parameters, cloud roles and a directory under ProgramData as hunt markers (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).
Defender takeaway
Rotate keys held in old directory exports and backups, require signed SAML assertions and IMDSv2, and hunt authentication and cloud audit logs for the parallel, many-target pattern an operator-steered agent produces; CrowdStrike expects China-nexus actors to keep adopting agent frameworks (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-29).

Silent Train: Lumen's Black Lotus Labs describes the rotating relay network Volt Typhoon used for one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against management and control-plane platforms (Quest KACE, Versa Director, N-able N-central, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN, Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator)

Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reports that Volt Typhoon used a covert framework it calls Silent Train, first seen in late 2023, for the phases that need protection: exploitation, credential access, data exfiltration and continued access to victims (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). A session starts from a virtual private server outside the US, passes through compromised non-US SOHO and IoT devices and leaves through a compromised US device before the victim; more than 27 device classes were enrolled, from TP-Link routers and Netgear Orbi devices to Fortinet appliances and CyberPanel servers, and the enterprise platforms stayed in chains for one to three months as final hops (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The operators exploit exposed web interfaces on the relay devices and deploy only what chained SSH needs, namely temporary SSH services, keys, configuration files and living-off-the-land utilities, with reverse tunnels over open-source proxies in later variants; sessions averaged about four hours, and at the end the operators removed all artifacts and dismantled the chain (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).

Lumen says its monitoring helped identify one likely and four confirmed zero-day campaigns against endpoint and network management platforms and SD-WAN orchestrators: Quest KACE, where the activity looked like an undisclosed flaw, affected more than 30 victims and fell after Quest's October 2025 updates (a moderate-confidence assessment); Versa Director in 2024; the N-able N-central flaws CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876; Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN through CVE-2026-20127, exploited by late 2025 and after Cisco's February 2026 disclosure; and Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator through the zero-day later designated CVE-2026-16812 (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). Post-incident analysis found in-memory webshells, credential harvesting and abuse of native platform features such as endpoint control and remote file transfers, and in several cases erased or altered logs (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The victims it names are US government, telecommunications, defence-industrial, managed-service and critical-infrastructure organisations, concentrated in Hawaii, California and Texas, and it names no European or Swiss victim (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28). The Hacker News carries the same findings from a report Lumen shared with it (The Hacker News, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Internet-reachable management and control-plane platforms (endpoint management, SD-WAN controllers and orchestrators, out-of-band administration), and edge devices with exposed web interfaces, which can be enrolled as relay hops without any data of the owner being the target.
Detection
Telemetry classes are administrative logins, API calls, remote file transfers and configuration changes on management platforms outside normal administration hours or workflow, in-memory web shells that leave no file on disk, and, on edge devices, temporary SSH services, unfamiliar keys and outbound reverse tunnels to unfamiliar upstream hosts (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28).
Defender takeaway
Restrict the administrative interfaces of management and control-plane platforms to a VPN, jump host or management network and prioritise their patching, as Lumen advises, and treat an edge device that shows temporary SSH services or reverse tunnels as a possible relay in someone else's intrusion chain.

HIGHCVE-2026-119977exploitedupdatedNATOA2

WordPress core 4.7 to 7.1.3: an unauthenticated race in the core update process can lead to remote code execution, fixed in 7.1.4 and backported to every supported branch, listed by CISA as exploited; Wordfence assigned CVE-2026-119977

WordPress 7.1.4, released on 2026-10-28, fixes a weakness in the upgrade process that can lead to remote code execution during the upgrade window, and backports follow for every branch that receives security fixes, currently through 4.7 (WordPress.org, 2026-10-28). During a core update with a complete package, the new files are unpacked into a predictable directory under wp-content/upgrade; the temporary copy includes the installer, and an unauthenticated attacker who requests it at the right moment can interact with the staged copy and reach PHP code execution (Wordfence, 2026-10-29). Wordfence scores it CVSS 8.1 for versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 and states that the attack complexity is high, because the attacker needs web access to the staging tree and must win a race that lasted only seconds in its lab (Wordfence, 2026-10-29). Patchstack reads the same flaw as needing wp-content/upgrade/ to be reachable over the web and would not call it practical to exploit (Patchstack, 2026-10-28).

Wordfence reports that its new firewall rule matched within nine minutes of deployment and that it recorded more than 18,500 requests for staged setup-config.php installer paths in the first 21 hours (Wordfence, 2026-10-29). CISA lists the flaw as exploited, and no source names a victim or describes a successful compromise (CISA, 2026-11-03). The fix randomises the staging directory, adds an index guard and prevents unsafe promotion of staged configuration data (Wordfence, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Any WordPress site on 4.7 to 7.1.3 with wp-content/upgrade/ reachable from the internet while a core update runs; the discoverer says the deciding factor is whether the updater already installed on the site has been fixed, so the update to 7.1.4 is exposed too, automatic updates included, although a partial package exposes the installer only if it contains the installer files (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06); on 5.9 or later the staging folder name can be predicted, on 4.4 to 5.8 a random suffix hides it unless the site leaks it, and 4.6 and earlier, which Picus counts as affected back to 2.7, get no fix (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). The fixed releases are 7.1.4 and the backport of each branch (7.0.8, 6.9.11 and so on down to 4.7.39) (Wordfence, 2026-10-29).
Detection
In web server access logs, requests under wp-content/upgrade/ and for setup-config.php inside a staging directory, repeated from one source against a few sites as Wordfence saw (Wordfence, 2026-10-29); between updates the directory holds only an index.php (Patchstack, 2026-10-28). Where an unpatched site updated with the directory reachable, check that wp-config.php, which the attack overwrites, still names your database (Picus Security, 2026-11-05) and look for administrator accounts, plugins and PHP files under wp-content/upgrade/ that nobody created (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06).

Triage: a request to a staging path outside an update window finds only an index.php and is probing, not compromise; a successful response from the staged installer during an update is the event that matters.

Defender takeaway
Deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ at the web server and confirm it answers 403 before the update runs, then confirm that the update completed on every site instead of assuming it, because a firewall that WordPress itself loads cannot block the request: the staged copy loads from its own files (Patchstack, 2026-10-28); Wordfence's blocking rule helps only where its firewall is set up to run before direct PHP requests reach their file (Wordfence, 2026-10-29).
Correction01 Nov 2026 13:52 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditbodycvessourcessourcing_notesummarytitle

The flaw now has an identifier: Wordfence tracks it as CVE-2026-119977, a time-of-check time-of-use race condition scored CVSS 3.1 8.1 (AV:N/AC:H/PR:N), affecting WordPress 4.7.0 to 7.1.3 with the same fixed releases as above (Wordfence Intelligence, 2026-10-31). The statement that no source assigns a CVE identifier is withdrawn; scanners and asset inventories can now match the flaw by that ID.

Update04 Nov 2026 03:25 UTCrun 2026-11-04T0256Z-intelcvesprioritytagsheadlinesummarytitlesourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

CISA added CVE-2026-119977 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-11-03 on evidence of active exploitation (CISA, 2026-11-03), and the Canadian Cyber Centre's advisory of the same day relays the listing for WordPress Core before 7.1.4 (Canadian Centre for Cyber Security, 2026-11-03). The listing names no victim, attacker behaviour or exploitation method, so Wordfence's probing telemetry above remains the only described activity and Patchstack's high-complexity rating still stands. A site that ran a full-package core update on 4.7 to 7.1.3 while wp-content/upgrade/ was reachable needs the compromise check in the Detection line, not only the update.

Update07 Nov 2026 03:51 UTCrun 2026-11-07T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryactionssourcesevidencesourcing_notebody

Umut Bayram of Picus Security, who found the flaw, shows that the update which installs the fix still unpacks its files with the site's old, unpatched code (Picus Security, 2026-11-05; The Hacker News, 2026-11-06). Picus says the new code's skip of wp-config.php already works in that first update but the randomised folder name does not, so the temporary installer sits at a predictable path on sites running 5.9 or later and, on 4.4 to 5.8, behind a random suffix that hides it unless the site leaks the path; an attacker who reaches it can no longer replace the live configuration but can still set up the temporary copy, log in to it, run PHP and from there read or write files in the live directory (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). Bayram told The Hacker News the deciding factor "isn’t partial versus complete. It’s whether the updater already installed on the site has been fixed", and that a partial package exposes the installer only if it contains the installer files; The Hacker News found WordPress.org offering an in-branch move such as 7.1.3 to 7.1.4 as a partial package, automatic updates included, so whether such an update is exposed depends on what that package contains, and only once 7.1.4 or the branch fix is installed do later updates use a random folder (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06). WordPress 4.6 and earlier get no fix (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06).

The order matters: Picus advises denying web access to wp-content/upgrade/ in the web server configuration first, confirming that the path answers 403, and only then updating; this does not break updates, because WordPress reaches the folder through the filesystem (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). An .htaccess file placed inside the folder does not work, because the old updater deletes the folder's contents before unpacking, and WP-CLI's wp core update is no substitute because it uses the same updater and folder (Picus Security, 2026-11-05). For sites that stayed on an affected version, Wordfence suggests looking for unexpected requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade, administrator accounts no one recognises, plugins no one installed and PHP files in wp-content/upgrade that no one put there (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06).

Code that its authors describe as an exploit has appeared in public GitHub repositories since earlier this week, and whether it works has not been established; WordPress's own advisory rates the flaw low, against Wordfence's CVSS 8.1 and CISA's listing as exploited (The Hacker News, 2026-11-06). None of these sources reports a compromise through the update that installs the fix; CISA's listing and Wordfence's probing telemetry above are unchanged.

Improvement08 Nov 2026 14:08 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditbody

The configuration check in the Detection line follows from the mechanism Picus describes: an attacker creates a malicious wp-config.php inside the temporary update directory and has the updater copy it over the live configuration, which can redirect the site to an attacker-controlled empty database (Picus Security, 2026-11-05).

HIGHCVE-2026-76418exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-76418, Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD: a crafted request to the remote access SSL VPN reloads the device when a tunnel group uses secondary authentication; Cisco reports active exploitation and CISA lists it (CVSS 3.1 8.6)

Cisco's advisory of 2026-10-28 describes CVE-2026-76418, a logic error in the remote access SSL VPN service of Secure Firewall ASA and Secure FTD: an unauthenticated, remote attacker who sends a crafted request while connecting to the SSL VPN makes the device reload, and a successful VPN login is not required to reach the affected processing path (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Cisco says its PSIRT became aware of active exploitation in October 2026 and names no actor or victim (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-29 (CISA, 2026-10-29), and CERT-FR restates the advisory (ANSSI / CERT-FR, 2026-10-29). The stated impact is a reload and denial of service, scored CVSS 3.1 8.6 with availability as the only impact; no code execution or data access is described (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).

The first fixed releases are ASA 9.16.4.104 (for 9.16 and earlier), 9.18.4.96, 9.20.4.50, 9.22.3.200, 9.23.1.48, 9.24.1.27 and 9.24.10.1, and FTD 7.0.11 (for 7.0 and earlier), 7.2.13, 7.4.9, 7.6.7, 7.7.14, 10.0.3 and 10.1.1 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Cisco lists no workaround; its mitigation is to remove secondary authentication from the tunnel group, which lowers the security posture of the remote access VPN, or, where DefaultWEBVPNGroup does not use secondary authentication, to disable the tunnel group list with no tunnel-group-list enable (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Cisco confirms that Secure FMC, Cloud-delivered Firewall, cdFMC and Secure Access are not affected (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
An ASA or FTD unit below the first fixed release of its branch whose running configuration has webvpn enabled on an interface and secondary-authentication-server-group on any tunnel group; the default tunnel group DefaultWEBVPNGroup counts even when the tunnel group list is disabled. On FTD, read the deployed remote access VPN policy and the resulting configuration in FMC or FDM (Devices > VPN > Remote Access) (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).
Detection
Neither Cisco nor CISA publishes an indicator. The mechanism points at device availability telemetry: unexpected reloads, HA failover flaps, uptime resets and crash files on units that terminate the remote access VPN, read against VPN authentication logs for connection attempts from external addresses that never complete a login.

Triage: a reload also follows upgrades, HA events and hardware faults; a reload that coincides with unauthenticated SSL VPN connection attempts from an external address is the pattern the stated mechanism produces.

Defender takeaway
Upgrade the units that terminate remote access SSL VPN with secondary authentication this week, perimeter units first; Cisco states denial of service as the only impact, so patching leaves no further step, and removing secondary authentication as a stop-gap trades an outage risk for a weaker VPN login.

ROUTINENATOA2

privatim revises its cloud guidance for Swiss public bodies (Merkblatt v3.02, 2 October 2026): sensitive data stays under the body's own keys, SaaS from Microsoft, Google, AWS and SAP is in most cases inadmissible for secrecy-bound data, and top management signs the residual risk

privatim, the conference of the Swiss data-protection authorities, dates version 3.02 of its guidance "Cloud-specific risks and measures" to 2 October 2026 (privatim, 2026-10-02); it replaces the version of 3 February 2022 (DCOD, 2026-10-27). For particularly sensitive personal data the public body must encrypt, the keys may be available only to it, and outsourcing such data, or data under a statutory duty of confidentiality, to SaaS from large international providers, with Microsoft, Google, AWS and SAP named, is in most cases inadmissible because of the untenable risk (privatim, 2026-10-02). Keys may stay with the provider only where no untenable risk follows and the provider is bound by contract to use them only with the body's express consent and to log every access (privatim, 2026-10-02).

The body, or its top management, is to confirm in writing that it has understood the risks and accepts the residual risk, and data the cloud services generate about their users, such as telemetry and logging data, is to be treated with the same care and contract terms as the content data (privatim, 2026-10-02). The five risk areas are contract design, places of processing including foreign authority access, confidentiality with encryption and key management, user data, and sub-processors (privatim, 2026-10-02).

Defender takeaway
The guidance addresses public bodies subject to Swiss data-protection law; a body that runs or plans SaaS from the named providers for sensitive or secrecy-bound data is advised to keep its own encryption keys, to have top management sign the residual risk, and to hold provider telemetry and logs about its users to the same contract terms.

ROUTINENATOB2

ANNUAL REPORT: Cisco Talos Incident Response trends Q3 2026: public administration tied with finance as the most targeted sector, help-desk vishing into remote-management tools, and ransomware operators uninstalling and killing EDR

Cisco Talos Incident Response reports that in Q3 2026 financial organisations made up 18 percent of its engagements, tying with public administration as the most targeted sector (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Phishing was the leading initial-access technique at 37 percent of engagements and exploitation of public-facing applications second at 33 percent; the phishing cases include numerous actors who phone the victim as the IT help desk to get remote access allowed through a legitimate remote monitoring and management (RMM) tool (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Ransomware and pre-ransomware cases were 27 percent of engagements, with The Gentlemen, Qilin, Rhysida and the closed group Interlock among the families and a new variant, VYPR, that Talos calls operationally immature: it had no leak site when seen, reused leaked Conti-derived source code and exfiltrated over several days (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

The VYPR intrusion began with a vishing call that had the user start a Microsoft Quick Assist session; the actor then used RMM software that ran PowerShell to download and install an MSI from a remote address, with MeshAgent, Rclone, PsExec, an IP scanner and mstsc as tools, and disabled EDR with several vulnerable drivers (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Interlock operators repeatedly tried to uninstall Cisco Secure Endpoint, used PsExec and taskkill to end security services and integrity checkers, turned off Windows Defender real-time protection and cleared event logs (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29). Talos names insufficient logging (over 40 percent of engagements), weak credential and secret handling, and absent or incomplete MFA as the most common weaknesses, and recommends centralised logging with at least 90 days of retention (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
An organisation whose help desk or staff can be reached by phone and whose endpoints permit Quick Assist or an unapproved RMM agent; Talos names public administration among the most targeted sectors in its caseload.
Detection
In process-creation and software-install telemetry, an RMM or Quick Assist session started after an inbound call, followed by PowerShell run under the RMM agent that downloads an installer from an external address; in endpoint and service-control telemetry, attempts to uninstall the EDR agent, PsExec or taskkill ending security services, Defender real-time protection switched off, vulnerable kernel drivers loaded, and event logs cleared.
Defender takeaway
Treat a remote-support session that nobody at the help desk started as the vishing signal and inventory which RMM tools and Quick Assist are permitted on endpoints; alert on EDR uninstall and security-service termination as a ransomware precursor; and centralise logs with the 90-day minimum retention Talos recommends, because actors delete logs on the endpoint.

GitLab's release page now says its security team has released six threat detections for self-managed instances (GitLab, 2026-10-12). GitLab's release of 2026-10-21 (19.5.1, 19.4.3, 19.3.6, 19.2.9) also fixes a second CVSS 10 regular-expression compiler flaw, CVE-2026-110264, so those builds are the better upgrade target (GitLab, 2026-10-21). Verification & coverage notes

A moderate window: six new entries and six changelog records. No deep dive and no critical entry: nothing met the stop-and-act bar, and the one candidate for a priority raise (GitLab CVE-2026-97229, now on CISA KEV) stays high: exploitation is reported by one observer (Alpine Linux, attempts against its own instance on 2026-10-20 to 26 with no confirmed code execution; CISA lists it and NCSC Switzerland restates the report), and the demonstrated path needs an account that can push to a public project. item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-29
item.description:
• Check Point gateways exploited (PHP2Shell, root escalation): Jumbo R81.20 t174, R82 t132, R82.10 t52, R82.20 t14. Check Point Research reports that from 2026-10-30 an attacker exploited unpatched Check Point gateways through the Mobile Access portal with PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619), escalated to root with CVE-2026-123039 (CVSS 7.8, a local flaw in the dynamic_server process that Check Point says was exploited against a couple of dozen customers), installed a persistent backdoor and in the first wave deleted files on a VMware ESXi host. The fix for both is in Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator R81.20 take 174, R82 take 132, R82.10 take 52 and R82.20 take 14 or later, with none listed for R81.10 or R81, and the standalone PHP hotfix is not stated to cover CVE-2026-123039; sk1000302 itself carries no statement on exploitation. →
  • Talos: UAT-11473 implants KeyDrift in Cisco SD-WAN controllers through CVE-2026-20127 to collect data-plane keys. Cisco Talos reports that a cluster it calls UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, the peering authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator (CVSS 10.0, fixed releases since February 2026, no workaround), and then ran the KeyDrift implant inside the controller's control-plane process to collect session metadata and what Talos assesses to be data-plane IPsec keys. Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says it is aware of limited exploitation, and Talos assesses with high confidence that the operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network. →
  • PHP2Shell: Trend Micro Apex Central and Apex One patched; Analyzer due 18 Nov; Quest KACE, NetApp ONTAP fixed. Trend Micro posted Critical Patch build 7351 for Apex Central and build 20113 for Apex One Service Pack 1 on 2026-11-11, each upgrading PHP to 8.2.35 (the Apex One readme does not name the flaw), and its advisory, updated 2026-11-12, now names both patches and lists Mobile Security for Enterprise (due on 2026-11-17) and Deep Discovery Analyzer (due on 2026-11-18) as impacted, with critical patches for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector; Quest says all KACE SMA and SDA versions are affected, with SMA 15.0 CU5 and 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix out and advice to block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until applied; and NetApp's advisory lists ONTAP 9 as affected only by CVE-2026-109618, with attacker access as the www user restricted to the PHP jail and hotfix builds from 9.12.1P20HF1 to 9.19.1P4. NetApp says it is aware of public discussion of the vulnerability and none of the three vendors reports an exploited case on its page, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited. →

Trend Micro posted Critical Patch build 7351 for Apex Central and build 20113 for Apex One Service Pack 1 on 2026-11-11, each upgrading PHP to 8.2.35 (the Apex One readme does not name the flaw), and its advisory, updated 2026-11-12, now names both patches and lists Mobile Security for Enterprise (due on 2026-11-17) and Deep Discovery Analyzer (due on 2026-11-18) as impacted, with critical patches for Deep Discovery Inspector and Email Inspector; Quest says all KACE SMA and SDA versions are affected, with SMA 15.0 CU5 and 15.1 CU2 and the SDA 9.3 hotfix out and advice to block ports 80, 443 and 52230 until applied; and NetApp's advisory lists ONTAP 9 as affected only by CVE-2026-109618, with attacker access as the www user restricted to the PHP jail and hotfix builds from 9.12.1P20HF1 to 9.19.1P4. NetApp says it is aware of public discussion of the vulnerability and none of the three vendors reports an exploited case on its page, although CISA lists both flaws as exploited. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 6Trending vulnerabilities 5Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 29

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures6 items

NOTABLECVE-2025-8088exploitedNATOB2

MDaemon mail server below 26.0.4 and Windows ClamAV 0.101.0 to 1.5.3: a crafted RAR emailed to any address runs code on the server through the bundled UnRAR flaw CVE-2025-8088, and ESET saw Russia-aligned attackers use it in Ukraine to deploy the HELLAGE and HELLTAG backdoors

ESET reports an active campaign in Ukraine in which Russia-aligned attackers exploited MDaemon mail servers and deployed two backdoor families, HELLAGE and HELLTAG (ESET Research, 2026-10-28). MDaemon uses ClamAV to scan attachments of incoming mail; old ClamAV versions carry CVE-2025-8088, the WinRAR path-traversal flaw ESET uncovered last year, which ESET says was fixed in ClamAV's source on 27 July 2025 (the release notes below date the fixed ClamAV builds 2026-08-07), while MDaemon kept shipping an old libclamunrar.dll until MDaemon 26.0.4 of 2026-08-25 (ESET Research, 2026-10-28). The chain ESET describes: a crafted RAR archive is mailed to any address at a vulnerable server, MDaemon invokes ClamAV to scan it, and the exploit writes a malicious DLL to the server's file system with no user interaction, so the message carries no lure (ESET Research, 2026-10-28). CERT-UA names the backdoors: HELLAGE steals email messages and other data, talks to a hardcoded server and can deploy more malware, and HELLTAG takes commands, transfers files and does reconnaissance through a hardcoded Telegram bot; ESET cannot attribute the campaign to a known Russia-aligned actor (ESET Research, 2026-10-28).

The exposure is wider than MDaemon. ClamAV's release notes of 2026-08-07 say it adopted the upstream UnRAR fix for CVE-2025-8088, which rejects path separators in NTFS alternate data stream names so that extraction cannot leave ClamAV's temporary scan directory on Windows, and that the issue affects ClamAV 0.101.0 through 1.5.3 with the fix in 1.4.6 and 1.5.4 (ClamAV, 2026-08-07). CISA has listed CVE-2025-8088 in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog since 2025-08-12 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
An MDaemon server on Windows below 26.0.4 that accepts inbound mail (ESET Research, 2026-10-28), and any other Windows host that scans mail or files with ClamAV 0.101.0 to 1.5.3 (ClamAV, 2026-08-07).
Detection
Because the attack needs no lure, the mail log shows an ordinary message with a RAR attachment. The telemetry that matters is file creation of a DLL by the ClamAV or mail-service scanning process outside ClamAV's temporary scan directory, inbound RAR attachments whose member names carry alternate-data-stream syntax with path separators, and the mail service process starting unexpected children or connecting to Telegram's bot interface; these follow from the described chain and are not an ESET detection list. An update does not remove a DLL or backdoor that was already written, so check the server after patching.
Defender takeaway
Patch the mail scanning path first on any internet-facing Windows mail server, then look for unexpected DLLs and persistence and treat stored mail as exposed, since HELLAGE steals email (ESET Research, 2026-10-28).

NOTABLENATOA2

Moldova's government digital services: attackers used flaws in services reachable without authentication to query about one million national identification numbers and extract data on about 750,000 of them between 19 and 23 October, and the Prime Minister says AI allegedly helped find the flaws

Moldova's Electronic Governance Agency (AGE) reported on 2026-10-27 that between 19 and 23 October attackers queried about one million national identification numbers (IDNPs) through state digital services and that, on preliminary estimates, data sets for about 750,000 of them were extracted; MOLDPRES had put the access requests at about 11 million on 2026-10-24 (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-24). AGE's technical explanation is that the attackers exploited vulnerabilities in services reachable without authentication and then used the data they obtained for further extractions; the first attacks hit an electronic service that logged the legal basis of processing incorrectly, which is why citizens saw entries for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue in the data-access history of the EVO app (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). Data that may be affected, not every category for every person, includes name, date and place of birth, first-degree relatives, insured status, family doctor, social benefits, pensions, disability, driving licence, photograph, vehicles and companies owned or run, IBAN, tax debts and payment history; AGE says card data is not held on the platform and it found no unauthorised change to state registers (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).

AGE stopped the extraction on 23 October at 11:30, reviewed 82 digital services and suspended the exposed ones, and its timeline says 82 public services and more than 30 information systems and administration panels were disconnected as a precaution on 23 October; it blocked further attempts on 25 and 27 October, and the Prime Minister's account is that 30 of the 82 services were disconnected (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27; MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). The Prime Minister says the incident is not isolated, that foreign state actors are being investigated and that the attackers automated the extraction, with the use of artificial intelligence allegedly facilitating the identification and exploitation of the vulnerabilities (MOLDPRES, 2026-10-28). Moldova has not attributed the attack to any country or group (The Record, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A public e-service of a federal, cantonal or communal administration that returns person data for an identifier without authentication, or whose output feeds other registers, since AGE says the extraction chained from unauthenticated services into further data (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27).
Detection
Citizens noticed the abuse because the data-access history in the EVO app showed processing for civil-status document requests and driving-licence issue that they had not made, so a data-subject-visible access log is a detection channel (Moldova Electronic Governance Agency, 2026-10-27). On the server side the relevant telemetry is per-service request volume and sequential or bulk identifier lookups from one source; the sources give no breakdown of the request pattern, so that is an inference from about 11 million requests against about one million numbers.
Defender takeaway
List the public services that answer for a person identifier without authentication and check what each one returns, whether it feeds other registers and whether its access log records the true purpose; rate limits and alerts on bulk lookups belong in front of every such service.

Machelen (Belgium) municipality: its own timeline shows a foothold through misleading instructions on an external website on 2026-08-20, found 22 days later after a high-privilege user was reached, with personal data confirmed stolen and Rhysida now listing municipal and social-welfare files

Machelen's own timeline records that on 2026-08-20 attackers gained access to an internal laptop through misleading instructions on an external website, explored it extensively from 24 August to 1 September, and on 10 September had access to a user with high access rights and other IT systems; the municipality found the incident on 11 September, isolated all systems, reported to the Belgian CCB-CERT, restarted part of its systems from a backup of a safe date on 14 September and recorded the first evidence of leaked data on 17 September (Municipality of Machelen, 2026-09-22). It confirms that personal data was leaked and says the scope is still being investigated (Municipality of Machelen, 2026-09-22); the mayor had said on 14 September that no personal data appeared to be affected, and ITdaily reports that this proved wrong (ITdaily, 2026-09-23). Ransomware.live recorded on 2026-10-27 that Rhysida listed Machelen on its leak site, describing the listing as municipal and social-welfare file servers of about 1.3 million files, with client files that include passports and identity cards, nursing-home medical files and civil-status records, which are the group's own claims (Ransomware.live, 2026-10-27).

Detection
The timeline puts 22 days between first access and detection, with the first laptop explored from 24 August to 1 September; it names neither the website nor the commands, so the telemetry to review includes endpoint process creation after a user followed instructions on a web page and later use of a high-privilege account from that workstation, which is an inference from the timeline.
Defender takeaway
Treat a user who followed instructions from a website on a work laptop as a possible intrusion that can sit unseen for weeks; review high-privilege account activity from the user's workstation for the weeks after the event, not only the day it is reported.

KeyDrift: Talos reports UAT-11473 exploiting CVE-2026-20127 in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN controllers to run an implant inside the control-plane daemon that collects data-plane keys, with infrastructure overlapping Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network

Cisco Talos reports that UAT-11473 exploited CVE-2026-20127, an authentication bypass in the peering authentication of Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28), and then installed a custom framework it calls KeyDrift (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). CISA has listed the flaw in its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog since 2026-02-25 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Cisco's advisory (CVSS 10.0) says an unauthenticated remote attacker can log in as an internal high-privileged non-root user and reach NETCONF to change the SD-WAN fabric configuration, and that there is no workaround (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Cisco's advisory, revised on 2026-10-28 to link Talos's post, says its PSIRT is aware of limited exploitation (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Lumen's Black Lotus Labs reported on 2026-10-28 that Volt Typhoon had exploited the flaw since late 2025 and after Cisco's February disclosure (Lumen Black Lotus Labs, 2026-10-28), and Talos assesses with high confidence that UAT-11473's operating infrastructure overlaps considerably with Volt Typhoon's Silent Train network (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28).

KeyDrift runs inside the control-plane daemon. The actor edits the runit launchers of sshd and of a look-alike aaamgr service and remounts /rootfs.rw executable: the sshd launcher starts a script that injects the PolyFlame library into every running vdaemon process by ptrace, and the aaamgr launcher runs a packed PolyFlame loader directly (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). PolyFlame is tasked in-band over the control-plane traffic and offers a command, file-write and file-read backdoor and an intermediate command relay; Talos recovered no hardcoded address, port or domain (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). A second component, LittleFilch, hooks SSL_read in vdaemon and collects peer system addresses and 32-byte values Talos assesses to be OMP-distributed IPsec data-plane keys, writing them RSA-encrypted to /var/tmp (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). Talos lists observed targeting as space and satellite services, defense and aerospace technology, and policy research, calls the activity historical and does not say how many controllers were affected (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
Every Catalyst SD-WAN Controller, Manager and Validator regardless of configuration, on-premises or in Cisco's hosted clouds, on a release below the first fixed one in the advisory's table; Cisco says controllers with ports exposed to the internet are at risk (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).
Detection
On the controller's authentication log, Cisco says to audit /var/log/auth.log for accepted public-key logins of the vmanage-admin account from addresses that are not among the configured System IPs, and to validate control-connection peering events, those of peer type vmanage first, against maintenance windows and asset inventory (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). On the host, Talos names modified runit run scripts that remount the overlay root executable and start a background script, an aaamgr service that runs a compiled, packed ELF, extra libraries mapped into vdaemon with ptrace activity against it and encrypted staging files under /var/tmp (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28). Cisco asks for admin-tech files and a TAC case when compromise is suspected (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).

Triage: an aaamgr service that runs as a compiled ELF is the discriminator, because the legitimate component is a Python package and does not normally appear that way (Cisco Talos, 2026-10-28).

Defender takeaway
Upgrade to the fixed releases and restrict the control components' management ports, then treat any controller that was internet-reachable on a vulnerable release as a compromise-assessment target, because Lumen dates exploitation of the flaw to late 2025, before Cisco's February disclosure, and the implant runs in the process that handles the fabric's control sessions.

testmetest: an npm worm in the Miasma and Shai-Hulud family now starts when an application imports the package, so install with --ignore-scripts no longer protects, and JFrog finds 42 third-party GitHub repositories already armed with its publisher

SafeDep counts 19 npm packages from the same operator between 2026-10-19 and 2026-10-27, eight of them published through four npm accounts, that carry a worm sharing code with the June Miasma worm and adding the token-revocation wiper of Mini Shai-Hulud; SafeDep has not confirmed the lineage, and JFrog says its evidence does not establish that the original Miasma operators are responsible (SafeDep, 2026-10-27; JFrog Security Research, 2026-10-26). The install trigger has changed twice: first a command expansion in a binding.gyp file, with no install script; then a postinstall script that loads a native addon which decodes and starts the worm; and, since SafeDep's update of 27 October, an addon that runs when an application imports the package, so a hardening step that disables install scripts does not stop it (SafeDep, 2026-10-27).

The payload exits on CIS locales and in known analysis sandboxes. It steals SSH keys, registry and Git credentials, .env files, browser logins, AI-tool, cloud, Vault and Kubernetes secrets and GitHub Actions secrets read from runner memory (SafeDep, 2026-10-27). It exfiltrates by committing encrypted data, with the victim's encrypted GitHub token, to a new public repository in the victim's own account, injects a GitLab CI job that requests npm and PyPI OIDC tokens, adds its loader to the victim's npm packages and publishes new patch versions, republishes to PyPI and RubyGems, commits a fake CodeQL workflow and AI-agent configuration files that infect the host again, and copies itself over SSH to the hosts in known_hosts (SafeDep, 2026-10-27). A persistence service checks the stolen GitHub token every 45 seconds for 48 hours and on an authentication failure deletes the home directory (SafeDep, 2026-10-27). JFrog found 42 armed third-party GitHub repositories of 11 legitimate owners with hooks for AI coding assistants and IDEs, and says the payload blobs were large enough to evade GitHub's search and API paths (JFrog Security Research, 2026-10-26).

Exposure
Any developer endpoint, build agent or CI runner that installed or imported one of the operator's packages, and any GitHub or GitLab account whose token such a host held (SafeDep, 2026-10-27).
Detection
In package metadata, a binding.gyp whose sources field runs node in a package with no C or C++ sources, a postinstall that requires a .node file and discards errors beside a large high-entropy file, and prebuilt addons with no native source; on endpoints and CI runners, a node process that downloads or finds and runs the Bun runtime and a child node process started from a temporary path named after its process ID; in GitHub and GitLab audit logs, a new public repository in a developer's own account with a generic project description, commits with a fixed automated-sync message, commits that add AI-assistant configuration files (.claude, .cursor, .gemini, .vscode tasks, CLAUDE.md or AGENTS.md), an injected CI job that requests OIDC tokens, and unexpected patch releases of your own packages (SafeDep, 2026-10-27).
Defender takeaway
An install that ran with scripts disabled is not clean once the package has been imported; for an affected host SafeDep's order is to disconnect it, remove persistence first, rotate all credentials, check the accounts for the repositories and commits above and reinstall the operating system (SafeDep, 2026-10-27). Because the wiper is triggered by the token's revocation, the host is isolated and cleaned before the GitHub token is revoked.
