Huntress: phished MDM enrolments in Hexnode and Rippling give attackers a management path that brings ScreenConnect back after it has been removed

Huntress reports several recent incidents in which attackers used legitimate mobile-device-management platforms, not flaws in them, as a trusted management path, naming Hexnode and Rippling as the two it saw and noting the list is not definitive (Huntress, 2026-10-28). In the first case, proposal-themed emails led a user to download an MSI named like a DocuSign installer that installed Hexnode components (gateway, agent and PostgreSQL components); ScreenConnect followed shortly after and connected to an attacker relay, the managed-service provider removed it, and it came back several hours later to the same relay while the Hexnode client was still installed (Huntress, 2026-10-28). In the second, a receptionist clicked a link in an email about tax planning that led to a fake Teams calendar page; about a minute later a Rippling enrolment registry key appeared, the agent was downloaded into a SYSTEM profile path and installed with SYSTEM rights, and about 35 minutes after that the attacker used the MDM to stage and run a ScreenConnect installer as SYSTEM (Huntress, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A managed Windows endpoint whose user can run an installer or follow an enrolment link, in an organisation without an inventory of its authorised MDM tenants, agents and RMM instances (Huntress, 2026-10-28).
Detection
The chain Huntress describes as a stronger signal is social engineering, then a new MDM enrolment, then an RMM installation, then outbound communication with an unfamiliar relay, correlated across identity, MDM, endpoint and network telemetry; in endpoint telemetry that is an MSI run from a browser download folder that installs an MDM agent, an enrolment registry key on a device nobody enrolled, a new SYSTEM-level agent in a vendor directory shortly after a click, and an RMM installed by that agent (Huntress, 2026-10-28). A repeat of the same RMM relay after the RMM was removed, as in the Hexnode case, points to a remaining MDM client as a possible source (Huntress, 2026-10-28).

Triage: a corporate enrolment started by IT looks similar in process telemetry; the discriminators are a tenant that is not in the authorised inventory, a trigger that is an emailed link or a user-run installer instead of IT's enrolment workflow, and an RMM install within minutes (an inference from Huntress's two cases).

Defender takeaway
Treat an unexpected MDM enrolment as a security event and keep an inventory of authorised tenants; after removing a rogue RMM, unenrol the device from the unauthorised tenant, disable accounts the attacker created, revoke sessions and tokens, reset credentials and reimage the endpoint if its integrity cannot be confirmed, as Huntress advises (Huntress, 2026-10-28).

Check Point's advisory sk1000302 says that under certain circumstances the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both scored CVSS 9.2, may allow remote code execution through firewall web interfaces; affected are Force, Spark and Cloud firewalls that use Mobile Access Portal (not Spark), Remote Access VPN with SSL Network Extender (not Spark) or with SAML realm authentication, the Identity Awareness captive portal, the UserCheck portal or Zero Phishing, on R81.20, R82, R82.10 and R82.20 and on Spark R81.10.x and R82.00.x, and end-of-support lines are also listed (Check Point, 2026-11-12). The standalone hotfix of 2026-10-23 implements the PHP 7.4 fix and needs a reboot (Check Point, 2026-10-29); the sk now says the fix is included in Jumbo Hotfix Accumulator R82.20 take 14, R82.10 take 52, R82 take 132 and R81.20 take 174, names Spark fixes from builds B998002843 and B996005005, and keeps the R81.10 hotfix (Check Point, 2026-11-12). Until then, Check Point's mitigation is a cp-httpd.conf block denying multipart Content-Type requests, removed before the hotfix (Check Point, 2026-10-29).

Check Point Research reports that from 2026-10-30, about a week after the fix, an attacker exploited unpatched gateways through Mobile Access portals with PHP2Shell and escalated to root with CVE-2026-123039: the first wave targeted Israeli organisations and included destructive activity against some, and a wider wave on 2026-11-02 targeted organisations in several countries (Check Point Research, 2026-11-12). CVE-2026-123039 is a local escalation: the root dynamic_server process runs whatever command it receives on a world-writable local socket without authenticating the caller, and Check Point says it observed an active exploit against a couple of dozen customers (Check Point, 2026-11-12). After root the attacker placed PHP web shells in the directory the Mobile Access portal uses for its login pages and the TSGA implant, a root-run passive backdoor that Check Point says provides encrypted remote access, configuration theft, backup and snapshot persistence, process injection and firewall-log tampering; it ran a scanner, moved by SSH to a VMware ESXi host and ran a wiper there (Check Point Research, 2026-11-12). The standalone PHP hotfix text names only the two PHP CVEs (Check Point, 2026-10-29), and sk1000362 lists no Jumbo take for R81.10 or R81, so protection there is not stated (Check Point, 2026-11-12).

Exposure
For the PHP flaws, a gateway on a listed release with at least one of the six portal or VPN features in use (Check Point, 2026-11-12); for CVE-2026-123039, a Force gateway, management or log server, Multi-Domain server or Maestro on R81 to R82.20 below those Jumbo takes (Check Point, 2026-11-12).
Detection
The vulnerable daemon logs every command it receives to /var/log/dynamicCli.log, and Check Point says any command that does not use the legitimate Clish wrapper may indicate a command executed as root and requires investigation (Check Point, 2026-11-12); Check Point Research also describes the web-shell, listener and SSH-to-ESXi behavior above (Check Point Research, 2026-11-12).
Defender takeaway
Install the Jumbo take that carries both fixes on gateways and on management and log servers, apply the cp-httpd.conf mitigation and stop dynamic_server where it has to wait (Check Point, 2026-11-12; Check Point, 2026-11-12), and treat a gateway that was exposed and unpatched since 2026-10-30 as needing a compromise check, because a hotfix is not stated to remove an implant already installed, which is an inference from the persistence Check Point Research describes (Check Point Research, 2026-11-12).

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, F5 BIG-IP: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the Configuration utility of every module and the APM and SSL Orchestrator access profiles on 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 21.1.0, and F5's cumulative critical releases 17.1.3.7, 17.5.1.11 and 21.1.0.4 carry the fix

F5's release notes for BIG-IP 17.1.3.7, 21.1.0.4 and 17.5.1.11, each updated on 2026-10-24, list K000163821 as the reference for the fix of the PHP vulnerabilities CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and describe each build as a critical release whose only new changes are PHP vulnerability fixes and which is cumulative and includes earlier hardened and critical releases (F5, 2026-10-24; F5, 2026-10-24; F5, 2026-10-24). NCSC-NL records F5 as confirming that BIG-IP 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 and 21.1.0 are vulnerable through the Configuration utility control plane in all modules and, for APM and SSL Orchestrator, through the access-profile data plane, and that earlier affected releases stay vulnerable until updated (NCSC-NL, 2026-10-26). CISA lists both PHP flaws as exploited since 2026-10-26; nothing found reports an attack on BIG-IP (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28).

Exposure
A BIG-IP on 17.1.0 to 17.1.3, 17.5.0 to 17.5.1 or 21.1.0 whose Configuration utility is reachable from a network the attacker can reach, or that publishes an APM or SSL Orchestrator access profile (NCSC-NL, 2026-10-26).
Detection
F5's article on exploitation and mitigations could not be read and no indicator is published in the sources found. The telemetry to review on an exposed system is access to the Configuration utility and the access-profile web paths from untrusted sources, and shells or downloads started by the web service; this is an inference, not an F5 statement.
Defender takeaway
Move to the cumulative critical release of your train and read K000163821 in a browser for F5's own mitigation list; until then keep the Configuration utility off untrusted networks, and treat an APM or SSL Orchestrator system that was exposed and unpatched as needing a compromise check.

WatchGuard Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and 12.5.22: seven of 17 fixed Fireware OS flaws are scored 9.0 or higher, among them unauthenticated memory-corruption and missing-authentication rows in the Access Portal, the SIP proxy and the FireCluster sync daemon; WatchGuard knows of no exploitation

WatchGuard's advisory listing of 2026-10-27 opens with 18 rows, 17 for Fireware OS and one for Mobile VPN with SSL Client for Windows, and seven of the 17 are scored 9.0 or higher (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). The fixes are in Fireware OS 2026.4, 12.12.4 and, for T15 and T35 models, 12.5.22. Three of the seven need no authentication but a specific feature. CVE-2026-93866 (9.2) is an integer overflow in the WebSocket handling of the Access Portal that lets a remote unauthenticated attacker write beyond the bounds of a heap buffer while the Access Portal is enabled (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-93857 (9.2) is a stack buffer overflow in the SIP proxy that gives remote code execution when a SIP proxy is configured on the Firebox (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-93865 (9.2) is missing authentication in the FireCluster synchronization daemon: a remote unauthenticated attacker invokes privileged administrative actions with a crafted request to the FireCluster management IP when clustering is enabled (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

The other four need a network position. CVE-2026-112709 and CVE-2026-112710 (9.2 each) are heap overflows in the authentication service that give denial of service and possibly code execution to an attacker who controls or intercepts traffic to the configured Active Directory server and returns a crafted response (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-103594 (9.5) is a stack overflow in WireGuard configuration processing for a man-in-the-middle with TLS-decrypted access between a Firebox that acts as a FireCloud Gateway and WatchGuard Cloud (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-103593 (9.1) is a stack overflow in the logging service that gives root code execution to a network-adjacent attacker who impersonates or intercepts traffic to the log server with a crafted certificate, in FIPS mode (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27). Six rows affect Fireware OS 2025.1 up to before 2026.4 and 12.0 up to before 12.12.4, T15 and T35 up to before 12.5.22, the WireGuard row starts at 2026.2 and 12.12, and each page states that WatchGuard is not aware of exploitation in the wild (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Firebox on a Fireware OS release inside those ranges with at least one of the listed features: the Access Portal, a SIP proxy policy, FireCluster membership, an Active Directory authentication server, the FireCloud Gateway role, or FIPS mode with an external log server; the three unauthenticated rows are reachable by any host that can reach the Access Portal, the SIP proxy policy or the cluster management address (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27; WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-27).
Detection
WatchGuard publishes no indicator and no workaround. For the three unauthenticated rows, connections to the cluster management address from hosts that are not cluster peers, WebSocket upgrade requests to the Access Portal from unexpected sources, SIP traffic from outside expected carriers, and restarts of the portal, SIP or sync services on the Firebox are the telemetry to review; this is an inference from the stated mechanisms.
Defender takeaway
Install the fixed release on appliances with the Access Portal, a SIP proxy or clustering first; where an upgrade has to wait, turn off a feature that is not used and keep the cluster management address off untrusted segments.

CVE-2026-108142, Veeam Backup & Replication: an unauthenticated authorization bypass on the CDP Coordinator Service of 13.x backup servers (CVSS 4.0 9.1), fixed in 13.1.2 and 13.0.3, with a Backup for Microsoft 365 SQL injection to code execution and a Veeam ONE MFA bypass fixed the same day

Veeam published three advisories on 2026-10-27. In Backup & Replication, CVE-2026-108142 (CVSS 4.0 9.1, critical) lets an unauthenticated attacker bypass authorization on the CDP Coordinator Service of Windows-based Backup & Replication and of the Veeam Software Appliance; it affects 13.1.1.18 and all earlier 13.1 builds and 13.0.2.29 and all earlier 13.0 builds, is fixed in 13.1.2 (build 13.1.2.57) and 13.0.3 (build 13.0.3.63), and does not affect 12.x (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27). The same advisory fixes two medium path-traversal flaws that need the Restore Operator role plus control over the contents of a backed-up NAS share and that write attacker-controlled files to an arbitrary path on the backup server, and a local privilege escalation in Veeam Agent for Linux version 13.1.1.4 and earlier that applies only to agents managed by a Backup & Replication server (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27). Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 8.5.0.1014 and earlier carry CVE-2026-106076 (9.0, critical): an authenticated organization-transfer peer injects SQL into the source server's configuration database, which gives cross-tenant read and write of configuration data and remote code execution as the PostgreSQL service account; the fix is 8.6 (build 8.6.0.1102), as it is for CVE-2026-106077 (8.3), which lets a user with the Backup for Microsoft 365 Administrator role read arbitrary files on the backup server as LocalSystem; two further flaws, an unauthenticated REST API authentication bypass with a forged federation token (6.9) and an installer file-write (4.3), need 8.6 Patch 1 (build 8.6.0.5011) (Veeam KB4957, 2026-10-27). Veeam ONE 13.1.0.7233 and earlier let an attacker with valid Administrator credentials disable multi-factor authentication globally before completing MFA verification (8.5, high; fixed in 13.1 P1, build 13.1.0.7940) (Veeam KB4951, 2026-10-27).

NCSC Switzerland relayed the Backup & Replication and Veeam ONE advisories on 2026-10-28, lists the exploitation status as unknown with the vendor reporting no evidence of active exploitation, and gives the prerequisite for the critical flaw as network access to the backup server's CDP Coordinator Service (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-28). heise adds that backup servers are a favourite target of ransomware groups (translated from German) (heise online, 2026-10-28), and Veeam itself says attackers will likely try to reverse-engineer a disclosed patch to exploit unpatched deployments (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A Veeam Backup & Replication or Veeam Software Appliance on a 13.x build below 13.1.2 or 13.0.3 whose CDP Coordinator Service accepts connections from a network the attacker can reach; 12.x is out of scope (Veeam KB4948, 2026-10-27). Veeam Backup for Microsoft 365 version 8 below 8.6 Patch 1 (Veeam KB4957, 2026-10-27) and Veeam ONE 13.1 below Patch 1 (Veeam KB4951, 2026-10-27) are the other affected builds.
Detection
Veeam publishes no indicator. The telemetry that bears on this flaw is authentication and authorization events and service-account activity on the backup server, and new or changed backup jobs, repositories, stored credentials and restore operators; this is an inference from the described flaw, not a Veeam statement. For Veeam ONE, an MFA setting switched off followed by an Administrator sign-in is the sequence the flaw describes.
Defender takeaway
Install the fixed builds on every backup server first, since backup infrastructure is what ransomware groups try to reach before encrypting, and keep backup servers off networks that untrusted hosts can reach; where a backup server was reachable and unpatched, review its jobs, repositories and credentials for changes nobody made.

Dream Research reports a production chain of a custom PHP2Shell build with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 that gave unauthenticated root on 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and led to an attack on the Active Directory of a US government-affiliated organization; CISA's catalog entry for the kernel flaw of 2026-10-28 says the same chaining. The earlier statement that no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise is replaced, an action for appliances that embed PHP is added, the URWB fix date in the vendor list is corrected from March 2027 to November 2026 (advisory version 1.9), and the PAN-OS hotfix status is updated to nineteen of twenty released (advisory of 2026-10-29). Removed from the text: the sentence on the release time, Karimi's two-source-address-clusters and PHPSESSID remarks in the main text (the 2026-10-27 section keeps his reliability caveat), VulnCheck's failed web-shell attempt in the main text (the Detection line keeps it), the lab log-path remark and most of Sansec's note on its CVE attribution (kept as a short clause); the 'no source ties a named CVE' statement of 2026-10-27 is dated, and the evidence record for Karimi's clusters remark is dropped.

CISA's catalog entry of 2026-10-28 for the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 says it can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Dream Research reports a chain that takes these flaws to root on appliances: a custom, non-public PHP2Shell build for the management web server of one large vendor's firewall software, which runs PHP 8.0.30 with a high memory limit, gave code execution as the nobody user, and the kernel flaw lifted it to root in one HTTP request in under 15 minutes (Dream Research, 2026-10-27). Dream found the build tuned to eleven firmware versions, nine exploitable, with offsets from the vendor's own PHP library, the deployment-specific calibration CrowdStrike expects a reliable exploit to need (an inference) (Dream Research, 2026-10-27; CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23). From about 19,000 internet-facing firewalls of that vendor it narrowed to 240, rooted 24 and left a PHP webshell on each, and from the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed) built a persistent outbound SSH tunnel, rooted the organization's firewall management server through it and began an attack on its Active Directory; Dream could not tell whether that attack succeeded, does not name the vendor, calls the campaign apparently Chinese and AI-assisted and does not attribute it to a named actor (Dream Research, 2026-10-27). The targets were firewalls whose management interfaces were reachable from the internet (Dream Research, 2026-10-27).

Palo Alto Networks' advisory as read on 2026-10-29 lists all PAN-OS hotfixes as released except 11.1.7-h12, due on 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

First published 2026-05-15 · open finding →

Update29 Oct 2026 04:52 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryupdated_atprioritytagstechniquesentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says it can be chained with the PHP2Shell flaws to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root; Dream Research describes such a chain used against 24 firewalls of one unnamed vendor and a US government-affiliated network. The CVE record moves to exploited, the priority from notable to high, and the earlier statement that no source reports exploitation of this CVE is replaced. Removed from the text: the sentence that an attacker can modify any file the user can read (the Detection line still carries it) and, from the summary, the clause on Aikido's report of working Kubernetes exploits for the Dirty Frag family.

CISA added CVE-2026-46300 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-28 and says in the entry that the flaw can be chained with CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 to implant PHP webshells and run commands as root, naming no actor or victim (CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). Dream Research describes a chain of this kind from artifacts its tooling recovered: a custom, non-public PHP2Shell build, tailored to the PAN-OS management web server, which runs PHP 8.0.30, gives code execution as the nobody user, and the Fragnesia exploit then overwrites /etc/pam.d/su in the page cache so that su root succeeds without a password; Dream says SELinux confines the web server's domain from modifying system files and that the whole chain runs in one HTTP request in under 15 minutes (Dream Research, 2026-10-29). From about 19,000 internet-facing PAN-OS firewalls that it found through a search engine, the attacker narrowed to 240 in the United States, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea, rooted 24 and planted a PHP webshell on each; on the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed) it set up an outbound SSH tunnel kept up by a systemd service and an rc.local entry, rooted the organization's firewall management server through the tunnel, decrypted the LDAP service-account password with root access and sprayed passwords against a domain that had no lockout threshold (Dream Research, 2026-10-29). Dream says the recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration but could not tell whether the password spray succeeded, calls the campaign apparently Chinese and AI-assisted and does not attribute it to a named actor (Dream Research, 2026-10-27).

Verification & coverage notes

Window 26 h (gap 24.0 h to 2026-10-28T0256Z-intel, normal cadence, no outage backfill). entities/registry.yaml (676 KB) was grepped per key instead of read whole; the 14-day prior_coverage.json (73 records) was read in full. Slice build: S1 took 6 essential and 14 rotation sources, S2 15 and 14, S3 14 rotation, S4 its 4-source pool; every slice ledger row came back attempted (20, 29, 14 and 4 records), and no continuation was needed. One Phase 2 follow-up agent (FU1) swept the PHP2Shell vendor status lists and the CERT-FR bulletins of 2026-10-28 and found the Check Point, F5 and Trend Micro, Quest KACE and NetApp gaps. No intel drops, so no S5.

Verification. Eight iterations ran: 1 to 4 and 6 returned NEEDS_FIXES, 5 and 7 returned CLEAN, and iteration 8, the confirmation pass of the iteration 7 CLEAN, returned NEEDS_FIXES at the 8-iteration cap, so the run publishes by the cap's fail-open with verification_residual_count 5 (truth 4, editorial 1; findings and remediations are in the record above). The iteration 8 wording fixes (the KeyDrift Cisco citation and fixed-release string, the VMware CISA and CrowdStrike order, the Machelen Detection absolute) were applied after the cap and were not re-verified. Left for the quality audit: the VMware vCenter and ESX 7.0 rows (extended-support fix only, in the Broadcom matrix since before this run), the legacy VMware em dashes and wording, and the Citrix NetScaler clause in the PHP2Shell entry (page unreadable on every transport). Declined with rebuttal in the iteration records: WatchGuard as an F7 include (three feature-dependent unauthenticated rows at 9.2 on perimeter firewalls; the store keeps comparable rows at notable; iteration 2 agreed) and the ConnectWise Trust Center anchor (the anchored URL answers 403 on every transport and raises a source-urls warning; iteration 4 accepted the decline). The status-page citation for ConnectWise is the incident permalink.

What this fire changed. Eleven new entries and nine changelog records. The two that matter most: Cisco's advisory for CVE-2026-20127 (version 2.1 of 2026-10-28 adds the Talos link; it says Cisco is aware of limited exploitation) is matched by Talos's description of the KeyDrift implant that UAT-11473 ran inside the SD-WAN controller process (new high entry, patch does not evict it); and CISA's KEV listing of the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300 on 2026-10-28, with its chaining to the PHP2Shell flaws and Dream Research's account of 24 rooted firewalls, moved that entry from notable to high and gave the critical PHP2Shell entry its first production-compromise chain. Three new entries close PHP2Shell vendor gaps (Check Point, F5 BIG-IP, and Trend Micro with Quest KACE and NetApp ONTAP).

KEV rows (kev-window.txt).

  • CVE-2026-41709 (VMware ESX, KEV 2026-10-28): COVERED-STALE on the VMSA-2026-0006 entry, given an update record: its CVE record now carries exploited and cisa-kev, and CrowdStrike's claim of zero-day use by WARP PANDA is attributed to CrowdStrike.
  • CVE-2026-46300 (Linux kernel, KEV 2026-10-28): COVERED-STALE on the Fragnesia entry, given an update record (exploited, cisa-kev, priority notable to high).
  • No NOT COVERED, MENTION-ONLY or RANSOMWARE rows.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md). ARX Group SA (Aurora leak-site claim of 2026-10-23): held, unchanged. S4 re-read the ransomware.live record and API, the Inside IT, Netzwoche and SRF feeds and ARX's own site and searched in four languages; no ARX, client or regulator statement and no Swiss press report exist, expiry 2026-11-07. Breachsense lists the claim and five infostealer logins for the ARX domain, an aggregator and not corroboration.

Supersessions and corrections. The PHP2Shell entry's "no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise" is replaced by Dream Research's recovered-artifact account (and its clause that Sansec's CVE attribution differs from the PHP advisories is cut to one half-sentence); the Oracle CPU entry's "none of the rows is reported exploited" now carries Defused's decoy telemetry for CVE-2026-101767 without marking the row exploited; the ZDI entry's "no fix merged upstream or shipped in a distribution kernel" is replaced by AlmaLinux's production kernels and TuxCare's networking-tree statement, and its evidence quote is replaced by one still on TuxCare's updated page; the Cisco PHP2Shell entry's "no fixed release before March 2027" for URWB becomes November 2026 (advisory version 1.9); the ConnectWise entry's advice to keep the old connections disabled until restoration instructions exist now says restoration runs through a new application each tenant must consent.

Contradictions and borderline includes.

  • Contradiction: Dream's headline says 25 servers rooted, its text says 24 firewalls rooted in the batch and a third government server exploited through the tunnel; the entry carries the 24 firewalls and the management server separately and says Dream could not confirm the outcome of the Active Directory attack.
  • Contradiction: NCSC-NL's PHP2Shell list gives 2026-11-11 for Check Point's Jumbo fix, while sk1000302 lists hotfixes since 2026-10-23 and calls the Jumbo fix planned for 2026-11-11; the entry follows the vendor page and says so.
  • Contradiction: Defused and BleepingComputer report exploit attempts against decoys for CVE-2026-101767 while Oracle has not tagged it exploited and no production compromise is reported; the row stays patch-available, not exploited.
  • Borderline include: Veeam Backup & Replication CVE-2026-108142 with the Backup for Microsoft 365 and ONE rows (no exploitation reported), kept under the "otherwise" limb of PD-11 (b): an unauthenticated authorization bypass on backup-server infrastructure of a product family that ransomware operators target, relayed by the NCSC.ch hub. After the first verifier pass the cves[] records are held to six rows, the lowest scored 6.9 (the unauthenticated REST API bypass in Backup for Microsoft 365); the three lowest rows (two medium path traversals needing the Restore Operator role, an installer file-write) stay in the prose only.
  • Borderline include: WatchGuard Fireware 2026.4 (three pre-auth rows at 9.2 in perimeter firewalls, configuration dependent, no exploitation reported); the store keeps comparable perimeter-firewall rows at notable.
  • Borderline include: testmetest npm worm, first coverage through the rotational lookback (SafeDep 2026-10-27 update, JFrog 2026-10-26), included because installing with --ignore-scripts no longer protects and the wiper fires when the stolen token is revoked.
  • Borderline include: Machelen municipality (routine): its own timeline names the foothold method and a 22-day dwell, satisfying the incident floor; Moldova's e-government extraction (PD-11 c) is the transferable parallel to the Swiss cantonal e-autoindex harvesting entry.

Single-source and reduced-confidence inclusions.

  • Check Point, Trend Micro, Quest KACE, NetApp and F5: each vendor is the disclosing party for its own products. F5's advisory K000163821 could not be read, so the F5 entry rests on F5's release notes for the fixed builds and NCSC-NL's record of the exposure scope, confidence medium; NetApp's advisory page renders only in a browser and was read from the advisory data behind it.
  • Veeam: vendor first-party, three KB pages, relayed by NCSC.ch and heise; single-source in the entry's frame.
  • Moldova: the agency's own account with MOLDPRES and The Record; Machelen: the municipality's own timeline with ITdaily; the Rhysida listing is the group's claim as Ransomware.live records it.
  • Huntress MDM enrolment: one vendor's research, single-source.
  • KeyDrift: the implant analysis is Talos alone; Cisco and Lumen are independent for the flaw and for Volt Typhoon's exploitation of it.

borderline-drop lines.

  • Cisco Secure Firewall ASA, FTD and FMC hardening CVE-2026-20329 to 20336: the Cisco primaries date from 2026-09-16 and 09-18, outside the window, only NCSC-NL's relay is inside it; authenticated rows, and the exploited ones are already covered.
  • Amadeus reservation data (Korean Air, Asiana, JAL): out of nexus, no Swiss entity, no vector beyond a supplier account credential, Amadeus silent; reopen if a Swiss or European carrier confirms.
  • Belgium FPS Finance cyberattack: incident floor not met (no vector, no actor, no data theft indicated).
  • SoftwareOne and The Gentlemen: single paywalled source, leak-site claim with partial denial, no listing seen (PD-6).
  • BACS weekly review week 43 (WhatsApp account takeover): published 2026-10-27, consumer fraud, no public-sector victim; Swiss Ice Hockey Federation MySIHF portal: private federation; Vaud CYBER26 exercise invitation and the Federal Council AI-regulation status report: no obligation or technical consequence; OFAC DPRK IT-worker designations: policy watch, four IT-worker entries already carry the lesson.
  • Acronis TRU Qilin encryptor analysis, Enclave AuthMask CVE-2026-80097 (fixed in September), EPICS Base CVE-2026-114595 to 114598, Tailscale Tailworm (needs an authorised peer, patched in 1.104.4), TeamViewer 15.83, 123 Reg AI-driven intrusion, Socket Searchjacked, Check Point Yoba, Eclipse Vert.x CVE-2026-102479, Zscaler Node2Shell decoy telemetry: below the bar (single source, narrow exposure, patch-cycle item or low delta, no exploitation, no constituency nexus).
  • CrowdStrike 2026 Legal Threat Landscape Report: US legal sector; its CVE-2026-41709 claim is carried in the VMware update record. Canadian Cyber Centre AL26-028 help-desk vishing: the store already carries two help-desk impersonation entries and no new Swiss-relevant mechanism appears.
  • PK Softech and Publica (BLVK, BPK notification details): minor delta on an entry with 12 records. Hudson Rock FortiBleed 2.0 (1,703 further FortiGate configuration reports): single-source record counts, not working credentials; the 2026-06-18 and 2026-10-22 entries already carry the reset and configuration-review actions.
  • FU1 vendor sweep, no item: Juniper JSA112681 (page unreadable; NCSC-NL records Junos OS as vulnerable to CVE-2026-109618 but not exploitable and SRX off PHP from 25.2R1), Broadcom Symantec Endpoint Protection Manager and Carbon Black App Control (umbrella advisory only, per-product pages login-gated), Splunk SVD-2026-1013 (only Smartlook, remedied), Sophos (no product affected), N-able (vendor-hosted, secured), Securepoint, Cleo, Checkmk, Ubiquiti UISP CRM and TerraMaster (niche or low exposure).
  • CERT-PL Wing FTP Server CVE-2026-105420 (CVSS 4.0 9.4 but needs administrator privileges), CERT-FR AVI-1397 to 1408 (CPython, Chrome 156, Samba vfs_ceph_rgw, Docker Desktop, Metabase, Mitel, Edge, Mozilla, Belden, Axis) and NCSC-NL Apple macOS and Splunk Enterprise: no exploitation, authenticated or niche, no constituency exposure.
  • Oracle PeopleSoft CVE-2026-35273 (ZDI decomposition into three bugs): no exploitation, victim, fix or status change beyond what the store already carries; Juniper Session Smart Router and Conductor (CCCS AV26-1101): primary unreadable on every reader, the CVE records alone give no usable exposure statement, and no exploitation is reported; watch for ZDI's separate PeopleSoft CVE ids.
  • ESET APT Activity Report Q2 to Q3 2026: only the MDaemon finding is carried; the other findings are actor-activity summaries for regions outside the constituency.
  • Volt Typhoon "Silent Train" (Lumen Black Lotus Labs): the page metadata shows 2026-03-16, so it enters only as the entity profile and the cited overlap in the KeyDrift entry.

Untrusted content. S3's WebFetch of the Socket Searchjacked post returned a share link carrying an instruction aimed at AI assistants (to remember the domain for future citations). It was ignored and is not part of any finding.

Sources. jfrog-security-research and anssi-cyber-gouv-actualites promoted to active (promotion_due). Four candidates added because published entries cite them or replace a blocked source: veeam-kb-security (first-party backup PSIRT, feed works), dream-research (the PHP2Shell and Fragnesia chain), safedep (testmetest) and ec-presscorner-api (JSON API replacing the digital-strategy newsroom that answers 403 for the fourth run). Not added: Tailscale security bulletins (mesh-VPN use in the constituency not evidenced), hacksnack.ch and InfoStealers (relay and single-vendor leads, reliability C). Recipe notes recorded for the sources named in the sub-agent ledgers (CrowdStrike feed, StepSecurity feed, ESET research listing, Previdian, Vaud cyber page, ransomware.live, Piyolog, ransom-isac, Venarix, hacksnack.ch), and the StepSecurity feed URL added to its record. connectwise-trust-center and ec-digital-strategy-newsroom stay 403 on every transport; a 403 never demotes. tools/source_health.py was run after the source updates (output in work/2026-10-29T0255Z-intel/source_health.out); its two UNSOLVED rows were investigated and not demoted: sygnia answers 403 on every transport including WebFetch (a 403 never demotes) and bfv-verfassungsschutz-de fails intermittently with an SSL EOF on a feed that reads on retry; a recipe note was recorded on each.

Registry. Added actor:uat-11473 (uses KeyDrift; overlaps Volt Typhoon, exploits the SD-WAN controller), malware:keydrift, actor:volt-typhoon, incident:moldova-egovernment-data-extraction-2026-10, incident:machelen-municipality-cyberincident-2026-09 (attributed-to Rhysida as a leak-site self-claim only), malware:hellage, malware:helltag and campaign:testmetest-npm-worm-2026-10 (overlaps Miasma and Mini Shai-Hulud, lineage unconfirmed), and 14 product entities through sync_products.py (two spellings merged into existing records as aliases).

Watchlist: products checked=0, hits=0; suppliers checked=0, hits=0 (no watchlists configured).

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport; the new application's identifiers on the Trust Center page are unreadable here); ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 on every transport, fourth run); ox-security (feed lists dated items but every article body is 403); previdian (listing feed 403, one featured CVE only); resecurity (empty JavaScript shell); golem-security (cookie wall); F5 K000163821 (my.f5.com is a JavaScript shell on every reader, so F5's exposure, mitigation and exploitation wording is unread); Juniper support portal (JavaScript shells); Broadcom per-product PHP2Shell pages (login-gated); the Cisco advisory's Snort rule links were not re-read after version 1.9; Palo Alto's PAN-OS hotfix status was re-read before the commit (19 of 20 released, only 11.1.7-h12 still carries an estimated date, 2026-10-30), so that build is the one to re-read at the next fire.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-28
item.description:
• DeadTag: expired tag domains send visitors to iPhone exploit kits; opening the page is enough on vulnerable iOS. Report URI and iVerify report that an operator they call DeadTag buys the expired domains of old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that carries the tag runs the operator's script, and sells the visitors on; Report URI counts more than 660 re-registered domains. For chosen iPhone visitors one chain ends at a page that serves the Coruna kit to iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified DarkSword kit to iOS 18.4 to 18.7, both of which attack the browser itself, so that opening the page compromises a vulnerable device and steals keychain passwords and crypto-wallet data. →
  • PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356): Magento upload flaw attacked since March, fixed in July, CISA lists it as exploited. Sansec reports that PolyShell, the unauthenticated file upload in the Magento and Adobe Commerce REST API that Adobe tracks as CVE-2026-48356, has been attacked since 2026-03-19, with a mass wave on 2026-03-30 that put a JavaScript loader on 471 stores in one hour. Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 of 2026-07-14 names the 2026-jul builds as the fix and still says Adobe knows of no exploits, while Sansec says Magento 2.4.9 carried a fix on 2026-05-12; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27. A store that ran an unpatched build may carry a webshell that the update does not remove. →
  • HPE ClearPass 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 are affected by PHP2Shell; a hotfix patch exists for each train. HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05171, released on 2026-10-22 and revised on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29, lists ClearPass Policy Manager 6.14.0 and earlier and 6.11.15 and earlier as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each scored CVSS 3.1 9.8, adds the 6.12 train in its machine-readable record, and names a hotfix patch for 6.14.1, 6.12.8 and 6.11.16. HPE asks customers to consider removing guest portals and all management interfaces from public access until the affected instances are upgraded; the bulletin says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass, although CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01DeadTag: expired tag domains send visitors to iPhone exploit kits; opening the page is enough on vulnerable iOS. Report URI and iVerify report that an operator they call DeadTag buys the expired domains of old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that carries the tag runs the operator's script, and sells the visitors on; Report URI counts more than 660 re-registered domains. For chosen iPhone visitors one chain ends at a page that serves the Coruna kit to iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified DarkSword kit to iOS 18.4 to 18.7, both of which attack the browser itself, so that opening the page compromises a vulnerable device and steals keychain passwords and crypto-wallet data. →
  2. 02PolyShell (CVE-2026-48356): Magento upload flaw attacked since March, fixed in July, CISA lists it as exploited. Sansec reports that PolyShell, the unauthenticated file upload in the Magento and Adobe Commerce REST API that Adobe tracks as CVE-2026-48356, has been attacked since 2026-03-19, with a mass wave on 2026-03-30 that put a JavaScript loader on 471 stores in one hour. Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 of 2026-07-14 names the 2026-jul builds as the fix and still says Adobe knows of no exploits, while Sansec says Magento 2.4.9 carried a fix on 2026-05-12; CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27. A store that ran an unpatched build may carry a webshell that the update does not remove. →
  3. 03HPE ClearPass 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 are affected by PHP2Shell; a hotfix patch exists for each train. HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05171, released on 2026-10-22 and revised on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29, lists ClearPass Policy Manager 6.14.0 and earlier and 6.11.15 and earlier as affected by the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, each scored CVSS 3.1 9.8, adds the 6.12 train in its machine-readable record, and names a hotfix patch for 6.14.1, 6.12.8 and 6.11.16. HPE asks customers to consider removing guest portals and all management interfaces from public access until the affected instances are upgraded; the bulletin says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass, although CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 2Trending vulnerabilities 3Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 15

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLENATOB2

DeadTag: re-registered domains of defunct analytics and advertising tags redirect visitors of thousands of sites, among them to a page that serves the Coruna and DarkSword iPhone exploit kits, which compromise a vulnerable device when the page opens

Report URI and iVerify describe a campaign they name DeadTag: attackers buy the expired domains behind old analytics and advertising tags that thousands of websites still load, so every page that still carries the tag runs the operator's script without the site owner changing or noticing anything, and the operator sells the visitors those tags bring in (Report URI, 2026-10-22). Report URI has identified more than 660 re-registered domains still embedded on thousands of sites and cautiously estimates 135 million visits a month (Report URI, 2026-10-22). The script is about 2 KB, does nothing for search engines, scanners and other bots, asks the operator's server what to do with each visitor and redirects the chosen ones, and Report URI found that the operator stopped answering when it probed from data-centre addresses or returned too often from residential ones; destinations include scam pages, a fake VPN pop-up and, for iPhones, a page that serves two exploit kits (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

One chain ends at a fake prediction-market page that picks the kit by the visitor's iOS version, Coruna for iOS 13 to 17.2.1 and a modified "P7" variant of DarkSword for iOS 18.4 to 18.7; both attack the browser itself, so opening the page is enough to compromise a vulnerable device, and the spyware they install steals keychain passwords, crypto-wallet app data and device and account information and reports to one server; Report URI notes that Coruna and DarkSword are separate exploit kits that have been seen in different campaigns, and that here both send their stolen data to the same server, which it reads as one operator running both (Report URI, 2026-10-22). iVerify reads DeadTag as mostly focused on European domains rather than .com (iVerify, 2026-10-21), and saw the P7 variant reach an employee's device at a customer organisation through a malicious Instagram ad while the employee was scrolling in the app (iVerify, 2026-10-21). The kit operator does not rely on DeadTag alone: Report URI found DarkSword loaders on hundreds of online shops on one e-commerce platform, PrestaShop (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
Any public website that still loads a script from a third-party domain whose provider no longer operates it, where the browser fetches nothing useful and the page looks normal, and any iPhone on iOS 13 to 17.2.1 or 18.4 to 18.7 that opens such a page (Report URI, 2026-10-22).
Detection
Inventory the external script references of each public site and flag any whose domain has been re-registered or no longer belongs to its provider; Report URI recommends script monitoring that shows when a new script or domain appears on a page, and a Content Security Policy that controls which domains a site may load code from (Report URI, 2026-10-22). A security scanner usually sees only an empty response from the malicious script, because the operator answers only selected visitors.
Defender takeaway
Remove dead third-party tags from every site you run, enforce a Content Security Policy and keep iPhones on the current iOS, with Lockdown Mode for people who may be targeted; for an iPhone that may have opened an affected page, Report URI advises restarting it, changing the passwords stored in its keychain and moving crypto assets to a new wallet (Report URI, 2026-10-22).

Builds on: 2026-09-30/star-blizzard-redflick-cosmicpulse-single-click-chain · 2026-09-13/gtg-20006-anthropic-russia-ai-orchestrated-espionage

threat28 Oct 03:54Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Report URI (Scott Helme) · iVerify Threat Intelligence Team
ROUTINENATOC3

ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal (canton Bern, communal wastewater-treatment association): SafePay has put about 49 GB into the darknet, which Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT, finds holds personal records, bank statements, weak passwords and a third party's monitoring credentials; the association declines to comment

The tracker DeXpose recorded on 2026-09-15 that SafePay had claimed an attack on ARA Lyss, the wastewater-treatment association at ara-lyss.ch, posting that the full leak would be published soon unless a company representative made contact (DeXpose, 2026-09-15). Inside IT reported on 2026-10-27 that SafePay has put the stolen data into the darknet, about 49 GB in the case of the Bernese association ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, that the security firm Risikomonitor analysed it, and that the association's management declined to comment (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). Risikomonitor's analysis, relayed by Inside IT and not verified independently, finds about 3,200 e-mail addresses and data on more than 1,200 identifiable persons; user folders and a data store with content up to March 2026 that hold 255 password hits, 195 of them very weak; bank statements and a transaction list with more than 100 payments by private persons with name and address; the full login data to the monitoring portals of the photovoltaic plants of another company's customers, stored on the same server; and a 2015 applicant list with birth dates, civil status, former employer and interview notes that was never deleted (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

BACS told Inside IT that SafePay, which relies on double extortion, is among the more active ransomware groups in Switzerland and, together with The Gentlemen, the third most active in 2026 after Akira and Payload, that it has no clear focus on Switzerland, and that it was first observed there in May 2025 (Inside IT, 2026-10-27). No source says how the attackers got in or that data was encrypted at the association.

Defender takeaway
A communal body or association should look for credentials, bank statements and applicant files on its own file servers before an attacker does: Risikomonitor found 255 password hits in files, another company's portal logins and a 2015 applicant list that had never been deleted, and those are what a published dump gives fraudsters (Inside IT, 2026-10-27).

Builds on: 2026-09-30/manno-ti-commune-ransomware-safepay-claim · 2026-10-21/aa26-293a-safepay-ransomware-edge-flaws-backup-nas-reset

incident28 Oct 03:53Zsingle-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Inside IT (article with Risikomonitor's analysis) · DeXpose (leak-site tracker, claim record)

02Trending vulnerabilities3 items

NOTABLECVE-2026-48356exploitedNATOB2

CVE-2026-48356 (PolyShell), Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source: an unauthenticated file upload attacked since March 2026, fixed for supported lines in July, and listed by CISA as exploited on 2026-10-27

Sansec named the flaw PolyShell: a missing validation in Magento's REST API that lets unauthenticated attackers upload executable files to a store, using a polyglot (code disguised as an image) to pass the image check (Sansec, 2026-03-17). It reports that its Shield service has blocked exploitation attempts against 79.5% of the Magento stores it protects since 2026-03-16, with first attacks observed on 2026-03-19, and that the vulnerable code has existed since the first Magento 2 release (Sansec, 2026-03-17). On 2026-03-30 a mass wave uploaded webshells, spread backdoor scripts across several directories and injected a JavaScript loader into the CMS pages of 471 stores within one hour (Sansec, 2026-03-30).

Sansec dates a fix in Magento 2.4.9 to 2026-05-12, without a backport to the supported 2.4.8 and 2.4.7 lines, and the backport to those lines to 2026-07-14, in bulletin APSB26-73 (Sansec, 2026-03-17). That bulletin rates the flaw Critical at CVSS 3.1 9.6, lists 2.4.9 among the affected versions, names the 2026-jul builds, 2.4.9-2026-jul included, as the fix for Adobe Commerce and Magento Open Source, and still says Adobe is not aware of any exploits in the wild (Adobe, 2026-07-14). CISA added CVE-2026-48356 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation and gives no detail (CISA, 2026-10-27; CISA KEV, 2026-10-27). Sansec's research of 2026-10-24 shows the operator behind the March wave still active: its newest loader domain, registered on 2026-10-06, sits in the CMS blocks of 83 stores, 60 of which already carried an earlier loader, and one of them, on Magento 2.4.7-p1, still lacks APSB26-73 and holds PolyShell webshells disguised as images (Sansec, 2026-10-24).

Exposure
Every Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce store without the 2026-jul fix, 2.4.9 included (Adobe, 2026-07-14); the anonymous guest-cart item routes need no credentials, and the upload becomes code execution on stock nginx for the oldest 2.x lines, on any non-stock nginx that hands every .php file to the PHP handler, and on Magento before 2.3.5 running on Apache without the engine switch set for that directory (Sansec, 2026-03-17).
Detection
Sansec calls any .php, .phtml or .phar file in the custom-options upload directory a strong indicator of compromise, and the uploaded file stays on disk even where execution is blocked (Sansec, 2026-03-17); also look for requests that add items to guest carts with embedded file data from unfamiliar sources (Sansec, 2026-03-17), script tags in the CMS block table and administrator accounts nobody created (Sansec, 2026-10-24).
Defender takeaway
Install the fix now, and treat a store that ran an unpatched build while internet-reachable since March as possibly compromised until its upload directory, CMS blocks and administrator accounts are checked, because an uploaded file stays on disk even where execution is blocked (Sansec, 2026-03-17), so the fix does not remove a shell already written (an inference), and deleting a loader script does not remove the access behind it (Sansec, 2026-10-24).

Builds on: 2026-10-14/adobe-october-2026-coldfusion-aem-commerce-unauth-critical

vulnerability28 Oct 03:54Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Sansec (PolyShell advisory) · Sansec (mass PolyShell attack wave) · Sansec (CMS block loader campaign) · Adobe (security bulletin APSB26-73) · CISA (alert, CISA Adds Two Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.27)
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, HPE Networking ClearPass Policy Manager: bulletin HPESBNW05171 lists the 6.14, 6.12 and 6.11 trains as affected by the PHP2Shell flaws and names a hotfix patch for each (CVSS 3.1 9.8)

HPE Networking's bulletin HPESBNW05171, released on 2026-10-22 and revised on 2026-10-23 and 2026-10-29, covers CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, the PHP flaws behind PHP2Shell, in ClearPass Policy Manager and scores each CVSS 3.1 9.8 with network access, no privileges and no user interaction (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). Its affected-products note lists ClearPass 6.14.0 and earlier in the 6.14 release train and 6.11.15 and earlier in the 6.11 train, while its machine-readable record also lists the 6.12 train and gives 6.14.1, 6.11.16 and 6.12.8 as the boundaries; the bulletin does not reconcile the two (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). The fix is a hotfix patch for each train, 6.14.1, 6.12.8 (added in revision 3, which HPE says "exceptionally" includes 6.12.8) and 6.11.16, downloadable from the HPE Networking Support Portal; versions past end of maintenance are presumed affected and are not covered, and HPE has not assessed versions past end of support, which it says should be considered potentially impacted (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

HPE recommends confining the CLI and web management interfaces to a dedicated layer 2 segment or VLAN, or controlling them with firewall policy at layer 3 and above, and asks customers to consider removing guest portals and all management interfaces from public access until the affected ClearPass instances have been upgraded (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). Other HPE Networking products and software versions it does not list are not known to be affected, and for Mist products the bulletin points to a Juniper reference advisory (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29). CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-27); the bulletin itself says nothing about exploitation of ClearPass (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).

Exposure
Every ClearPass Policy Manager on the 6.14, 6.12 or 6.11 train without the hotfix patch; the guest portal and the management interfaces are the surfaces HPE asks to take off public access (HPE Networking, 2026-10-29).
Detection
HPE gives no indicator and no post-patch check; CISA's PHP alert advises monitoring for PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools (CISA, 2026-10-21), which on a ClearPass node would be processes started by the web worker account (an inference, since HPE does not describe how ClearPass runs PHP).
Defender takeaway

The advisory gives no affected-version ranges and no workaround steps; its bug records carry platform-specific information, workarounds and fixed releases, and a product it does not list is, in Cisco's review, not affected (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).

Cisco says it is aware that a public announcement is available and knows of no malicious use of the flaws against any Cisco product (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 (CISA KEV, 2026-10-27). Exposure
Every Expressway Series and Expressway Select unit and every Duo Access Gateway not on a release Cisco lists as fixed (15.5.21 and 3.2.0), since Cisco gives no affected-version ranges; the advisory names no version-check command and no component that runs the PHP; its bug records CSCwx37062 and CSCwx37073 carry platform-specific information (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28).
Detection
Cisco publishes no indicator and reports no attack on its products, but lists Snort rules 67359 and 67360 as action links for the advisory (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); beyond that, CISA's PHP alert advises monitoring for PHP worker processes launching shells or downloading tools (CISA, 2026-10-21), which on these products would be processes started by the web worker account (an inference, since Cisco does not describe how they run PHP).
Defender takeaway
Move Expressway to 15.5.21 and Duo Access Gateway to 3.2.0, the fixed releases the table names (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28); an Expressway already upgraded to X15.5.20 for the clustered-device flaw (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-21) is not named as fixed in the PHP table, which lists only 15.5.21 (an inference from the table, not a Cisco statement), so apply the bug record's workaround until 15.5.21 is installed (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-28). Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul and Unified Industrial Wireless Software move to 26.2.1.9, available since 2026-11-06.

CVE-2026-61425 and the follow-up batch, Balbooa Gridbox for Joomla: a client-supplied cookie is accepted as proof of identity, giving anonymous Super User access

First published 2026-07-26 · open finding →

Update28 Oct 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27, fixing two unauthenticated read-side SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 (the sort-by parameter of store and category post lists) and CVE-2026-102789 (an editor task without a permission check), both scored CVSS 4.0 9.3 by the Joomla CNA and affecting every release up to 2.20.4.1. No exploitation is reported, Joomla 3 sites have no fix, and the action now points at 2.20.4.2.

Balbooa released Gridbox 2.20.4.2 on 2026-10-27 with two security fixes rated Critical, for the versions 2.20.4.1 and earlier (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). CVE-2026-102788 is in the sort-by URL parameter of store and category post lists and CVE-2026-102789 is a missing permission check on the editor task that loads blog posts (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27); Balbooa's fixes are a strict allowlist validation for the sort-by parameter and a user edit-level check on the editor task (Balbooa, 2026-10-27). mySites.guru says the sort value previously went into the ORDER BY part of the database query and reads the second flaw as a second anonymous route to the same query. mySites.guru reports that the Joomla CNA scores both CVSS 4.0 9.3 and lists every release from 1.0.0 to 2.20.4.1 as affected, and that only two PHP files differ between 2.20.4.1 and 2.20.4.2, one per fix (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

mySites.guru reads both flaws as read-side, although the CNA's vector also rates integrity and availability High: an anonymous visitor can extract the Joomla user table, with its password hashes, and every other table the site's extensions created. mySites.guru says about 95% of the Gridbox sites it monitors ran an affected version on the morning of the release, that sites on the Joomla 3 line stop at Gridbox 2.17.0.2, which has no fix for this year's flaws, and that there is no public report of exploitation yet (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27). Nothing here is reported exploited, unlike the July batches above; the version to be on is now 2.20.4.2.

Detection
In web access and database query logs, store or category list requests whose sort-by value is not one of the known sort keys, repeated anonymous calls to the Gridbox editor's blog-post task, and slow-query bursts from the web account; since the reported impact is data read out, the post-patch check is credential hygiene on a site that was exposed, starting with administrator accounts nobody created, since the password hashes can be worked on offline.
Defender takeaway
Update to 2.20.4.2 now, communal and agency sites included, and move Joomla 3 sites to a supported Joomla (mySites.guru, 2026-10-27).

IDC Frontier's seventh report of 2026-10-27 says its investigation with an external security firm is complete and names the cause: a third party exploited a vulnerability in open-source software used in the authentication system of the IDCF Cloud Portal, the portal customers use to start virtual servers and check billing, and so entered that system (translated from Japanese; IDC Frontier, 2026-10-27). It is rebuilding the portal in a new environment, replacing the affected authentication system with an external identity provider and limiting portal access to customer IP addresses with mandatory multi-factor authentication.
