CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS and Panorama: the PHP2Shell flaws affect every release below its train's hotfix through the management web interface, and Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces; all twenty hotfixes are out

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Update28 Oct 2026 03:38 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryprioritycvesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodytagssources

Palo Alto Networks' advisory now says, as read on 2026-10-28, that active exploitation has been observed targeting the PAN-OS management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation; severity is Critical with urgency Highest (CVSS-B 9.2, up from 8.7 for availability impact only), and the priority moves from notable to high.

Palo Alto Networks' advisory now states that active exploitation has been observed targeting the Palo Alto Networks management interface exposed to the internet (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28). A copy of the page taken on 2026-10-27 at 17:10 UTC said instead that very limited exploitation had been observed (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-27); the vendor timeline records no change of wording, and its entries of 2026-10-27 are two removals of hotfix estimated dates and the 16:40 UTC change that raised the severity to Critical and the urgency to Highest (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28). The vendor score is now CVSS-B 9.2 with high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability when management is reachable from the internet, and 7.7 when it is reachable only from an adjacent network; the earlier text scored availability impact only (8.7) and knew of no exploitation. The advisory names no actor, victim or post-exploitation behaviour. CISA's catalog flags both PHP flaws with forensic triage requirements (CISA KEV, 2026-10-27). The hotfix table has moved on since the previous record: as read on 2026-10-28, fourteen builds are released and six are due by 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).

Sources: Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, Impact of Critical Vulnerabilities in PHP on Palo Alto Networks Products) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-23) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-24) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-25) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, revised 2026-10-27) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, 2026-10-27) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 (threat brief, revised 2026-10-25) · PHP (security advisory) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, Internet Archive copy of 2026-10-27 17:10 UTC) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.27) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, as read on 2026-10-29) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, as read on 2026-10-29) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory, as read on 2026-10-30) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (advisory record with revision history, as read on 2026-10-30) · Dream Research (report on the chained PHP2Shell and Fragnesia exploit against PAN-OS, updated 2026-10-29) · Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 (threat brief, updated 2026-10-29)
NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, NetScaler ADC and Gateway: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the management GUI on the NSIP, management-enabled SNIPs and the cluster IP of every supported version; fixed in 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32 and the FIPS and NDcPP builds

First published 2026-10-23 · open finding →

Update28 Oct 2026 03:37 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Citrix revised bulletin CTX697263 on 2026-10-27 to name the fixed builds (14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, the 14.1-FIPS and the 13.1-FIPS and NDcPP builds), which CERT-FR restates; no source reports an attack on NetScaler.

Citrix revised bulletin CTX697263 on 2026-10-27 to name fixed builds: NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.49 and later, 13.1-64.32 and later of 13.1, ADC 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS and later, and ADC 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 and later (Citrix, 2026-10-22). CERT-FR's notice of 2026-10-27 lists the same first fixed builds for ADC and Gateway (CERT-FR, 2026-10-27). Neither page says NetScaler has been attacked, and no source reports an attack on it.

Sources: NetScaler Product Security (Citrix Tech Zone) · Citrix security bulletin CTX697263 · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · CERT-FR

04Action items15 items

  • Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • List every appliance and management server whose web interface embeds PHP (firewalls, network access control and security consoles), take each interface off the internet and install its vendor's PHP2Shell fix, because Dream Research reports Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewalls rooted through an exposed management interface.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Inventory Joomla sites for the Balbooa Gridbox page builder and update every one to 2.20.5.0, which also closes an unauthenticated file deletion and three further flaws fixed on 2026-11-04 and, from 2.20.4.2, two unauthenticated SQL injections, CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, and the unauthenticated blind SQL injection in the front-end blog author parameter fixed in 2.20.3.1, present in every earlier build, 2.20.3 and 2.20.2.3 included. Anything below 2.20.2 is also exposed to the exploited follow-up batch, which 2.20.1 does not close.
    FindingCVE-2026-61425 +11→
  • On any site that ran Gridbox 2.20.1 or earlier while internet-reachable, review the Super User list and administrator-group members, remove accounts that entered an admin group through self-registration rather than an explicit administrative action, and review template files and the web root for changes, with particular attention to files written since 20 July, when the cookie bypass was disclosed.
    FindingCVE-2026-61425 +11→
  • List every third-party script domain on the public websites your organisation, its agencies and its hosting suppliers run, and remove or re-verify each whose provider has shut down, because DeadTag buys exactly those expired domains.
    FindingDeadTag: expired tag domains send visitors to…→
  • Update every Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x runtime to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, including the Node binary inside container images (a Dockerfile that pins 24.22.0 keeps the flaw until the pin changes), and upgrade the PyPI Brotli package to 1.2.1 and brotlicffi to 1.2.1.0 wherever either is installed; judge a Node.js build by its release version, because process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched builds too, and move any application on an end-of-life Node.js line to a supported release. On every WordPress host, upgrade the operating system's libbrotli package to a patched revision (check the package revision, because Debian and Ubuntu backport the fix into 1.1.0) and rebuild WordPress container images, since the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable libbrotli1 when Patchstack wrote.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable. On every VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager apply Broadcom's workaround, KB460732 on 9.1.1 and KB460734 on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, until its patch ships. Upgrade every Splunk Enterprise 10.0 instance to 10.2 or higher and disable or remove the Splunk Visual Exporter app on every Splunk Enterprise instance, because the upgrade does not remediate it, and install Citrix hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR or 2605.1-3 on Unicon eLux Scout.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 lists every PAN-OS hotfix for this flaw as released.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Take the management interface of every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall and Panorama off the internet now by restricting it to a jump box or trusted internal addresses, because Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces, and install the hotfix for your maintenance release, which Palo Alto's table lists for every line from 10.2.7 to 12.2.4 (11.2.10-h17 adds the Brotli fix).
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Rotate the directory bind account, HA replication keys, certificate private keys and device authentication keys of every PAN-OS firewall and Panorama that was reachable from the internet while unpatched and shows a PHP web shell or a tunnel, because the chain Dream Research recovered harvested exactly those from rooted firewalls, and the hotfix does not remove a web shell or tunnel already in place.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Update every Magento Open Source and Adobe Commerce store, those on 2.4.9 included, to the 2026-jul fix in bulletin APSB26-73, then check for compromise: any script file in the custom-options upload directory, administrator accounts nobody created and loader scripts in CMS blocks, because a store that ran an unpatched build since March 2026 may already hold a webshell that the update does not remove.
    FindingCVE-2026-48356→
  • Install the HPE ClearPass 6.14.1, 6.12.8 or 6.11.16 hotfix patch for CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 on every ClearPass Policy Manager node from the HPE Networking Support Portal, and until it is installed take the guest portal and the CLI and web management interfaces off public networks, confining management to a dedicated layer 2 segment or behind firewall policy.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Upgrade every Cisco Expressway-C, Expressway-E and Expressway Select unit to 15.5.21, including units already moved to X15.5.20 for CVE-2026-76466, which Cisco's table does not name as the PHP2Shell fix, and until then apply the workaround in bug CSCwx37062; take any Duo Access Gateway to 3.2.0 and any Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul or Unified Industrial Wireless Software to 26.2.1.9.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Install NetScaler ADC and Gateway 14.1-73.49, 13.1-64.32, 14.1-FIPS 14.1-73.49 FIPS or 13.1-FIPS and 13.1-NDcPP 13.1.37.286 (or later) on every appliance whose NSIP, a management-enabled SNIP or the cluster IP answers on its GUI or API, internet-reachable ones first; until each has its build, restrict GUI and API access on those addresses to trusted administrative hosts with ACLs, keeping NetScaler Console access working.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-28T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 5 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Window 26 h (gap 24.0 h to 2026-10-27T0256Z-intel, normal cadence, no outage backfill). entities/registry.yaml (672 KB) was grepped per key instead of read whole; the 14-day prior_coverage.json (70 records) was read in full. Slice build: S1 and S2 excluded 0 sources by the two-previous-fires rule, S3 excluded 1, S4 took its whole 14-source pool. No intel drops, so no S5. Every slice ledger row came back attempted (17, 22, 14 and 14 records); no continuation was needed.

Verification. Iterations 1 to 7 each returned NEEDS_FIXES (their findings and remediations are in the record above) and the first CLEAN landed at the 8-iteration cap, so no confirmation pass was possible: the run publishes on that single CLEAN as a fail-open and the waiver is recorded. Open advisories, all pre-existing wording or length from earlier fires and left to the quality audit: the Gridbox entry's legacy em dashes, its re-floated high priority and the CVE-2026-61425 CNA score difference (9.4 against the discloser's 10.0), and the PHP entry's length on a non-deep-dive.

What this fire changed. Five new entries (Cisco PHP2Shell advisory, HPE ClearPass PHP2Shell, the CISA-listed Adobe Commerce upload flaw CVE-2026-48356, ARA-Region Lyss-Limpachtal, DeadTag) and nine changelog records. The two that matter most: Palo Alto's advisory of 2026-10-27 now states active exploitation against internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces (PAN-OS entry notable to high, PHP entry stays critical with the statement added), and CISA's KEV listing of the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 on 2026-10-27 moved the Node2Shell entry to exploited and high.

KEV rows (kev-window.txt).

  • CVE-2026-111497: COVERED-STALE on two entries, both given update records (Node2Shell entry; the .NET entry, whose CVE record now carries exploited, cisa-kev and says Microsoft's own record still read not exploited on 2026-10-25).
  • CVE-2026-48356 (Adobe Commerce and Magento upload flaw, KEV 2026-10-27): NOT COVERED, shipped as a notable entry. It was first held back as borderline (CISA's listing and Adobe's bulletin give no exploitation detail, no constituency nexus); the verifier then found Sansec's PolyShell reporting, which the CVE record itself links: attacks since 2026-03-19, a mass wave on 2026-03-30 and the fix timeline (2.4.9 on 2026-05-12, supported-line backport 2026-07-14). The entry now rests on Sansec, Adobe and CISA together, and the store already carries four Adobe Commerce or Magento entries.
  • No RANSOMWARE rows.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md). ARX Group SA (Aurora leak-site claim): held, unchanged: S2 and S4 searched in German, Italian and English and read Inside IT, Netzwoche, SRF, Blick, ICTjournal, NZZ, RTS and swisscybersecurity.net; no ARX, SBB or ASTRA/USTRA statement and no Swiss press report exist, expiry 2026-11-07. The 2026-10-14 strike of the ARA Lyss row is overtaken by Inside IT's report of 2026-10-27 and the new ARA Lyss entry.

Supersessions and corrections. Palo Alto's statement replaces the PAN-OS entry's "no malicious exploitation" text and its availability-only score (8.7 to 9.2); the PHP entry's "no source ties a named CVE to a production compromise" now carries the Palo Alto exception. Camping.Care: a second customer's notice says the supplier is investigating the cause and does not mention PHP, so the entry now says the PHP link rests on SRF, Blick and TCS. Manno: the entry's "claim could not be corroborated, no dataset" statements are replaced by Inside IT's report that about 30 GB were published (single source, Risikomonitor's analysis unverified, rating B3). IDC Frontier: the seventh report names the cause, so "intrusion route not public" is replaced.

Contradictions and borderline includes.

  • Contradiction: Palo Alto's exploitation wording. An Internet Archive copy of the advisory taken 2026-10-27 17:10 UTC says "very limited exploitation", the page read 2026-10-28 says "active exploitation ... exposed to the internet", and the vendor timeline records no such change; the PAN-OS and PHP entries state both and tie neither to the 16:40 UTC revision.
  • Contradiction: Adobe's bulletin APSB26-73 (2026-07-14, updated 2026-08-11) says no exploits are known for CVE-2026-48356, while Sansec reports attacks since 2026-03-19 and CISA lists the flaw as exploited; Adobe's CVE record scores it 9.3 where the bulletin says 9.6. The entry states both.
  • Contradiction: HPE HPESBNW05171 names ClearPass 6.14.1 and 6.11.16 as versions "providing some level of mitigation" in its workaround text, while its affected list covers 6.14.1 and 6.11.16 and below and its remediation names hotfix patches for both; the entry quotes the bulletin and does not resolve it.
  • Borderline include: Balbooa Gridbox CVE-2026-102788 and CVE-2026-102789, an unauthenticated read-side SQL injection with no exploitation report, folded into the July Gridbox entry as an update record (the store's pattern for later Gridbox batches, which moved its action to 2.20.4.2). Kept under the "otherwise" limb of PD-11 (b), the leg that holds being a two-file fix diff that hands over the technique; the July Gridbox flaws were exploited, these two are not reported exploited, and no Swiss nexus is established.

Single-source and reduced-confidence inclusions.

  • ARA Lyss-Limpachtal: Inside IT relays Risikomonitor's analysis; DeXpose carries the claim; C3, routine, no encryption mapped because no source states it.
  • Cisco, HPE ClearPass, Balbooa (with mySites.guru, on the Gridbox update): vendor first-party; Cisco and HPE carry cvss: n/a or the vendor's score only.
  • Adobe Commerce CVE-2026-48356: the exploitation history rests on Sansec's own telemetry and scans (a security vendor) with CISA's listing and Adobe's bulletin; confidence high, reliability B.
  • DeadTag: Report URI and iVerify published jointly, so one account from two vantage points, credibility 2.

borderline-drop lines.

  • Gotenberg CVE-2026-42589 (VulnCheck canary telemetry, 1,358 events): internal document-conversion service, five-month-old flaw, not in CISA KEV, no established constituency exposure.
  • Oracle October CPU, 90 unauthenticated rows at CVSS 9.0 or higher (73 distinct CVE ids) against the 12 in the existing entry's title: the entry states the full tally, the CPU is applied as a whole and none is reported exploited; not widened. Oracle Alert CVE-2026-109618 rev 2 Oracle Communications rows: telecom signalling products, no nexus (Secure Backup and Solaris are already in the OT-products entry).
  • Cisco eMudhra informational (revised 2026-10-27): vendor-status churn on a covered entry that already carries the Cisco rows.
  • Chrome 156.0.8078.73/.74 (52 fixes, four Critical), Mozilla MFSA 2026-118 to 122, Apple iOS 27.2, 26.7.2 and 18.7.11 (162 CVEs), GLPI 11.0.9 and 10.0.27, Joomla extension releases of 2026-10-26/27, EUVD criticals (Pie Register, llama.cpp ggml-rpc, OpenRemote): none reported exploited, no constituency nexus.
  • Tailscale and headscale audit by Cyberdione Labs ("Tailworm", fixed in v1.104.4): needs an approved peer whose policy allows forwarding, no CVE, no exploitation, constituency exposure not established.
  • Yoba (Check Point, fake GitHub AI-app projects with DLL sideloading): commodity technique, no constituency specificity.
  • Arctic Wolf on Microsoft Teams external-chat impersonation: known technique, primary dated 2026-10-26 outside the window, Swiss relay only.
  • HMICFRS inspection of police and fire and rescue cyber posture: UK regulator report, awareness level, no Swiss obligation.
  • Kaspersky managed-Kubernetes isolation chain (provider anonymised, fixed), EDK II CVE-2026-97631 (the 2026-10-25 audit's reopen conditions are unmet), Popcorn Time updater (sinkholed since March, no exploitation), Sysdig pickle research, Bishop Fox PHP2Shell guidance (marginal delta on an entry that already carries KEV, public exploit and hardening): no change to what a Swiss SOC does.
  • Swiss Ice Hockey Federation MYSIHF (valid-account theft, private federation), BACS weekly review week 43 (WhatsApp account takeover, consumer fraud; week 42 was also not published): no public-sector nexus.
  • Moldova government digital services (about 750,000 records through unauthenticated services, no service or flaw named), University of Copenhagen test environment, GMO Onamae Desktop Cloud (Japan), Navigate360 / Canadian Crime Stoppers (investigation opened by the Privacy Commissioner), UNM Health, ENGIE, Medienwerkstatt Sulgen: out of nexus or no vector, actor or behaviour beyond the impact. Leak-site claims without victim or A/B-press confirmation (ECOM, SunTechnics Fabrisolar, Bristol City Council, OCMW Machelen, Alliance Police Nationale) stay out (PD-6).
  • Convertr / Plausible CE CVE-2026-8467 (Magecart skimmer, suspected entry): suspected only, out of nexus; a pointer for the next audit.

Sources. karimi-honeypot-data promoted to active (promotion_due). Two candidates added because published entries cite them: ellio-threat-research, jfrog-security-research. Not added: Eye Security Research and Eclypsium (S3 leads, unused), risikomonitor-news and hacksnack.ch (S2 and S4 leads, reliability C and D, relays only). Recipe notes recorded for hpe-networking-psirt (changes.csv), cisco-psirt (feed), paloalto-psirt (advisory JSON), inside-it-ch (__NEXT_DATA__), apa-ots, ransomware-live and databreaches-net. connectwise-trust-center and ec-digital-strategy-newsroom stay 403 on every transport; a 403 never demotes.

Registry. Added incident:ara-region-lyss-limpachtal-ransomware-2026-09, campaign:deadtag, tool:coruna and tool:darksword, the aliases Brotli2Shell, HTTP2Shell and Broccoli2Shell on tool:node2shell, and seven product entities through sync_products.py (five from the new entries, Bun and Istio from the Node2Shell update).

Watchlist: products checked=0, hits=0; suppliers checked=0, hits=0 (no watchlists configured).

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport); ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 on every transport, third run); resecurity (empty JavaScript shell, newest post 2026-10-14 by search); golem-security (cookie wall); apa-ots (feed holds only the 15 newest releases, no lookback sweep possible); nau-ch, push-security, novee-security (nothing in the horizon; novee-security marketing only, demotion candidate); Juniper PHP2Shell reference advisory (Salesforce shell on every reader) and QNAP QSA-26-18 (reader returned navigation only) were not re-read, so any QNAP revision after 2026-10-27 is unverified; the Citrix community post is 403 on every direct transport and was read only through the reader.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-27
item.description:
• PHP2Shell hits NetModule routers (fix: NRSW 5.0.0.105), macmon, Schneider, B&R, HMS, Wibu and Oracle products. Industrial, building and network-access vendors have published their own notices for the PHP flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, which CISA added to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Belden says all versions of NetModule NRSW, the router software of the Bern-headquartered NetModule AG, are affected up to release 5.0.0.104 and recommends upgrading to release 5.0.0.105, with disabling the web interface as the fallback; macmon 6.x and 7.x, Schneider Electric Security Expert and Control Engineering, B&R APROL, HMS Netbiter, Wibu-Systems CodeMeter License Central and Oracle Secure Backup and Solaris 11 carry fixes or remediations at varying stages. →
  • Gheist abuses stolen GitHub tokens to dump secrets through Actions; GitHub's hold covers public repositories only. Wiz Research has tracked since 2026-09-15 an automated campaign, Gheist, that uses stolen GitHub tokens to commit a secret-dumping Actions workflow to every repository each token can reach, more than 13,500 branches from more than 850 accounts. GitHub's approval hold of 2026-07-28 stops the workflow on public github.com repositories, but not on private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server, where Wiz saw the runs complete and the organizations' own workflows assume AWS roles on the attacker branches. →
  • Camping.Care booking data stolen: TCS and a second campsite warn of WhatsApp fraud; PHP link not vendor-confirmed. TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 guests after data was stolen at Camping.Care, the Dutch supplier of the booking system for all TCS campsites; TCS confirmed the theft to SRF on 2026-10-26, SRF reports it in connection with the PHP security hole and Blick says the attackers used the two critical PHP flaws, though no source names a CVE or the entry point. Names, telephone numbers and reservation numbers are already used in fraudulent WhatsApp messages; TCS says account and IBAN data were not affected and the hole is closed. A second customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, has warned its guests of the same fraud in a notice that says Camping.care is still investigating the cause and does not mention PHP. →

Active threats, incidents & disclosures 2Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 8Action items 12

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures2 items

NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Camping.Care booking system (TCS Camping): customer and booking data stolen in connection with the PHP flaws, with real reservation numbers already used in WhatsApp fraud and 15,000 guests warned as a precaution

TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 guests as a precaution because the provider of its booking system, Camping.Care, suffered a data theft; TCS confirmed to the SRF consumer programme Espresso on 2026-10-26 that fraudsters could steal customer and booking information, and SRF reports the case in connection with the worldwide PHP security hole (SRF, 2026-10-26). Blick describes Camping.Care as a Dutch company whose booking system handles reservations for all campsites of the Touring Club Schweiz, writes, citing SRF, that the hackers used the critical PHP flaw to steal customer and booking data and that Camping.Care is not the only software supplier hit (Blick, 2026-10-26). No source names the CVE identifiers, the entry point, the date of the intrusion or an actor, and TCS says the hole has since been closed (SRF, 2026-10-26). The stolen data already in criminal use includes, among other data, names, telephone numbers and reservation numbers: guests received fraudulent WhatsApp messages that refer to existing reservations (SRF, 2026-10-26). TCS says account details and IBANs were not affected and that credit card data is not stored in the booking system (SRF, 2026-10-26). A second customer, Campingplatz Hüttenberg in canton Thurgau, told its guests in a notice (page date 2026-10-23) that Camping.care had informed it of WhatsApp messages to guests of several campsites that contain real booking information and a link, that Camping.care is investigating the cause and that booking data must be assumed to have been used without authorisation; the notice does not mention PHP, and Netzwoche points out that it does not say whether the attackers used one of the PHP flaws (Campingplatz Hüttenberg, 2026-10-23; Netzwoche, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
The guests who booked through the TCS campsite booking system, about 15,000 of whom TCS has warned, and any other customer of the Camping.Care platform, one of which, Campingplatz Hüttenberg, has warned its own guests; Blick says Camping.Care is not the only software supplier hit (Blick, 2026-10-26; Netzwoche, 2026-10-27).
Detection
The only signal the sources describe is on the recipient side, unsolicited WhatsApp messages that quote a real reservation with the correct name, telephone number and reservation number; no source gives intrusion telemetry from the supplier's systems (SRF, 2026-10-26).

Triage: TCS Camping sends no automated booking details, payment requests or reservation links over WhatsApp, so a WhatsApp message of that kind that quotes a genuine reservation is the fraud, however accurate its details (SRF, 2026-10-26).

Defender takeaway
For a booking, ticketing or citizen-portal application that a supplier runs on PHP, ask the supplier in writing whether its runtime was updated to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 (CISA, 2026-10-26) and whether customer data was accessed before that, because SRF, Blick and a TCS spokesperson tie this theft to the PHP flaws (SRF, 2026-10-26; Blick, 2026-10-26; watson.ch, 2026-10-26), although a customer's notice says the supplier is still investigating the cause (Campingplatz Hüttenberg, 2026-10-23) and no source says how the intrusion happened; and tell the people whose data the supplier holds that a message quoting their real booking details is no proof that it comes from you.

Gheist: stolen GitHub tokens plant a secret-dumping workflow in every repository they reach; GitHub's July approval hold stops it on public github.com repositories but not on private ones or GitHub Enterprise Server

Wiz Research has tracked since 2026-09-15 a campaign it calls Gheist, after the user agent on its API calls, that uses stolen GitHub access tokens to create a branch and commit a workflow named sync-check in every repository each token can reach: more than 13,500 planted branches from more than 850 compromised accounts, from personal projects to private enterprise repositories (Wiz, 2026-10-25). Wiz traces the tokens to infostealer logs and earlier supply-chain compromises (Wiz, 2026-10-25). The push triggers the workflow, which prints the repository's secrets, and those of any deployment environment, into its own run log; GitHub masks secret values only when they appear verbatim, so a base32-encoded value prints in full, the tool downloads the log through the GitHub API and deletes the run seconds later, and because the secrets leave through GitHub's own API there is no attacker domain or connection to block (Wiz, 2026-10-25). In enterprise organizations the tool cycled through the tokens of several users and automation accounts within minutes and cloned private repositories before planting the workflow; hours later cloud credentials from the same organization were used to enumerate AWS Secrets Manager (Wiz, 2026-10-25). Around 2026-10-19 the second variant added a job for repositories with a self-hosted runner that searches the host, and through the Docker socket its root filesystem, for tokens, private keys, environment files and Terraform state; Wiz calls the job buggy (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Since 2026-07-28 GitHub holds potentially malicious workflow runs in public repositories until a collaborator approves them, and every public Gheist run Wiz checked stayed held; the hold applies to public repositories on github.com only and not to GitHub Enterprise Server (Wiz, 2026-10-25; GitHub, 2026-07-28). In private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments Wiz saw runs on the attacker branches complete and be deleted, and cloud audit logs showed the organizations' own workflows running on those branches and assuming AWS roles (Wiz, 2026-10-25). As of 2026-10-24 Wiz called the attack ongoing and distinct from the earlier GhostAction campaign (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Exposure
Organizations whose developers or automation accounts hold GitHub tokens that an infostealer or earlier compromise could have exposed, above all with private repositories, GitHub Enterprise Server, cloud OIDC workflows or self-hosted runners (Wiz, 2026-10-25).
Detection
In GitHub audit logs, workflow runs on a branch named ci-sync- plus six random characters that were deleted within a minute of completing, and API activity with the user agent gheist; in cloud audit logs, role assumptions whose OIDC subject names such a branch, which shows Actions ran on an attacker branch even where GitHub logs are not collected; on self-hosted runners, the helper files Wiz lists (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Triage: the planted commit is unsigned but authored as the token's owner, so the author name alone proves nothing; one new workflow file with a fixed commit message on a branch the owner did not create is the pattern (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

Defender takeaway
Rotate every secret available to a repository where a planted branch exists, revoke the tokens that pushed the commits and check their owners' devices for infostealers, treat a self-hosted runner host and its instance role as compromised if a planted branch ran there, and scope OIDC trust to protected branches or environments with required reviewers on environments that hold production secrets (Wiz, 2026-10-25).

NetModule AG is headquartered in Bern, Switzerland (Belden, 2022-03-14). Belden's macmon 6.x and 7.x use PHP in the web interface: a patch for 7.x is in the service portal, 6.x must move to 7.x, and the HTTPS web interface and guest portal must not be reachable from the internet unprotected (Belden, 2026-10-22).

Schneider Electric lists EcoStruxure Security Expert (fixed in 1.48.4.0), ProLeiT LINEoptimize (remediation through ProLeiT support) and EcoStruxure Control Engineering, where its revision of 2026-10-26 gives an automatic update if the hosting virtual machine can reach the debian.org and sury.org repositories and a Schneider patch otherwise (Schneider Electric, 2026-10-26; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26). B&R says APROL up to R 4.4-65 is affected, with patches planned for 2026-10-26 and 2026-10-29 (B&R, 2026-10-23). Expel's Marcus Hutchins calls it by far the highest-quality confirmation of in-the-wild exploitation he has seen (BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26).

VulnCheck's page, updated as of 2026-10-26, extends its working exploit to mod_php on PHP 8.2.28 to 8.2.34 and 8.3.22 to 8.3.35 as well as 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 (VulnCheck, 2026-10-26). Huntress's analysis of 2026-10-26 reads the activity as scripted tooling steered by an operator, rates LLM involvement low to medium on its own telemetry, adds a detection for service principals that assign themselves or a sibling a directory role, and notes that Graph reads leave no Entra audit record.

Huntress published its analysis of what drove the 2026-10-15 activity on 2026-10-26, working from Entra sign-in and directory audit logs in the tenants it monitors. It says its telemetry aligns with Microsoft's Storm-0940 and ARTEX account without independently confirming it, that it is highly confident an operator, a person or an LLM, adapted the tooling between runs, and that its confidence that an LLM was involved in the escalation tooling is low to medium on its own telemetry and medium to high once Microsoft's attribution is included (Huntress, 2026-10-26). Its evidence for adaptation: a certificate upload that failed on a thumbprint mismatch ended one run with no retry, and the next run 55 seconds later retried the same error with growing waits until it worked; in a second tenant that refused removal of the Global Administrator role, the actor granted a different role to a sibling principal and the original service principal was then deleted (Huntress, 2026-10-26). Microsoft Graph reads are not recorded in the Entra audit log and no victim Huntress knows of had Graph activity logging enabled, so a clean audit log does not show that no Graph access took place (Huntress, 2026-10-26). Huntress recommends alerting when a service principal assigns itself Global Administrator or Privileged Role Administrator, deletes itself, or when one vendor principal grants a role to a sibling, and turning on Graph activity logs where licensing allows (Huntress, 2026-10-26).

Apple's iOS and iPadOS 18.7.11 of 2026-10-26 deliver the CVE-2026-86950 fix to iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation, four weeks after the 26.7.1 releases that did not list those devices; the flaw remains exploited against targeted individuals and KEV-listed.

Apple's security content for iOS 18.7.11 and iPadOS 18.7.11, released 2026-10-26, lists CVE-2026-86950 as fixed for iPhone XS, iPhone XS Max, iPhone XR and iPad 7th generation and repeats Apple's statement that it is aware of a report of exploitation in an extremely sophisticated attack against specific targeted individuals on versions of iOS before iOS 27 (Apple, 2026-10-26). The notes for iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1 of 2026-09-28 list the fix for iPhone 11 and later and for iPad models from the iPad 8th generation, and the CISA catalog record for the flaw names no other Apple document, so in the documents these sources name the fix reaches those four device families four weeks after the others (Apple, 2026-09-28; CISA, 2026-09-29). SANS Internet Storm Center says this round delivers the corresponding iOS 18 patches for a flaw patched a month earlier and that no new vulnerability is marked as already exploited (SANS ISC, 2026-10-27).

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

First published 2026-10-24 · open finding →

Update27 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessummarytags

NCSC Switzerland rates exploitation of the Brotli flaw unknown with a proof of concept available and names rejecting Content-Encoding: br as the interim measure; Palo Alto lists PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (hotfixes due by 2026-10-30), and PHP for Windows and Ubuntu shipped fixes. Still no source reports exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration.

NCSC Switzerland (BACS) published advisory 13105 on 2026-10-26 on the Brotli decoder flaw: it names Node.js, Microsoft .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages and Bun among the affected dependents, rated the exploitation status unknown with a proof of concept available in its text of that day, and gives as the temporary measure disabling Brotli decoding of untrusted data and rejecting Content-Encoding: br until patched, with services restarted and containers rebuilt after updating (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26).

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS 12.2 before 12.2.4-h1, 12.1 before 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.1.10-h3, and 11.2 before 11.2.4-h23, 11.2.7-h23, 11.2.10-h17, 11.2.13-h4 and 11.2.16-h1 as affected, but only on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls that have inspection of Brotli-compressed traffic and TLS decryption enabled on the dataplane; PAN-OS 11.1 and 10.2 and the management interface are not affected, and the hotfixes carry estimated dates from 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26). Brotli encoding is disabled by default in PAN-OS 11.2.4 and later, the command show system setting brotli shows whether a firewall is exposed (Enabled: yes), and set system setting brotli-encoding disable is the vendor's interim mitigation; Palo Alto rates the urgency moderate and is not aware of malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26).

PHP rebuilt its Windows packages as 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 on 2026-10-26 with Brotli 1.2.1; the vulnerable decoder is reachable there through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled, which cURL leaves off by default (PHP, 2026-10-26). Ubuntu lists brotli fixes for 26.10 (1.2.0-4ubuntu0.1), 26.04 LTS (1.2.0-3ubuntu0.1), 24.04 LTS (1.1.0-2ubuntu0.1) and 22.04 LTS (1.0.9-2ubuntu0.1), marks 20.04 LTS as needing evaluation and its nodejs package on 20.04, which vendors Brotli, as vulnerable (Ubuntu, 2026-10-26).

Sources: Node.js project · Node.js project (release v22.23.4) · Node.js project (release v24.22.1) · Node.js project (release v26.12.1) · Google Brotli · ENISA EUVD · Imperva Threat Research · OpenSourceMalware · Envoy Proxy (security advisory) · .NET Blog (Microsoft) · Microsoft (dotnet/announcements, CVE-2026-111497 advisory) · NCSC Switzerland (BACS, Cyber Security Hub advisory 13105) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status) · PHP (news archive, updated Windows builds for the Brotli fix) · Ubuntu Security (CVE-2026-111497) · CISA (alert, KEV additions) · ELLIO Threat Research Lab · Tenable Research · JFrog Security Research · Akamai Security Intelligence Group · Cisco PSIRT (advisory, Vulnerabilities in node.js Affecting Cisco Products) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, timeline of 2026-10-29) · Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0008.1) · Datadog Security Labs · Zscaler ThreatLabz · Patchstack · Splunk (advisory SVD-2026-1015) · Citrix (security bulletin CTX697300) · Keycloak project (release notes 26.8.2)

QNAP's advisory table now lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756 and TVR OS 1.0.5 as resolved, leaving Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) without a fix, and no longer names QuMagie as affected; CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26.

Update27 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelcvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytags

CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26; no source reports an attack on NetScaler, and Citrix's bulletin still names no fixed build, so restricting management access remains the control.

CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, as flaws in PHP rather than as a NetScaler finding (CISA KEV, 2026-10-26). No source reports an attack on NetScaler through them. Citrix's bulletin CTX697263, whose revision history ends on 2026-10-22, still lists NetScaler ADC and Gateway as impacted, points to the Tech Zone post for mitigation and names no fixed build (Citrix, 2026-10-22), so the management-interface restriction stays the control until Citrix lists a fixed build.

Sources: NetScaler Product Security (Citrix Tech Zone) · Citrix security bulletin CTX697263 · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · CERT-FR

04Action items12 items

  • Update the PHP runtime, not the CMS or its plugins, on every internet-facing server and container image to 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 or 8.2.35 or to your distribution's patched package, restart PHP-FPM, Apache and every long-running worker, rebuild images, and confirm the running version, because a distribution backport can keep the old version string; isolate any application that cannot be updated from public networks until it is.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • After updating, set session.upload_progress.enabled=0 on every PHP host and keep it there until PHP's next regular bugfix release: CVE-2026-115560, which the October releases do not fix, needs session upload progress to be enabled.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • List every appliance and management server whose web interface embeds PHP (firewalls, network access control and security consoles), take each interface off the internet and install its vendor's PHP2Shell fix, because Dream Research reports Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS firewalls rooted through an exposed management interface.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Upgrade every Belden NetModule NRSW router to 5.0.0.105, and where that is not yet possible disable its web interface after confirming SSH access, with the CLI settings http.status=0 and https.status=0; patch macmon 7.x from the service portal and move macmon 6.x to 7.x, and keep the web interfaces of both off networks that are not trusted.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Update every Node.js 22.x, 24.x and 26.x runtime to 22.23.4, 24.22.1 or 26.12.1, including the Node binary inside container images (a Dockerfile that pins 24.22.0 keeps the flaw until the pin changes), and upgrade the PyPI Brotli package to 1.2.1 and brotlicffi to 1.2.1.0 wherever either is installed; judge a Node.js build by its release version, because process.versions.brotli reads 1.2.0 on patched builds too, and move any application on an end-of-life Node.js line to a supported release. On every WordPress host, upgrade the operating system's libbrotli package to a patched revision (check the package revision, because Debian and Ubuntu backport the fix into 1.1.0) and rebuild WordPress container images, since the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable libbrotli1 when Patchstack wrote.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Update every Envoy proxy that has the Brotli decompressor configured to v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 or v1.36.12; the advisory names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable. On every VMware Cloud Foundation SDDC Manager apply Broadcom's workaround, KB460732 on 9.1.1 and KB460734 on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, until its patch ships. Upgrade every Splunk Enterprise 10.0 instance to 10.2 or higher and disable or remove the Splunk Visual Exporter app on every Splunk Enterprise instance, because the upgrade does not remediate it, and install Citrix hotfix 2609.1, 2508 CU2 LTSR or 2605.1-3 on Unicon eLux Scout.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • On every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall on PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 or 11.2 that has TLS decryption enabled, run show system setting brotli and, where it returns Enabled: yes, run set system setting brotli-encoding disable until the hotfix for the release is installed; Palo Alto's timeline of 2026-10-29 lists every PAN-OS hotfix for this flaw as released.
    FindingCVE-2026-111497→
  • Take the management interface of every PA-Series and VM-Series firewall and Panorama off the internet now by restricting it to a jump box or trusted internal addresses, because Palo Alto reports active exploitation against internet-exposed management interfaces, and install the hotfix for your maintenance release, which Palo Alto's table lists for every line from 10.2.7 to 12.2.4 (11.2.10-h17 adds the Brotli fix).
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Rotate the directory bind account, HA replication keys, certificate private keys and device authentication keys of every PAN-OS firewall and Panorama that was reachable from the internet while unpatched and shows a PHP web shell or a tunnel, because the chain Dream Research recovered harvested exactly those from rooted firewalls, and the hotfix does not remove a web shell or tunnel already in place.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
  • Push iOS and iPadOS 26.7.1, macOS Tahoe 26.7.1 and macOS Sequoia 15.8.1 through device management now, and iOS and iPadOS 18.7.11 to every iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation, starting with the devices of staff who could be individually targeted; Apple describes the exploitation only on iOS before iOS 27.
    FindingCVE-2026-86950→
  • In every GitHub organisation your teams or suppliers administer, private repositories and GitHub Enterprise Server included, search for branches named ci-sync- plus six random characters that add only the workflow file sync-check.yml, and for any workflow run on them; for every hit, rotate all repository, organisation and environment secrets that repository could read and revoke the token that pushed the commit, because deleting the run or the branch does not undo the exposure.
    FindingGheist abuses stolen GitHub tokens to dump secrets…→
  • Update every QNAP NAS on QTS, QuTS hero or QuTScloud to the builds of 2026-10-23 (QTS 6.1.0.3656 or 5.2.11.3661, QuTS hero h6.1.0.3656, h6.0.2.3656 (h5.3.x included) or h5.2.11.3661, QuTScloud c5.2.9.3661), every QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) to 3.0.3.1756, every TVR OS to 1.0.5 and every Notes Station 3 to 3.9.15, and every QNE (ADRA) to 1.0.7.q327.
    FindingCVE-2026-109618 +1→
Verification & coverage notes1 run

2026-10-27T0256Z-intel · Sonnet 5.5 · window 26 h · 3 entries published

Verification & coverage notes

Window of 26 h (gap 24.0 h) on a Tuesday with one dominant story: CISA's KEV listing of the PHP2Shell flaws on 2026-10-26 and the first documented code execution against honeypots. The container clock agreed with the network date (skew 0 s); the previous fire (2026-10-26T0256Z-intel, publish ok) was on origin/main. A container restart at about 03:13Z killed the first four research sub-agents before any returned; they were re-spawned once at 03:15Z (their progress and checkpoint files are kept as *.attempt1.* under work/<run-id>/, used as leads only) and all four returned by 03:35Z, so the restart cost about eighteen minutes and no entry depends on the lost work.

  • Published (new, three): the TCS Camping and Camping.Care booking-data theft that SRF and Blick tie to the PHP flaws (notable, PD-11(c): the first Swiss-linked victim report of the exploited PHP flaws, a supplier-borne exposure with a transferable lesson for public bodies whose portals run on PHP suppliers; single-source-victim, TCS's own confirmation, B2); Wiz Research's Gheist campaign, stolen GitHub tokens planting secret-dumping workflows, with GitHub's own changelog confirming that its approval hold covers public repositories on github.com only (notable, PD-11(a) and (d)); and a PHP2Shell vendor-notice entry for industrial, building and network-access products, led by NetModule NRSW (router software of the Bern-headquartered NetModule AG, all versions, no fix, web interface to be disabled) and macmon 6.x/7.x, with Schneider Electric, B&R, HMS, Wibu-Systems, Johnson Controls and Oracle (notable, PD-11(b): no fix and an out-of-band response on an exploit-listed flaw; one entry per estate class as for QNAP and Synology, not one per vendor).
  • Updated (eight changelog records): the main PHP2Shell entry (update: KEV listing and Karimi's honeypot report; the statements that neither flaw is in KEV and that no source ties a confirmed compromise to the flaws were replaced where they stood, the 2026-10-26 section's sentence was narrowed to production systems, the main analysis was held at its previous 1,977 words); PAN-OS (update: nine hotfixes released, one action added); NetScaler (update: KEV listing, no fixed build in Citrix's bulletin); QNAP (update: QVR Surveillance and TVR OS resolved, QuMagie no longer listed); the Brotli entry (update: NCSC.ch advisory 13105, PAN-OS firewalls with Brotli inspection and decryption, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu; one action added); Apple CVE-2026-86950 (update: iOS 18.7.11 fixes iPhone XS, XS Max, XR and iPad 7th generation); ARTEX (update: Seoul police arrest of a criminal group's leader, BleepingComputer names the framework); ConnectWise Cloud Backup (improvement: Huntress's analysis, detections and the Graph logging gap).
  • KEV sweep: CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (COVERED-STALE on four store entries) are dispositioned by the four updates above plus the new vendor-notice entry; no NOT COVERED or MENTION-ONLY row and no RANSOMWARE row (CISA marks ransomware use unknown). The KEV remediation deadline is not carried in any entry.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA row stays held, unchanged and unappended: S4 re-checked it and the ransomware.live record still shows no press link, with no ARX, SBB or ASTRA/USTRA statement and no Swiss press report; the 2026-11-07 expiry stands.
  • Single-source: gheist-stolen-github-tokens-secret-dumping-workflows (Wiz telemetry, B2), original lab research; pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release (vendor's own product, A).
  • borderline-drop: PK Softech and Publica, EDÖB head Lobsiger's SonntagsBlick interview relayed by Inside IT and Ticinonline (2026-10-25 and 26) and Publica's re-stated "no darkweb publication", a conditional possible widening of the proceeding, a re-confirmed status and a breach-notification count; the entry already carries the formal investigation (S2 and S4, same drop as the previous fire).
  • borderline-drop: Medienwerkstatt Sulgen TG (Akira claim, victim confirms ransomware and copied data), private print firm, no public-sector customer stated, no vector or behaviour beyond the impact (incident floor), the only link is the actor already in the Publica entry; University of Copenhagen test-environment breach, out of nexus, no vector.
  • borderline-drop: Cisco Talos on attackers using 25+ legitimate platforms to mail the lure under the brand's own DKIM and DMARC (2026-10-21, first coverage from a rotational lookback), drafted as an entry and dropped after the first verifier pass: six-day-old vendor research with a vendor tally and consumer-retail examples, the lesson is a generic gateway-inspection point and a Tier 2/3 responder changes nothing in the next seven days because of it (PD-11, awareness only).
  • borderline-drop: Arctic Wolf Labs on more than 400 Teams external-chat helpdesk-impersonation cases (2026-10-26); the store carries six Teams-vishing entries and three already carry the external-access allow-list lever; the new content is one audit event name (ChatCreated) and a tenant-pattern description.
  • borderline-drop: CYFIRMA's PHP2Shell advisory (Lazarus-ecosystem actor, 216 hosts, closed I2P channel), single vendor, nobody can check the channel, confidence inconsistent between narrative and evaluation, no Swiss nexus (dropped by the previous fire too); Symantec's AI-honeypot "Skynet" capture and Semperis on Prince of Persia (both lookback), relevant only to bodies that expose model endpoints or indicator-led infrastructure tracking with no European case; Forever Security's planted AGENTS.md (2026-10-22), vendor-run reproduction, success rates are the vendor's claims, delivery of the file unknown.
  • out-of-window: CrowdStrike's report on four actors running Claude Code as an intrusion operator (2026-10-23, recovered through a Hacker News recap of 2026-10-26; the crowdstrike record was not in any slice), primary source three days before the window start and not a rotational lookback; offered to the audit.
  • borderline-drop: Risikomonitor's Swiss unpatched-domain figures (Inside IT, 2026-10-26); scope differs from the 2026-10-22 figure so it is not a trend; Fortinet FG-IR-26-186 and -187 revisions, Synology Hyper Backup "not affected", NetScaler Product Security (no new post readable), Tailscale "Tailworm", Wasmtime sandbox escapes, Chromium Mobile rows in MSRC, Sansec Magecart items, Plex and EG SiteGuard KEV additions (2026-10-20, out of window, consumer or Japan-specific), no delta for the reader or out of scope.
  • Contradiction: S1, S2 and S3 each framed the KEV listing and the honeypot report as separate items; they were merged into one update. S2 read CISA's due date of 2026-10-29 as a signal; it is a US federal obligation and is not carried (PD-13). The Phase 4 re-fetch of two pages read with guessed URL slugs returned 404 (corrected to the URLs in the findings; nothing was cited from a guessed URL).
  • Contradiction: the Palo Alto Brotli advisory (CVE-2026-111497) still shows 12.2.4-h1 and 12.1.7-h11 with 10/28 estimated dates while the PHP2Shell advisory, revised at 2026-10-27T04:03Z, lists both as released; the Brotli entry cites the Brotli advisory as stated and the PAN-OS entry the PHP2Shell one.
  • Candidate sources added: belden-psirt (first-party NetModule and macmon advisories, on no slice source) and karimi-honeypot-data (packet-level exploitation ground truth). Not added: arctic-wolf-labs (its item was dropped), forever-security (no feed, vendor interest) and hacksnack-ch (derivative SME news, offered by S2 and S4). Recipe notes from the source ledgers were appended to the matching sources/sources.json records, among them the BACS card-markup change that breaks the documented split, the Fortinet RSS reset, the SSD Disclosure recipe and the Help Net Security extract behaviour.
  • Reader credit: extract fell through to the metered reader for the CISA alert, the QNAP page and the Dark Reading articles; S4 reported two more on tcs.ch and news.ku.dk.
  • Audit hand-offs: the IDC Frontier entry does not cite the provider's sixth report of 2026-10-18; Eichstätt (Germany, municipal ransomware through an unnamed third-party vulnerability despite two-factor authentication, statements of 2026-10-22 and 23) fell about twelve hours outside the lookback and is a municipal lesson; the main PHP2Shell entry's main analysis (1,977 words) and several others touched this fire remain over the 550-word bound as carried debt, none grown by this fire.
  • Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport, failing on every run since 2026-10-19); ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 on every transport); community.citrix.com Tech Zone NetScaler post (403 on every transport for S1; a later extract read it, last updated 2026-10-22 and still saying fixes are planned for 2026-10-27, so whether they shipped is unconfirmed); rapid7 and cisa.gov all.xml discovery feeds (unreadable); lumen-black-lotus-labs (landing page without a post listing); php.risikomonitor.com (figures render client-side).
  • Watchlist: products checked=0, hits=0; suppliers checked=0, hits=0
  • Essential-coverage: all 21 essential records of S1 and S2 were attempted; none missed.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-26
item.description:
• JPCERT/CC and NICT: attackers decompile the public app, then call internal APIs; AI platforms scan exposed web apps. JPCERT/CC (alert AT-2026-0030, updated 2026-10-23) and NICT describe a wave of personal-data leaks from Japanese web systems in which attackers analyse the published Android app to find API endpoints and keys and then call internal management APIs the app screens never use, place JSP web shells as .war files on application servers behind the public web server, and, per the latest update, run AI penetration-testing platforms (Cairn, CyberStrikeAI, ARTEX) against internet-facing web applications, WSUS servers included. No actor is named, JPCERT/CC says it confirmed AI used to scan for known vulnerabilities and attack through APIs, and Macnica could not confirm AI use. →
  • Microsoft ships out-of-band .NET fixes: hosts updated on 13 October still carry the Windows sockets flaw. Microsoft released .NET 8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3 out of band on 2026-10-25 to fix the Brotli decoder flaw CVE-2026-111497 (CVSS 3.1 8.1, publicly disclosed, rated Exploitation More Likely) and to deliver the corrected fixes for CVE-2026-70197 (Windows sockets memory corruption, CVSS 3.1 8.1) and CVE-2026-102870 (Blazor debugger), which the 2026-10-13 release did not fully address. Brotli exposure needs an application that decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data, which ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not do by default; CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 as exploited since 2026-10-27, although Microsoft's record still said not exploited on 2026-10-25 and no source reports an attack on .NET. Microsoft's record, revised on 2026-11-12, also lists Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2019 to 2025 as affected, with the November 2026 cumulative updates as the fix. →

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

NOTABLENATOA2

Japan's wave of personal-data theft from web systems: JPCERT/CC and NICT describe attackers who decompile the published Android app to find internal APIs, drop JSP web shells as .war files on application servers, and run AI penetration-testing platforms against exposed web applications and WSUS servers

JPCERT/CC's alert of 2026-10-08, updated on 2026-10-23, says that around September 2026 Japanese organisations disclosed a run of personal-data leaks through unauthorised access, and singles out an attack type that may be increasing: systems the operator never expected strangers to reach, such as business-intelligence tools and staff-management systems, were hit alongside public apps (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23). It does not tie them to one method and groups them in five: per-target scanning for known flaws and exposed configuration and backup files; unauthorised calls to application management APIs; the Metabase SQL injection CVE-2026-72898; .war files carrying a JSP web shell that runs commands passed in query parameters, placed on application servers reachable from the public web server; and, added on 2026-10-23, attempts through AI penetration-testing platforms it names as Cairn, CyberStrikeAI and ARTEX, including against exposed WSUS servers (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

In the API case the attackers analyse the published smartphone app to find endpoints and keys, then attack internal APIs the app screens cannot reach: changing user rights, creating accounts, toggling a header or sending malformed tokens to compare responses, and blind NoSQL injection to find account data; some use API keys stolen elsewhere (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23). NICT calls this an app-to-backend attack: the app need not be vulnerable, and backend authentication, authorisation or input-validation faults leak data (NICT, 2026-10-13). On attack servers JPCERT/CC found Android packages, reverse-engineering tools and a Python script that answers requests with HTTP 302 redirects and appears to have been used to test for server-side request forgery (JPCERT/CC Eyes, 2026-10-21).

No source names an actor. JPCERT/CC says it confirmed that the attackers used AI to scan for known vulnerabilities and attack through APIs (JPCERT/CC Eyes, 2026-10-21), while Macnica could not confirm AI use (Recorded Future, 2026-10-22). API-attack access also arrives through Tor exit nodes and residential proxies (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

Exposure
An organisation that publishes a mobile app with a backend API, runs internet-facing web applications, or leaves BI tools, staff-management systems or WSUS servers reachable from the internet (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23); NICT asks operators to inventory public APIs and servers and check their access logs (NICT, 2026-10-13).
Detection
In API and web access logs, calls to internal or management endpoints from clients that never load the app screens, role-change and account-creation calls outside the admin console, one endpoint called in sequence with and without a header or with malformed tokens, blind NoSQL-injection-style probing of account lookups, and use of API keys extracted from the app; in web server telemetry, scans for exposed configuration and backup files and .war deployments to application servers (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

Triage: the app's own User-Agent proves nothing, because JPCERT/CC saw attack requests carrying it; the endpoints called and the sequence (header toggling, malformed tokens, role changes) discriminate, and a TLS fingerprint that matches a generic Python client does not identify the attacker alone (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23).

Defender takeaway
Treat the published app package as public and test the backend for authorisation gaps on internal endpoints (IDOR and BOLA), server-side request forgery, remote code execution and SQL injection (NICT, 2026-10-13). JPCERT/CC's measures are per-endpoint and per-method access control including non-public APIs, expiring least-privilege API tokens with fast revocation, rate limits on login, password reset, SMS and search, no long-lived secrets in apps, and no management functions on the internet (JPCERT/CC, 2026-10-23; JPCERT/CC Eyes, 2026-10-21).

CVE-2026-111497 / CVE-2026-70197, Microsoft .NET: an out-of-band release fixes a Brotli decoder flaw and delivers the Windows sockets fix that the 13 October update did not contain, in 8.0.33, 9.0.22 and 10.0.14 (CVSS 3.1 8.1)

Microsoft released out-of-band security updates for .NET 8, .NET 9 and .NET 10, with .NET 11 Release Candidate 3, on 2026-10-25 (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). .NET Framework is not affected (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-111497 is a buffer overflow in the Brotli decoder that .NET uses and may let an unauthenticated attacker read or corrupt process memory, leading to information disclosure, denial of service or elevation of privilege (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25); Microsoft scores it CVSS 3.1 8.1, marked it publicly disclosed and not exploited on 2026-10-25, and rates it Exploitation More Likely (MSRC, 2026-10-25). Node.js fixed the same CVE on 2026-10-21 (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). Microsoft says an application is exposed only if it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic response decompression that includes Brotli, or the BrotliStream and BrotliDecoder APIs, and that ASP.NET Core and HttpClient do not decompress Brotli by default (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25).

The release also corrects two fixes of 2026-10-13: Microsoft says that release did not fully address CVE-2026-70197 and CVE-2026-102870 (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-70197 is a Windows-only out-of-bounds write: reusing one SocketAsyncEventArgs instance across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets can keep an undersized cached native address buffer, and an unauthenticated attacker can then write out of bounds during ReceiveFromAsync (CVSS 3.1 8.1, high attack complexity) (dotnet/runtime #136445, 2026-10-25); the Security Update Guide rates it not exploited, not publicly disclosed and Exploitation Less Likely (MSRC, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-102870 is code execution in the Blazor WebAssembly debugger when a developer evaluates an expression that involves attacker-controlled application data (CVSS 3.1 8.8, user interaction required); it needs the standalone Server and DevServer package references updated, because updating only the shared runtime is not a substitute (dotnet/announcements #492, 2026-10-25). CVE-2026-114148 is a local privilege escalation through incorrect file ownership in Linux tarballs (CVSS 3.1 7.8), affecting ASP.NET Core tarballs of .NET 8 and 9 and source-built tarballs of .NET 8 to 11 (dotnet/announcements #495, 2026-10-25). No source reports an attack on .NET, but CISA lists CVE-2026-111497 as exploited since 2026-10-27 (CISA, 2026-10-27).

Exposure
A framework-dependent host shows its runtime with dotnet --list-runtimes, which must list 8.0.33, 9.0.22 or 10.0.14; self-contained applications and container images carry their own runtime and must be checked per artifact (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25). The Brotli path is any code that enables request or response Brotli decompression or calls the Brotli APIs on untrusted data; CVE-2026-70197 needs Windows code that reuses one SocketAsyncEventArgs across IPv4 and IPv6 datagram sockets (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25; dotnet/runtime #136445, 2026-10-25).
Detection
No source describes an exploitation indicator. An attempt on the Brotli path would show in web access logs with Brotli request encoding on endpoints that decompress request bodies, then crashes of the hosting process, as JFrog reproduced (JFrog, 2026-10-25).
Defender takeaway
Install the updated runtime on every .NET host, including Windows hosts patched on 2026-10-13, which still carry CVE-2026-70197 (.NET Blog, 2026-10-25), and the November 2026 Windows cumulative update on every Windows system (Microsoft Security Response Center, 2026-11-12); treat the Brotli flaw as exploited, as CISA lists it (CISA, 2026-10-27). Where an update has to wait, Microsoft advises avoiding decompression of attacker-controlled Brotli data: remove the br entry from an existing request decompression configuration or Brotli from an existing automatic decompression setting, and do not add decompression where an application does not already use it (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25).

Envoy and Microsoft have shipped fixes for the same Brotli decoder flaw: Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 lists v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 for deployments with the Brotli decompressor configured, and Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14) covers applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data. Two more vendors have shipped fixes for the same decoder flaw. Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 says a buffer overflow in its Brotli decompressor allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code with a crafted Brotli-compressed stream; it names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable, v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 as fixed, and limits the impact to deployments that have the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23). Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3) fixes the same CVE, and an application is exposed only when it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic decompression or the Brotli APIs (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); .NET Blog, 2026-10-25 lists the fixed releases. As of 2026-10-26 no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration against Node.js.

The retracted claim was removed from the summary, immediate action wording, sourcing note, Detection paragraph, the 2026-10-24 section, the evidence quote and the techniques T1003 and T1557, which only that account supported. cve-2026-111497-node2shell-brotli-decoder-rce-nodejs-pypi (update: Envoy's own advisory of 2026-10-23 and the .NET release; Bun and Istio rest on The Hacker News alone and were not carried). pan-os-panorama-php2shell-mgmt-interface-no-fixed-release (correction: the statement that Unit 42 had seen a proof of concept is no longer on Unit 42's page, so statement, quote and citation were removed; S3 and S1 disagreed on whether this entry needed a change, the page grep settled it).
  • KEV sweep: tools/kev_window_diff.py found 0 additions with dateAdded in the window and no ransomware-flag change on a store-covered CVE; S1 confirmed independently against catalogue 2026.10.23 (newest dateAdded 2026-10-23, CVE-2026-114625 and CVE-2026-110447, both covered). PHP2Shell is not in KEV.
  • Backlog: the ARX Group SA row stays held, unchanged and unappended. S2 and S4 re-checked it today: the ransomware.live record is unchanged since 2026-10-23, there is no ARX, SBB or ASTRA statement and no Swiss press report; the hold condition is unmet and the 2026-11-07 expiry stands.
  • Single-source: cve-2026-111497-microsoft-net-oob-update-brotli-sockets-fix, vendor advisory for its own product (Microsoft's blog, four dotnet advisories and the Security Update Guide are one assessor), A2.
  • borderline-drop: Tailworm (Cyberdione Labs, 11 claimed Tailscale and headscale flaws, 2026-10-25); single uncoordinated report, proof of concept withheld, no independent reproduction, no CVE or fix, constituency use not established.
  • borderline-drop: OpenAI frontier-training containment disclosure (2026-10-25), own-environment account with no defender decision beyond fixes already shipped.
  • borderline-drop: Semperis on Prince of Persia (2026-10-22), single vendor, indicator-led, no European victim, no new endpoint behaviour.
  • borderline-drop: OPNsense PHP2Shell hotfixes 26.7.7, 26.1.11 and 26.4.2p4 (2026-10-21), out of window by five days and not a rotational lookback, no exploitation against OPNsense; the PHP entry already says to update the runtime on every host and image.
  • borderline-drop: CSIRT Italia alert AL01/261025 (2026-10-25), 81.9 % of Italian PHP services potentially vulnerable; a national exposure statistic that ACN says can include backported fixes; no new action.
  • borderline-drop: EDÖB head Lobsiger interview in the Blick (2026-10-24), possible widening of the PK Softech proceeding to the federal bodies; the Publica entry already carries the 2026-10-22 formal investigation and the widening is conditional.
  • borderline-drop: CYFIRMA PHP2Shell early warning v3 (24 October), single vendor, closed I2P channel nobody else can check, confidence inconsistent between narrative and evaluation, names the EU but not Switzerland.
  • borderline-drop: Chrome 156 stable (2026-10-20), about 6 h outside the record's lookback, no exploited flag, no store coverage.
  • borderline-drop: Drupal SA-CONTRIB-2026-253 (Monster Menus), needs an authenticated role, exploit maturity theoretical; PaperCut September bulletin additions, administrator-only; Atlassian October third-party bulletin, Atlassian rates the criticals lower risk.
  • borderline-drop: Medienwerkstatt Sulgen TG (Akira claim, 2026-10-23), private sector, out of window; ECOM and White & Case Qilin listings (2026-10-25), leak-site claims without a victim statement (PD-6), no public-sector nexus.
  • borderline-drop: French party and company leak wave of 23 to 25 October (PCF, La France insoumise, Renaissance, FSU, Alliance Police Nationale, Orange, Engie, ADMR, DEKRA), no shared vector or actor named, no Swiss nexus.
  • borderline-drop: ABC wipes devices after AdFection ad exposure (2026-10-23) (victim-side corroboration of a covered entry, no new behaviour; Quest Diagnostics, Capcom, Railway, Parkview, Yamato, Bathurst RSL and the Oberspreewald-Lausitz district administration) out of nexus, out of window or impact-only.
  • Candidate sources added: dotnet-blog (first-party .NET servicing channel; surfaced the out-of-band release that no slice source did), nict-cynex-lettice (named the app-to-backend attack, cited by JPCERT/CC) and datadog-security-labs (dated RSS, primary cloud-identity and supply-chain research); the S3 candidates macnica-security-research and S4's cyfirma-research were not added (Macnica is context for an entry that did not cite it; CYFIRMA's item was dropped). Twenty-one recipe notes from the source ledgers were appended to sources/sources.json. The transluce record is a single report, not a feed, and is a candidate for the next lifecycle review.
  • Jina reader credit: extract fell through to the reader on the two MSRC per-CVE pages in this run and, in S2, on three European Commission and Council of Europe pages.
  • Contradiction: S1 and S3 reported the PHP2Shell retraction as a correction; it was recorded as an update because it is an exploitation-status change in the world (Unit 42 withdrew its own claim on 2026-10-25), not an error in the entry as written.
  • Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport, seventh consecutive failing run; status page read instead); ox-security (article bodies 403, feed only); schneier (feed 403); digital-strategy.ec.europa.eu (403 on every transport, not in slice); arx-group.ch and arxgroup.ch (no readable victim site); community.citrix.com Tech Zone NetScaler post (403, its 2026-10-27 fixed builds are not out yet); news.admin.ch /de/nsb (403).
  • Verification: three iterations of the single cti-verification definition, each covering every claim in scope (152, 152 and 151 claims checked). Iteration 1 found two truth findings (the retraction worded as an intrusion withdrawal; an unsupported "independently" about NICT), one missing citation, one Visual Studio gap and a priority question on the PHP entry; iteration 2 found four low-confidence wording findings; iteration 3 found two low-confidence unsupported-citation findings. All truth and editorial findings were fixed in the same iteration's remediation; the PHP priority challenge (F16) was declined with a recorded rebuttal and the verifier accepted it as a judgement call in iteration 2. The first spawn of iteration 3 was lost to a container restart at about 04:30Z (the working tree survived) and the iteration was re-spawned clean. The final verdict is NEEDS_FIXES with two truth findings, both fixed afterwards, so the fire published on the low-residual early exit (decision rule 5) and no confirmation pass followed; verification_residual_count is 2, the two F3 findings applied after the last pass and not re-checked by a fresh verifier. The next audit should give the PHP, Japan and .NET entries an independent pass.
  • Essential-coverage: all 21 essential records of S1 and S2 were attempted; none missed.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-25
item.description:
• PHP2Shell hits QNAP NAS before login: QTS, QuTS hero, QVR, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE all have fixed builds. QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP in the web components of QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud and several QNAP applications and can be triggered before authentication, and fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 are out for QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud. As of 2026-10-28 (revision V1.2) the table lists QVR Surveillance (ARM32) 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS 1.0.5 and Notes Station 3 3.9.15 as resolved; QNE (ADRA) has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, which since 2026-11-02 lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 as the fix; QNAP has seen scanning and exploitation attempts in the wild but no reports of exploitation targeting its products, and CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26. Synology's advisory, revised on 2026-10-31, fixes its PHP packages (except the end-of-life PHP 7.3), Mail Station and Calendar, with builds for DSM 7.2 and above, DSM 7.0 to 7.1 and, for PHP 7.4, Mail Station and Calendar, DSM 6.2. →
  • Public root exploit for a Linux page-cache write past the Dirty Frag fix; AlmaLinux kernels carry the fix, no CVE yet. Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative copied public Linux kernel lists on five kernel reports on 2026-10-21 before any fix was merged, and Sysdig ranks ZDI-CAN-33367 as the one to act on: a local privilege escalation through skb_zerocopy() that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with a public exploit that TuxCare reproduced as root on AlmaLinux 8 to 10, CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04. A reviewed patch is in the kernel's networking tree but not in mainline, AlmaLinux announced on 2026-10-28 that fixed kernels are in production for 8, 9 and 10, none of the six reports has a CVE, and two ksmbd reports that ZDI scores CVSS 9.0 matter only where the in-kernel SMB server runs; no exploitation in the wild is reported. →
  • Required LDAP and SMB signing did not stop NTLM relay: a re-authenticated session kept the attacker's key. SpecterOps (LDAP, 2026-10-23) and Blackfield (SMB, 2026-10-21) independently show that a domain controller or file server that requires signing still accepts a relayed NTLM authentication when the attacker first opens a signed session of its own and then re-authenticates it as the victim, so the session keeps a signing key the attacker knows. Microsoft fixed the SMB variant in September 2026 and the LDAP variant in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update; SpecterOps reports no reply to its report and Blackfield found no CVE for the SMB change; public tooling exists and neither researcher reports use in attacks. →
