Trending vulnerabilities 2Research, reports & policy 1Updates to prior coverage 14Action items 9

01Trending vulnerabilities2 items

NOTABLECVE-2026-109618 +1exploitedupdatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, QNAP QTS, QuTS hero and QuTScloud: the PHP2Shell flaws reach the NAS web components before authentication; fixed builds of 2026-10-23, and QVR Surveillance, TVR OS, Notes Station 3 and QNE (ADRA) now fixed

QNAP's advisory QSA-26-18 says the PHP2Shell flaws CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS 4.0 9.2) affect the PHP used in the web components of its operating systems and several of its applications, can be triggered before any application-level authentication, and could let an unauthenticated remote attacker execute code on the device (QNAP, 2026-10-24). Its revision of 2026-10-24 lists fixed builds dated 2026-10-23 for QTS (6.1.0.3656 and 5.2.11.3661), QuTS hero (h6.1.0.3656, h6.0.2.3656, which also covers h5.3.x, and h5.2.11.3661) and QuTScloud (c5.2.9.3661), while revision V1.2 of 2026-10-28 lists Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier as resolved by 3.9.15 and the table lists QVR Surveillance 3.0.3 and earlier on ARM32 models as resolved by 3.0.3.1756 and TVR OS 1.0.4 and earlier as resolved by 1.0.5 (QNAP, 2026-10-28). QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, which since its revision of 2026-11-02 lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 as the fixed version (QNAP, 2026-10-22). QNAP's PSIRT says it has observed scanning and exploitation attempts against the flaws in the wild and blocked attempts against its own website, online store and cloud services (QNAP, 2026-10-22), and its advisory says it has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products (QNAP, 2026-10-24). PHP inside Container Station containers or third-party applications is not covered by QNAP's updates (QNAP, 2026-10-24).

Synology's advisory Synology-SA-26:14 rates its PHP 7.3 to 8.4 packages, Mail Station and Synology Calendar critical and lists fixed releases for each except the end-of-life PHP 7.3 package, which gets no fix; revision 3 of 2026-10-29 added PHP 7.4 for DSM 6.2, 7.0 and 7.1 and PHP 8.0 for DSM 7.0 and 7.1, and revision 4 of 2026-10-31 added Calendar and Mail Station for DSM 6.2, 7.0 and 7.1 (Synology, 2026-10-31). Synology says the PHP built into DSM is not exposed to external attack surfaces and considers the risk of exploitation very low (Synology, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
A QNAP NAS on QTS, QuTS hero or QuTScloud below the fixed builds, or a QNAP device running QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) below 3.0.3.1756, TVR OS below 1.0.5, or Notes Station 3 below 3.9.15, whose management or web ports are reachable from outside, which QNAP ties to router port forwarding, UPnP and myQNAPcloud publishing; the management ports default to 8080 and 443 (QNAP, 2026-10-24). QNE (ADRA) below 1.0.7.q327 has its own advisory and the same exposure routes (QNAP, 2026-10-22). On Synology, a DSM with one of the listed PHP packages, Mail Station or Calendar installed (Synology, 2026-10-22).
Detection
QNAP's compromise check is a review of QuLog Center for unexpected logins or access and a Security Center and Malware Remover scan with current definitions; if compromise is suspected it says to disconnect the device and change all passwords (QNAP, 2026-10-24).
Defender takeaway
Update QTS, QuTS hero, QuTScloud, Notes Station 3, QVR Surveillance (ARM32 models) and TVR OS now (QNAP, 2026-10-28) and QNE (ADRA) to 1.0.7.q327 (QNAP, 2026-10-22); where a device has to wait, remove internet exposure (port forwarding, UPnP, myQNAPcloud publishing) and allow the management ports only over a VPN or from trusted subnets, which QNAP says reduces exposure without fixing the flaws (QNAP, 2026-10-22). On Synology, update the listed packages to the build for the installed DSM generation, DSM 6.2 and 7.0 to 7.1 included; the PHP 7.3 package gets no fix (Synology, 2026-10-31).
Update27 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytagstitleaffected_productsentities

As of 2026-10-27 QNAP's advisory table lists QVR Surveillance 3.0.3 and earlier (ARM32 models) as resolved by QVR Surveillance 3.0.3.1756 and TVR OS 1.0.4 and earlier as resolved by TVR OS 1.0.5, while Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier and QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier remain in "Fixing" with the fixed version to be announced; QuMagie is no longer among the listed affected products, and the revision history still ends at V1.1 of 2026-10-24, so these table changes carry no dated revision (QNAP, 2026-10-27). QNAP still says it has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products (QNAP, 2026-10-27). CISA added both PHP flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26, as flaws in PHP rather than as a QNAP finding (CISA KEV, 2026-10-26).

Update31 Oct 2026 03:39 UTCrun 2026-10-31T0256Z-inteltitleheadlinesummarycvessourcesevidenceactionsbody

QNAP revised advisory QSA-26-18 to V1.2 on 2026-10-28 ("Notes Station 3 Resolved Published"), and its table now lists Notes Station 3 3.9.14 and earlier as resolved by Notes Station 3 3.9.15 (QNAP, 2026-10-28). QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier is no longer in that table: it has its own advisory, QSA-26-19, released on 2026-10-22, whose status is Fixing and whose fixed version is still to be announced (QNAP, 2026-10-22). Both advisories still say QNAP has received no reports of exploitation targeting QNAP products, and QSA-26-19 repeats that until fixed versions are available the most effective protection is to keep the device off the internet (QNAP, 2026-10-22).

Update02 Nov 2026 03:46 UTCrun 2026-11-02T0256Z-intelsummarycvessourcesbody

Synology's advisory Synology-SA-26:14 now lists fixed builds for DSM 7.0 to 7.1 and DSM 6.2. Revision 3 of 2026-10-29 adds PHP 7.4 for DSM 6.2, 7.0 and 7.1 and PHP 8.0 for DSM 7.0 and 7.1, and revision 4 of 2026-10-31 adds Calendar and Mail Station for DSM 6.2, 7.0 and 7.1 (Synology, 2026-10-31). The fixed builds are PHP 7.4.33-0122, PHP 8.0.30-0104, Calendar 2.4.8-10948 and Mail Station 30000002.3.19-10333 on DSM 7.0 to 7.1, and PHP 7.4.33-0010, Calendar 2.4.8-0948 and Mail Station 30000002.3.19-0333 on DSM 6.2; the table lists no PHP 8.0 build for DSM 6.2, gives the PHP 8.1 to 8.4 builds without a DSM split and still offers no fix for PHP 7.3 (Synology, 2026-10-31).

Update08 Nov 2026 13:55 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditactionsbodycvesevidenceheadlinesummarytitle

QNAP revised advisory QSA-26-19 to V1.1 on 2026-11-02 ("Resolved Published"), and its table now lists QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7 and earlier as resolved by QNE (ADRA) 1.0.7.q327 (QNAP, 2026-10-22). The advisory still describes the network restrictions as steps that reduce exposure without fully fixing the flaws (QNAP, 2026-10-22).

Sources: QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, revision V1.1) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, affected-products table as of 2026-10-27) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-18, revision V1.2) · QNAP PSIRT (QSA-26-19, QNE (ADRA)) · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (version 2026.10.26) · QNAP (statement on PHP2Shell) · Synology PSIRT (Synology-SA-26:14) · Synology PSIRT (Synology-SA-26:14, revision 4)
NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

Linux kernel ZDI-CAN-33367: a public local root exploit for an skb_zerocopy page-cache write that gets past the Dirty Frag fix, with no CVE and no mainline fix, among six reports Trend Micro's ZDI copied to public lists, two of them ksmbd flaws scored CVSS 9.0

On 2026-10-21 Trend Micro's Zero Day Initiative sent five Linux kernel reports and copied public mailing lists on every one, several with no fix in any released kernel; none of the six reports, the five kernel ones and a ConnMan report, has a CVE (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). ZDI-CAN-33367 matters most: skb_zerocopy() moves shared page-cache pages into a new socket buffer without the marker the Dirty Frag fix added, so IPsec ESP decrypts in place and an unprivileged local user writes attacker bytes into the cached copy of a read-only file, which gives root through a setuid binary or /etc/passwd; the public exploit needs unprivileged user namespaces and networking modules such as nlmon and act_pedit (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). TuxCare reproduced a root shell on AlmaLinux 8 to 10 (Dirty Frag fix installed), CloudLinux 9 and 10, Debian 12 and 13 and Ubuntu 24.04 and 26.04 (AppArmor user-namespace restriction bypassed) (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). A reviewed patch from the netdev list is now in the kernel's networking tree but not in mainline, and a kernel with only the fix for CVE-2026-90049, a bug in the same function, is not covered (Sysdig, 2026-10-24; TuxCare, 2026-10-27). AlmaLinux has put fixed kernels into production (4.18.0-553.178.1.el8_10, 5.14.0-687.60.1.el9_8, 6.12.0-211.69.1.el10_2), and TuxCare's rebootless patch is out for EL9 and EL10, with EL8 ready and Debian and Ubuntu in progress (AlmaLinux, 2026-10-28; TuxCare, 2026-10-27).

Two reports concern ksmbd, the kernel's own SMB server, not Samba. ZDI-CAN-33774 is a pre-authentication race in the SMB1 or SMB2 handler choice: its public proof of concept leaks 28 bytes of kernel heap per attempt and can crash the kernel, ZDI labels it remote code execution, nothing public shows code execution, and a fix is queued in ksmbd-for-next (Sysdig, 2026-10-24; Phoronix, 2026-10-22). ZDI-CAN-33549 is an SMB Direct integer underflow that needs an RDMA interface, a writable share and an SMB Direct client, and its proof of concept crashes the kernel (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). ZDI scores both 9.0, and Red Hat Enterprise Linux does not include ksmbd by default (The Hacker News, 2026-10-22).

Exposure
A Linux host where a local user or workload can run code and unprivileged user namespaces are on (shared hosting, CI runners, container nodes, login nodes) on the distributions above. For ksmbd, look for the ksmbd module, the ksmbd.mountd daemon and a kernel-owned listener on TCP 445 (Sysdig, 2026-10-24).
Detection
The exploit is one unprivileged process that unshares into new user and network namespaces and writes sysctls, brings up an nlmon interface, installs XFRM state over netlink, adds an nftables NFQUEUE rule, attaches a tc pedit action with a redirect and then calls splice() into a socket on the loopback address; Sysdig says nothing legitimate does all of that from one unprivileged process, so syscall-level runtime telemetry sees it (Sysdig, 2026-10-24). The write lands in the page cache, not the file, so a disk-content integrity check does not show it.
Defender takeaway
Restrict unprivileged user namespaces where nothing depends on them (Sysdig says user.max_user_namespaces=0 should block the public exploit, untested by TuxCare, and breaks rootless containers and some build tooling), do not rely on Ubuntu's AppArmor restriction, set seccomp RuntimeDefault on Kubernetes pods and install the fixed kernel where your distribution has shipped it; unload ksmbd where unused and keep TCP 445 to trusted networks where it must stay (Sysdig, 2026-10-24).
Update29 Oct 2026 05:00 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-inteltitleheadlinesummaryupdated_atsourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

AlmaLinux says its fix for ZDI-CAN-33367 is now in the regular kernel updates in the production repositories for every supported release: kernel-4.18.0-553.178.1.el8_10 for AlmaLinux 8, kernel-5.14.0-687.60.1.el9_8 for 9 and kernel-6.12.0-211.69.1.el10_2 for 10, installed with a metadata refresh, an upgrade and a reboot; the earlier testing-repository kernels also carry the fix (AlmaLinux, 2026-10-28). TuxCare's status of 2026-10-27 adds that the upstream fix has been accepted into the kernel's networking tree but not mainline, that no CVE exists and no exploitation has been reported, that its rebootless patch is out for EL9 and EL10 on AlmaLinux, CloudLinux, RHEL, Oracle Linux and Rocky Linux with EL8 ready for release, and that Debian and Ubuntu work is in progress (TuxCare, 2026-10-27).

Builds on: 2026-05-09/cve-2026-43284-cve-2026-43500-linux-dirty-frag-deterministic

vulnerability25 Oct 03:35Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Sysdig Threat Research Team · TuxCare · The Hacker News · Phoronix · AlmaLinux OS (ZDI-CAN-33367: Patched kernels released, updated 2026-10-28)

02Research, reports & policy1 item

NOTABLENATOB2

NTLM relay past required signing: SpecterOps and Blackfield re-authenticate a signed LDAP or SMB session with a relayed victim identity, and Microsoft fixed it in the September and October 2026 updates

SpecterOps and Blackfield show that NTLM relay to a server that requires signing works again when the attacker first owns a signed session and then re-authenticates it with the victim's identity, so the session keeps the attacker's signing key. For LDAP, the attacker signs a session to a domain controller with valid credentials or, where accepted, an anonymous NTLM context, coerces a victim over SMB, and sends the victim's relayed authentication with a malicious LDAP modification in one SASL record signed with the attacker's key; the controller checks the signature once, switches to the victim's identity and runs the modification with the victim's rights (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). The tested controller enforced LDAP signing and channel binding and the attack still worked over 389/TCP; the demonstration writes the resource-based constrained delegation attribute, and relaying a domain controller's machine account to another controller leads to DCSync and domain compromise (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). Blackfield shows the SMB counterpart: a server keeps the original signing key on re-authentication without checking that the identity matches, so on any host that requires SMB signing, domain controllers included, a relayed privileged authentication yields a privileged session still signed with the low-privilege key, provided the attacker can capture or coerce that authentication (Blackfield, 2026-10-21).

SpecterOps reported the LDAP flaw to Microsoft on 2026-10-06, received no response, and says the fix shipped in the 2026-10-13 cumulative update, KB5126646, while the SMB variant was patched quietly in September 2026 (KB5122882) (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). KB5126646 is the October update for Windows Server 2025 and KB5122882 the September update for Windows Server 2022 (Microsoft, 2026-10-13; Microsoft, 2026-09-08), so each release needs its own cumulative update of the month. Blackfield found no CVE or KB note for the SMB change, says similar changes seem to have reached the other supported versions in the following weeks without having traced every build, and warns that one or two end-of-life versions may never receive it (Blackfield, 2026-10-21). Both publish tooling; neither reports use in attacks (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23; Blackfield, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Windows Server domain controllers and SMB servers without the September 2026 (SMB) or 2026-10-13 (LDAP) cumulative update of their release; SpecterOps tested Server 2016 domain controllers and above and says every Server 2022 and 2025 domain controller it tested accepted the relay with LDAP signing required (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23). The LDAP variant needs a signed session the attacker controls, a victim coerced to authenticate over SMB and LDAP reachable on 389/TCP (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23).
Detection
Neither researcher publishes detection guidance. The demonstration ends in an LDAP modification of msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on the victim's own computer object, and msDS-KeyCredentialLink (shadow credentials) is the other write (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23), so directory-service change auditing on computer objects for those two attributes is where it surfaces, attributed to the victim's own computer account while the connection comes from the attacker's host. Patching does not remove values a relay already wrote.
Defender takeaway
Confirm that every domain controller runs the 2026-10-13 cumulative update of its Windows release and every Windows server the September one, because required signing did not stop this relay before them. SpecterOps also advises enforcing LDAP signing and channel binding together, restricting LDAP on 389/TCP where possible and reducing NTLM; Blackfield says SMB signing stays necessary but is not sufficient (SpecterOps, 2026-10-23; Blackfield, 2026-10-21).

Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC, Copeland xweb and Dixell xweb refrigeration controllers compromised in France, six more European countries and Switzerland, with France blaming the IRGC unit Shahid Kaveh for the October campaign; Midnight Blue reports six unpatched pre-authentication flaws in AK-SM 800A firmware up to 5.3.2

First published 2026-10-13 · open finding →

Update25 Oct 2026 03:37 UTCrun 2026-10-25T0256Z-intelheadlinesummarytechniquessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

ANSSI's director general told the French Senate on 2026-10-21 that elementary flaws were exploited, starting with controllers directly on the internet, administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, not vulnerabilities researchers had published, so a firmware update alone does not close the exposure. Forescout, on 2026-10-22, counts 12,976 exposed service observations in 99 countries, 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1, and over 20 hacktivist-claimed refrigeration attacks since January 2026, and says the French access vector remains unconfirmed.

ANSSI's director general, Vincent Strubel, told the French Senate foreign-affairs committee on 2026-10-21 that the attack rested on elementary security flaws, starting with refrigeration equipment directly on the internet and administered without particular protection, and weak passwords, and he dismissed analyses that tied it to vulnerabilities researchers had published over the previous two years (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21). Le Monde Informatique reports the same hearing and adds that the systems were reachable without a firewall or network segmentation and that the management interface was protected only by weak passwords (Le Monde Informatique, 2026-10-22). Neither outlet reports evidence beyond the testimony, and ANSSI names no actor; the account sits against Copeland's acknowledgment of a vulnerability in its end-of-life XWEB EVO controllers and the earlier report that ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in a Danish company's software, and no source reconciles them; the two outlets also differ on the date and the count, Public Sénat giving the night of 12 to 13 October and more than 700 supermarkets, Le Monde Informatique the night of 11 to 12 October and at least 300 Intermarché and Netto shops. Le Monde Informatique adds that ANSSI can alert and advise but has no means to impose connection rules on retailers (Le Monde Informatique, 2026-10-22), and Public Sénat reports that ANSSI ran a rapid check with health-sector players because laboratories and pharmacies that store vaccines use the same kind of refrigeration equipment (Public Sénat, 2026-10-21).

Forescout's Vedere Labs says on 2026-10-22 that the access vector, exploited vulnerabilities, attacker infrastructure, persistence and responsible actors in the French incidents remain unconfirmed, and that the reported changes, made in rapid succession, used ordinary supervisory functions (Forescout, 2026-10-22). Its tracking of hacktivist groups counts over 20 claimed attacks on refrigeration systems since January 2026, the most active being the pro-Russian groups Z-Pentest Alliance and NoName057(16) through internet-exposed human-machine interfaces, and its count of exposed services is 12,976 observations on 6,017 public addresses in 99 countries, with 3,762 exposed Danfoss StoreView observations on AK-SM 800A units, 80 percent of the 4,697 StoreView observations, on firmware older than 4.3.1 (Forescout, 2026-10-22). Forescout adds that the manufacturers' documentation presents internet remote maintenance through port forwarding as a supported option, so the exposure is not only an accident of configuration (Forescout, 2026-10-22).

The Python Software Foundation announced CVE-2026-115557 on 2026-10-24: the ssl module now carries a denylist of known compromised certificates that is rejected whatever the SSLContext policy, so it works without revocation checking (Python Software Foundation, 2026-10-24). Single-source items and carve-outs: the Danfoss update's ANSSI account is testimony reported by two outlets (Public Sénat and Le Monde Informatique), no transcript was reachable, and the entry says so; the PHP update's Tenable and Siemens statements are first-party vendor advisories for their own products; the EDÖB's account of its proceeding is its own release, relayed by Der Bund; ReliaQuest's sequence is one vendor's lab result and is reported as such. No contradiction between sources needed a verification: contradicted entry.

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport including WebFetch, sixth consecutive failing run counting from 2026-10-20; the status page is the working route), apa-ots (Angular shell, no recipe), resecurity (JS shell), lore.kernel.org (proof-of-work challenge on every message page, so the ZDI postings were read through Sysdig, TuxCare, The Hacker News and Phoronix), consilium.europa.eu (403 everywhere, sanctions watch rested on WebSearch), rapid7-research feed (malformed XML, per-post extract works), edoeb-ch-press listing (stale cache, the release page reads), ahnlab-asec (listing via the reader is stale, WebFetch lists it), schneier (reader fallback only, two keys answered HTTP 402 before a third served). S2 and S3 each reached the metered reader through extract fallbacks on pages the direct transports could not read.

Candidate sources: two added (openjdk-vulnerability-advisories, the first-party advisory of record that published the second Java alert before any outlet; blackfield-ch, the Swiss researcher blog behind the independent SMB finding). Proposed and not added: csa-sg-alerts (a relay of vendor facts that surfaced items already dispositioned), publicsenat-fr (carried the ANSSI testimony; a general political outlet, revisit if it surfaces a second primary), pwn-watch (discovery lead only), status-connectwise (a per-incident pivot, not a rotation source). imperva-threat-research and opensourcemalware were promoted to active from sources.promotion_due. trendmicro-research got its feed back as rss_url and fetch_method: rss; 24 recipe notes from the sub-agent ledgers were appended.

Source health: tools/source_health.py probed 266 records; the first sweep flagged one, the new candidate blackfield-ch (its feed carries a single short item, below the content check's minimum, so the record was switched to the bridge method with the listing as the probed route), and the second sweep ended with no unsolved record.

Self-identification: this fire's main agent is Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) per the harness model line; the four research sub-agents reported Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) in their own return headers.

Audit note: the PK Softech and Publica entry now carries twelve changelog records and is the longest entry in the store; the previous fire's verifier already suggested consolidating its per-fund statements and splitting its first action, which stays audit work.

Verification loop: seven iterations of the single cti-verification definition, each a cold spawn that answered a claim ledger. Iteration 1 (226 claims) found 7 truth and 6 editorial defects and iteration 2 (159) found 3 and 4; iterations 3 to 6 (58 to 160 claims, post-fix scope) found 1, 1, 3 and 5 truth defects, mostly in the run record's own notes, and no iteration returned CLEAN. Every finding was fixed in the entries or the run record before the next pass. Iteration 7 (128 claims, 126 ok) found one low-confidence F3 (the Danfoss Forescout figure's denominator), fixed with the denominator named; with truth plus editorial at 1 and no F1 or F4, the fire takes the low-residual early exit (verification_residual_count: 1). The carried-forward F11 note on the summary length of the PK Softech, Danfoss and PHP2Shell entries was declined in every pass and stays audit work.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-24
item.description: • Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now. CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 (not 9.4, and not 10.2 or later) among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app, present in every version, to be disabled. →
item.content:encoded:
TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Node2Shell Brotli flaw is now on CISA KEV, with exploit traffic seen against Node.js 24.22.0; update now. CISA added CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder bundled with Node.js, to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 on evidence of active exploitation, and ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, though its own copy of the attacker's chain got no shell. Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 fix it, and because the flaw is in Google's decoder the PyPI packages Brotli (1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy, Microsoft .NET, PHP for Windows, Ubuntu and, with Brotli inspection and TLS decryption enabled, PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls carry it too; Palo Alto and Cisco report no malicious use against their own products. Broadcom lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager 9.1.1.x as critically affected (CVSS 3.1 9.8), with the patch pending and only workarounds available, and Splunk lists Splunk Enterprise 10.0 (not 9.4, and not 10.2 or later) among the products that include affected Node.js packages, with 10.2 or later as the upgrade target and its Visual Exporter app, present in every version, to be disabled. →
Trending vulnerabilities 1Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 10

01Trending vulnerabilities1 item

HIGHCVE-2026-111497exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-111497, Node.js and Google Brotli (Node2Shell): an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder lets crafted compressed data run code, reached through fetch() and Express 5 or body-parser 2 request bodies; fixed in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1 and in the PyPI packages Brotli 1.2.1 and brotlicffi 1.2.1.0 (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

Node.js shipped security releases on 2026-10-21 for CVE-2026-111497, an out-of-bounds write in the Brotli decoder it bundles: an invalid block switch was reported as a need for more input instead of a format error, so the streaming decoder kept appending input to an eight-byte internal buffer (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). An attacker who can supply Brotli data that an application decompresses with node:zlib can corrupt process memory, which can lead to a crash, disclosure of process memory or remote code execution (Node.js project, 2026-10-21). Imperva ran code carried in Brotli data against the official 24.22.0 image in its laboratory (Imperva, 2026-10-22).

CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation" (CISA, 2026-10-27). ELLIO's sensors recorded exploit traffic against Node.js 24.22.0 on 2026-10-26, although the chain got no shell against ELLIO's own copy (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Cisco and Palo Alto say they know of no malicious use against their own products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28).

Fixes are in Node.js 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1; end-of-life lines stay affected (Node.js project, 2026-10-21; ELLIO, 2026-10-26). The decoder is Google's, so Bun (fixed in 1.4.4), Istio, the PyPI packages Brotli (fixed in 1.2.1) and brotlicffi (1.2.1.0), Envoy and Microsoft .NET carry the flaw too (ELLIO, 2026-10-26; Tenable, 2026-10-26; OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23; Envoy, 2026-10-23; .NET Blog, 2026-10-25).

Exposure
A service on Node.js 22.x, 24.x or 26.x below the fixed releases that decodes Brotli from an untrusted party, either request bodies inflated by Express 5 or body-parser 2 or compressed responses that fetch() consumes from a server an attacker influences (Imperva, 2026-10-22); Python code that decompresses untrusted data with the PyPI packages (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-23); Envoy with the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23); .NET applications that decompress attacker-controlled Brotli data (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager, critical on 9.1.1 with no patch yet (Broadcom, 2026-10-28); PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1 and 11.2 firewalls that inspect Brotli traffic with TLS decryption enabled (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29); Splunk Enterprise 10.0 and the Visual Exporter app in every Splunk Enterprise version, and Citrix Unicon eLux Scout (Splunk, 2026-10-28; Citrix, 2026-10-30); and WordPress hosts through the xmlrpc.php pingback and the operating system's libbrotli, where Patchstack shows a worker crash only (Patchstack, 2026-10-30). Read the Node.js release number, not process.versions.brotli, which says 1.2.0 on patched and vulnerable builds alike (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).
Detection
In web server, proxy and WAF logs, requests that carry a Brotli content encoding to endpoints that parse bodies, followed by worker crashes or restarts. A shell or new outbound connection from that workload is the strongest signal, and payload signatures, WAF content matching and body-size limits do not catch it (Datadog, 2026-10-29). Where systemd-coredump is enabled, forced crashes write core files that can hold other visitors' session cookies and key material, so restrict who can read them (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).
Defender takeaway
Replace the runtime, the two Python packages and any Envoy with the decompressor configured now, as CISA lists the flaw as exploited, and move Splunk Enterprise 10.0 to 10.2 or higher and disable its Visual Exporter app (Splunk, 2026-10-28); where an update has to wait, reject Content-Encoding: br as NCSC Switzerland advises (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26) and, if the application accepts no compressed request bodies, set the body-parser inflate option to false (Akamai, 2026-10-26).
Update26 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-26T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidencesourcessummary

Two more vendors have shipped fixes for the same decoder flaw. Envoy's advisory of 2026-10-23 says a buffer overflow in its Brotli decompressor allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service or potentially execute arbitrary code with a crafted Brotli-compressed stream; it names v1.39.2, v1.38.5, v1.37.7 and v1.36.11 as vulnerable, v1.40.0, v1.39.3, v1.38.6, v1.37.8 and v1.36.12 as fixed, and limits the impact to deployments that have the Brotli decompressor configured (Envoy, 2026-10-23). Microsoft's out-of-band .NET release of 2026-10-25 (8.0.33, 9.0.22, 10.0.14 and 11 Release Candidate 3) fixes the same CVE, and an application is exposed only when it decompresses attacker-controlled Brotli data through ASP.NET Core request decompression, HttpClient automatic decompression or the Brotli APIs (dotnet/announcements #494, 2026-10-25); .NET Blog, 2026-10-25 lists the fixed releases. As of 2026-10-26 no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory demonstration against Node.js.

Update27 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-27T0256Z-intelactionsaffected_productsbodycvesentitiesevidenceheadlinesourcessummarytags

NCSC Switzerland (BACS) published advisory 13105 on 2026-10-26 on the Brotli decoder flaw: it names Node.js, Microsoft .NET, Visual Studio, PowerShell, the Python Brotli and brotlicffi packages and Bun among the affected dependents, rated the exploitation status unknown with a proof of concept available in its text of that day, and gives as the temporary measure disabling Brotli decoding of untrusted data and rejecting Content-Encoding: br until patched, with services restarted and containers rebuilt after updating (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26).

Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS 12.2 before 12.2.4-h1, 12.1 before 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.7-h11 and 12.1.10-h3, and 11.2 before 11.2.4-h23, 11.2.7-h23, 11.2.10-h17, 11.2.13-h4 and 11.2.16-h1 as affected, but only on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls that have inspection of Brotli-compressed traffic and TLS decryption enabled on the dataplane; PAN-OS 11.1 and 10.2 and the management interface are not affected, and the hotfixes carry estimated dates from 2026-10-27 to 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26). Brotli encoding is disabled by default in PAN-OS 11.2.4 and later, the command show system setting brotli shows whether a firewall is exposed (Enabled: yes), and set system setting brotli-encoding disable is the vendor's interim mitigation; Palo Alto rates the urgency moderate and is not aware of malicious exploitation (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-26).

PHP rebuilt its Windows packages as 8.5.12-1, 8.4.27-1, 8.3.36-1 and 8.2.35-1 on 2026-10-26 with Brotli 1.2.1; the vulnerable decoder is reachable there through the cURL extension when automatic HTTP response decompression is enabled, which cURL leaves off by default (PHP, 2026-10-26). Ubuntu lists brotli fixes for 26.10 (1.2.0-4ubuntu0.1), 26.04 LTS (1.2.0-3ubuntu0.1), 24.04 LTS (1.1.0-2ubuntu0.1) and 22.04 LTS (1.0.9-2ubuntu0.1), marks 20.04 LTS as needing evaluation and its nodejs package on 20.04, which vendors Brotli, as vulnerable (Ubuntu, 2026-10-26).

Update28 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-28T0256Z-intelheadlinesummaryprioritytagscvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbodyaffected_productsentities

CISA added CVE-2026-111497 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-27 "based on evidence of active exploitation", naming no actor or victim (CISA, 2026-10-27). ELLIO's sensors recorded a public checker that maps hosts decompressing Brotli and then, on 2026-10-26, one Brotli-coded request body of about 23 MB built against Node.js 24.22.0 on x86-64, which ELLIO reads as adoption by an operator focused on mass exploitation; its own test of the attacker's chain against that build got no shell in 50 attempts, so a failed attempt shows as a worker crash (ELLIO, 2026-10-26). Tenable relays the report and has not confirmed it (Tenable, 2026-10-26); Cisco and Palo Alto report no malicious use against their own products (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-27; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28). Palo Alto's advisory, as read on 2026-10-28, shows six of the nine PAN-OS hotfixes released and the other three, 12.1.4-h13, 12.1.10-h3 and 11.2.4-h23, due on 2026-10-29 and 2026-10-30 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

JFrog reproduced a remote crash of a ClickHouse server with one request carrying a crafted 23 MB body, with the fix merged but not released when it wrote (JFrog, 2026-10-25). Akamai gives a lever for Express 5 and body-parser 2 services that accept no compressed request bodies: set the inflate option to false (Akamai, 2026-10-26). A Node.js build is judged by its release version, because the bundled version string reads 1.2.0 on patched builds as well (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).

Update29 Oct 2026 07:03 UTCrun 2026-10-29T0255Z-intelsummaryupdated_atentitiesaffected_productscvessourcesevidenceactionsbody

Broadcom's advisory VMSA-2026-0008, issued on 2026-10-27 and revised as 0008.1 on 2026-10-28 to clarify the impacted products, lists VMware Cloud Foundation's SDDC Manager as affected because it uses Node.js: a malicious actor with network access to SDDC Manager may exploit the flaw to execute arbitrary code (Broadcom, 2026-10-28). Broadcom rates it critical, CVSS 3.1 9.8, on SDDC Manager 9.1.1 only and important, 7.5, on 9.1.0, 9.0.x and 5.2.x, none has a patch yet, and workarounds are in KB460732 for 9.1.1 and KB460734 for the others (Broadcom, 2026-10-28).

Palo Alto Networks' timeline of 2026-10-29 removes the estimated dates of 11.2.4-h23, 12.1.4-h13 and 12.1.10-h3 because those builds are released, so every PAN-OS hotfix listed for this flaw is now available (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

Correction01 Nov 2026 13:56 UTCrun 2026-11-01T1312Z-auditaffected_productsbodycvessources

The 2026-10-26 section's statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory held only for that day: CISA listed the flaw as exploited on 2026-10-27, and NCSC Switzerland's advisory, updated on 2026-10-29, now gives the status as actively exploited with a proof of concept available (NCSC Switzerland, 2026-10-26). ELLIO's capture is not the only attack telemetry: Zscaler's decoys recorded 402 events from 20 source addresses against 12 customers within a day of disclosure, 60% of them exploitation attempts and the rest reconnaissance (Zscaler ThreatLabz, 2026-10-28).

Datadog, which reproduced the bug, finds no conventional indicators because no attacker infrastructure is involved and lays out three layers to correlate (Datadog, 2026-10-29): decoder errors, where a vulnerable Node.js build returns Z_BUF_ERROR "unexpected end of file" (which benign truncated input also produces) and a patched one ERR__ERROR_FORMAT_BLOCK_SWITCH; process signals, a worker exiting with signal 139 right after a Brotli transfer or pinned at full CPU inside a decompression call; and decompressed output carrying bytes the client never sent, the memory-disclosure path, so endpoints that echo or reflect decompressed content are the ones to check first. Payload byte signatures, WAF content matching and body-size limits do not catch it, because the WAF forwards compressed bytes and the middleware counts decompressed size (Datadog, 2026-10-29). Palo Alto's advisory also lists Prisma Cloud Application Security Transporter Client before 0.2.9 as affected, fixed in 0.2.9 (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-29).

Update03 Nov 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-11-03T0256Z-intelsourcesevidenceactionsbody

Patchstack reports that WordPress ships no Brotli of its own but links the operating system's libbrotli through libcurl, so one unauthenticated POST to xmlrpc.php can take down a PHP worker on a stock install: the pingback method makes WordPress fetch an attacker-named URL and decode the Brotli reply (Patchstack, 2026-10-30). A laboratory demonstration killed a worker or pinned it at full CPU, its author says no code execution is included, and Patchstack says no public chain aims at PHP; the fix is a patched libbrotli package, and the official wordpress:latest image still carried a vulnerable one when Patchstack wrote (Patchstack, 2026-10-30).

Update05 Nov 2026 03:52 UTCrun 2026-11-05T0255Z-intelsummaryaffected_productsentitiescvessourcesevidencesourcing_noteactionsbody

Splunk's advisory SVD-2026-1015, published on 2026-10-28 and updated through 2026-11-06, lists Splunk Enterprise, the Splunk Visual Exporter app, SOAR Automation Broker, UBA, Attack Analyzer, Python for Scientific Computing, several AppDynamics components and Smartlook as including packages affected by four Node.js flaws, CVE-2026-111497 among them; the page gives no CVSS score, no attacker position and no exploitation statement, and it covers the Brotli flaw and three DNS and TLS hostname-validation flaws together, so it does not show which of them reaches a given product (Splunk, 2026-10-28). Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable while 9.4 and 10.2 or later are not (as revised on 2026-11-06), Splunk recommends upgrading to 10.2 or higher for the bundled Node.js runtime and plans to upgrade the packages in a future 10.0 release, and the upgrade does not remediate the Visual Exporter app, which every Splunk Enterprise version includes and which Splunk says to disable or remove (Splunk, 2026-10-28). The page gives no fix for the other listed products.

Citrix bulletin CTX697300, published on 2026-10-30 and revised on 2026-11-03 with remediation for the LTSR and Cloud Gateway products, lists Unicon eLux Scout as affected by CVE-2026-111497 alone and names the fixes as hotfix 2609.1 for Scout On-Prem, 2508 CU2 LTSR for Scout On-Prem LTSR and 2605.1-3 for Scout Cloud Gateway On-Prem, without a vulnerable version range or an exploitation statement (Citrix, 2026-10-30). Neither Splunk nor Citrix says anything on malicious use against its products.

Correction08 Nov 2026 13:53 UTCrun 2026-11-08T1309Z-auditactionsbodycvesevidencesourcing_notesummaryaffected_productssources

Splunk revised advisory SVD-2026-1015 on 2026-11-05 and 2026-11-06: Splunk Enterprise 10.0 is vulnerable, versions 9.4 and 10.2 and higher are not affected, and 10.2 or higher stays the upgrade target for 10.0 (Splunk, 2026-10-28). A 9.4 instance therefore needs no upgrade for the bundled Node.js runtime; the Visual Exporter app is still included in every Splunk Enterprise version and is still to be disabled or removed (Splunk, 2026-10-28). The revised list adds Splunk Observability Cloud and the Splunk Observability OpenTelemetry Collector as affected and names Splunk Synthetic Runner 1.71.0 or higher as its fix (Splunk, 2026-10-28). Keycloak 26.8.2, released on 2026-11-05, fixes the flaw in its bundled Brotli decoder (Keycloak, 2026-11-05). The 27 October update's statement that no source reported exploitation outside Imperva's laboratory was already outdated when written: ELLIO had reported exploit traffic in the wild on 26 October (ELLIO, 2026-10-26).

vulnerability24 Oct 03:33Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: Node.js project · Node.js project (release v22.23.4) · Node.js project (release v24.22.1) · Node.js project (release v26.12.1) · Google Brotli · ENISA EUVD · Imperva Threat Research · OpenSourceMalware · Envoy Proxy (security advisory) · .NET Blog (Microsoft) · Microsoft (dotnet/announcements, CVE-2026-111497 advisory) · NCSC Switzerland (BACS, Cyber Security Hub advisory 13105) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status) · PHP (news archive, updated Windows builds for the Brotli fix) · Ubuntu Security (CVE-2026-111497) · CISA (alert, KEV additions) · ELLIO Threat Research Lab · Tenable Research · JFrog Security Research · Akamai Security Intelligence Group · Cisco PSIRT (advisory, Vulnerabilities in node.js Affecting Cisco Products) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, as read on 2026-10-28) · Palo Alto Networks PSIRT (CVE-2026-111497 portfolio status, timeline of 2026-10-29) · Broadcom (VMSA-2026-0008.1) · Datadog Security Labs · Zscaler ThreatLabz · Patchstack · Splunk (advisory SVD-2026-1015) · Citrix (security bulletin CTX697300) · Keycloak project (release notes 26.8.2)

02Updates to prior coverage9 items

NOTABLEupdatedNATOB2

ARTEX: Microsoft reports Storm-0940, a China-state aligned actor, running an open-source multi-agent LLM penetration-testing framework against hundreds of organizations, with privileged cloud access in under three hours in some cases, and Expel sees the same infrastructure abuse Okta self-service registration

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:45 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Wiz Research independently reports an ARTEX-using actor overlapping with Storm-0940 against software vendors in October, and adds log signatures that mark the agent: source-map-then-route sequences, unsigned-JWT SSO probes and one-second-cadence spray bursts with a user agent per burst.

Wiz Research reports an actor using ARTEX-associated tooling, overlapping with Storm-0940, against IT and software vendors throughout October 2026, focused on Okta, Entra and Cognito and on Microsoft 365 integrations, with most attempts failing (Wiz, 2026-10-22). It describes the log signatures of the agent: source-map and OpenAPI downloads followed minutes later by calls to internal routes that appear only in those files, fabricated OAuth callback values, unsigned JWTs tried against more than 60 SSO route variants in two minutes, account-recovery and sign-up calls, and password-spray bursts of 20 to 60 minutes against Entra and Okta with a unique user agent per burst and a median gap of one second between attempts (Wiz, 2026-10-22). Wiz says chaining, automatic adaptation to rate limits and blocks, and tests against heavily scrutinised Microsoft OAuth flows separate the agent from a human operator (Wiz, 2026-10-22).

Sources: Microsoft Threat Intelligence · Expel · CrowdStrike Counter Adversary Operations · Recorded Future Insikt Group · Wiz Research · BleepingComputer · Yonhap News Agency · Google Threat Intelligence Group and Mandiant · Check Point Research · CERT-EU · Netzwoche (Gohack26 report)
HIGHCVE-2026-73570exploitedupdatedNATOA1

CVE-2026-73570, Zimbra Collaboration: a pre-auth command injection patched without a CVE in July is exploited, with probing before disclosure and root escalation, secret theft and cluster-wide movement observed

First published 2026-08-20 · open finding →

Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:44 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_note

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the chain and found that several public proofs of concept never trigger it, so a failed test does not show a host is patched; its process-lineage detection for the Swatchdog notification path is added to the detection guidance.

Elastic Security Labs reproduced the exploit chain in its lab and describes it stage by stage: an SMTP client sends a recipient address with an unclosed angle bracket, Postfix logs it to /var/log/zimbra.log as an illegal-address warning, Zimbra's bundled Swatchdog daemon matches a log line of the form "Service status change: <host> <service> changed from stopped to running", and the notification routine places the service field into a Perl backtick string that /bin/sh runs, giving code execution as the zimbra user, who can read every mailbox and send as any local identity (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Its practical finding is that several public proofs of concept write a payload that Swatchdog never matches, so a failed test looks like a patched server; Elastic's own proof of concept proves execution with an out-of-band callback that changes nothing on disk, and it says upgrading to 10.1.20 or later is the only complete fix (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Its detection is a process sequence on one host within 30 seconds, a shell started by the Perl Swatchdog script with snmptrap in its command line followed by any child of that shell other than snmptrap; on a healthy host the notification shell starts only snmptrap, so any other child is the discriminator (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23). Where exploitation is found, Elastic lists standard indicators of remote code execution, phishing mail originating from the server, compromise of local databases, signing keys and LDAP exports, and less direct surfaces beyond the mail store (Elastic Security Labs, 2026-10-23).

Sources: Zimbra (vendor security advisories) · CERT-FR (ANSSI) · ENISA EU Vulnerability Database · The Hacker News · Microsoft Threat Intelligence · CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog · Zimbra (10.1.20 release notes) · Zimbra (10.1.21 release notes) · NCSC Switzerland, Cyber Security Hub · ACN / CSIRT Italia (bulletin BL01/261005/CSIRT-ITA) · Elastic Security Labs
NOTABLECVE-2026-107656 +1updatedNATOA2

Fortinet FortiSandbox GUI authentication bypass (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 9.6) and FortiSIEM 7.5.0 unauthenticated path traversal to code execution (CVE-2026-106173, CVSS 9.4): both critical, fixed 2026-10-13, neither reported exploited

First published 2026-10-23 · open finding →

Improvement24 Oct 2026 03:43 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodycvesevidenceheadlinesourcessourcing_notesummarytags

Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw CVE-2026-106173 on 2026-10-20; the fix and the unexploited status are unchanged.

A public proof of concept exists for the FortiSIEM 7.5.0 flaw: Horizon3.ai published a deep dive and the exploit for CVE-2026-106173 on 2026-10-20 (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20; The Hacker News, 2026-10-20). First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Update24 Oct 2026 03:42 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelaffected_productsbodycvesevidencesourcessourcing_notesummaryentities

Ruby released 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 on 2026-10-23 with fixes for the regular-expression engine bugs behind four GitLab flaws, this one included; any Ruby application that compiles attacker-controlled patterns is exposed to them, and Ruby has requested no CVE identifiers of its own.

The Ruby project published an advisory on 2026-10-23 and released Ruby 4.0.9, 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 with fixes for the bugs in its Onigmo regular-expression engine behind four GitLab flaws: CVE-2026-89078 (a double free when parsing a pattern fails after an alternation), CVE-2026-93577 and CVE-2026-97229 (an integer overflow in the size of a compiled pattern) and CVE-2026-110264 (an overflow of internal IDs in a pattern with many repeats) (Ruby, 2026-10-23). Ruby's table gives the first release of each series that carries each fix: the fix for CVE-2026-110264 first appears in 4.0.9, so 4.0.8 is not enough, and 3.4.12 and 3.3.13 carry all of them; GitLab fixed its own servers by patching the Ruby it ships (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

The advisory widens the exposure beyond GitLab to any Ruby application that compiles a regular expression from a string an attacker controls, says Regexp.timeout does not protect against these bugs and that limiting pattern length does not reliably protect, and says Ruby has not requested CVE identifiers of its own and that operators should track the issues under GitLab's identifiers (Ruby, 2026-10-23).

TeamUpdraft's updates of 2026-10-21 and 2026-10-22 say the attacker used a compromised key to access its site, that there is no evidence the attacker still has access, and that the speed of the exploits and the initially faulty backdoor plugins suggest AI was used to accelerate the attack, which is the vendor's inference and comes with no technical evidence (TeamUpdraft, 2026-10-19). It asks users to look at the sites listed under their UpdraftCentral account for any they did not knowingly connect since 2026-10-19, says it is seeing a pattern of unexpected Editor roles, and stresses that UpdraftPlus Premium users should check for unexpected plugins and new administrators even if they never used UpdraftCentral (TeamUpdraft, 2026-10-19).

Nethemba reports that the attacker kept going after the fix: on 2026-10-20 it tried the secret triggers of already removed backdoors on at least six sites of four administrators, and on the morning of 2026-10-21 it sent UpdraftCentral commands to two of Nethemba's sites after 1.26.13 had been released, blocked by Nethemba's own blocking plugin, with the keys no longer existing (Nethemba, 2026-10-19). A site that has a stolen key and neither updated nor deleted it by hand therefore stays exposed, and a removed backdoor is still probed. Nethemba also reads the code of UpdraftPlus Premium as storing the teamupdraft.com account password in the site database as entered and deleting it only after add-ons are claimed with a token, so it can stay in the database and in backups; a reader found it on all three of their premium sites and in backups going back to 2022, and Nethemba on one of its three, while the vendor says it is removed after the first connection and Nethemba has not found the samples it analysed reading it (Nethemba, 2026-10-19).

PK Softech, software supplier of Swiss pension funds: malware and a data outflow at Publica, with the City of Zurich fund PKZH saying its insured persons' test data was stolen, the Bernese funds BPK and BLVK and Pensionskasse Post also reporting the supplier incident, and the Federal Prosecutor's Office investigating

Update24 Oct 2026 03:41 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelactionsbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummary

The Ticino cantonal fund IPCT says in a letter of 2026-10-23 that data of about 1,800 of its insured persons (about 1,700 who left in 2024 and 2025, with exit-benefit amounts and IBANs, and about 80 on disability pensions) sat on the attacked supplier server for two ongoing projects; it has no certain evidence the data were taken but finds it plausible, and it writes to all insured because it cannot exclude more.

The Ticino cantonal pension fund IPCT has put numbers on its exposure in a letter of 2026-10-23 to its roughly 17,000 active insured and 10,000 pensioners (IPCT, 2026-10-23). PK Softech told it in the late afternoon of 2026-10-14 that the authorities had established that personal data were taken from the supplier's servers, without saying which funds the data belonged to, and the fund's checks to date found among the documents on the attacked server data of about 1,800 persons, held there for two ongoing projects of spot checks and recalculations (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 1,700 are persons who left the fund through resignation or death in 2024 and 2025: surname, first name, postal address, date of birth, AHV number and insured number, the exit-benefit amount and the receiving fund with its bank account (IBAN), and the personal IBAN for about 50 who were paid out directly, with no e-mail address or telephone number (IPCT, 2026-10-23). About 80 are insured persons on a disability pension whose passive pension data was being updated: name, date of birth, AHV number, insured number, passive insured salary, passive retirement assets, degree and start of invalidity, with no contact data (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

The fund says it has no certain evidence that these data were taken but that it appears plausible, that savings capital and pensions of all insured are untouched, that the cantonal administration's IT centre hosting the fund's infrastructure was not breached, and that it filed a criminal complaint against unknown persons and was recognised as private plaintiff, while the Federal Prosecutor's Office and the federal police investigate (IPCT, 2026-10-23; Ticinonline, 2026-10-23). It decided to send the letter to all insured because its information is partial, the analyses are still evolving and it may never have certainty, and it asks them to watch for unexpected e-mails, calls and messages over the coming weeks and never to disclose passwords, access data or personal data unless sure of the requester (IPCT, 2026-10-23). The letter names PK Softech's other customers as Publica, large cantonal public funds such as Bern and Zurich and company funds such as Migros and Post, for hundreds of thousands of insured persons in total (IPCT, 2026-10-23).

LiteLLM 1.107.0: the PyPI wheels and the official Docker images carried a credential stealer and a dormant remote-code loader that Python starts at every launch, published through the maintainers' own release workflow with stolen developer tokens

First published 2026-10-22 · open finding →

Update24 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-24T0255Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

The maintainers' root-cause post of 2026-10-23 replaces the earlier log-leak hypothesis: a master key committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked gave the attacker an organization owner's GitHub CLI token on 2026-10-10, eleven days before the release, and Socket independently found secret-stealing workflows running that day.

The maintainers published a root-cause post on 2026-10-23 that supersedes the earlier hypothesis that the tokens were read from the logs of an internet-exposed internal deployment: their request logs show the first token came from a different service, an experimental agent platform whose administrative key had been committed to a public repository on 2026-05-27 and never revoked (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23). The attacker used the key on 2026-10-10 to obtain an organization owner's GitHub CLI token, so access began eleven days before the release, and the same day throwaway branches in two repositories ran workflows that posted CI secrets to an external capture endpoint and were deleted minutes later, yielding the tokens of two further maintainers (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23).

Socket found the same activity independently from the repository's Actions performance metrics, including a second run on 2026-10-12 that took 14 further secrets, and says it has not established how the attacker first obtained access (Socket, 2026-10-23). On 2026-10-21 three credentials did different jobs: the owner's token overrode branch protection and later force-pushed the history clean, a second maintainer's token approved the production gate and a third maintainer's token deleted the run records, after the maintainers had relaxed the release rule earlier that week so that any two engineers could trigger and approve a release (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23). The maintainers say they are revoking every token tied to every internal system and vendor platform, and that the attacker's activity on other systems focused on upstream inference API tokens (LiteLLM, 2026-10-23).

Other vendors report no successful exploitation. CrowdStrike has not observed any in the wild or in its honeypots and expects a reliable exploit only against a specific deployment profile, such as a fixed Docker image (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23); Wordfence knows of no compromise among the more than 74,000 attempts its firewall intercepted (Wordfence, 2026-10-22); and Sophos corrected on 2026-10-22 its earlier report of successful exploitation to scanning and a small number of failed attempts, one of them a blocked attempt to deliver a likely Mirai-derived botnet variant (Sophos, 2026-10-22). PHP calls it an unlikely vector, issues no emergency release, suggests session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release, says a host that applied that setting from the 2026-10-21 advisory should keep it, and will publish the full advisory with the next release (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP has not stated affected versions or a severity score, and no exploitation is reported (The Hacker News, 2026-10-23).

Window: gap 24.0 h from 2026-10-23T0256Z-intel, window 26 h, developing-story window 72 h. The container clock agreed with the network date (skew 0 s) and the first fetch of origin/main was current. A Saturday-morning fire in the fourth day of the PHP2Shell story: the new signal is a first vendor-reported intrusion through it, a third PHP code-execution path, one new runtime flaw (Node2Shell) and several second-day corrections to entries the store already carries. The 26 h window held no new critical.

Container restart: at about 03:27Z the container was restarted while S1 was finalising; S1's findings file was already complete on disk (nine items, a 28-row source ledger, ended_at still PENDING in its header) and was taken as S1's return, with S1.ended_at written from the file's last write time (03:26:46Z). No continuation was needed because the ledger answers every slice record. S2, S3 and S4 returned normally. One reading note: the WebFetch summary of Socket's page reported that its share links carry a prefilled prompt asking an assistant to remember the domain; it was ignored.

KEV sweep (work/2026-10-24T0255Z-intel/kev-window.txt, catalogue 2026.10.23): two additions inside the window, CVE-2026-110447 (Collabora CODE server) and CVE-2026-114625 (Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator), both COVERED and already exploited in their entries; no RANSOMWARE row. Neither PHP2Shell CVE and not CVE-2026-115560 is KEV-listed.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): no row was open at the start. One row added and held: ARX Group SA, a leak-site claim against a Swiss engineering consultancy for federal infrastructure projects, held to 2026-11-07 on a named condition (ARX, a federal client or Swiss press confirms), because PD-6 bars publishing a leak-site claim alone.

Published (1 new): cve-2026-111497-node2shell-brotli-decoder-rce-nodejs-pypi (notable, vulnerability; multi-source: the Node.js project and Google Brotli release with Imperva's independent exploit validation, OpenSourceMalware for the PyPI packages and ENISA's record for the CVSS; it clears PD-11(b) on its own mechanics: unauthenticated code execution through a decoder reached by two ordinary Node.js request and response paths, a public independent demonstration and a patch that ships no CVE for the Python packages; not exploited, so not high).

Updated (9, through the changelog): six update records and three improvement records, none a second entry. update: the PHP2Shell entry (Unit 42's confirmed-intrusion claim set against CrowdStrike, Sophos, Wordfence and SANS ISC, the new informational advisory CVE-2026-115560, vendor status moves; one new action; priority stays critical), the PAN-OS entry (WF-500 now unaffected after a correction the advisory timeline dates 2026-10-23, and the table no longer distinguishes Panorama; 2026-10-24 added threat-signature details), the LiteLLM entry (the maintainers' root-cause post replaces the earlier log-leak hypothesis; Socket's independent reconstruction), the Publica/PK Softech entry (the Ticino fund IPCT's letter of 2026-10-23: about 1,800 persons, data fields, no certain evidence of theft), the TeamUpdraft entry (vendor-stated entry vector, attacker activity after 1.26.13, account password stored by UpdraftPlus Premium) and the GitLab CVE-2026-110264 entry (Ruby's upstream fix versions and the exposure of other Ruby applications). improvement: FortiSIEM CVE-2026-106173 (Horizon3's public proof of concept of 2026-10-20 was missing), Zimbra CVE-2026-73570 (Elastic's reproduction: failed public proofs of concept do not show a patched host; process-lineage detection) and ARTEX (Wiz's independent telemetry and log signatures). Entity registry: tool:node2shell registered by hand and five product entities synced (product:node-js, product:google-brotli, product:python-brotli-pypi, product:brotlicffi-pypi, product:ruby).

Corrections inside the updates worth the operator's eye: the LiteLLM entry carried the maintainers' superseded hypothesis, which its own source now calls inaccurate, and the old evidence quote was replaced; the Node2Shell entry states that OpenSourceMalware's "no advisory database lists the PyPI packages" is superseded by two PYSEC advisories in ENISA's record dated 2026-10-23, so dependency scanners keyed on those identifiers can flag them.

Borderline drops: borderline-drop: Linux ksmbd ZDI-CAN-33774 and ZDI-CAN-33549 — two CVSS 9.0 reports posted to a public kernel list with no mainline fix and no CVE; a niche module, no exploitation, revisit when the CVEs or fixes land; borderline-drop: Pillow 13.0.0 EPS filename argument injection CVE-2026-112900 and siblings — library-cycle fixes, conditional on Ghostscript and attacker-controlled filenames, no exploitation; borderline-drop: Splunk Enterprise CVE-2026-76268 — the advisory of 2026-10-07 is outside the window and Horizon3's write-up of 2026-10-22 fell inside the previous fire's window, where nothing covered it; dropped deliberately on the merits: the Patroni REST API is reachable from the cluster network, no exploitation is reported, the proof of concept is an unverified repository claim and the upgrade (10.4.3, 10.2.7) or the sidecar workaround sits in the regular cycle; reconsider if exploitation is reported; borderline-drop: Oracle E-Business Suite CVE-2026-101767 (Horizon3 write-up) — a row of the October CPU already covered by the CPU entry, not exploited, patch-cycle; borderline-drop: Aokigahara infostealer (Check Point, Symantec) — no delivery vector and no constituency nexus; AI-tool credential theft is an incremental infostealer feature; borderline-drop: SOCRadar INC and The Gentlemen AI workbench — one vendor's reading of attacker-held records with unverified counts, techniques and CVEs already covered by other entries; borderline-drop: Railway platform compromise — no constituency nexus found, the transferable lesson (secrets held in platform variables, AI-key hunting) is carried by the LiteLLM entry; borderline-drop: Caisse des Dépôts PEP's and Ircantec — public-employer portal accounts taken over by social engineering, but no mechanism, no data scope and a contested seller claim (incident floor); borderline-drop: Medienwerkstatt Sulgen TG and Landkreis Oberspreewald-Lausitz — private firm with business-contact data only; a precautionary county shutdown with no confirmed attack (incident floor); borderline-drop: ConnectWise Cloud Backup restoration timetable — no change to what a partner does (connections stay disabled until instructed); borderline-drop: eMudhra leaves the TLS business — the open item is a certificate replacement the entry already asks for. S1 also dropped, with reasons in its findings file, the PaperCut September bulletin rows, the October Patch Tuesday QUIC and OpenSSH for Windows rows, CGM CLININET, rsyslog dynaFile, EDK2 PXE, Laravel TokenGuard, the Atlassian October bulletin, the Zimbra and Okta Access Gateway authenticated chains and Wasmtime; S2 dropped the EFK Microsoft 365 audit (third sighting), the St. Gallen SKIPD strategy, BIT cloud capacity and the BACS consumer material.

Single-source items and carve-outs: the PAN-OS, GitLab and FortiSIEM-sandbox statements rest on first-party vendor pages for their own products; the IPCT figures are the fund's own letter, relayed by Ticinonline; the ARTEX and Zimbra additions are single research sources (Wiz, Elastic) that say what they saw in their own telemetry or lab; Unit 42's confirmed-intrusion claim is single-vendor and is reported as such beside four contrary assessments.

Coverage gaps: connectwise-trust-center (403 on every transport, fourth consecutive run; the status page supplied the restoration plan and is the working route), ec-digital-strategy-newsroom (403 everywhere; now a documented unreachable host in the health tool), databreaches-net (no cheap transport), ibm-support-security-bulletins (no listing transport), community.citrix.com (403, so the revision status of Citrix's PHP guidance could not be checked), lore.kernel.org (proof-of-work challenge) and the rapid7-research feed (error). Not reached by any sub-agent and left to the audit: SAP Security Patch Day of 2026-10-13, which no earlier fire covered either.

Candidate sources: four added (nodejs-security-releases, ruby-lang-news, imperva-threat-research, tio-ch-attacco-informatico); S1's note that PHP, Node.js and Ruby runtime advisories were found two days late through CERT relays supports reading the project security feeds of the main server runtimes every fire. rsi-info-ticino is proposed and not added until its listing is probed; trendmicro-research was moved to the TrendAI blog instead of adding a duplicate. Four sources promoted to active by the promotion rule (arista-security-advisories, hpe-networking-psirt, splunk-advisories, watchguard-psirt).

Source health: the sweep flagged four records, all resolved in this fire: ec-digital-strategy-newsroom added to the documented unreachable hosts in tools/source_health.py (13 of 13 tool tests pass), ssd-disclosure given a health_cmd for its dated posts API, dfirreport and venarix given a 120-day staleness limit for their publisher cadence. The second sweep ended with no unsolved record.

Self-identification: this fire's main agent is Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) per the harness model line; the four research sub-agents reported Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) in their own return headers.

Verification loop: three cti-verification passes, all NEEDS_FIXES, with truth plus editorial counts of 12, 5 and 2, and every claim in each pass's scope answered against the ledger (306, 315 and 253 claims). Iteration 1 found a mis-assigned footnote on Cisco's Duo and URWB rows, the Panorama and WF-500 table wording and dating on the Palo Alto advisory (its timeline dates the WF-500 correction to 2026-10-23, not 2026-10-24), a fourth Threat Prevention condition, a tense error on the IPCT letter, a Fortinet citation that did not carry the not-exploited clause, Nethemba's blocking plugin as a second blocker, an unhedged Publica sentence, Unit 42's missing foothold qualifier and a missing Exposure line on the Publica entry; all were fixed. Iteration 2 found the Panorama fix incomplete (the advisory's mitigation text names Panorama), a Patchstack time zone, a stale run-record sentence and two missing citations; all were fixed. Iteration 3 found two low-confidence wording defects (TeamUpdraft's key-cutoff sentence after the vendor's own page changed, and a Fortinet clause that attributed cron to a second file) and two advisories; it exited under the low-residual rule (truth plus editorial of 2, no F1 or F4), and all four were fixed after the pass without a further independent read, so verification_residual_count records the final pass's 2. Declined advisories: the Fortinet record type (improvement stays, the proof of concept predates the entry) and the Publica entry's length (consolidation is the audit's job). The Splunk CVE-2026-76268 drop was logged as a deliberate drop after the first pass flagged it as a missed angle; passes 2 and 3 found no missed angle.

Publish note for the audit: the Publica/PK Softech entry now carries eleven changelog sections and about 71 KB; the verifier suggests consolidating its per-fund statements and splitting its first action.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-23
item.description:
• Fortinet advisories: FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0 have no fix for a 9.8 JSON API flaw; FortiMail RCE rows too. Fortinet's coordinated hardening release of 2026-10-22 fixed critical and high-severity flaws in FortiOS, FortiManager, FortiAnalyzer, FortiMail and FortiAuthenticator, and the advisories withheld until Patch Tuesday were published on 2026-11-10 with critical rows in FortiMail (unauthenticated code execution, SQL injection and IBE account takeover, CVSS up to 9.8), FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager (an unauthenticated JSON API flaw at 9.8, oftp port flaws, FGFM code execution), FortiOS, FortiAuthenticator and FortiClient. The October builds fix most rows, but FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 8.0.0 through 8.0.2 have no fixed build for CVE-2026-126170 until the upcoming 8.0.3 (workaround: set rpc-permit none), and FortiOS 7.0, FortiMail 7.2 and FortiAnalyzer and FortiManager 7.2 and 7.0 are left to migrate or wait; none of the 2026-11-10 advisories states exploitation. →
  • Arista confirms exploitation of a VeloCloud Orchestrator flaw: any tenant login, even read-only, reaches operator rights. Arista's Security Advisory 0199 of 2026-10-22 fixes CVE-2026-114625 (CVSS 3.1 9.9) in on-premises VeloCloud Orchestrator: any authenticated user, down to the lowest built-in tenant role, can gain operator privileges and reach functions meant for internal use only, and Arista says the flaw is known to be actively exploited. Fixed releases are 5.2.3.18, 6.1.3.10 and 6.4.2.12; hosted and dedicated Orchestrators were already patched, and Arista names no actor, victim count or start date. →
  • FortiSandbox auth bypass (9.6) and FortiSIEM pre-auth RCE (9.4) fixed; FortiSIEM PoC is public, no exploitation listed. Fortinet's PSIRT published two critical unauthenticated advisories on 2026-10-13: an authentication bypass in the FortiSandbox GUI (CVE-2026-107656, CVSS 3.1 9.6; fixed in 5.0.7 and 4.4.10) and a path traversal in the FortiSIEM phQueryMaster service that allows code execution (CVE-2026-106173, 9.4; FortiSIEM 7.5.0 only, fixed in 7.5.1, workaround: restrict tcp port 27918). Fortinet lists neither as known to be exploited, and Horizon3.ai published a write-up and a proof of concept for the FortiSIEM flaw on 2026-10-20. The FortiSandbox ranges include 5.0.6 and 4.4.9, the builds that fixed CVE-2026-25089, one of three FortiSandbox flaws reported exploited in June, so a unit patched for that one is still affected. →
