CVE-2026-109618 / CVE-2026-109619, PHP (PHP2Shell): two unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in the runtime, fixed on 2026-10-21 in 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35, with attack traffic already observed and no upstream release for 8.1 and older (CVSS 4.0 9.2)

The PHP project released PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 on 2026-10-21 to fix two critical vulnerabilities that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both CVSS 4.0 9.2, and urges all PHP users to update immediately (PHP, 2026-10-21; PHP, 2026-10-20). CVE-2026-109618 is memory corruption when PHP handles an out-of-memory error: it aborts the request with longjmp() while internal request data is only partly initialised, and request cleanup then treats the invalid data as valid (PHP, 2026-10-21). CVE-2026-109619 is stale global state: request-owned state survives a fatal error after its memory is freed, and a later request on the same worker uses it (PHP, 2026-10-21). Every PHP installation serving web requests is at risk, including PHP-FPM, Apache with mod_php, php-cgi, FrankenPHP and LiteSpeed; the project rates mod_php highest, with a demonstrated exploit where an unauthenticated request can trigger the attack before any application code runs (PHP, 2026-10-21). The confirmed impact is unauthenticated code execution as the web worker account, validated against mod_php with default settings, and for the second flaw against both mod_php and FPM through session upload progress, which is on by default and needs no session_start() call (PHP, 2026-10-21; PHP, 2026-10-21). The advisory for the second flaw also lists heap use-after-free and memory disclosure among the confirmed impacts (PHP, 2026-10-21), and Sansec says the leaked worker memory can hold passwords, session tokens, API keys and TLS private keys from other requests, and files the upload-progress memory disclosure under CVE-2026-109618 where the PHP advisories list it under CVE-2026-109619 (Sansec, 2026-10-21).

The fixed branches are 8.2 to 8.5; PHP 8.1 and older no longer receive updates, and the project published minimal source backports for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 for people who build from source, while distributions and LTS vendors received the patches in advance (PHP, 2026-10-21). Cloudflare says all web servers running PHP 5.4 or later are affected (Cloudflare, 2026-10-21). The fix is in the runtime, so updating WordPress, a plugin or a theme does not change exposure (Wordfence, 2026-10-20). Products that embed PHP are affected through it: Palo Alto Networks lists PAN-OS 12.2, 12.1, 11.2, 11.1 and 10.2 as affected, with all twenty hotfixes released, and notes that the issue applies to PAN-OS software on PA-Series and VM-Series firewalls and on Panorama (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-30), and ENISA, the Commission, CERT-EU, Europol EC3 and the CSIRTs network point to NCSC-NL's repository for software that bundles PHP (ENISA, 2026-10-21).

CISA added both flaws to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog on 2026-10-26 and revised its alert the same day; the alert names no actor and does not say how CISA learned of the exploitation (CISA, 2026-10-26; CISA KEV, 2026-10-26). Code execution was documented in a honeypot report by Adel Karimi of Perplexity dated 2026-10-24: on three disposable targets running PHP 8.4.26 under single-worker Apache mod_php, 35 execution-stage requests were each followed by a shell started directly by an Apache worker, in a four-stage multipart chain (memory pressure, memory disclosure, more memory pressure, an execution request adjusted to the leaked layout); the chain is consistent with CVE-2026-109618, the records do not establish a CVE-2026-109619 path and no second-stage download was observed (Karimi, 2026-10-24; SecurityWeek, 2026-10-26; BleepingComputer, 2026-10-26). Earlier reports describe scanning and attempts: Cloudflare saw attack traffic against its customers while the flaws were still leaked (Cloudflare, 2026-10-21), watchTowr's honeypots recorded exploitation on 2026-10-21 (watchTowr, 2026-10-21), and VulnCheck's canary hosts recorded scanning from 08:37 UTC that day (VulnCheck, 2026-10-21). VulnCheck says it holds a working exploit for CVE-2026-109618 that, as of 2026-10-26, supports mod_php on PHP 8.2.28 to 8.2.34, 8.3.22 to 8.3.35, 8.4.10 to 8.4.26 and 8.5.10 to 8.5.11 with default settings and display_errors off, and WordPress on default Docker installs (VulnCheck, 2026-10-26). Palo Alto Networks' advisory for both flaws now states that active exploitation has been observed targeting its management interface exposed to the internet, after a copy of 2026-10-27 said very limited exploitation, and names no victim or actor (Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-28; Palo Alto Networks, 2026-10-27); Dream Research's recovered artifacts, described next, add a detailed account of a production compromise through these CVEs, while Unit 42 retracted on 2026-10-25 its update of 2026-10-23 that had linked an attack on a European government agency to these flaws and says it is unable to confirm that the initial access is associated with them (Unit 42, 2026-10-25), and CrowdStrike, Wordfence and Sophos reported no successful exploitation (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23; Wordfence, 2026-10-22; Sophos, 2026-10-22). Dream Research describes the chain it recovered: a custom PHP2Shell build tailored to the management web server of Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS (PHP 8.0.30), combined with the Linux kernel flaw CVE-2026-46300, gave unauthenticated root on 24 internet-facing firewalls and led, through the second of two firewalls of a US government-affiliated organization (the first crashed), to an outbound SSH tunnel, the rooting of the organization's firewall management server and a password-spraying attack on its Active Directory, and CISA's entry for the kernel flaw says the same chaining (Dream Research, 2026-10-29; CISA KEV, 2026-10-28). In Switzerland, SRF reported on 2026-10-26 that TCS Camping is warning about 15,000 customers in connection with the PHP flaw after a data theft at its booking-system supplier Camping.Care, and Blick, citing SRF, writes that the attackers used the two flaws; neither names a CVE (SRF, 2026-10-26; Blick, 2026-10-26).

PHP posted an informational advisory on 2026-10-23 for a third code-execution path, CVE-2026-115560, that the October releases do not fix: it needs an application that sets session.serialize_handler to php_binary or php_serialize, switches it to php with ini_set() before session_start(), and leaves session upload progress enabled; PHP calls it an unlikely vector, issues no emergency release, suggests session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next regular bugfix release and will publish the full advisory then (PHP, 2026-10-23). PHP has not stated affected versions or a severity score for CVE-2026-115560, and no exploitation is reported (The Hacker News, 2026-10-23).

Assessments of how easy exploitation is diverge. Sansec says an attack needs specific knowledge of the target server and specific conditions on it, that nobody has shown a single request that works against any vulnerable server, as there was for Log4Shell and Shellshock, that a researcher who tested the public proofs of concept found they do not work against a default PHP installation, and that mass exploitation is therefore less likely than it first expected, while it advises updating anyway (Sansec, 2026-10-21). CrowdStrike expects no single universal exploit but says a reliable one is feasible against a specific deployment profile, such as a fixed Docker image, because an attacker can calibrate offsets and heap grooming in advance (CrowdStrike, 2026-10-23), and the SANS Internet Storm Center, reading the public proofs of concept, finds a universal, reliable one-click exploit quite difficult (SANS ISC, 2026-10-23). Red Hat rates CVE-2026-109618 Important (CVSS 3.1 8.1 with high attack complexity, against 9.8 at NVD), says reliable exploitation requires precise heap manipulation and timing, and says its standard Red Hat Enterprise Linux deployments use PHP-FPM, whose workers exit on early initialization failures, so code execution is difficult in practice and typically needs non-default behavior such as parsing a second request body during script execution (Red Hat, 2026-10-21). That sits against VulnCheck's weaponized exploit above, and the advice of the PHP project, BACS, CERT-EU and ENISA to update is unchanged. Vendors of products that embed PHP report as follows: Citrix lists the NetScaler management GUI on every supported version (NetScaler Product Security, 2026-10-22); Cisco lists Expressway, Ultra-Reliable Wireless Backhaul, Duo Access Gateway and ISE Portal Builder, with fixes at 15.5.21, 26.2.1.9 (November 2026) and 3.2.0 (Cisco PSIRT, 2026-10-30); Fortinet keeps only FortiDDoS, FortiSOAR and FortiSOAR PaaS under investigation (Fortinet PSIRT, 2026-10-26); Splunk lists its products as unaffected or remedied (Splunk, 2026-10-26); Tenable's patch SC-202610.2 updates the bundled PHP in Security Center and Enclave Security to 8.2.35 (Tenable, 2026-10-23; Tenable, 2026-10-23); Siemens lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 devices running PAN-OS as affected (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-23); and WatchGuard says none of its products are affected (WatchGuard PSIRT, 2026-10-21).

Exposure
Every internet-facing server or container image that runs PHP, and every product, appliance or administration interface that embeds it, internal ones included; BACS stresses that operators often do not know a product uses PHP, and that distribution packages can carry the fix under an unchanged version number, so the running version and the vendor's security information decide (BACS, 2026-10-21). On WordPress the running PHP version is shown under Tools > Site Health > Info > Server (Wordfence, 2026-10-20).
Detection
AWS, as relayed by Inside IT, advises an operator who cannot exclude a compromise to start the investigation at least from 2026-10-17, its earliest honeypot exploit attempt (Inside IT, 2026-10-22); the telemetry is, in web access logs, multipart POST requests to PHP endpoints from unfamiliar sources, including multipart requests that use the upload-progress code path, which VulnCheck's canaries saw scanners send (VulnCheck, 2026-10-21); in PHP error logs and process telemetry, worker crashes and fatal errors, and processes started by the web server or PHP worker account, since the code runs with the web worker's privileges (PHP, 2026-10-21), above all a shell started directly by an Apache worker, as in Karimi's honeypots and, since 2026-10-28, on GreyNoise's sensors, where it went on to open bash reverse shells over /dev/tcp, and create a .ssh directory under /var/www (Karimi, 2026-10-24; GreyNoise, 2026-11-01), which CISA also names as the behaviour to watch for (CISA, 2026-10-26); on Windows servers running IIS with PHP-CGI, Morphisec reports the web worker w3wp.exe starting php-cgi.exe, which started cmd.exe and a packed payload that tried to open a reverse shell (Morphisec, 2026-10-28); and in the web root, new or changed files. BACS asks operators to examine logs and systems for unusual requests, crashes, changed files and unexpected processes, and says an update does not remove a compromise that has already happened (BACS, 2026-10-21). ReliaQuest, which reproduced exploitation of CVE-2026-109618 in controlled labs, reports a sequence across the PHP error, Apache access, Apache error and system logs: a POST that returns HTTP 500, PHP memory exhaustion reported "in Unknown on line 0" where an ordinary memory error names the application file and line, heap corruption, and an abort of the Apache worker that handled the request within seconds; each event can be benign alone, the full sequence on the same process is the stronger indication, and linking request to crash needs the process ID in the Apache access log as well as the error log (ReliaQuest, 2026-10-22).
Defender takeaway
Update the PHP runtime on every internet-facing host today and restart the workers, internet-facing systems first and then internal and embedded installations, and take the management interface of every appliance that embeds PHP off the internet; where an update must wait, CERT-EU advises isolating internet-facing applications from public networks until the fix is applied and verified (CERT-EU, 2026-10-21). The project's interim settings (disable session upload progress, enforce memory_limit=-1 administratively, a low post_max_size, block multipart requests at the proxy where uploads are not needed) reduce only some attack paths, and BACS says a web application firewall alone is not enough (BACS, 2026-10-21; PHP, 2026-10-21). PHP 8.1 and older need a vendor backport, the project's source backports or an upgrade, ASLR is not a safe reason to wait on x86-64 given VulnCheck's exploit, and an update does not remove an attacker who is already in. The October releases do not fix CVE-2026-115560, so keep session upload progress disabled on updated hosts until PHP's next regular release (PHP, 2026-10-23). Because the flaws can disclose worker memory, rotating session secrets, API keys and other credentials that the PHP workers handled is a reasonable step on hosts that were reachable while unpatched.

BACS told RTS it knows of no reliable, confirmed substitute for the updates and that the interim measures give no guaranteed full protection (RTS, 2026-10-21).

Attack traffic was reported on the day: Cloudflare saw it against its customers while the flaws were still leaked, watchTowr's honeypots recorded exploitation, and VulnCheck's canary hosts logged scanning from 08:37 UTC and at least one unsuccessful web-shell attempt through a session file, while VulnCheck says it holds a working exploit for CVE-2026-109618 that succeeds on x86-64 with ASLR enabled; no source reports a confirmed compromise (Cloudflare, 2026-10-21; watchTowr, 2026-10-21; VulnCheck, 2026-10-21). Public-sector sites went offline as a precaution, mostly on the evening of 2026-10-21. The canton of Basel-Stadt activated its crisis staff and shut down every PHP-run cantonal website with no restoration time given, while stating that no security-relevant incident had been registered (Canton of Basel-Stadt, 2026-10-21). The Ticino cantonal administration temporarily disabled some online services, the website of the University of Geneva was unreachable, and the EPFL site displayed a notice that its pages were currently unreachable, although nau.ch says it still worked (nau.ch, 2026-10-21); RTS lists the EPFL and University of Geneva sites as temporarily suspended (RTS, 2026-10-21). Several Neuchâtel canton and city sites were unreachable without an official statement; Arcinfo presumes a link to the PHP flaw, which the state had not confirmed (RTS, 2026-10-21). Lodur, the platform many Swiss fire brigades use to manage their fire brigades and alarm groups, was out of service because its provider took its servers offline as a precaution: users could neither read stored data nor edit alarm groups, though the Valais cantonal fire office said this does not necessarily mean the alarm-triggering systems are down (nau.ch, 2026-10-21; RTS, 2026-10-21). Publica took its website offline on the afternoon of 2026-10-21 as a precaution, says it has closed the vulnerabilities with security updates and was back online that evening, and states the outage is unrelated to the cyberattack on its software supplier (Publica, 2026-10-21). Dutch authorities took DigiD, MijnOverheid, Overheid.nl, TweedeKamer.nl and the tax authority offline for a time, and most were back by that evening (Security.nl, 2026-10-21); RTS reports that the site of the Paris police prefecture was also suspended (RTS, 2026-10-21). Basel-Stadt said it would report on progress on the morning of 2026-10-22, and no restoration status had been published as of the early morning of 2026-10-22 UTC.

Oracle October 2026 Critical Patch Update: six unauthenticated network CVSS 10.0 rows in Access Manager, SOA Suite, E-Business Suite and JD Edwards, and WebLogic CVSS 9.8 flaws reachable over HTTP and T3/IIOP

Oracle's Critical Patch Update advisory of 2026-10-20 contains 1295 new security patches (Oracle, 2026-10-20). Its risk matrices score 112 rows at CVSS 3.1 9.0 or higher, and 90 of those, covering 73 distinct CVE ids, are marked as remotely exploitable without authentication with a network attack vector (Oracle, 2026-10-20). Six rows score 10.0: CVE-2026-87337 in the Access Manager Authentication Engine (HTTP), CVE-2026-91231 in the SOA Suite Adapters (HTTP), CVE-2026-91216 and CVE-2026-91221 in the SOA Suite Fabric Layer (T3 and IIOP), CVE-2026-101809 in the E-Business Suite Workflow Notification Mailer (HTTP, 12.2.3 to 12.2.15) and CVE-2026-91299 in the JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Orchestrator security component (HTTP, 9.2.0.0 to 9.2.26.5) (Oracle, 2026-10-20). WebLogic Server 12.2.1.4.0, 14.1.1.0.0, 14.1.2.0.0 and 15.1.1.0.0 carry CVE-2026-91323 (HTTP) and CVE-2026-83399 (T3 and IIOP) at 9.8 and CVE-2026-87302 (HTTP) at 9.1; Identity Manager's End User Self Service has CVE-2026-91408 (T3 and IIOP, 9.8) and Access Manager's SAML path CVE-2026-87251 (9.8) (Oracle, 2026-10-20). The advisory states no exploitation for any row and carries only Oracle's standing sentence that it receives reports of attempts to exploit already-patched flaws (Oracle, 2026-10-20); for CVE-2026-101767, Defused's decoys have since recorded exploit attempts, described in the update below. Oracle points to My Oracle Support documents for patch availability (Oracle, 2026-10-20).

Exposure
A WebLogic, SOA Suite, Access Manager or Identity Manager server whose HTTP, T3 or IIOP listener, or SAML endpoint, answers from a network that is not the management network; an E-Business Suite 12.2.3 to 12.2.15 web tier with the Workflow Notification Mailer, or whose URL firewall allows the Thin Client Framework servlet, as the default configuration does (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20); a JD Edwards EnterpriseOne 9.2 server with the Orchestrator. The product version comes from the product's own version command or the inventory.
Detection
Oracle names no indicator. For the E-Business Suite flaw CVE-2026-101767, Horizon3 lists unauthenticated POST requests to the Thin Client Framework servlet followed by backend database activity, SQL reconnaissance shortly after unauthenticated web requests, and the oracle account spawning a shell through the Concurrent Manager (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20). Otherwise watch web and application-server access logs and the WebLogic and SOA server logs for requests to the affected components from untrusted sources, T3 and IIOP connections from unexpected networks in flow or load-balancer logs, and Java process-creation events where the middleware process spawns a shell, an interpreter or a download tool.
Defender takeaway
Apply the October 2026 update to the six 10.0 components first wherever they are reachable beyond the management network, together with any E-Business Suite web tier exposed to CVE-2026-101767, whose chain Horizon3 has described, then to the WebLogic and Identity Manager rows; where a patch cannot go in at once, remove the Thin Client Framework servlet from the EBS URL firewall allowlist and restrict the EBS web tier to trusted networks (Horizon3.ai, 2026-10-20). Oracle's next scheduled update is the Critical Security Patch Update of 17 November 2026 (Oracle, 2026-10-20).

Composer's token leak was triggered on the default path by GitHub's new hyphenated installation-token format failing Composer's validation when it loaded its configuration, not by package-resolution errors, and it concerned GITHUB_TOKEN and GitHub App installation tokens rather than personal access tokens. Hosted-runner tokens usually expired with the failing job, self-hosted runner tokens stay valid for up to 24 hours and App tokens for up to an hour, and GitHub rolled the format change back on 2026-05-13. No source links the bug to Mini Shai-Hulud, and the advisory rates it High 7.5 with fixes in 2.9.8, 2.2.28 and 1.10.28.

The leak was not tied to package-resolution errors: GitHub's new format for GitHub App installation tokens contains a hyphen, fails Composer's character validation when its configuration loads, and the exception prints the full token to stderr, so any workflow with such a token in Composer's auth hit it on the default path, including the auto-injected GITHUB_TOKEN (Packagist, 2026-05-13). Classic ghp_ personal access tokens are not affected by the validation bug itself, though the advisory notes the same leak applies to any future credential that fails validation (Composer, 2026-05-13). Packagist's relevant permission point is that App tokens can carry permissions broader than the workflow's own permissions: declaration, not that every GITHUB_TOKEN can write workflow files (Packagist, 2026-05-13).

The exposure was bounded: hosted-runner tokens usually expired with the failing job, self-hosted runner tokens stay valid for up to 24 hours and App tokens for up to an hour, and GitHub rolled the format change back on 2026-05-13 before planning a new rollout from 2026-05-18 (Packagist, 2026-05-13). Neither the Packagist post nor the advisory mentions Mini Shai-Hulud or exploitation; the advisory rates the flaw High 7.5, fixed in 2.9.8, 2.2.28 and 1.10.28 (Composer, 2026-05-13).

Mini Shai-Hulud first hit official SAP npm packages on 2026-04-29, and in the TanStack compromise of 2026-05-11 the fork pull request added a payload file that the pull_request_target benchmark job built; the release job's own publish step was skipped while the malware published directly with the OIDC token it read from runner memory. The provenance on the malicious packages is genuine rather than forged, the payload runs from a prepare script of an optional git dependency and its memory scraper runs under sudo. The compromise is CVE-2026-45321, scored 9.6 and in CISA's KEV catalog since 2026-05-27, and the restore-only cache action and npm audit signatures replace a cache option and a command that do not exist.

Mini Shai-Hulud's first wave hit four official SAP npm packages on 2026-04-29 with malicious preinstall scripts (The Register, 2026-04-30). In the TanStack compromise no reconnaissance step is reported; the pull request added a bundled payload file that the pull_request_target benchmark job executed when it checked out and built the PR's merge ref, rather than slipping in lockfile, dependency or .github changes, and the release job never reached its publish step: tests failed, Publish Packages was skipped, and the malware published directly with the OIDC token it read from runner memory (TanStack, 2026-05-11). No npm token was needed for that publish, but the payload itself steals credentials and spreads with them (StepSecurity, 2026-05-11).

The SLSA provenance on the malicious packages is genuine, an attestation of a compromised pipeline rather than a forgery, and no source ties it to EU procurement (StepSecurity, 2026-05-11). The payload runs from the prepare script of an optional git dependency, not from postinstall (TanStack advisory, 2026-05-11), and its memory scraper runs as sudo python3, so a filter for non-root readers of /proc/<pid>/mem misses it (StepSecurity, 2026-05-11). The compromise is CVE-2026-45321, scored 9.6 (TanStack advisory, 2026-05-11) and listed by CISA as known exploited on 2026-05-27 (CISA KEV catalog, 2026-05-27). The cache action has no save: false input; restore-only caching is the separate restore action (actions/cache README), npm verifies attestations with npm audit signatures (npm Docs), and GitHub Security Lab warns that combining the pull_request_target trigger with an explicit checkout of an untrusted pull request may lead to repository compromise (GitHub Security Lab, 2021-08-03).

The two flaws are fixed by separate updates rather than one combined out-of-band release: Malware Protection Engine version 1.1.26040.8 fixes CVE-2026-41091, and Microsoft typically ships engine updates once a month or as needed (MSRC, 2026-05-19); Antimalware Platform version 4.18.26040.7 fixes CVE-2026-45498, which is a denial of service (CWE-400), not a privilege escalation (MSRC, 2026-05-19). The "Turn off routine remediation" policy named earlier only decides whether Defender remediates detected threats automatically or prompts the user (Microsoft Learn); it does not hold back engine updates, so the check is whether engine and platform updates reach each host.

The hunt signals given earlier, junction events on Defender paths and SYSTEM processes spawned by MsMpEng.exe, have no source. The behavior observed in the wild is renamed exploit binaries staged in the user's Pictures and Downloads folders (Help Net Security, 2026-04-17) and, for RedSun, a Defender remediation of an EICAR test string whose file rewrite is redirected so that the Cloud Files infrastructure runs the attacker's binary as SYSTEM (Vectra AI, 2026-04-21). The researcher has since said CVE-2026-41091 is RedSun and CVE-2026-45498 is UnDefend (The Hacker News, 2026-05-21).

The five NOT COVERED rows are dispositioned: the four Plex Media Server flaws (CVE-2026-96652, -96654, -96655, -96656) and EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition (CVE-2026-106931) are borderline-drops below. No RANSOMWARE row.

Backlog (state/coverage_backlog.md): no open row, nothing carried or added.

Published: php-critical-release-pre-announced-cve-2026-109618-109619 (high, the release lands about 11 h after the fire; the next fire reads php.net and writes the update), oracle-october-2026-cpu-six-unauthenticated-cvss-10-rows (notable, no exploitation reported; the scheduled-release duty), aa26-293a-safepay-ransomware-edge-flaws-backup-nas-reset (notable), emudhra-intermediate-ca-keys-recoverable-trust-store-updates (notable, dated trust-store consequence on 2026-10-27), apt28-hookedge-backdoor-nato-police-shipbuilder-ssh-tunnel (notable, law-enforcement and government target class) and teamupdraft-updraftcentral-stolen-keys-backdoor-plugins (high, active exploitation of a vendor-held management key against WordPress estates). Updated: CVE-2026-0257 PAN-OS (update: Unit 42 names Qilin and Inc and reports the vCenter and ESXi pivot; S1 and S3 returned the same update and it is one record), PK Softech / Publica (update: Tamedia's Akira and ransom report, unconfirmed; the actor and ransom sentences of the main text moved, the dated earlier sections were left as history), ConnectWise Cloud Backup (improvement: Sophos X-Ops as a second observer of the sweep) and Metabase (update: a Swiss victim, Republik, found through its own statement as relayed by swissinfo.ch and Netzwoche).

borderline-drop lines:

  • borderline-drop: Plex Media Server CVE-2026-96652, CVE-2026-96654, CVE-2026-96655, CVE-2026-96656 (S1) - KEV-listed, Plex says actively and widely exploited with a public proof of concept since 2026-10-16 and fixes in 1.43.3.10861, but it is a consumer media server and no source shows a public-sector deployment; relevance to the constituency fails the gate and doubt resolves toward drop.
  • borderline-drop: EG Secure Solutions SiteGuard Server Edition CVE-2026-106931 (S1) - KEV-listed, vendor and JVN confirm exploitation, but a Japan-only host WAF with a local attack vector and no constituency exposure.
  • borderline-drop: Chrome 156.0.8078.47 (S1) - 353 fixes including six Critical, no exploitation statement; the regular browser cycle.
  • borderline-drop: Apache Tomcat 11.0.27, 10.1.61, 9.0.123 JNDIRealm SASL fail-open bypass and the HTTP/2 and AJP mix-ups (S1) - not exploited, configuration-dependent reach.
  • borderline-drop: Eptura Archibus CVE-2026-107186, -107187, -107188 (S1) - already dropped by the previous fire; Rapid7's own red-team chain only, normally internal.
  • borderline-drop: Unblu Spark CVE-2026-9589 and CVE-2026-14933 (S1) - need authentication or an agent joining the attacker's session, cloud already fixed, no exploitation.
  • borderline-drop: Windows Active Directory Domain Services CVE-2026-70229 (S1) - high attack complexity, rated Exploitation More Likely but not exploited; the Patch Tuesday cycle, and S1's reading of the October CVRF found Windows Shell CVE-2026-96951, already covered, as the only exploited CVE.
  • borderline-drop: Fortinet FortiSIEM CVE-2026-106173 (9.4, unauthenticated) and FortiSandbox CVE-2026-107656 (9.6) from the 2026-10-13 bundle (S1) - Fortinet states neither is exploited, both are outside the window, and the monthly cycle covers them; S1 offered a catch-up entry and the gate says no.
  • borderline-drop: SAP 2026-10-13 Patch Day, Siemens and Schneider October bundles and the CISA ICS advisories of 2026-10-20 (S1) - nothing at CVSS 9.0 or above that is pre-auth and exploited; Roundcube 1.7.5 and 1.6.20, Laravel, Mattermost, Juniper SSR, Duplicator and the older Linux kernel chains dropped as out of window or out of scope.
  • borderline-drop: JPCERT/CC and Macnica on app-to-backend API attacks with AI-assisted scanning (S3) - Japanese wave built on basic access-control and configuration weaknesses with no Swiss case and nothing a defender does differently tomorrow.
  • borderline-drop: NorForge's open Cairn control panels (S3) - builds on the Gambit entry already in the store, victims in the US, Japan and Australia, no new defender lever.
  • borderline-drop: Sophos X-Ops Entra intrusion through vishing and SMS-code password reset (S3) - published 2026-10-19, one customer case of a well-known pattern; the ConnectWise entry already carries the tenant-review lever.
  • borderline-drop: Hunt.io Graylog Log4Shell chain and GreyNoise's skynox7 proxyjacking (S3) - no constituency nexus.
  • borderline-drop: Zeabur second breach, Bullhorn outage, Canva and Canny, IDC Frontier's sixth report (S4) - no Swiss nexus, no actor or exfiltration finding yet, or recovery status only.
  • borderline-drop: DD-Automation (Aesch BL), SafePay leak with an "Armasuisse" folder (S4) - single paywalled Inside IT report from 2026-10-16, no victim statement, the Army says the folder holds nothing critical, and nothing to hunt; the Armed Forces supplier nexus is why the next fire re-checks it, and a victim statement or a second source makes it publishable.
  • borderline-drop: Skyguide radar-picture outage of 2026-10-20 (Skyguide: no sign of a cyberattack), BACS week 42 TWINT and hotel-booking phishing (consumer targeting), Swiss Government Cloud tender (procurement, no obligation change) (S2).

Single-source and carve-outs: the Oracle entry rests on the vendor's own advisory (reliability A); AA26-293A is single-source-national-cert; the APT28 entry's new victims and tradecraft rest on Symantec alone, with Recorded Future independent on the backdoor; the Akira and ransom claim on the Publica entry rests on Tamedia's paywalled article (standfirst and key points read) relayed by Inside IT and is unconfirmed by the Confederation and Publica; Republik's account rests on swissinfo.ch and Netzwoche, its own page was not read. Contradictions carried in the entries: PHP's affected range (CERT-EU "PHP 5 onwards", Sansec "5.4 or later", both unconfirmed) and the two PHP CVE ids absent from CVE.org and EUVD at 03:38 UTC; which UpdraftPlus release removes which keys (TeamUpdraft's statement against Nethemba's code reading); Google's eight subordinate CAs against six TLS intermediates; Unit 42's text dating the KEV listing of CVE-2026-0257 to 13 May against the catalogue's 2026-05-29, which the entry keeps.

Verification: seven independent passes. Iteration 6 returned CLEAN; the confirmation pass (7) returned NEEDS_FIXES with one low-confidence truth finding (a start-time attribution on the TeamUpdraft entry), one low-confidence editorial contradiction (Huntress and Sophos sweep timings on the ConnectWise entry) and no F1 or F4 finding. Under the early-exit rule the fixes were applied and the run published without an eighth pass; the two residuals are the declined standing items (older em dashes and workflow wording in append-only text, living-page source records) that the audit sweeps.

Coverage: all 21 essential sources were attempted and every slice record was attempted (S1 26, S2 19, S3 14, S4 12; the previous two fires' attempts excluded 116 sources from the rotational ranking, and 12 were topped back up in S4's domain where the exclusion would have emptied the slice). Entities added: five, plus seven product records from sync_products.py. Promoted: forescout-research. New candidates: nethemba, jpcert-eyes, bs-ch-medienmitteilungen. Self-edit: tools/source_health.py now lists connectwise-trust-center as a documented unreachable host (the previous fire set the record to blocked but the tool still flagged it needs-demote); the health sweep ends with no unsolved record. ivanti-advisory-hub in the rotation gap list is a state id with no record in sources.json; the real record ivanti-psirt was read.

Next-fire watch: php.net release at 2026-10-21 14:00 UTC (CVE ids, fixed versions, whether the leaked tool appears; an update on the PHP entry), Cisco PSIRT publications of 2026-10-21 (Expressway, IOS XR, Secure Client, Snort, Unified Communications), CERT-FR's avis on the Oracle CPU, the DD-Automation re-check. For the audit: the ENISA Threat Landscape 2026 (news item of 2026-09-22) and Microsoft's Digital Defense Report 2026 (secondary coverage of 2026-10-14) have no store entry; three September Swiss public-sector incidents from the Vaud SOC digest have none either (CHUV through an external laboratory, 2026-09-08; a Basel-Stadt school print system, 2026-09-04; SRG SSR, 2026-09-28); the vaud-soc-cyber-threat-review recipe note was corrected (the October edition is due about mid-November).

Coverage gaps: apa-ots (no listing or feed route), swisscybersecurity-net (feed 404), news-admin-ch (only the 12 newest cards reachable), tagesanzeiger.ch (paywalled body, standfirst read), ncc-research (listing carries no dates), technadu (extract served by the metered reader, boilerplate only), rapid7-research (feed malformed, listing read through url).

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-20
item.description:
• Three configuration-dependent NGINX heap flaws (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in 1.30.6, 1.31.7 and Debian trixie, not bookworm. The nginx 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) releases of 2026-10-14 fix five security flaws, three of them heap-corruption bugs that F5 scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and an unauthenticated attacker can reach with crafted HTTP requests, but only on configurations that combine alias with rewrite and $request_filename, use a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or enable asynchronous file I/O with server-side includes; the other two concern HTTP/3 and TLS session ticket key rotation. F5 says the heap flaws restart the worker, with code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed; no exploitation or public proof of concept is reported, nginx.org rates all five medium, and Debian fixed trixie with DSA-6575-1 while its bookworm package is still marked vulnerable. →
  • OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it. OVHcloud says a hacker used a developer's GitHub account to replace the release binaries of its command-line tool for versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, available for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times; the first replacement was at about 12:47 UTC and OVHcloud deleted the files at 14:21 UTC after a customer's pinned SHA-256 failed. Its postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on the developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue. Anyone who installed or updated the tool from a release asset in that window must rotate every secret on that host; the source tag and the Go module were untouched. →
  • Siemens confirms exploitation of a Software Center DLL side-loading flaw; attackers bring their own signed copy. Siemens ProductCERT says it validated active exploitation of CVE-2026-110936, a DLL side-loading flaw in Siemens Software Center versions before V4.0.9.8, which it fixed in advisory SSA-580366 of 2026-10-15; installed copies update themselves the next time the application starts. The attackers did not abuse an installed copy: they delivered a genuine, validly signed copy of version 3.5.8.7 with their own files beside it through what Siemens calls the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign, so the check that finds it is behaviour on any Windows PC, not a Software Center inventory. →

TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Three configuration-dependent NGINX heap flaws (CVSS 9.2) are fixed in 1.30.6, 1.31.7 and Debian trixie, not bookworm. The nginx 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) releases of 2026-10-14 fix five security flaws, three of them heap-corruption bugs that F5 scores CVSS 4.0 9.2 and an unauthenticated attacker can reach with crafted HTTP requests, but only on configurations that combine alias with rewrite and $request_filename, use a regex map whose captures are referenced before its output variable, or enable asynchronous file I/O with server-side includes; the other two concern HTTP/3 and TLS session ticket key rotation. F5 says the heap flaws restart the worker, with code execution only where ASLR is disabled or bypassed; no exploitation or public proof of concept is reported, nginx.org rates all five medium, and Debian fixed trixie with DSA-6575-1 while its bookworm package is still marked vulnerable. →
  2. 02OVHcloud CLI release binaries carried a secret-stealing build for about 90 minutes; a pinned hash caught it. OVHcloud says a hacker used a developer's GitHub account to replace the release binaries of its command-line tool for versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, available for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times; the first replacement was at about 12:47 UTC and OVHcloud deleted the files at 14:21 UTC after a customer's pinned SHA-256 failed. Its postmortem traces the account compromise to a poisoned editor extension installed on the developer's personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, ties it to the GlassWorm actor through a Solana wallet, and names a missing release-immutability setting as the main issue. Anyone who installed or updated the tool from a release asset in that window must rotate every secret on that host; the source tag and the Go module were untouched. →
  3. 03Siemens confirms exploitation of a Software Center DLL side-loading flaw; attackers bring their own signed copy. Siemens ProductCERT says it validated active exploitation of CVE-2026-110936, a DLL side-loading flaw in Siemens Software Center versions before V4.0.9.8, which it fixed in advisory SSA-580366 of 2026-10-15; installed copies update themselves the next time the application starts. The attackers did not abuse an installed copy: they delivered a genuine, validly signed copy of version 3.5.8.7 with their own files beside it through what Siemens calls the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign, so the check that finds it is behaviour on any Windows PC, not a Software Center inventory. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Trending vulnerabilities 2Research, reports & policy 1Updates to prior coverage 18Action items 24

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

NOTABLEupdatedNATOA2

OVHcloud CLI: release binaries of already-published versions were replaced on 2026-10-19 with a build that steals secrets from disk, uploaded through a developer's GitHub account

OVHcloud's founder says a hacker used the GitHub account of one of its developers to add to the official command-line tool's releases a binary whose job is to retrieve secrets from the disk, that versions v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 are compromised, and that v0.10.0 and v0.16.0 are clean (Octave Klaba, 2026-10-19). A user whose CI pins a SHA-256 reported on GitHub that the assets of v0.13.0 to v0.15.0 were replaced between about 12:47 and 13:12 UTC, weeks after publication, by an uploader who is not a public member of the ovh organisation, with a local build of a later commit that has uncommitted changes and no release version flag, while the v0.15.0 tag and the Go module proxy still point at the original commit (GitHub issue #300, 2026-10-19). An OVHcloud maintainer replied that all the binaries involved were deleted at 16:21 (GMT+2) and that v0.16.0, with a signed tag, is an immutable release (GitHub issue #300, 2026-10-19). OpenSourceMalware, working from GitHub's server-side records, says no tag was pushed and no release workflow ran, ties the same account's earlier force-pushes carrying a hidden loader (from 2026-03-05) to the GlassWorm campaign while saying that whether the same actor did both is its inference, notes that the project's release tooling replaces existing assets as normal behaviour, and says it has not analysed the payload because the files were deleted before anyone archived them (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-19). OVHcloud's advisory gives the root cause: the account belongs to a developer who installed the editor extension color-picker-universal 2.8.91 on a personal MacBook on 2025-10-20, and the releases were replaced with stolen keys, not from that laptop; the malicious assets were online for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20). Whether any secret was stolen is not public.

Exposure
OVHcloud says only users who installed or updated the tool between 14:47 and 16:21 (UTC+2) on 2026-10-19, which is 12:47 to 14:21 UTC, are affected, and that a v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 download from before that day is not (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20); OpenSourceMalware reads the channels as macOS, Linux (x86_64, arm64) or Windows (x86_64) through the install script, the Homebrew cask, a direct download of a v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 asset or a CI step that fetches the release tarball, and says go install, builds from source and the vendor's Docker image were not affected (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-19).
Detection
An archive whose SHA-256 differs from the original release's for an unchanged version number, which is how the reporter caught it; release-API records of weeks-old assets replaced by an uploader who is not the original publisher; and, on a retained binary, build metadata showing a modified working tree and no release version (GitHub issue #300, 2026-10-19). OVHcloud says each run of the malicious binary leaves a working folder named envchecker followed by digits in the temporary directory and never deletes it, so its presence on a host that ran the tool shows exposure; the stealer reads the databases and histories of AI coding assistants and agents (VS Code, Cursor, Continue, Sourcegraph Cody, OpenCode, Hermes, Claude) as well as cloud, Kubernetes, Terraform, npm, SSH and Git credentials, and exfiltrates through Solana RPC calls and an upload endpoint (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20). Deleting the binary does not undo a run: OVHcloud says to change all the secrets on the disk (Octave Klaba, 2026-10-19).

Triage: a replaced asset alone is not proof, since the project's release tooling replaces assets routinely; the discriminators are an uploader who is not the original publisher, a modified-tree build without the release version, and a digest that changed without a version bump (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-19; GitHub issue #300, 2026-10-19).

Defender takeaway
A host that installed or updated the tool from a release asset between 12:47 and 14:21 UTC on 2026-10-19, the window as OpenSourceMalware reads it (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-19), needs its secrets rotated, not just the binary removed (Octave Klaba, 2026-10-19), and then v0.16.0 or later (GitHub issue #300, 2026-10-19); pinning release digests or building from the source tag, as the reporter did, is the durable lever against a swapped asset on a mutable release.
Update22 Oct 2026 03:47 UTCrun 2026-10-22T0256Z-intelbodyevidencesourcessourcing_notesummarytechniques

OVHcloud published its advisory and postmortem. It says the compromised account belongs to a developer who installed the editor extension color-picker-universal 2.8.91 on a personal MacBook on 2025-10-20; the extension queries a Solana wallet that OVHcloud says belongs to the GlassWorm actor, a persistent Node.js service was registered on the laptop, and several personal repositories of the account were compromised in March 2026. The release replacement was made with stolen keys, not from that laptop, and OVHcloud says neither the developer's OVHcloud laptop nor its internal CI/CD was compromised as far as it knows (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20). OpenSourceMalware reads the same account as already compromised for seven months, which is its assessment, and says that the same actor made both steps is its inference (OpenSourceMalware, 2026-10-19).

OVHcloud describes the payload as the original CLI recompiled with embedded stealer code that copies a list of credential files and AI-agent data stores into a temporary folder named envchecker, archives them and exfiltrates through Solana RPC calls and an upload endpoint; the malicious assets were online for 1h33 and downloaded about 250 times (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20). It names the missing release-immutability setting as the main issue, says it allows developers to attach personal GitHub accounts to the organisation, and reports that it enabled immutable releases on every repository, suspended the account, reviewed write access and repository logs without finding another compromise, and published v0.16.0 with a signed tag as the clean release (OVHcloud, 2026-10-20).

Builds on: 2026-05-28/crowdstrike-google-and-shadowserver-simultaneously-sever-all

incident20 Oct 03:36Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: GitHub issue ovh/ovhcloud-cli #300 (external reporter, with OVHcloud maintainer replies) · Octave Klaba, OVHcloud founder (post on X) · OpenSourceMalware · OVHcloud (security advisory and postmortem)

02Trending vulnerabilities2 items

NOTABLECVE-2026-15176 +4updatedNATOA2

CVE-2026-15176 / CVE-2026-93479 / CVE-2026-97205, NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus: three unauthenticated heap-corruption flaws rated CVSS 4.0 9.2, reachable only in specific configurations and fixed in 1.30.6 and 1.31.7

nginx's change log for 1.30.6, dated 14 October 2026, lists five security fixes, which nginx.org's advisories page ties to 1.30.6 (stable) and 1.31.7 (mainline) (nginx.org change log, 2026-10-14; nginx.org, 2026-10-14); three of them are CVE-2026-15176, a heap buffer overflow in the core module that CCB describes as reachable where a location uses alias together with rewrite and a set or return directive referencing $request_filename, or where $request_filename appears in an access-log format; CVE-2026-93479, a heap buffer overflow in script evaluation that affects configurations whose regex map captures are referenced in root or an access-log format before the map's output variable, or that use a non-cacheable variable in a string expression; and CVE-2026-97205, a use-after-free when asynchronous file I/O is enabled, which Daily CyberSecurity relays from F5 as triggered by an SSI page with include virtual commands (Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium, 2026-10-19; Daily CyberSecurity, 2026-10-14). Each is scored CVSS 4.0 9.2 and reachable by an unauthenticated network attacker, the first two under conditions beyond the attacker's control, with CCB's warning and vector covering the first two and Daily CyberSecurity all three (Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium, 2026-10-19; Daily CyberSecurity, 2026-10-14). F5's CNA text says the overflow may restart the worker process and that attackers can execute code where ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-10-20). Daily CyberSecurity reports that F5 has confirmed no public proof of concept for any of the three, and no exploitation is reported (Daily CyberSecurity, 2026-10-14). Help Net Security reports that VulnCheck flagged exploitation attempts against an earlier NGINX flaw, CVE-2026-42945, three days after the flaw and its proof of concept were public (Help Net Security, 2026-05-18). The other two are CVE-2026-95101 (with HTTP/3, part of an unknown frame might be treated as the request body, bypassing client_max_body_size or injecting data into the proxied request) and CVE-2026-97629 (with TLS session ticket key rotation, one key was left uninitialised, which might allow forging a session) (nginx.org change log, 2026-10-14); nginx.org rates all five medium (nginx.org, 2026-10-14).

Exposure
Nginx 0.1.29 to 1.31.6 depending on the flaw, with branches older than 1.30 outside the range of CVE-2026-93479, and NGINX Plus R33 to R36 and 37.0.0 to 37.1.0 for the first two (nginx.org, 2026-10-14; Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium, 2026-10-19). A build is affected only if its configuration matches one of the patterns above, which nginx -T prints with every include; the version string alone is not enough, because distribution packages carry their own fixes. Debian fixed trixie with DSA-6575-1 (trixie-security 1.26.3-3+deb13u10) (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-10-25), while its tracker still marks bookworm (1.22.1-9+deb12u10) vulnerable (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-10-20).
Detection
F5 says the overflow leads to a worker restart, so process-supervision and error-log telemetry for unexpected worker exits and respawn bursts, matched against the unauthenticated requests to the affected locations in the access log, is the signal (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-10-20). Patching does not remediate a compromise that already happened (Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium, 2026-10-19).
Defender takeaway
Upgrade to 1.30.6 or 1.31.7 (NGINX Plus 37.0.5.1 or 37.1.0.1), starting with internet-facing instances whose configuration matches a pattern above; until a package is fixed, F5's workarounds are aio off or ssi off for CVE-2026-97205, named captures confined to the matching block for CVE-2026-93479, and no alias in the affected locations or no $request_filename reference for CVE-2026-15176 (Daily CyberSecurity, 2026-10-14).
Update25 Oct 2026 14:03 UTCrun 2026-10-25T1308Z-auditheadlinesummarysourcessourcing_noteactionsbody

Debian fixed the five flaws in trixie with DSA-6575-1, which ships nginx 1.26.3-3+deb13u10 in trixie-security (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-10-25). Bookworm's package, 1.22.1-9+deb12u10, is still marked vulnerable, so Debian has not shipped a bookworm fix (Debian Security Tracker, 2026-10-20).

Builds on: 2026-07-20/cve-2026-42533-nginx-pcre-capture-clobber-preauth-rce · 2026-05-15/cve-2026-42945-nginx-open-source-plus-f5-waf-products-18-yea · 2026-06-19/cve-2026-42530-cve-2026-42055-nginx-http-3-quic-use-after-fr

vulnerability20 Oct 03:55Zmulti-sourceOpen finding →
Sources: nginx.org (change log for nginx 1.30.6) · nginx.org (security advisories) · Centre for Cybersecurity Belgium (CCB) · Debian Security Tracker · Debian Security Tracker (DSA-6575-1, nginx security update) · Daily CyberSecurity · Help Net Security
NOTABLECVE-2026-110936exploitedNATOA2

CVE-2026-110936, Siemens Software Center: a ClickFix campaign runs a genuine signed copy of the application and side-loads its own DLLs, and Siemens confirms exploitation (CVSS 4.0 8.4)

Siemens ProductCERT says it has validated active exploitation of CVE-2026-110936, a DLL side-loading flaw in Siemens Software Center that Siemens fixed in version 4.0.9.8 and described in advisory SSA-580366 of 2026-10-15 (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19). The advisory scores it CVSS 4.0 8.4 (6.7 on CVSS 3.1, with a local vector and high privileges required) and lists every version before V4.0.9.8 as affected (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-15). The attackers did not rely on a copy already on the victim's PC: they used a genuine, validly signed copy of Software Center and placed their own files next to it, chosen as a carrier because it is signed and trusted and because version 3.5.8.7, the latest at the time, loaded helper files from its own folder without checking them; the Siemens program itself was not modified, and Siemens says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached to its knowledge (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19). Siemens labels the activity the Romulus multi-platform ClickFix campaign and names no actor (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19); one address that Siemens lists as the distribution channel of its malware bundle also appears among the ROMULUS hosts in Forescout's write-up of a ClickFix delivery platform, which does not mention Siemens software, and Forescout says it has no evidence that its panel is related to RomulusLoader, the malware Proofpoint reported (Forescout Vedere Labs, 2026-10-15). Huntress documented the same chain with other signed applications on 2026-09-28 and warned to expect more signed hosts (Huntress, 2026-09-28).

Exposure
Any Windows PC whose user pasted a command from a web page into the Run box or PowerShell, whether or not Siemens software is installed there, because the attackers bring their own copy; installed Software Center versions before V4.0.9.8 are affected as well until the application starts and updates itself (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19).
Detection
In process-creation telemetry, the signed Software Center executable running from a folder under the user profile's local Programs directory and started by msiexec, which Siemens names as the signal; in image-load and file telemetry, unexpected DLL and data files beside that executable outside the default installation folder; in persistence telemetry, a Software Center start-up entry or scheduled task on a PC that never had the product, and a service-named folder that the malware creates under the same Programs directory (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19). Siemens says to detect on folder and behaviour rather than on the file's fingerprint, because the file itself is genuine; where a PC matches, it says to isolate it, stop the process first, then remove the start-up entry and the task and reset passwords.

Triage: a real installation runs from the Siemens install location; the same executable running from the user profile's Programs folder, started by msiexec, with unexpected files beside it or start-up entries on a PC that never had the product, is the abuse (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19).

Defender takeaway
Update Software Center to V4.0.9.8 or later wherever it is installed, and hunt for the execution pattern above on every Windows endpoint, since the carrier is delivered with the lure and patching an installed copy does not stop it; the same hunt covers the other signed applications Huntress describes, and the lever at the front of the chain is the paste step into the Run box or PowerShell (Siemens ProductCERT, 2026-10-19; Huntress, 2026-09-28).

ROUTINENATOA2

BACS publishes five security classes for authentication methods: static secrets should in principle no longer be used, and only session-bound methods resist real-time phishing

BACS published on 2026-10-19 the technology assessment "Sicherheitsklassen für Authentifikationsverfahren, -mittel und -dienste", which sorts authentication methods, tokens and services into the three classes tief (low), mittel (medium) and hoch (high), with mittel and hoch each split further, five classes in all (BACS, 2026-10-19). The scheme follows the NIST authentication assurance levels 1 to 3 with slight adjustments and extends them for resistance to real-time phishing; BACS says the classification gives no basis for formal testing or certification and can serve organisations as a basis for security requirements and recommendations (BACS, 2026-10-19). In the assessment, class tief covers any method whose authentication information is static and identical at every login, such as a password or a cryptographic key, and the class does not rise when the secret travels over TLS; BACS concludes that methods in this class should in principle no longer be used (BACS, 2026-10-19). Class mittel needs authentication information generated anew for each login plus at least one further security feature, and the starred variant additionally needs session binding, which ties the session cryptographically to the authentication information or to the device, network or application; the assessment names TLS channel binding, Device Bound Session Credentials and OAuth DPoP as examples, against session hijacking, real-time phishing and adversary-in-the-middle attacks (BACS, 2026-10-19). BACS says the difference between mittel and hoch lies mainly in the use of additional hardware to store the cryptographic keys (BACS, 2026-10-19). Its annex of examples places a password, a static API key and a secret held in a cookie such as a session ID in tief; a password with an SMS code, a software authenticator app, Kerberos tickets, bearer tokens (SAML, OIDC, OAuth, JWT) and synced passkeys in mittel, the passkeys starred; and hardware OTP tokens, hardware certificates in TLS and FIDO2 without synchronisation or key export in hoch, with a footnote that SMS verification should be used only where no better alternative exists (BACS, 2026-10-19).

Defender takeaway
The classification binds no one and sets no deadline; it is a rough guideline (BACS's own term) that cantonal and communal bodies can use when writing authentication requirements. A login that rests on a static secret is class tief, which BACS says should in principle no longer be used, and a login resists real-time phishing and session hijacking only where it is session-bound (the starred classes) (BACS, 2026-10-19).

Update20 Oct 2026 03:40 UTCrun 2026-10-20T0256Z-intelsummarytechniquesactionssourcesevidencebody

Rapid7's incident analysis of an early-October NetScaler compromise shows CVE-2026-88771 chained with the SAML crash CVE-2026-88779, with the call-home crash handler running the payload as root after a reboot, followed by persistence that synchronises to the HA peer, internal reconnaissance and exfiltration of the appliance configuration and key material; an appliance that was reached needs the configuration secrets rotated as well as the patch.

Rapid7 published an incident analysis on 2026-10-19 of an early-October compromise of a NetScaler ADC on an affected 14.1 build, build number not given (Rapid7, 2026-10-19). Its logs show CVE-2026-88771 chained with CVE-2026-88779: text similar to a Pitboss crash message was inserted into an authentication username, repeated nsaaad crashes and a Pitboss reboot followed, and after the reboot the call-home crash handler processed the retained text and executed a payload as root, a chaining that avoided waiting 24 hours for the injected payload to run (Rapid7, 2026-10-19). The crash-and-reboot cycle recurred over several days and let the operator refresh persistence and deploy new components (Rapid7, 2026-10-19).

After the first root execution the operator installed cookie-authenticated PHP web shells behind Apache aliases that look like CSS files and answer with HTTP 404 bodies, set /bin/sh to mode 6555, and kept access through cron entries, boot scripts, watchdog loops, an outbound agent that polls every 15 seconds and an HTTP-fronted TCP proxy, with logic that synchronises implant files to the HA peer and forces a failover so the implanted node stays active (Rapid7, 2026-10-19). A Go tool recovered from the appliance mapped routes, DNS, LDAP and Active Directory, management services and VMware vCenter, and the configuration, historical configurations and system backups were staged and exfiltrated, one archive through the web root; Rapid7 says the archive can hold encrypted credentials, LDAP and RADIUS bind information, SSL private keys and key-encryption material (Rapid7, 2026-10-19). Rapid7 says the activity overlaps public WHIPSHOT and SLAPSHOT reporting and names no actor (Rapid7, 2026-10-19).

Rapid7 recommends patching to the fixed builds for both CVEs and verifying the September builds, collecting volatile evidence before rebooting or rebuilding, inspecting both nodes of every HA pair, and rotating all credentials and keys exposed through the configuration (Rapid7, 2026-10-19).

  • borderline-drop: Darktrace CikaBika, Calif Big Fish OpenBSD, KELA reports, AhnLab ARTEX, Sonatype Q3 index (S3) - outside the lookback, no CVE or exploitation, or statistics.

Single-source and carve-outs: cve-2026-110936-siemens-software-center-clickfix-sideload rests on Siemens ProductCERT alone for the exploitation of its own product (single-source, Admiralty A2); bacs-authentication-security-classes-technology-assessment is BACS on its own publication (single-source-national-cert). The Publica update attributes the federal note to SonntagsBlick (Blick is reliability C); the Finance Department's confirmation is limited to the Federal Council briefing. Reduced-confidence inclusions: none. Contradictions carried: OVHcloud lists v0.11.0 to v0.15.0 as compromised and the GitHub reporter checked v0.13.0 to v0.15.0 (both stated in the OVHcloud entry); the Debian tracker marks bookworm and trixie vulnerable while upstream marks 1.30.6 fixed (carried as distribution lag in the NGINX entry).

Dates for the next fires: Oracle's October Critical Patch Update lands 2026-10-20 (S1 read the pre-release: 1283 patches, 34 unauthenticated in E-Business Suite and 132 in Fusion Middleware; CVSS 9.9 for Essbase and Trusted Answer Search; the risk matrices carry the CVE ids, read with extract of oracle-cpu), the Atlassian monthly security bulletin is due 2026-10-20 and was not listed at 03:00 UTC, and Cisco publishes Expressway, IOS XR for ASR 9000, Secure Client, Snort and Unified Communications advisories on 2026-10-21. The 2026-10-21 fire should carry all three.

Candidate sources: opensourcemalware (S4) and forescout-research (S1) added, each cited by an entry this run. Not added: cve-services-api (S1's suggestion to sweep covered CVEs for state and SSVC changes through the CVE Services API found the Atlassian restoration and CISA-ADP's rating of CVE-2026-103849; the endpoint is on the gate's blocked-URL list, so a fire may read it but not cite it, and the audit can decide whether to make it a standing duty) and d3lab (S3, Italian phishing lab, no item this fire).

Coverage gaps: blick-ch (the 121 h lookback cannot be served: RSS holds about 12 h and the news sitemap about 48 h, so Blick items of 2026-10-15 to 2026-10-17 were not enumerated), kela-cyber (undated listing and gated reports), ahnlab-asec (reader-only listing and two of three reader keys exhausted), reliaquest (sitemap lastmod is not a publication date; no new post found), connectwise-trust-center (403 on every rung, no ConnectWise update after 2026-10-19 01:15 UTC could be read), my.f5.com (JavaScript shell on every transport; F5's text came through the CNA record as republished by Debian and by relays), parlament.ch committee pages (JavaScript-only), cyber.gouv.fr (Incapsula wall on the direct transport), hub.ivanti.com (unreadable on every transport; ivanti-advisory-hub is a stale fetch-gap id, the record is ivanti-psirt), ec-digital-strategy-newsroom and Europol feed items (undated listings).

Essential-coverage: all 21 essential records were attempted (S1 11, S2 10) and returned content; every authority feed was quiet.

Excluded as recent attempts: the belt-and-braces exclusion of the previous two fires' attempts removed 19 candidates from the S1 to S3 allocation; the breaches pool for S4 is 19 sources and both previous fires had attempted all of them, so S4 took 14 of them oldest-first from the rotation cursor instead of an empty slice. The slices were S1 14, S2 14, S3 14 and S4 14 standard or candidate records.

Source bookkeeping: last_successful_fetch moved for the sources whose items shipped, and consecutive_quiet_periods rose by one for the 41 sources whose ledger rows show a swept source with no in-horizon item. Promotions: bishopfox-blog, borncity and gambit-security met the three-run bar (sources.promotion_due).

Process: the container restarted mid-run (about 03:38 UTC) and killed the first FU1 spawn, which had written only progress lines; its work was lost and it was re-spawned once with the progress carried forward. The repository state on disk was intact. A stop hook asked three times for a commit while the run was mid-pipeline; nothing was committed before Phase 6.

Source health: tools/source_health.py probed 253 records; the first sweep put two on the UNSOLVED list (redcanary, stale since 2026-08-20 after its blog moved into Zscaler's, repointed to Zscaler's dated feed; connectwise-trust-center, unreadable on every transport today, set to blocked), and the second sweep ended with one needs-demote row for connectwise-trust-center that the blocked setting classes as handled on the next probe.

Self-identification: main agent Claude Sonnet 5.5 (claude-sonnet-5-5) from the harness-injected model line; all five research sub-agents (S1 to S4 and the FU1 follow-up) reported Sonnet 5.5 from their own prompt line.

Verification: four iterations, none CLEAN, ending on the low-residual early exit (rule 5). Iteration 1 (NEEDS_FIXES, 11 truth, 5 editorial, 4 advisory) caught that the NGINX entry named three flaws where nginx's own change log lists five and cited a rolling index page as a dated source, a stale ConnectWise title, an unsupported "about a week", an unsourced "unsigned" in the Siemens triage line, a Romulus name collision with RomulusLoader, a false run-record note about Forescout and the Publica enumeration that is Blick's gloss rather than the note's; all but four low-confidence items were fixed. Declined with rebuttal: the NGINX vulnerability-gate objection (F7: three unauthenticated pre-auth flaws scored 9.2 by F5 in the web server public-sector estates rely on, a national authority warns to patch at once, an earlier NGINX flaw was exploited three days after its public proof of concept, Debian stable is unfixed, and the entry says plainly that nothing is exploited), the Publica priority-high suggestion (F16: one outlet's reading of one confidential note, standing actions unchanged), the unreadable Citrix SAML guidance page (403 on every rung, unchanged earlier text) and the ConnectWise rolling advisory index (no per-incident permalink exists). The Atlassian record was retyped from update to improvement on the verifier's reading of the update-versus-improvement rule, so the entry is not re-floated. Iteration 2 (6 truth, 1 editorial, 4 advisory) was all wording precision (a "nobody analysed" absolute, a superlative in the Publica headline, an attack-complexity qualifier attached to a flaw whose page does not carry it, shorthand and a missing reference). Iteration 3 (2 truth, 2 editorial, 2 advisory) found that one address in Siemens' indicator list also appears among Forescout's ROMULUS hosts, which the Siemens entry now says without printing it. Iteration 4 (1 truth, 0 editorial, 1 advisory) found a weakness label that only the advisory carries and a vague closing sentence in an old Citrix paragraph; both were fixed and the fire published on the early exit with a residual count of 1 (the iteration's own truth count, already remediated). The 2026-10-19 note that Loxone was worth a re-check is answered in the borderline-drop list.

item.title: CTI Daily Brief · 2026-10-19
item.description: • Calendar-invite phishing spreads: Outlook and Gmail add the lure on their own and keep it after the email is deleted. Netcraft reports that phishing lures delivered as ICS calendar files, adopted by widespread campaigns of the EvilTokens Microsoft 365 token-stealing kit, are now spreading to low-effort scams. Outlook with Exchange Online (desktop, web and mobile) and Gmail with Google Calendar add such an invite to the calendar automatically as tentative and keep it after the email is deleted, so purging the message leaves the lure in place. EvilTokens invites posed as meetings, alerts or voicemail and led to a device-code page that has the victim authorise an attacker's device through OAuth; Sublime Security, quoted by The Guardian, reports exponential growth in calendar phishing. →
item.content:encoded:
TL;DR · the day in one read
  1. 01Calendar-invite phishing spreads: Outlook and Gmail add the lure on their own and keep it after the email is deleted. Netcraft reports that phishing lures delivered as ICS calendar files, adopted by widespread campaigns of the EvilTokens Microsoft 365 token-stealing kit, are now spreading to low-effort scams. Outlook with Exchange Online (desktop, web and mobile) and Gmail with Google Calendar add such an invite to the calendar automatically as tentative and keep it after the email is deleted, so purging the message leaves the lure in place. EvilTokens invites posed as meetings, alerts or voicemail and led to a device-code page that has the victim authorise an attacker's device through OAuth; Sublime Security, quoted by The Guardian, reports exponential growth in calendar phishing. →
Active threats, incidents & disclosures 1Updates to prior coverage 9Action items 10

01Active threats, incidents & disclosures1 item

NOTABLENATOB2

Phishing lures sent as ICS calendar invites land in Outlook and Gmail calendars without a click and stay after the email is deleted; EvilTokens used them for Microsoft 365 device-code phishing

Netcraft reports that attackers send phishing lures as ICS calendar files because the "text/calendar" type is treated as low risk by major email clients, and that the mail client's normal invite handling then places the lure in the victim's calendar with no user interaction, often keeping it there after the original email is deleted (Netcraft, 2026-10-16). In Netcraft's client table, Outlook desktop, Outlook on the web and Outlook Mobile with Exchange Online and Gmail with Google Calendar add the event automatically, mark it tentative and keep it after the email is deleted, Apple Calendar connected to Exchange Online often does the same, and Apple Mail with iCloud does not add it (Netcraft, 2026-10-16).

Campaigns using the EvilTokens toolkit, which steals Microsoft 365 tokens, used ICS invites disguised as meetings, alerts or voicemail notifications; the link leads to a page that gives the user a device code and tells them to enter it on Microsoft's device authorization page, which grants an attacker's device access to the account through OAuth (Netcraft, 2026-10-16). Netcraft now also sees smaller scams carrying ordinary phishing content inside ICS files (Netcraft, 2026-10-16). Sublime Security reports "exponential growth" in calendar phishing, with lures such as voicemail notices, payment receipts and renewal warnings that link to fake Microsoft, Google or PayPal logins or give a phone number, and Cofense says some senders use legitimate platforms such as Zoom to send the invitations, so filtering those platforms would also block real meetings (The Guardian, 2026-10-11).

Exposure
Users of Outlook with Exchange Online and of Gmail with Google Calendar, whose clients add external invites to the calendar on their own (Netcraft, 2026-10-16).
Detection
Netcraft names no telemetry; from the delivery path it describes, the traces are inbound external messages carrying a calendar part or ICS attachment in mail-flow logs, tentative events from external organizers the user never accepted in calendar audit logs, and, for the EvilTokens variant, a device-code sign-in to the account shortly after such an event (Netcraft, 2026-10-16). When responding to a reported phish of this kind, remove the calendar entry as well as the email, because the entry persists after the email is deleted (Netcraft, 2026-10-16).
Defender takeaway
Treat email-attached invites as part of the phishing attack surface: review whether the mail client settings add invites from outside the organization automatically for staff who do not expect them, and extend phishing guidance and purge procedures to calendar entries for those who do (Netcraft, 2026-10-16).
